If I could give 6 stars for service I certainly would. I suggest you tip these guys well.

My older brother took me here for lunch once, many years ago. I've been meaning to go back ever since. It's really expensive, and I cannot afford it at the moment but the second I can, I'm stepping through those black doors and eating some of the best Scandinavian food there is to be had. It's glorious.

I especially like the ginger-tasting beverage they give you midway through some of the pris fixe menus.

Amazing. I've been to the restaurant twice, the cafe once, and to a special brunch another time. Every time has been absolutely amazing -- there is nowhere else in New York, or maybe even the US, where you can get Scandinavian food like this. The herring is absolutely amazing, the aquavits are interesting (though, admittedly, perhaps not so authentic), and the Arctic Circle is my favorite dessert in the world (though when I was there in December of 2008, it was no longer on the menu...*sigh*). 

No complaints about the service or ambiance, though I would hope that would be the case given the prices.

i visited Aquavit cafe during restaurant week in February by the coercion of an eastern european friend with low expectations; she had previously dragged me to a  Polish restaurant which served entrees that i felt were a waste of space in my stomach.  thence, i filed away all eastern european cuisine, as i like all my food to be retardedly spiced.

okay, so i didn't get that at aquavit, but the food was great nonetheless. i really doubted that any swedish meatballs could ever trump IKEA's, but hey, surprise! good meatballs are to be found outside of IKEA as well.

alas, they don't sell them by the bag here.

i was born in NYC, but grew up in stockholm for most of my life, before returning for university.  my parents, understandably, are picky when it comes to scandinavian food outside of scandinavia.  

aquavit has yet to disappoint.  from an interior design that reminds me of the classy simplicity of stockholm bars and restaurants to a diverse menu of traditional and modern takes on the food up north.  of course the swedish meatballs are wonderful, along with the herring and potato leek soup.  the picks on a chef's tasting, which we've had on many a special occasion, are absolutely divine - especially the elk carpaccio, arctic char, the venison, and the lingonberry gelee.  wonderful.

what more can i say?  the next time my parents are in the country, we'll be back.

Had a pretty satisfying meal here.  We both tried the restaurant week menu.  We started with the herring sampler, and  I had the panbiff med lok.  Despite the Klingon sounding name, this is basically a fancy pan fried Salisbury steak with caramelized onions on top.  I also tried some of the skate wing.  Both were prepared very well, with great flavors.  The skate wing wasn't really a skate wing salad through, more like skate wing with a small amount of roasted veggies.  I also tried some lingonberry aquavit.  Strong, but good.  You can taste the lingonberry in the background when you're drinking it.

Aquavit was the perfect restaurant for dinner on that idyllic spring evening two years ago after I'd spent the day wandering along the avenues of Manhattan enjoying the unexpected beauty of nature in the city. As my Norwegian then-boyfriend, K., and I walked through the stylish bar and lounge on the way to the dining room, he said with approval, "This is very Scandinavian," noting Danish designer Arne Jacobsen's egg chairs and swan sofas. But even to my American eye, Aquavit had clearly been planned to exemplify the sexy, spare, nature-inspired aesthetic that is the hallmark of contemporary Scandinavian design. Inside the dining room an earth-toned palette and pale woods were complemented by black leather chairs and elegantly simple flowering branches in lieu of more formal, fussy floral arrangements.

Chef Marcus Samuelsson, who has distinguished himself by creating a new Scandinavian cuisine, offers the best traditions of Swedish food with modern seasonal preparations in his tasting menus at Aquavit, which ranks among the elite restaurants in New York. K., a fan of herring, chose the sampler appetizer. Not wanting to miss out on the full Scandinavian experience, I tried some of his pickled herring, which was served with a glass of Carslberg beer and the requisite shot of the restaurant's own aquavit. The eponymous spirit, classically emboldened by juniper berries and herbs, was a bit medicinal for my taste, but as it warmed my body it was easy for me to imagine how those long, dark, Nordic winter nights could be passed quite pleasantly with a bottle of aquavit and the company of a handsome Viking.

While my mind was still occupied with that fantasy, I continued my day's ode to spring by tasting the nettle soup, which was the very embodiment of the season with its beautifully vibrant green color bathing a perfectly poached egg. The soup's fresh and delicately earthy flavors coaxed me back from my fantasy and prepared my palate for my brioche-encrusted salmon entree with port wine sauce. The fish, moist under the delicate crust, was accompanied by a mosaic of spring vegetables and small cubes of beef cheeks that had been dried and then rehydrated, as a nod to an old Scandinavian method of preserving meat. The beef was amazingly tender to the bite, but even more surprising was the richly intense flavor concentrated in the tiny cubes.

As I was savoring my salmon and K. his seared tuna and scallop entree, I noticed the group at the table next to us had ordered a variety of desserts, but one was presented with particular flourish and announced as the "Arctic Circle." The state of the world being what it is these days, we couldn't pass up the opportunity to enjoy the Arctic Circle before it disappears and so ordered our very own. The goat-cheese parfait iceberg, served in a sea of refreshing sorbet and passionfruit sauce, didn't have a chance to melt away since we found it the perfect end to our meal.

Yet, courtesy of the chef, there was more to come--in the form of a small cardboard box that the waiter placed on our table. When I lifted the lid the scent of ginger rose from an assortment of mini cookies. I have never been fond of ginger cookies, but since these were Aquavit gingersnaps and a traditional Scandinavian favorite, I tried one. The bite-sized cookie, crisp on the outside yet tender inside, was delicious and sang with notes of fresh ginger, and I was converted on the spot. K. graciously allowed me to have all of the gingersnaps and I savored every one, grateful to him and to Marcus Samuelsson for my chic introduction to a sophisticated new Scandinavian cuisine.

Marcus works his magic (though nowadays he's not in the kitchen personally all that much - but when I went here in 2001 & 2002 he WAS!  You can have a light (read: less pricey) meal in the cafe section or go whole-gravlax in the main airy, beautiful dining room.

Be sure to try the namesake Aquavit - Scandanavian jet-fuel.

Wandered in for lunch one day while touring the city. The main dining room was full so we ate in the cafe. The space looked a bit worn. There were stains on the carpet and the upholstery but to make up for it, it was the herring festival. They had the smorgasbord set up in the cafe and it was herring 50 different ways (or so it seemed). 

My son, not being a fan of herring, went with the steak frites. My wife and I tried to sample every variety and iteration of herring they were serving. I think we succeeded, twice. The herring was great the Carlsbergs were cold and our son thought the steak was one of the best that he has had. Our meal was a success.

LINGONBERRY LOVIN' 

I must say that I thoroughly enjoyed my first trip to Aquavit. 

DECOR: 
The design is very Scandinavian and is stylish, modern, accessible, and efficient. It's like a more refined Ikea sans the stressed-out couples ready to kill each other over a disagreement on what color their Poang or Klippan should be. 

SERVICE: 
Excellent. My server made great recommendations and refilled my drink without having to ask me what I was having. She simply asked if I wanted another and then checked to see what I ordered on my bar tab. A little touch that would go unnoticed by many, but I appreciated the level of thoughtfulness. 

FOOD: 
Wonderful. Right of the bat, I loved that the crusty crouton came with a light, airy salmon mousse instead of butter. I could eat a tub of the stuff if left to my own devices. I then moved on to the herring sampler and selected the pickled, curry, and matjes varieties based on my server's recommendations. It was my first experience with herring and I found it absolutely delicious; not fishy at all. 

There were about 10 entrees that I wanted to try, but I opted for the classic Swedish meatballs for a very reasonable $19. Wow. This dish was fantastic. Imagine perfectly cooked meatballs in a light cream sauce resting on a bed of buttery mashed potatoes, accompanied by thinly-sliced pickled cucumbers, and plump lingonberries for tartness and acidity. Those lingonberries really made the dish pop and I left wondering if I could ever go back to the lowly cranberry. 

All in all, it was a fantastic meal and I can't wait to go back.

This review is for the lunch set.

Absolutely underwhelmed.

Herring sampler was overly salty. I couldn't even finish eating it.

Pork loin entree was dry. Enough said.

Princess cake dessert was...well, pretty mediocre. 

Service was also amiss.  I was promised more water "shortly" and it only came 10 mins later when I waved someone down.  

Sigh.

Swedish sampler...nice presentation and tasty  bites of herring, salmon, elk, an oyster on the half shell, and a meatball: $22.  The New Brunswick, Canada oyster appetizer: excellent oysters on the half shell.   Avoid  the salmon burger---way tooo salty!!!!!  A bottle of sparkling Voss water set us back $9

I had the prix fixe menu with my wife last Friday.  Incredible!  The food was perfect.  I was very happy but not overly full after the dinner.  Herring sampler was incredible.

Service was very good with a couple of minor glitches (they brought us two intermezzo courses one after the other -- I ordered a Carlsbad beer on two occasions but neither came).  The beer mix up was fine considering the accompaniments to the herring sampler and we were not charged for them.

I would definitely go back!  It is not a cheap meal (at all) but definitely worth it for a special occasion.

Remember in Scooby Doo, there was always Red Herring, who they blamed every crime on?  Well...  Herring definitely doesn't do justice here.  

Only being in New York for one Sunday, I decided that Aquavit would be the brunch buffet I dive into as it's not one of the more casual ones, but it's not as pricey as some high end hotel ones.  $48 still wasn't a very good price... at least for what they offered.  Decor is very clean cut and modern.  Good.  Sunday brunch buffet?  Meh. I've experienced better.

To start off, the complimentary bloody mary was overly heavy on the horseradish, and this made it practically undrinkable.  Other people ordering it requested more tomato juice after taking their initial sip...
After taking a few sips of the unbearably spicy beverage, we were onto the buffet.  

Obviously they place their famous herrings on the front end.  Mediocre they looked, and mediocre they were...  With many variations they all tasted pretty much the same.  Curry herring, herb herring, tomato herring... all very herring-like... with some extra flavors.  Sweeter herring preparations were better here.

Cold cut meats were as ordinary as could be, with roast beef and ham all tasting like they came straight out of the grocery store.  They didn't even offer some nice cured meats.  The one cheese they had was not bad, though.  In redemption, both hot and cold smoked salmons were mighty delicious.  With creme fraiche and a sweet brown mustard, the salmons were awesome.  Tomato, mushroom, and beet salads were all extremely boring, without any twist.

Hot foods:  Brisket, Swedish meatballs, and this cream potato casserole thing.  All were ok at best.  Meatballs were tasty, but dry.  Brisket the same.  My favorite thing here was definitely the potato strips.

Desserts:  Pretty run-of-the-mill.  A fly was in the rice pudding though.  One redeeming aspect was the extremely fresh raspberries.  I ate about an entire plate of just their raspberries.

So in short, good service, good sampling, good atmosphere, not so good brunch.  Overpriced and bland.

This is for the main dining room dinner setting. 

I went to Aquavit twice. Both times ordered Chef tasting menus including a special valentine menu for the second time I ate there. 

I love the long hall way with a contemporary wood/loft feeling. There is a rest/waiting area and and the end of the hall is a long sleek bar. It's not a busy bar but I enjoyed it while I waited for my friend. The drinks are decent, you will need to try Aquavit (obviously haha) 

The main dinning room's decor resembles a relaxed hotel/cafe setting. There is a great group/long table in the entrance followed by a main dining area and some booths along the wall. Colors are simple and nothing too busy. 

Crowd is usually pretty typical midtown (business men and some young professionals) It's def. not a place you go to see the crowd. 

The food was fantastic. I loved the fact that when I ordered a tasting with my friend each course for us was different, so it was essentially tasting 18 different dishes between the two of us. There were about 9 courses. The first couple ones are small portions, nicely presented with the right amount of sauce for every bite. I loved their herring and lobster roll. The arctic char was great as well. Dessert was very nice with multiple flavors of sorbet etc. 

I had a great time there and I think the food is not the typical American, Asian Fusion, Italian or French. It's a special restaurant and a great option for people who want something different.

I went here for dinner in the Dining room during winter restaurant week, but ended up ordering the Full tasting menu.  Overall the food was pretty good, but lacked that "wow" factor I was hoping for.  The decor is clean and the wait staff was attentive. 

Perhaps the most memorable part of the experience was watching a  young couple that sat a few tables away take several flash-photos of each plate that was served on their tasting menu.  It was pretty hard not to laugh at the guy who was sitting closest to them as he was visibly annoyed while trying to carry on a smooth conversation with his date.  The couple taking pictures were acting as if each dish was a little puppy. I'm surprised there's not more photos on Aquavit's Yelp profile!

I just had the Restaurant week dinner here last night.

Read some reviews from other websites before i came here and it was pretty dead on.

First time hving swedish food...besides ikea..that doesnt count haha..did it tickle my tastebuds? the appetizer and dessert did. the entree however.. was very disappointing .

for appetizers,i listened to yelpers advice and went for the  herring plate. i LOVED IT ..highly recommended ! Friend got the chilled corn soup..she thought it was so-so.

the entrees were so anticlimatic ! my friend went for the salmon which was promising but my swedish meatalls. not so cool..in fact...so sad but i have to say i've sometimes had better swedish meatballs at ikea. 
Our dinner was around 9pm but the meatballs were dry and tasted like it has been sitting in the kitchen for the whole night...

Dessert was amazing though....for RW... u get to choose between Arctic circle and the chocolate mousse... i vote for the arctic circle..the goat cheest parfait tasted like nothing i've ever had and the passionfuirt filling in the center wil surprise you. Chocolate mousse was above standard.

Verdict? I loved the decor, atmosphere and service here. kind of like gotham bar and grill but with less people. Good experience for RW but probably won't come back regularly for dinner. The bar/lounge area however, is very nice....a drink wouldn't hurt :D

Once again I feel disappointed by my NYC restaurant week experience at one of the "top" restaurants available during this promotion, Aquavit. My husband is a chef and we dine out very frequently.  We typically like to order a pre-dinner aperitif, champagne or cocktail.  Because we were dinning at aquavit, we decided to each try one of their many specialty cocktails made with their house made concoctions.  We also order from the three course restaurant week menu and a bottle of wine to follow.  Our bottled water and popcorn amuse came out right away, as did bread, quickly followed by our appetizers, no drinks.   This began our night on the wrong foot, who knows if it was a bartending error, or server mistake, but it should be said the restaurant was not even half full come our 6:15 reservation.  We decided to slow down the process ourselves, and thank goodness we choose two cold appetizers, my husband the salad and me the herring.    I noticed that the table to our left also received the herring sampler, however had it delivered on a different set up and had each portion explained to them.  
Again I will say the obvious, I think that restaurant week is an excellent opportunity to appeal to dinners that have never been to your restaurant and you should treat the RW attendant the same as a customer to your regular menu.  If we had been treated more fairly I might actually consider dinning again, if not solely for the dessert portion of the meal which was show stopping. 
 The entrees have mixed reviews; my husbands chicken was moist and flavorful with cheesy grits, however the regular string beans could have been better, haricot vert? My meatballs were so dry; my husband got the feeling they were leftovers from the day before.  No one actually check on us through our meal, and my husbands small outburst regarding the rock hard nature of my MB went unanswered, I actually sent him outside because I was embarrassed. Ikea's meatballs are ten times more moist and flavorful. Once the dessert and dessert wine came out our meal took a turn for the better, the chocolate moose was superb and the Arctic Circle was surprisingly refreshing for a cheese parfait.  Despite our $24.00 coupons I doubt we will be back to dine again.

I am another Restaurant Week customer for Aquavit. Like the last reviewer, I also went for the Herring Plate (absolutely fantastic unless you count a few distinctly "herringish" burps later on in the evening, sorry for the gross-out) and then for the Meatball entree, which unlike others I will have to say was pretty fantastic. I come from a family of swedish heritage and these meatballs were the closest any of us present had tasted to our traditional family recipe, which we enjoy every christmas. Also, their Arctic Circle dessert was rich and delicious. 

More pluses I will add that I haven't seen here:

Portions for all the dishes were satisfying without being overpoweringly large. We also had the salmon dish and the chicken from the RW menu at our table and all were sumptuously sized but not supersized. Quite a bit of bang for the buck, if you're counting (which I am). 

Also, complimentary appetizers of a selection of breads and a dish of surprisingly savory seasoned popcorn were quite delicious. 

Cocktails before the meal were outrageous. I had just my standard Blue Point beer (pretty reasonably priced at $6 for a restaurant in this price range) but others had an Aquavit salted greyhound which was divine, and another option from the champagne cocktails which was quite sweet and fruity, if that's your trip. I should also mention the mini RW wine list (two whites and two reds) is extremely reasonable at $35 a bottle -- that was an unexpected delight. We got a cote-du-rhone varietal which was new to all of us, but which went incredibly well with my choices of herring and meatballs. 

Decor and ambience at this place is unique and very pleasing on the eye -- nice low lighting in the dining room, wonderful choices in everything from cutlery to furniture. 

Lastly, the SERVICE at Aquavit is, in my limited experience, outstanding. There wasn't a moment in the entire evening we didn't feel attended to. I felt we were extremely well taken care of, but at the same time I don't think it was special treatment -- I think that is simply the standard here, even though restaurant week is doubtless one of the busiest times of the year.

All in all, I feel like I made a great choice for restaurant week! And now I have a place in my little mental list of places to revisit, time and money allowing, which is pretty near the top.

Loved it. My husband went for their Summer Tasting menu while I stuck with Restaurant Week menu. I loved everything I had, including the herring plate, Swedish meatballs, and best of all Arctic Circle, which has got to be one of THE best desserts I've ever had in my life. I have a tendency to inhale my food but this I took forever to eat because I wanted to SAVOR it! Thought the serving size was not skimpy at all, especially considering what a deal the RW menu is for this restaurant. My husband was very pleased with everything he had as well, except one dish (arctic char) where cold broth was poured over the fish and made it lukewarm. The broth was, of course, supposed to be hot. When my husband pointed it out to the waiter, he quickly took the dish away and brought us three different bites of food (lobster roll, grilled cheese, I forget what the last one was) AND comped us a glass of wine. The fish came out perfect the second time, BTW.

Edit:
We've gone back twice since, once to their cafe for the crayfish week and the other time for a prix-fixe dinner at the dining room. Crayfish sampler was NOT good, but it may be that we don't really care for crayfish (too much work!) The three-course dinner was lovely, my husband LOVES their herring sampler and seared tuna, I was happy with my venison though the foie gras ganache was a little disappointing. Arctic Circle is still our favorite dessert EVER, we'll come back JUST for their herring sampler and Arctic Circle. Their wine selection isn't that great, especially by glass, but my husband loved all the aquavits he finally tried -- he ordered a flight of three and ended up with THREE extra shots! Rather generous! They really need to change the cushions on the booth couch though, seems like they haven't changed them since it opened. Also our waiter this time wasn't quite as knowledgeable and sophisticated as last time, my husband guessed he might be a bus boy filling in for a waiter. For these reasons I don't think it can quite compete with other finer, four-star restaurants but the food is undoubtedly good and it's a nice change from all the new-American and French cuisine so four stars are staying.

Fantastic. The service was amazing, the food delicious. 

Ate in the Dining Room for Restaurant Week.
Had three of the Aquavits( which are housemade flavored vodkas) to start ($17).  Lingonberry, Lychee, and Orange blossom.

All were good, the Lingonberry was my favorite.

Did the restaurant week menu ($35).

Started with the Herring Plate which was delicious.  The cheese and potatoes to go with it really complemented the fish well.  Yummy.

Complimentary Popcorn was a nice touch. A good way to cleanse the palate in between courses.  Bread was yummy too.

Main Course was the Swedish Meatballs.  I had to do it. I went to sweden in the fall and had them their as well and these were just as good.  The mash potatoes were amazing. 

Desert was the Arctic Circle which is one of the strangest if not amazing desert ever. I don't really know what was in it, except that involved, goat cheese, raspberry, and had a cheesecake like consistency.  Really yummy though. 

My bf had the Salmon which the piece I tried melted in my mouth. Really cooked to perfection. For appetizer and dessert he had the same thing I  had.

The last thing to note here is the service which is outstanding.  My boyfriend ordered a beer, and after he poured half of it in his glass, the waiter offered to keep the remainder of it cold while he drank the first half!  Really beautiful restaurant and a place I would go back to in a heartbeat.

Its super dark in here. With that said, blinding people by taking pictures is not a good idea. I came here for restaurant week, and damn it was dark in there! 

The chilled beet soup, is just that, cold, from the fridge, the smoked salmon was ok. the soup overall was ok. The herring plate is pretty good considering you enjoy herring and cheese. 

Main dish time! My god, their swedish meatballs were horrid! they were dry and the ones at ikea were better! I have no idea what was going on there! But the salmon, my god the salmon was amazing! Cooked to perfection, tender, flavorful, god they know their fish. And if you like fish, definitely order this!

Dessert was pretty amazing, who thought goat cheese parfait would be so tasty? Called Arctic Circle its so damn good! Aside from the fact that you're gonna bang on your plate when you try to take some off your spoon from the top of the dessert. Just try to be discreet, knock that sucker over and devour it! The chocolate mousse was too sweet for me, but the sorbet was refreshing. 

I like how they only gave you one piece of bread instead of a basket. And the popcorn they gave you was kinda cute. Its still popcorn afterall, they try to class it up by saying they put some dill or cheese on it, but its still popcorn!

Tried the 3course RW menu.  Party of 4 on a rainy Thursday night. We had reservations.

The Herring sampler was fine. Easily the best thing of the night, but not worth a trip back.

The salmon was the same as any other salmon.  I suppose that by choosing RW to visit Aquavit Cafe, i became a beggar and not a chooser.

The meatballs were plain, as though a fifth-grader had pounded some meat together and forgotten seasonings. To be fair, they WERE balls - not squares or anything.

The arctic circle was quite good, but again, it was just goat cheese made into cheesecake with a touch of sweet. 


The worst and most disappointing piece of the affair was that the staff let down the magic curtain, the 4th wall - I was not dining in a place that tried to welcome me, I was sitting in a diner with a waitress who was happy to bring me any of the dishes she didn't understand either. 

We were surrounded by people in jeans.

We were the last to leave.  We received coupons for $24 off our next visit, if it should fall within August.  We left them on the table.

YUM! 
I had the restaurant week menu here....it was sooooo good! 
loved the meat balls, tasty and great mash! 
loved the arctic circle dessert, a goat cheese cheese cake/ ice cream consistency dessert with passion fruit in the center....loved it ! 
The waitress was super nice and the service superb.
worth the trip!

Let me preface by disclaiming that I'm a huge seafood fan, and have had some of the best in the world from CA to Tokyo.... and I've had a hard time finding great (not just good) seafood in NYC.

So, came here for Restaurant Wk..

The Herring sampler appetizer was awesome; some of the best tasting fish I've had in NYC; though I think the cheese/potatoes are better had separately from the fish.

For my entree, I had the seared salmon... again one of the best fish dishes I've had in a long time.

The Scandinavian touch was a good change in the style of seafood that I've never had before, and the popcorn appetizer (though awkward to have in such a classy setting) was a pleasant surprise too.

Also had the Coconut Espresso aquavit; nothing really special here, just an overpriced, shot-sized martini.

The -1 star is for the fact that it can feel a bit stuffy, and our waiter (and hostesses) were a bit haughty.. so definitely not a regular place, but all in all, a great restaurant and would definitely come back again. And keep in mind, it can be pricey, but again, great place for those once-in-a-while occasions.

Four of us decided to try Aquavit last Friday during Restaurant Week.  Maybe that was our mistake, because I can find no other explanation for the haughtiness with which we were treated.  The waiter came to our table 3 times within the first minute after being seated for our drink order, but only gave us one cocktail menu that we were forced to pass around to each other in the very dark dining room. We should have requested little flash lights and magnifying glasses - apparently they are provided if one knows to ask. No sooner did our cocktails arrive, then our appetizers were slammed down with what I assume was an amuse-bouche; a dish of popcorn.  Cold, plain popcorn.  What were they thinking? Within seconds of finishing our appetizers, the plates were whisked away and the main course presented.  Any second offers on bread? No. Was the food good?  Yes, but certainly not transcendent.  The enormous portion of "attitude" served far negated the meal. We will not be returning to Aquavit.

Restaurant Week(s) Summer 2009

The herring starter was delicious, full-flavored with a lasting impression on the palate.  The cheese and potatoes in the center of the plate did not add, but thankfully, nor did it detract from the rest of the dish.

The salmon was perfectly cooked and coaxed into such a state that it would melt tenderly as it hit your tongue.  Having said that, it was not an exceptional piece of salmon that stood head and shoulders above every other piece of salmon I've ever had, nor was it an exceptionally composed dish that demonstrated any revolutionary feats of cookery.  But it was certainly delicious, paid due service to the product at hand, and I enjoyed it.

I read one previous review describing how horrible the Swedish meatballs were. One of my friends ordered the meatball entree, and I have to say that she probably got lucky (or the other reviewer was very unlucky).  The meatballs I tried were savory, juicy, and absolutely fulsome in flavor.  They were certainly better than the ones you get at IKEA.  But given other negative reviews about the meatballs, then perhaps overall consistency in execution is a problem.  In contrast,  everyone at our table who ordered the salmon received a dish of the same, superb quality, and other reviewers seem to be consistently happy with the salmon as well.

The arctic circle dessert was the real highlight of the meal for me.  The blueberry sorbet was marvelously intense in flavor and served as a perfect counterpoint to the rich creaminess of the goat cheese parfait and passionfruit curd.  No one even thought twice about whether or not they were missing out by not ordering the... ummm... you know... what was that other dessert again?

I've read a few posts about concerns regarding "worse service" for customers during Restaurant Week, so I was a bit guarded when I arrived.  But needless to say, our waiter was attentive and polite, and without any air of haughtiness.  

PS - we each received a coupon for $24.07 off our next meal at Aquavit (to be redeemed before October 1st).  Considering that the summer tasting menu is $55, this would mean that a repeat visit could garner more dishes for less than the $35 we paid for our 3 course Restaurant Week meal!

We had lunch at Aquavit yesterday and it was fantastic. The service was attentive and efficient, and the decor is classic Scando design without the trendiness (which is a plus.) The breads and herbed butter are tasty (eventhough I'm not big on bread), and my friend and I both had the herring and cheese sampler for appetizers which were fantastic. The curried herring and the herring with the salmon roe were my favorites, though they were all exceptionally good. The salmon entree was good -- fresh and tasty though it played second fiddle to the herring, and my friend's Swedish meatballs were soft and delicious and similar to the ones I've had in Sweden (I'm surprised some Yelpers preferred Ikea meatballs which are like little rocks of vague flavor.) The Arctic Circle for dessert was fantastic -- goat cheesecake with passion fruit center and raspberries with a little wafer and a drizzle of chocolate. I'll definitely come back just for that, and the herring will make me want to stay.

Went here on a business lunch and had a great time.  The service was really great.  Our waiter was super friendly and answered all of our questions (and we had a lot--there were 8 of us at the table) amiably and in detail.

The design of the restaurant is very impressive.  You enter into a long hallway (great-room, rather) that has the bar and a sitting area (where, I also noticed, you can have lunch) and the dining rooms branch off from the hall.  It feels very Scandinavian--all neutral tones and clean design lines. 

The food was really good.  Scandinavian isn't my favorite cuisine but I had an excellent meal.  I ordered the Smörgsbord, which is a sampler of 10 different bites.  Herring, salmon, meat, and an oyster were all part of the plate.  It was good and I am glad I got to try so many things.  However, what was really excellent was the Lobster Roll appetizer.  It's not a traditional "roll" as you'd expect.  Rather, the lobster is wrapped to look like an thin egg-roll--i think they use some variation of crepe for the roll(?).  It is topped with Roe and is also served with shrimp to the side.  And, it came with ginger aquavit, which was a big plus!

Also, the lemonade was pretty good.  I don't like it too sweet, and this lemonade was just the right amount of tartness.  

For desert I had a scoop of salted carmel ice-cream (it was good, but nothing to rave about) and an excellent double espresso.  They know their coffee.

I'm glad I went here; it's a great alternative to the gazillion Italian and steak restaurants in midtown.

Pros:
Design, ambiance
Good lemonade and coffee
Excellently prepared food

Cons (and this is really nitpicky):
It's Scandinavian food, so you better like your salmon and herring and Swedish meatballs

I would give it half a star if that's an option. To start with, we had a very standoffish waiter who seemed to think he was way better than what he was doing. Regardless, I ordered the chilled corn soup and seafood stew. The soup was good, but nothing worth noting. 

The seafood stew on the other hand was a total disaster. The mussels were cold, fishy, and never cooked in the stew to catch any of the flavor. Shrimps were overseasoned and overcooked. There were two different cuts of fish, salmon and something else that tasted blend, both overcooked. They didn't even use fresh salmon for the stew, it was cooked over-salted smoked salmon. It really tasted like they pre-cooked the ingrediants and just splashed some blend sauce over it.  I would never go back.

My husband, child, and I came here during RW.  I ordered the chilled corn soup, the swedish meatballs, and the arctic circle for dessert.  The soup reminded me way too much of meat soaking in an egg-milk mixture and was generally very unappetizing.  Nate was our waiter and he was great, though, he offered to change it for something else since he saw that I hadn't eaten anything.  Now for the Swedish meatballs...seriously, they're better and WAY cheaper at IKEA.  LOL  The dessert (Arctic Circle) was AMAZING.  The meal was pretty mediocre, but the dessert was definitely worth going back for.  BTW, there are absolutely no changing tables in the bathrooms.  not kid-friendly.

Came here for Summer Restaurant Week 2009:

Appetizer -- Herring plate: really an acquired taste. Even the waitress agreed that it's one of those dishes that you either love it or you don't. The different flavors were really amazing, but herring is just too fishy for me. 

Entree -- Swedish meatballs: tasty, although a bit dry. Not what I expected however...totally didn't amaze me. I tried a piece of the salmon and that was very tender.

Dessert -- Chocolate mousse: very creamy, with a hint of hazelnut. Got a little too sweet after a couple of bites, but very yummy. 

Really clean, simple decor. The high ceilings and dim lighting really make the place feel very modern and chic.

Oh my...that was...superb. (Be warned that I am prepared to gush throughout this review) 

The general ambience was clean, fresh and simple. I much preferred the light and airy Cafe to the darker but more elegant Dining Room. Service was prompt and polite. Our waitress was especially nice. 

Aquavit was my first foray into Swedish cuisine (Swedish meatballs out of the Betty Crocker cook book do not count) and quite frankly I was overwhelmed with delight. I generally complain about fish that tastes too "fishy," but in this case I would say that the herring plate was in fact "fabulously fishy." The plate consisted of several "bites" of fish. Each was prepared in a slightly different way and I enjoyed every one of them. The Swedish meatballs were moist and succulent and the lingonberries and mashed potatoes made you feel as if you were eating a 5-star version of your favorite home cooked meal. The dessert was tantalizingly good. Goat cheese parfait with blueberry sorbet, "Wonderful!" But when my fork discovered the passion fruit curd in the center my happiness was beyond belief! I walked back to the subway with little sighs of satisfaction after each block and every few minutes I would say to my friend, "Wow that was really good."

I ordered from the restaurant week menu. I was very disappointed with the entree and dessert. I got the Swedish meatballs and I must say the ones I order from ikea are much better. The other choices were the salmon and chicken. Not exciting at all. I understand prices are lower for prefixed menus during restaurant week, but I would not recommend the food here. Atleast differentiate from the IKEA meatballs. The only difference was that Aquavit gave me less sauce and the meat was very dry. 

Aside from the bad meatball dish review, I would recommend this restaurant for a date or business dinner as the atmosphere is great. The seating allows privacy and it is not noisy.

I ate in the Cafe last night - which had a nice atmosphere - our waitress was very nice throughout the night .. 

I had the watermelon margarita - which is made with house-infused tequila and well of course watermelons - it was DELICIOUS!!! by far one of the best drinks i have had in new york - perhaps ever.. it tasted better than biting down into a juicy fresh watermelon.

We also had the Herring sampler appetizer - AMAZING! i was very pleased that my fellow yelpers steered me in the right direction..

with our entrees, we had the Swedish Meatballs and the Beef Reyding.. it was .. alright at best.. the food was good - but definitely not as great as expected.

I think the next time I come - I will head straight for the bar for a drink and the herring.. and then move on to another location for entrees.

I had dinner here, and it was a very beautiful restaurant with candles everywhere.  The staff was super friendly and helpful.  I had a watermelon margarita that tastes just like a real watermelon (it's probably because there wasn't a lot of alcohol in their cocktails). 

The important part: 
The food however deserves 2-2.5 stars.  I tried the Swedish Meatballs and Beef Rydberg.  The meatballs were very plain and the beef consisted of flavorless cubes of meat.  The herring sampler appetizer (I chose curry, vodka lime, and pickled) was good, but not much better than what you would find at a Jewish deli.  My rating is this low because what I ordered were hearty dishes that belong in a hole-in-the-wall, mom-and-pop joint or grandma's kitchen.  For such an elegant restaurant as Aquavit, I expected some creativity in their dishes.

My last day in NYC, I made appointment to go to Aquavit because I wanted to try something different compare to the regular fine dining of French, Japan, etc. I found the right place plus the Chef is well known for his style of cooking. The place was nice and trendy and they have great affordable option for lunch such like a 3 course prix dinner for $24, a 1 lbs crawfish and crawfish buffet for $27 and a $55 Chef tastering menu. I enjoy how they offer such affordable lunches and dinner esspecially in these hard time. I order the herring tasting plate, swedish meatball for my entree and a artic circle for desert. My friend order  the corn chowder w/beets and raw salmon, Salmon w/tomato for a entree and a chocolate mouse for desert. I enjoy eating the herring alot esspecially all of the different types of how they prepare it. The swedish meatball was good and simple. The highlight of the meal has to be the desert. I am not a desert fan but they all came out great and it outshine the meal easliy. They even brought out a extra desert because it was my friend birthday. We did enjoy the meal and the price came out to $70 with tip. It one of the cheapest fine dining I been thru but don't let the price fool you. I had a great time there.

tried during restaurant week. the herring app was good. u have to like herring though. the artic circle dessert was best. the swedish meatballs did dissapoint a bit. i have had better swedish meatballs when I go xcountry skiing up in lapland lake xcountry ski center.

The herring is where it's at, certainly on par with what I've tasted in Holland and Iceland. We had one server who was a little impatient and overeager to get our orders but other than that service was fine. One looked like he had stepped right off the Mad Men set so that certainly improved my dining experience, as did the raspberry aquavit cocktail I had to sip on. The salmon was a nice cut, rather large actually, but the roasted fennel and tomatoes were tastier to me. As a pescetarian I can't attest to the quality of the famous meatballs. The arctic circle dessert was too much, but in a good way. I only wish there had been less goat cheese, more passionfruit curd. YUM. I plan on returning to the cafe for herring and aquavit when I can.

I got reservations for here because it was doing Restaurant Week and why not choose the best.
For dress code, they don't allow sneakers and I think slacks are suggested.
The service is impeccable and it's the best I've experienced. You get a choice of bread with dill butter. The Scandinavian crunchy one is worth a try.
Before appetizers, we were offerred two amuse-bouches. One was a small piece of tuna with a fruit salad. The fish just melts in your mouth. The other was a salmon tartar with caviar.
For appetizers, I ordered the herring plate. It comes with a fantastic cheese that I'm still dying to find out the name of. The herring is prepared in four different ways. I love variety. Don't get turned off because it's herring. It's worth the try, be adventurous.
For the main course, I ordered the Swedish meatballs with lingonberry jam and potato mash. I've only had Swedish meatballs out of a microwable Smart Ones, so this was a great change. Dare I say better than Italian meatballs and the jam complemented the heavy saltiness very well. The mash was smooth and perfect.
I also got the try the seared salmon and it was unbelievable.
For dessert, the Arctic Circle is extravagant and the sorbet with it is the best I've ever had. I'm not a huge sweets person, but my girlfriend loved the mousse.
Such an fantastic deal for Restaurant Week. Definitely somewhere worth to go even without that. The best restaurant I've been to yet.

Aquavit literally means "water of life", so you can understand when I say their cocktails and "aquavit" is good, although pricey for a small pony glass.  It's not meant to be done as a shot, but sipped slow and enjoyed, however people have been known to chug.

Anyway, I went there during the crayfish event, which happens every Tuesday in August and lovingly gorged on their crayfish buffet which, of course, included herring (done very well, might I add), cured salmon, and crayfish sides.  It was a wonderful assortment.

But all non-crayfish aside, Aquavit's offerings are wonderful and their service is on the money.  By the way, they do have a dress code, and reservations and strongly suggested.  

They do offer a special pre fixed menu available during restaurant week, which is a great time to stop by.  This place does look like something out of a high end IKEA commercial, but then again it's Scandinavian cuisine, so it kind of comes with the territory.

My salad was fine and my dessert (the Arctic Circle) was excellent, but my entree really didn't live up to expectations.  I ordered the only vegetarian entree: the zucchini ravioli.  The flavors and textures were muddled; the zucchini was nothing special; and the portion was way too small.  I ended up feeling jealous of my friend's big dish of Swedish meatballs!

ate in the cafe for the first time last night (sat). were seated promptly but then waited maybe 15 minutes for menus, water and any sort of acknowledgment that we existed at all (there were several empty tables). when we DID get server's attention, we gave drink, appetizer and entree order at same time. waited a WHILE for the appetizers - and still no drinks. by the time entrees arrived (probably more than an hour after our arrival), were cold. though the flavors were good, even the best food could not make up for the extreme waits and lackluster service. had been told that we had to try desserts... 30 minutes after ordering, they came out. without a doubt the WORST dining experience we've ever had in the city. i created a yelp account only to warn others of it. canceling plans for dining room reservation later this month--will NEVER return!
I've been many times...the food is excellent; the atmosphere boring and stuffy.  The desserts AMAZING!

Aquavit is a classic example of the sadly enduring off-themed vegetarian option; the conspicuous zucchini ravioli slides in at the bottom of the menu, you know, for "those people." But while so often the vegetarian option is merely an acceptable entree for "us" while our "normal" friends enjoy the cognitive arts of chefs, this ravioli dish is remarkably ballsy. The sweetness of the zucchini is fostered and explored in two forms - the delicate buttery stuffed pasta and the ribbons of flesh mingled with coconut and pine nuts with the aromatic dill pesto permeating all but not overwhelming the pallet http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/f7apP8A_0_KqcGQTK4V2TQ?select=kapca2l8jmcui0SIX69nig Unfortunately the fragile poise of this dish is not met every night; on my last visit the dish fell heavy before me, the zucchini excessively sauteed and the pasta overly salted http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/f7apP8A_0_KqcGQTK4V2TQ?select=ovCIa9sjPSuI4FyiFgiZSg 

The first course menu offers me next to nothing; my meager salad http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=XIZ93IR3Yrj2GDlhs_Wf8A&select=xUOghWaRWRU-I3kU2fSqBw paled in comparison to the bountiful Herring Sampler http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=XIZ93IR3Yrj2GDlhs_Wf8A&select=GjPg5lLr5B1LjFtNjHSW7g 

Dessert is a laudable course at Aquavit, the star of which is the highly regarded Arctic Circle, a tubular goat cheese parfait filled with passion fruit curd and topped with a thin crisp cradling the velvety blueberry sorbet http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=XIZ93IR3Yrj2GDlhs_Wf8A&select=OtODDyewFyyem_6yTC0r2A But personally I dig the Chocolate Mousse, the light gianduja mousse sits proudly on a delicate wafer with an island of peanut powder and grape sorbet http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=XIZ93IR3Yrj2GDlhs_Wf8A&select=RzdyPd1e-YHqYocL-DQ5hA 

The bright semi-causal cafe offers a slightly lower priced menu and matched service http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/f7apP8A_0_KqcGQTK4V2TQ?select=r0jw0-u3WejdKjiA8ll6dw while the Dining Room's formal setting and ample attendants ensure an exceptional experience http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/f7apP8A_0_KqcGQTK4V2TQ?select=Mh81Pc5w0pEUmvsodG6bXg For example, in the cafe you are given bread with chilled dilled butter, but in the dining room you choose your bread http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=XIZ93IR3Yrj2GDlhs_Wf8A&select=pkp9SNrZSUfFYkab9X3AgA The dining room also offered us an amuse-bouche between each course - the first of which was a petite spoon of tuna which I did not eat. So when the second one came out, without request, the waiter convivially offered me an alternative small dish of ambrosial tomato salad. I am smitten!

The place is great food.  The decor is a bit plain Scandinavian starkness. Watch out for the wine list.  There are only a few bottles under $100.  I'd stick with the aquavit and beer.  

My food suggestion:
At the Bar: Caraway aquavit, herring sampler, gravlax and beer.

Came here for a business lunch. That had extended their restaurant week menu so we all ordered apps, main, and dessert without breaking the bank. Food and service were both excellent. Fish was cooked to perfection and their chocolate dessert was not too sweet just perfect! The atmosphere is great too if you wanted to take out of town guests here also.

Very good restaurant, and being a Scandinavian-American, I have to say I feel that it manages to stay very authentic as well. The wine menu is great, but if you want to keep it authentic, go with the beer and aquavit, it's how we like it up north.

Other reviews have called it plain, as I can tell, well there is truth to that, but again this is really just what you'd get in Scandinavia, so all true to form. I doubt anyone would leave this place complaining about the food, but you really need to end the night with an Arctic Circle. Absolutely amazing.

Came here for lunch a couple weeks, and I was a little disappointed.  Perhaps it's because I don't like dill or because I have no palette for Scandinavian food.  Either way, I was unimpressed. 

Atmosphere - the aquavit restaurant was holding a private event, so we went to aquavit cafe.  I felt like I was in an ikea store!

Starters :
-Our table shared the smoked salmon.  Really good and probably the best thing I had here
-I had the cauliflower soup.  There's a reason why most places don't serve this soup.  It was so heavy and bland at the same time.  The high fat from this dish threw me off for the rest of the meal 

Entree: 
-I completely regret not going with my initial instinct to get the swedish meatballs.  Instead, I got the smorgasbord.  If you don't like dill like myself, this is a nightmare.  Half of the things on the plate had that stuff on it!  I was able to remove some of it, but some dishes had the stuff mixed in too deeply.  The dish included a lot of variations on trout, salmon, potato and dill.  Of the whole selection, nothing really stood out as good.

Ahh, the food of my people! Yes, not the most sophisticated of palates, but a pleasure nonetheless.

The NFT guidebook I had was a little out of date because I discovered, to my dismay, that when I got to the address in the book, there was no restaurant to be had. But, I called up and, even though it was creeping up on 9:30, I could be seated in the bar and order from the full menu. 

Luckily, they hadn't moved that far, and Keir was MOST helpful on the phone, and when I got to the new location, he greeted me by name. I thought that was a stellar touch.

So, I was seated in the bar, near a big table of "Madmen" types (minus the suits and cigarettes) and ordered the prix fixe menu for an exceedingly reasonable price. The herring, normally reserved for Christmas Eve dinner with the in-laws, was delicious! Could have gobbled twice as much as the sampler platter offers. But the Swedish meatballs were fantastic and not better or worse than what Mom used to make. Just, as good as. Which is fine by me. Also offered were the thinly sliced pickled cucumbers. Was I dreaming that I was 12 years old again, and nothing bad was ever going to happen to me?

The dessert-Arctic Circle. Goat cheese parfait??? What on earth--I LOVED IT. Just the right amount of food. The Swedes are ever so sensible.

All in all, a wonderful evening-the aquapolitan was also delightful. Service was present yet not intrusive. After making my homage to the Paris Theatre, this was a wonderful cap to a great evening. I even got a little tipsy on one cocktail. 

Hej hej.

If yelp allowed me rank in decimal increments I would have ranked this place at 4.7.  It is definitely not a place I would go to again unless someone else is paying.  As it was my boss At Macquaire paid for it and it was magnificent, though a little stuffy and too formal. Also I realize that portions are always smaller at the ritziest restaurants but these portions were microscopic and not appropriate for a growing boy like myself.  By the end of the meal I was ready for three more entrees but reluctantly ate desert.

I had foir gra and an appetizer and washed down with a sampler of vodka which other colleagues had as well.  The reason it was not a top notch experience is that my colleagues and I were entertaining a Japanese corporate guest who spoke little English and it quickly got awkward when we all ran out of things to talk about like a date gone sour.  To improve the situation, we drank more alcohol.

Still a fan of the place. But just wanted to note that I probably would not come here besides during Restaurant Week. This is New York for goodness sakes. Plenty of other places to try and spend money on. Remember, no meatballs.

One of the best dining experiences I've had. I used to live in Sweden and found aquavit (the drink) to be pretty loathesome, but they had some interesting infusions -- I recommend the saffron aquavit.

We went here b/c my dad loves the food! The swedish meatballs were delish and the staff was great. We were seated in the cafe (b/c I had my 7yo daughter with me and thought it would be best) There were only 3 other groups of people in there, a little sad for a saturday night. But we enjoyed the quiet and ate our food and enjoyed it!

MJ's Star : 4
Price : Restaurants Week Lunch $24.07, Beer $6, Coffee $5 (except tax & tip)

Absolutely delicious. It's not cheap, but the prices are very fair, you'll get a very good meal at Aquavit with very attentive and cordial service. It's an excellent quality/price ratio, especially for a formal setting. Highlights include the 4 herring sampler and the artic circle. Nice setting for a date you are interesting in talking (and listening!) to, it's quiet enough to entertain a comversation at normal volumes.

A friend suggested we have lunch at the cafe. Though less expensive than the restaurant, I can't imagine there's any difference in the food. I was first to arrive and the wait staff seated me promptly. They struck exactly the right tone of being attentive and helpful without being overbearing, or trying to rush us through our lunch. The decor seemed to be in a modern Scandanavian style: clean and clutterfree but not cold in any sense of the word.

We both had outstanding meals. I had a small mixed green salad with radishes and apples with just the right amount of dressing to barely coat the lettuces. My cold-smoked salmon on a potato pancake was perfect, the pancake holding its firmness under the salmon and a delicious soft white creamy cheese. My friend had the gravlax and mussels. We were also served bread, which I didn't have, though it looked delicious: mutli-grained and crusty and fresh. That we were served unsalted butter proved to me that this restaurant has nothing to hide as far as freshness goes. We did not have dessert or any of the wines or aquavits.

I would definitely eat here again, and have already suggested Aquavit to a number of friends who are looking for a new stylish lunch place. Good for a business lunch, after shopping or just a nice treat for oneself. The acoustics made for a good noise level. I was so happy to eat somewhere without that awful background din that so many restaurants have. I could speak in normal tones without yelling, nor did I hear other diners' conversations. I'm looking forward to trying the dinner in the restaurant soon, and trying a dessert (although quite frankly, the two appetizers I had as my meal were satisfying without being filling).

Long story short: just the kind of place I like: good fresh food, mostly fish, cleanly prepared with ingredients that enhance, not hide, the flavors of the food.

Restaurant Week Winter 2010 Dinner

Did not live up to my standards as a NYT 3-star restaurant-- understood why they didnt get a michelin star.

The amuse bouche was the most exceptional thing we had. The RW special White Wine was very good too. The artichoke bisque was very well done and the smoked venison added good texture. The entree's, however, were sub par and lacking the flavor and artistic execution of peer restaurants. The service was very light, and I found myself being judged "can i get you ice water", "you're probably most interested in the restaurant week selections". The Chocolate Mousse dessert was unexpectedly good and well-presented-- exceeding my expectations compared to the rest of the meal.

I first tried Aquavit for lunch during Restaurant Week a couple of years ago and remembered enjoying the herring sampler, but my memory wasn't sharp enough to write a Yelp review until I went back. After seeing Marcus Samuelsson as a guest on Top Chef two seasons ago, I was itching to return and try the dinner menu, and to remind myself what herring tastes like.

We went with the Restaurant Week menu as well this go-round. The amuse bouche was some type of cheese with a sweet sauce, and while it's shameful that I can't remember its name or actual components, I can say with confidence that it was a pleasing kick-start for the palate.

The garnishes in the matjes herring appetizer cut into the strong flavor of the fish well, but my dinner companion wasn't a fan of its intensity. I've had herring before, and even I was a little taken aback at how powerful the fishy taste of the dish was. After the initial shock, however, I really enjoyed the way the flavors of the dish combined and complemented one another. The anjou pear salad was light and tasty, and the walnuts added a touch of flavor that made it all the more enjoyable.

The seared salmon entree was fantastic, medium rare and cooked so well that it practically melted in my mouth, and I'm always a big fan of crispy skin, as it adds both flavor and texture to the dish that is indescribable. The brandade and roe enhanced the richness of the salmon without taking away or overwhelming anything. My dinner companion had the cornish hen and was not very impressed: He claimed the bird was a little too dry.

We tried both desserts. The spice cake was tasty, though not as moist as I would have liked, but the cream cheese and sorbet with it helped remedy the issue and completed the dessert. I expected very little of the chocolate mousse and was pleasantly surprised, particularly by its bottom layer that was sweet, dense, and a little crunchy.

The service was good, the wait staff very attentive, something I always look for in an establishment hosting Restaurant Week as it speaks volumes to how the place is run. My friend isn't so keen on returning - I suppose the matjes herring proved too much for him, and the cornish hen too disappointing - but I'd come back to try out some of the other dishes anytime, as the off-menu prices are pretty reasonable, and Scandinavian fare piques my interest. I'd also return to have just the seared salmon and/or the chocolate mousse again. Mmm, delicious.

I was extremely disappointed with my experience at Aquavit. We made reservations for a Wednesday night at 8:30pm for Restaurant Week. A friend and I arrived early to have drinks at the bar and upon checking in with the hostess, nobody asked to check our coats (as they were checking everyone else's). A little bit past 8:30pm we realized the bar was empty and none of the hostesses were bothering to come get us. I went to the front and was ignored for a good 5 minutes before I had to rudely approach a hostess to say my party has been here waiting. She said it would be a little longer but made no apologies. 20 minutes later I again had to ask and they still said it would be longer (of course again with no apologies). Once we were finally seated and brought water, when the bread waiter came over he was extremely curt and rude to me, throwing down one small piece of bread while for one of my friends he gave her 2 huge pieces without asking if the rest of us wanted more. Another waiter who was clearing our amuse bouche (which left something to be desired) knocked over and spilled out part of my $17 martini but just walked away without even apologizing or offering a refill. Dinner was not worth it at all. The herring was much too sweet, and left a strange aftertaste. My cornish hen was next to impossible to cut into with the dull knives we were given. Dessert (chocolate mousse) was good, but we weren't there for a top-notch dessert. The entire dining experience was just extremely disappointing for a restaurant we had all heard such good things about and to top it all off, when I got home I spent the next day and a half extremely ill with food poisoning. I'm glad we only wasted $35 as we went during Restaurant Week, but nonetheless, a top level restaurant should be on its game at all times, regardless of whether its a Wednesday night during RW. Overall, just horribly disappointing.

My favorite restaurant in New York--I love to go here on special occasions because of the unique food with attentive service. I love their aquavit cocktails (especially the spicy mango martini), but they're very potent!

This review is for Aquavit Cafe.  Food rating is 4 stars.

My bf and I came here for Restaurant Week at the Aquavit Cafe.  Oddly enough, after looking at the menu and after speaking to the waitress on her recommendations, we decided to order the items off the regular menu instead of the Restaurant Week menu.

We ordered the following:

1) Artichoke Bisque - truffle crème fraîche, soft-baked egg, smoked venison - both bf and I liked it.  We both like artichoke and was expecting a bit more artichoke flavor... but that wouldn't appeal to the masses, so I guess that's why the artichoke flavor is toned down.  The smoked venison was a nice touch on the bisque; however, it was a tad bit too tough, but flavor-wise, it was good.  http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/f7apP8A_0_KqcGQTK4V2TQ?select=7EAgfndqZJBbqZV6ZdIgxQ

2) Scandinavian Bouillabaisse - cod, scallops, shrimp, mussels, parsley aioli - the seafood was cooked separately than the broth.  The seafood was noticeably saltier even when we ate it together with the broth.  Otherwise, the seafood was pretty fresh.  I personally loved the broth and drank up all of the soup.  http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/f7apP8A_0_KqcGQTK4V2TQ?select=Mu0tWqkpL6HEYLfNbVEG5A

3) Smorgasbord - assortment of Swedish bites - the menu didn't say what was included.. so I'm taking a guess and here it is:
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/f7apP8A_0_KqcGQTK4V2TQ?select=5qd3rcbKPipfxdyGM8-FCw
(See picture - front row from left to right)

1) Herring with  Västerbotten cheese - loved the cheese.  I'm personally not a fan of Herring... but if I did, this would be a really good & fresh fish.
2) Cold Smoked Salmon - potato cake, sour cream, & red onion - YUM!  Tastes exactly as described.
3) Venison Tartare - horseradish, pickled beets, mustard - tastes exactly as described.  The meat on top was more a dried meat though.  Also, I hate mustard, but you can't really tell when it's mixed into the sauce.

(See picture - back row from left to right)
1) Herring with boiled potato - again I'm personally not a fan of Herring... but if I did, this would be a really good & fresh fish.
2) Gravlax - cured salmon, expresso mustard sauce, lemon, dill - this was my favorite - YUM!
3) Toast Skagen - shrimp, trout roe, brioche - good but didn't love.  If you love mayo - this would be great for you.  I don't personally like mayo too much.

For dessert, we had Spiced Creme Brulee - malted orange ice cream - I had forgotten the "spiced" in the creme brulee when the waitress served it at the table, so the first bite was a bit confusing on my tastebuds.  Once I took the second bite, I really liked it.  Definitely recommended!  http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/f7apP8A_0_KqcGQTK4V2TQ?select=Rh7CALZOad9GE5S09-8rHg

For drinks, I started with a Cranberry Caipirinha at the bar, which was made of Aquavit NYC, Lime, & Cranberries.  Loved the drink.  The balance was really nice (almost like those drinks you get at speakeasies).  YUM!  Oddly enough, when I ordered it again at my table, it tasted different, and the balance was all gone.  The alcohol slapped you in the face with almost no lime or cranberries to soften the alcohol taste.  I never return drinks or food (unless its a steak that was cooked medium instead of medium rare).  I asked the waitress nicely and she graciously replaced my drink.  The replacement drink was just as terrible, but I didn't have the heart to tell her because she was so nice (her name is Melissa by the way).  I had already made her do all that work.  My warning - just be careful of the different bartenders.  =P  Some are just not as good as others.
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/f7apP8A_0_KqcGQTK4V2TQ?select=8aZhdHNaXUDQzP7Yva8hKA

Prior to the meal, we were served with bread (but with DILL butter) and a Goat Cheese Croquettes with Lemon Thyme Honey.  The dill in the butter is really light - so people who don't like dill can definitely handle it on their bread.  My bf loves dill, and he complained that it wasn't enough dill (he's super critical)  The Goat Cheese with Lemon Thyme Honey - YUM!
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/f7apP8A_0_KqcGQTK4V2TQ?select=3BheJWohdGpH4rzIliqgHQ
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/f7apP8A_0_KqcGQTK4V2TQ?select=OGpPGCPIW2tnbYa_JS5OXQ

I loved my waitress - Melissa.  However, I can see some of the other hostesses there can get a bit snooty.

This review is four stars for the food, but I gave it five because the service was so over the top. 

I went here for dinner tonight for restaurant week. The space is really great, all clean lines, it reminds me of an art gallery or a modern art museum. The walls were bright white with large paintings and the ceilings are really high, almost two stories up. I loved how open it was, yet it still managed to seem intimate. 

We arrived and they had lost our reservation. The host was incredibly apologetic and accommodated us anyway. I made the rez through OpenTable.com, so it wasn't definitely the restaurant's fault that it was lost, but either way they rectified it instantly. 

We were seated right away and our Captain, Jaret came right over. He was so friendly and we liked him immediately. He recommended drinks, we went with the white cosmopolitan and crimson flower (I later switched to an apple aquavit, which was amazing!) both drinks were delicious!

We went with the restaurant week menu, where I had the Artichoke Bisque, which was a soup full of flavors that seemed foreign, but I really enjoyed. My dining companion had the pear salad, which was a basic salad, nothing to write home about. 

Main courses: I went with the Barley "risotto" which was really a mushroom risotto made with barley instead of Arborio rice. It was really good, again with the interesting flavor combinations. My companion had the salmon and while it was a small serving size, she really liked it too. 

For dessert, we split the chocolate mousse and spice cake. Both were good, the Spice cake tasted a bit like a ginger cookie (my favorite type!) and the chocolate mousse was so smooth, it melted in your mouth. 

I was impressed by the food, and fascinated by the flavor combinations, which is always a pleasant surprise. The reason I had to give it five stars is for the service. From the host seating us right away and giving us a table to fix the reservation mix up to the Captain who made sure we were happy throughout dinner. He even recommended the Clove infused Aquavit, which we both applauded. 

If you go here, ask to be seated in Jaret's section. He really put the joy of the meal over the top, which is hard to do considering how delightful the food was. 

Keep in mind: the cocktails were as good as the food. Go have a drink at the bar if you don't have the time or don't want to splurge on dinner. The cocktails were awesome. The white cosmo is such a great, light drink. 

I will probably go back and try the full menu or the Chef's Tasting Menu, they both looked so good!

Great place! Love the dining room and decor, though the seats in the booths are not the most comfortable. 

Love the selection, you can do a tasting menu, or the regular prix fix for about $80 (I think!) or for the duration of RESTAURANT WEEK they have an additional $35 prix fix!!! 

Great wine list, they have some cheap options for all of y'all (including me!) on a budget! We had the $35 bottle of white wine recommended with the restaurant week menu and it was actually really delicious! 

If you haven't ever tried Norwegian Acquavit they have plenty of them in their menu, infused with different fruits or in cocktails. They have a tasting flight which might be worth trying. Strong stuff though, I had it in Norway and boy is it strong!! 

The amuse of goat cheese with some sort of sweet jam was delicious. I am a fan of goat cheese for sure. This one was creamy and strong in flavor. 

I ordered the herring from the RW menu, and it was perfectly tangy, great consistency, with some salmon roe, and some crème fraiche which balanced the whole dish very well. You MUST eat herring at a Scandinavian restaurant!! 

The seared salmon entree with mashed potatoes was very well cooked and super filling, I was very much satisfied after eating it. 

Now the chocolate mouse with banana ice cream was perfection, the extremely thin crust on the bottom of the mouse was so delicious. 

Was a great meal, I would highly recommend this place for a date or for out-of-towners as they serve things here you wouldn't normally find everywhere. 

We had to wait a little to be seated, and service was a bit slow at first but they apologized, and made up for it, served us water constantly, recommended the wine. I would definitely come back!!

hmm, where should I start?

I'll start with the good. 

Service are above average. I had an 8:30 reservation and was 5 minutes late because we have trouble finding this place. We were told to wait for about 10 minutes for a table, and ended up with a table for 6 even though we are a party of 3. 

Our waiter was attentive, but he gave no suggestions when one of my friend was having trouble choosing between 2 entries. He also offered a replacement for my main course when he found out that I couldn't eat it. I'll explain that later. He also gave us extra bread and butter because one of my friend is a bread thief =x ok, she was just hungry and likes bread.

The seats were very comfortable, but the table was a bit too low. then again, my height is above average and I couldn't cross my legs while sitting down at their tables, which makes it a bit uncomfortable.

The decor is very simple and modern. Lighting in the cafe is just right, not too dark and not too bright.

For drinks, we had CRIMSON FLOWER, pomegranate molasses, blueberry and elderflower aquavit, fresh lemon juice, $12 and AQ DOUBLE APPLE, fuji apple aquavit, house made sour, green apple puree, $12. Both drinks were tasty.

The lucky one of our group ordered from their regular menu. He had TOAST SKAGEN, $13, shrimp, trout roe, brioche as appetizer and SCANDINAVIAN BOUILLABAISSE, $26, cod, scallops, shrimp, mussels, parsley aioli as main course. both are very good and the seafood was very fresh.

Now with the bad.
2 of us went with the restaurant week pre fix menu.  I started with ARTICHOKE BISQUE, truffle crème fraîche, crispy venison, cold-pressed rapeseed oil, it was super salty, it was a good thing that I stole some bread from the bread thief. =x My friend started with MATJES HERRING, yellow beets, sour cream, pickled red pearl onion. Again, it was super salty, she ended up putting it on her bread. My main course was MUSHROOM "BARLOTTO", pearl barley, roasted mushrooms, Västerbotten cheese, parsley. It was so salty that I left it aside after 3 bites. Her main course was WHOLE ROASTED CORNISH HEN, parsnip, spinach, brussels sprouts, sage béchamel. It was tender, but bland. Dessert was CHOCOLATE MOUSSE banana sorbet, hazelnut. The banana sorbet does not belong with the tasty chocolate mousse cake.

At the end of our meal, our waiter offered each of us a gift certificate with a value of $24.07, but none of us would go back again. The food is just way too salty for our taste.

Chef Marcus Samuelsson does Swedish right.  Known for occasionally using berbere spice from his native Ethiopia in dishes on "Iron Chef," he is talented.  

The menu nicely represents Scandinavian fare, and the Aquavit Restaurant Week menu is served identically in both the Cafe and Dining Room.  

The decor here is Scandinavian.  Simple, eye-pleasing, albeit in need of some updating.

If you hate herring, brave your resistance to try some here. It is a *must* at Aquavit because the quality is high. The Matjes Herring is slightly salty, with yellow beets, sour creme and a surprise crunch, nicely presented.  The Whole Roasted Cornish Hen looks "Georgia O'Keefe-y" - beautiful.  Parsnip, spinach, brussel sprouts, sage bechamel, and the juiciest bird as your centerpiece. Succulent.  

I once opted for the Seared Salmon with potato and smoked shrimp brandade, and while it was very good (okay, perfect), I was left salivating for the cornish hens on my companions' plates.  Don't be the fool who opts for the salmon just to be different if you really want to try the hen.

Skip the $9 Voss water, ask for the tap you drink at home, anyway, and try an aquavit with your dinner.  The blueberry and elderflower aquavit is popular. Your waiter will be happy to explain the many infusions of their aquavits, and the infusions are in view by the bar near the comfy leather Arne Jacobsen chairs.

Any dessert will satisfy and the accompanying sorbet is always perfect.  

If you do manage to try the herring and like it (as I expect you might), do not miss Herring Week in July. To. Die. For!

Regarding service:  My experience has been that dinner service rocks, lunch service does not.  At dinner you can also avoid the Midtown suits that frequent restaurants in the area.  I give it a four-star rating on the scale of Scandinavian food, and dinner service.

I came here on the inaugural night of Restaurant Week, and it was pretty disappointing.  We had a reservation for 6 people in the dining room at 8 pm, but we didn't all get there until 8:30.  I had the pickled herring appetizer, the salmon main course, and something I can't even remember for dessert.  For all you people reading about the Arctic Circle, that is NOT on the RW menu.

Let's start with the bad: I have no idea what kind of decor they're going for.  It seemed to be "sleek" in the front until I noticed the messy paint job on the columns, and their decorations in the rest of the place seemed to be square jars of unindentifiable things that were backlit with candles.  Our table didn't have a tablecloth (just placemats on the round tables), and the little square vase centerpiece was overstuffed with waxy red flowers.  The chairs were interestingly oversized squareback leather [I'm sensing a "square" theme here], and the smaller tables had tall rectangular vases with tall red flowers on the dividers.  A lot of things looked somewhat understandably like a better version of IKEA.  

I know pickled herring is an acquired taste, but it really didn't go with the sour cream or anything else they served it with.  Our salmon had a mashed potato side that had been squirted into a pile that unfortunately resembled doo-doo, and that was cold while the salmon was hot, telling me that someone had pre-plated and not bothered to keep the plates hot.  I can't even remember what dessert I had because it was so unmemorable.  Others at the table who had the artichoke bisque appetizer said it was better, and I think the cornish hen entree was acceptable.  The entrance is confusingly  masked with heavy drapes where the left leads to the ramp and the right leads up the steps.  The entrance is set back from the street with a discreet sign (not necessarily a negative, just be on the lookout for it.)

Good: They didn't mind our party being so late at all.  There's a nice long white leather bench for you to sit on near the entrance to wait for your friends if you're the first one there. The bathrooms were nice (although my stall ran out of toilet paper), and the service was phenomenal.  The waiter heard us discussing what something on the menu was and glided over to ask if we had a question, and after we finished our food, we just sat there talking for nearly 2 hours.  They never rushed us or tried to hand us the check and just kept refilling our water--and this was a Friday night.  That seriously spoke volumes to me since so many places treat RW guests like second-class citizens.  Gratuity was automatically added in for our party of 6, and they gave us all "coupons" for $24.07 off our next visit. 

The clientele seemed to be more business dinner-y than I expected (I saw a lot of laptop bags and what were clearly client dinners), but we still felt at ease.  Jeans aren't allowed in the main room, but there's the "cafe" area that's practically the same.

Talk about Swedish aesthetic! This place is amazing! The ambience and atmosphere is sophisticated but not stuffy.

We came here as our grand finale to NY RW. The menu was simple but probably showcased their specialties. Yelpers told me to go for the herring starter which was unbelievable!

J had to cornish hen which was succulent and juicy and I had the salmon which was perfect! But we were both blown away by the herring starter- so I highly recommend it.

Cocktails here are not cheap but very sophisticated and high quality. J was drink with his 1 dirty martini and the 1 bottle of wine we got paired with our meal. Definitely a go. I'd come back since their prixe fixe menus aren't too expensive (under $100 pp)

I heard there's Herring Week in July - it will not be missed! See you there! :D

Went for extended restaurant week dinner in the cafe. Was in the main dining room years ago, which was more impressive but the cafe was still nice. 

Had the sampler of 3 aquavits (house made vodkas) which were delicious. Dessert, chocolate mousse with banana frozen yogurt was also amazing. Less amazing were the beet salad and the salmon entree offered on the RW menu. 

Still a good night, next time i'd go back to the main dining room

Brought back great memories of Sweden. The decor is sleek and stylish. We sat in the cafe and enjoyed the more relaxed atmosphere (though the other tables were still pretty dressy).

Service was smooth.

The swedish meatballs were tasty with a side of ligonberries.

Definitely recommend it...

I went with my sister during the restaurant week.  I had the artichoke bisque, cornish hen and chocolate mousse. My sister had herring, barlotto and spice cake.  Cornish hen and barlotto are too salty for us.  The others are just average. 

The staff are very friendly and the ambiance is nice.

Had a chance to dine here at the Cafe last night for Restaurant Week.  The service was great, as everyone was attentive, and I was impressed with the decor of everything from the tables to the salt and pepper shakers.
