I will say the plating for the dishes were some of the most impressive I have ever seen.  

The artichoke bisque was tasty, but a little too rich and creamy for me.  Didn't get enough of the artichoke taste.  On the other hand, the herring was one of the most flavorful dishes I've had in a while.  There was a lot going on (yellow beets, pickled onions, dill, salted herring, etc).  Be prepared to have the taste of herring stick with you for a good portion of the meal though.

As some helpful advice, definitely order some wine, as it'll help clean your palette as each dish is uniquely different from the last.

The salmon and cornish hens were cooked very well, but were ultimately fairly routine with the taste of each meat.

I was disappointed with the spice cake, but l got to say, the chocolate mousse was one of the best desserts I've ever had.  The banana salted caramel ice cream with the mouse on top of the cookie crust with toasted macadamia nuts was unreal.

Great evening.

Service is fantastic here--both at the bar and in the dining room. If you can, show up early and try your hand at the many wonderful flavors of Aquavit at the bar. Wonderfully blended flavors dance on your tongue as you drink it down straight.  My favorite was the strawberry (again) but there are tons of great ones.

The food is tasty, too. I started with the tuna appetizer--the tuna was fresh and smooth, with just the right flavor. The salmon was perfectly cooked and light in flavor. Dessert was something delicious with blueberries, yum!

Oh, I almost forgot. The atmosphere is great! Low lighting, cushy chairs and booths and great decorations.

We had been to Aquavit several years ago on a visit to Manhattan, though at the old location.  The old location was visually stunning with the very open area and the waterfall within the restaurant.  This site was still beautiful, though more intimate.  The meal at that first visit was mindblowing...just unbelievably good.  

On this visit to NYC, we decided to return to Aquavit, though this time for brunch.  The was consistently good across the board, and given some of the prices I've seen around Manhattan for Sunday brunch, this was actually a very good value.  I had a taste of most of the items available, and I can honestly say I really liked everything I tried.  This is one of my favorite restaurants in Manhattan, we will definitely be back here when we're back in town.

We came for the smorgasbord brunch and just got so much more than even the name implies.  For $48 you get a version of a bloody mary and at least four platefuls of amuse-bouche sized foods (that's all I could put down).   Round one went to the herring.  Definitely try the vodka-lime and grainy mustard.  Salmon was on board for round two and I was so impressed by the cold salmon with the espresso mustard sauce.  This also is where they had a potato/bacon hash under a fried egg and a cheese quiche.  Both were just that good and I really would have died happy right there, but I would have lost out on the sweedish meatballs and sausage with lingonberries, Janssons Temptation (Potato casserole with cream and anchovy), and a pork shank that one of my companions cried out in happiness after eating it.  Lastly, the desserts while also small, packed in a lot of flavors across many textures.  My eating companions were horrified I was able to eat 6 items from the desserts after everything else we had devoured.  

To top the food, the decor was modern and clean but tempered with lovely flowers and the service was the best I may have ever had.  The wait staff was simply exceptional.  It made me sad being reminded of how it should be done and rarely is.

**UPDATE**
Came back here on a Saturday night and had an equally delicious meal.  Thumbs up for the meatballs and the bouillabaisse.
**UPDATE**

Came for dinner on Sunday night and dined in the Bistro (not the super fancy dining room).  I have to say that I've avoided coming here just because the space seems so fancy and intimidating, but I've been missing out a little, I think.

First of all, the service is great, which is to be expected of a restaurant like this.  Everyone is friendly and very knowledgeable about the drinks and the food.  We started the evening off with 3 flights of Aquavits which are their house made liquors.  I chose the cucumber, horseradish (WINNER) and fig and cardamom.  All three were great.  They have a wide variety of aquavits that range from the salty to the sweet and fruity.  Tickle your fancy however you like.

The food was actually very reasonably priced in the Bistro and they do have a prix fixe menu that's $35 for three courses.  I ordered the pear and blue cheese salad to start which was delicious.  We also ordered the venison tartar and some truffle fries which were great.  This is very obviously a seafood restaurant so we all ordered seafood for our main course and no one was disappointed.  I had the cod and it was perfectly cooked with a fresh bed of horseradish on top.  For a restaurant that makes food this good, I was surprised to see that it was virtually empty in the Bistro, though it was a Sunday night.  

So, let's recap.  Come here for:
1) seafood
2) yummy aquavits
3) prix fixe
4) sunday funday dinner

i just had an amazing dinner here, in the dining room.  a friend of mine procured some $24 off coupons during restaurant week, which we were more than happy to employ.  

i will first say that our waiter was one of the best i've ever had.  he was the world's most encouraging waiter.  "oh, the veal! an excellent choice.  and the steak!!  another excellent choice!!"  i've never felt more confident about my meal decisions.  

now on to the food.  it was friggin' awesome.  my friend and i got the prix fixe.  first course, i had quail, she had king crab and sea urchin.  the quail was crispy and delish with a side of chicken liver pate.  (turned me into a liver lover.) the king crab was mighty tasty and we were both glad to have tried sea urchin at least once.  (it was a little like fish jello, but not altogether unpleasant.)

second course she had venison which came with morels.  both were super salty and delicious.  the morels had such a nice meaty flavor.  i got 2 kinds of steak.  the short rib was amazing!!! it was one of the most flavorful meats i've ever had (that's what she said).  it was like bbq but without all the superfluous flavors.  just hearty chared meat.  can't say enough about how wonderful that was.

and finally our desserts were also great.  maybe not the best desserts i've ever had (hence the 4 stars), but highly satisfying.  banana mousse and chocolate mousse.  the caramel icecream with the chocolate mousse was actually a little on the salty side (and i'm a huge salt fan). 

oh, and i forgot about the drinks!!!  we both got cocktails made with their housemade aquavits.  i had a manhattan that was so strong, it kept me drunk all through dinner and an hour after.  so no complaints there.  

final score: A-, adventurous menu, delicious and strong cocktail, unbelievable service, satisfying dessert

It's sad to say that I always thought Scandinavian food consisted of meatballs and pasta so I was pleasantly surprised with the extensive seafood menu. The halibut, the herring and octopus were all excellent. 

The decor is super modern with an open concept like feeling. Service was spectacular. Did I mention the martinis are yummy as well?

The closest I had to Scandinavian food before Aquavit was at Ikea.

I love to try different foods, and the Aquavit palate offers exactly that. It's not a place I would frequent very often, but it is ideal for business lunches. I went on a weekday and the patrons were mostly suits talking gently in hushed tones. It was not packed, so people-watching wouldn't be a distraction at lunchtime (unless Lil' Wayne made an impromptu appearance). The decor mostly consists of dark wood contrasting with white details. It's simple and clean, and the branches in the vases make it feel like a very sophisticated, but not fancy schmancy place.

Ordered:
HORSERADISH HERRING: salmon caviar, fingerling potato, sour cream- caviar was smooth and complemented the coolness of the herring. Someone once told me that Aquavit's herring will "change your life." I don't know about that, but it was tasty and a perfect starter.
SWEDISH MEATBALLS: potato purée, pickled cucumber, lingonberries, cream sauce- I've never had lingonberries so I was excited to try this dish. The meatballs were well-cooked and the cream sauce gave it a nice kick. The waitress came and cracked an egg over my dish; apparently, it was supposed to taste even better when egg-drenched. I thought it was different and quite hilarious, but didn't dare laugh in the main dining room, lest I get removed before dessert.
CARMELIZED BANANA MOUSSE gingerbread, caramel sauce, walnut ice cream- I was rather full by this time (which is good because dishes at these prices usually come sparse), but enjoyed this yummy ending. The walnut ice cream tasted like butter pecan. I didn't complain.

If you like to try new things like "dandelion" and "skansk mustard" (and don't mind shelling out the cash), Aquavit is for you!

The $24 weekday  lunch pri fix in the cafe (vs the main dining room) is a good deal... I had the herring, barlotto (risotto with barley apparently), and the chocolate mouse cake.  I was pleased with the service, decor,and of course the tasty food.  A much better deal than coming to dinner...

This is still a unique and tasty restaurant for special occasions.  My wife took me there for my birthday a few weeks ago and we loved it.  The service is still good and the menu is unlike anything else in NYC.  I think you might have to wear a suit to eat there, as everyone was wearing one except me.  better to call ahead.

the most beautiful dining room i've ever sat in, modern lines, sleek, warm furniture. the food and ambience was awesome. the service was good but the staff was uppity. otherwise, perfect for a quiet, anniversary dinner.

Very beautiful dining room, even got to listen to Swedish carolers during the holidays. Tried the Smörgsbord for a sampling of hot and cold dishes. Herring, swedish meatballs, boiled potatoes, salmon... if you like Scandanavian food - this is a great place

I love Aquavit.  I'm a traveler and there is a lot about aquavit that simulates the good parts of travel.  Am I in Sweden?  Am I in 2002?  There is something a bit dated about the place, but for me that adds to it's charm.  I wish it was still in it's old space with the waterfall, but the new place exudes a fun euro class that afford me the illusion of spending a few hours somewhere... Maybe Sweden in 1998?

The food is consistently interesting, healthy, delicious, and beautiful.

Came here during the restaurant week, a while ago. I really enjoyed the food and atmosphere here. the appetizer herring was delicious.

Well, even though that was r-week, their wine list is not r-week price. Even though we didn't drink a lot, ended up spending close to 90 each... 

Well, I don't know much about Scandinavian food, but I think their taste is accessible to many people. All the food was delicious there...!

5 Stars. Easy. Aqauvit is a really awesome restaurant.  The food is amazing, both in taste and presentation.  The drinks are creative and made with love.  The service is clean, efficient and kind.  My parents brought me here for my birthday, and we all enjoyed the prix fixe menu.  The venison tartare was very good, topped with a Vasterbotten cheese crouton, and the main course of sea scallops and Maine lobster, with three different sauces was amazing.  There are three intermezzo course as well (so you get your money's worth).  On our night we had a lobster bisque, gingery-lemon pudding shot and something else which was not as notable.  For dessert, definitely try the most popular option the Arctic Circle - the combination of goat cheese, mango and berries is sublime.  The caramelized banana mouse is also excellent.  

Really, this is such a great place, perfect for a really special dinner occasion.  Those two-star with complaints about the $24 lunch menu haven't had the true experience, also - breaking news! - herring is often served salty - knowledge is power, so don't be an ignorant diner. The informative staff isn't there just to put food on the plate - ask questions.

Aquavit was recommended to me by a part Swedish friend.  The front doorway is dwarfed by the towering building itself.  My friend and I were seated quickly.

We sat in the Bistro dining area and ordered the Smörgsbord and the Swedish meatballs along with the Scandinavian Bellini and Lingonberry Spritzer.  The Smörgsbord included Toast Skgen (shrimp, trout roe, brioche), Venison Tartare (horseradish, pickled beets, mustard), Gravlax (cured salmon, hovmastar sauce, lemon, dill), Cold-Smoked Salmon (potato cake, sour cream, red onion), Matjes Herring (yellow beets, red onions, sour cream).  

My favorites were the Toast Skgen which had a perfect combination of creamy shrimp and roe with the crunch of the brioche.  I also really liked the meatballs, which had a slightly home-cooked taste, but went perfectly with the tartness of the lingonberries.  The service was nice and not snooty at all, which was cool.  At about 20 dollars, the Smörgsbord is a great value, and I'd recommend a trip to Aquavit to anyone who makes it Manhattan.

I finally had the pleasure of dining at this famous Scandinavian establishment during their Herring Festival to celebrate the Summer Solstice which is a major event especially for the families and friends to get together to celebrate the Midsummer, the longest day of the year. 

Herring Festival is being held at the front dining room which is the Aquavit Bistro. If you want to try dining at the Aquavit but you prefer to be more casual with somewhat lower price point menu items then Bistro is the right place for you. It is a smaller room, located by the entrance before you get to the lounge area. 

We were offered the regular bistro menu along with the $35/per person Herring Festival self serve buffet option. It had an $11 option to get a shot glass of flavored aquavit (alcoholic drink distilled either from grain or, more commonly, potatoes) and a glass of Carlsberg beer. 

We were there for the Herring Festival and the buffet looked incredible for the price they were offering at. It consisted of ten different types of pickled herring, salmon, meatballs, boiled potatoes, sliced cheese, tomato salad, dessert and more. You can't find a better deal than this at this type of a restaurant in New York City. Each dish was better than the next and after two trip to the buffet we were happily satisfied with the selection and quality of the food. We finished another set of aquavit from the selection of about dozen flavors. It's strong drink but depending on the flavor it goes down very smoothly. 

On the way out our waiter notified us about their on going prix-fix lunch $25 and dinner $35 menus which gave us another reason to come back to this great place. Of course one of these days I would like to dine in the back, main dining room but we can save that for a special occasion. By the way long time chef Marcus Samuelson left the helm to the new executive chef Marcus Jernmark who we had the delight of briefly meeting after our superb meal. Some of his dishes like the Venison Tartar, Hot-Smoked Brook Trout, Seared Arctic Char, Chatham Cod Confit, etc. looked so tempting that we could have easily stayed if our full stomachs allowed us. Also to top that of Chef Jernmark offers an amazing tasting menu.

Beautiful decor and excellent service.
Food preparation is very different than a typical French or seafood restaurant.

We went here during summer restaurant week.  I ordered the cold green tomato soup, the salmon and the cardamon cake.  My husband got the pickled herring, the beef and the chocolate cake (forgot the actual name of the dish).  We both thought our dishes were okay - good but not great.  The flavor combination just didn't do it for us. Perhaps we just don't really enjoy swedish food but I'm glad to have tried something new.  Why the four stars then?  Well aside from the fact that yelp doesn't allow me to give half stars, the service was impeccable, which is very rare for restaurant week.  We never felt rushed and our waiters were really polite and friendly.  Also the quality of the food was excellent.  The ingredients were of high quality and extremely fresh.  I would go again for those two reasons only.  Perhaps next time, I'll actually love the food!

My husband and I ate here for Restaurant Week and I have to say, we did not walk away particularly impressed. I had the pickled herring, grilled roast beef, and cardamom cake. My husband had the chilled green tomato soup, cold poached salmon and chocolate cake. The chilled green tomato soup was probably the best dish - very fresh and light. But the poached salmon tasted unnecessarily fishy and in general, the portion size for all items was too large. I did have a martini with the cucumber aquavit and that was delish! It isn't that the food was bad it was just...unremarkable. I wouldn't recommend to anyone looking for a meal that features stellar food.

I'm a huge fan of Sweden and love visiting Stockholm.  Aquavit in NYC is 100% authentic, combined with an excellent staff and friendly service.  They have some of the most creative and tasty cocktails I've had in the city.

Went to the Aquavit Bistro for lunch Restaurant Week Summer 2010.

apps:
*Chilled Green Tomato Soup: The taste takes much getting used to, as it doesn't resemble red tomatoes; overall it made me think of green peppers and cilantro. They call it a "soup,"  but it's more like a salsa. 
*Pickled Herring Smorrebrod: The popular choice, and for good reason; I liked.

mains (or "main," because we both ordered the only dish that sounded good):
*Warm Roast Beef: Meat is tender, but dry.

dessert:
*Budapest cake: choc hazelnut cake, nothing surprising. My socks are still on.

I've heard that Aquavit has waned ever since the renowned chef had left, and agree with others that it's not the most impressive (is it too harsh to say it reminds me of cruise-ship fare?). Everything's $$$$ but I would maybe return only to try their Swedish meatballs.

Let's start with the namesake - the Aquavit, or essentially, infused Scandinavian vodka. 

I tried a flight of: 

Blueberry and Elderflower
Lemon and Ginger
Fig and Cardamom
Coconut and Espresso
Lingonberry

And I still managed to remember the pleasing food, atmosphere, and service. Now is a great time to go, because: 

Regular 3-course = $78
Regular plate a-la-carte = ~ $45
Restaurant Week 3-course = $35

Add in a $35 bottle Red/White/Rose wine during the Restaurant week promotion, and you should be well set to enjoy a plate of upscale Scandinavian potatoes and oily fish (herring).

Those venturing into this current RW cycle might want to forgo the hunt for minuscule slices of wild boar under a wilderness of salad in the appetizer round, but take a chance on the cold poached salmon. For those wanting to explore the regular menu, the Arctic Char stands out, and the signature Arctic circle dessert is a worthy bite. 

And of course, don't forget the Aquavit. 

Skoal!

Despite a few mishaps during RW lunch, I'm still a big fan of Aquavit

We dined in the Bistro portion of the restaurant, which looks straight out of the 1970s but in an endearing way. The service is excellent and very professional. Although we did spot a roach halfway through the meal, we were offered complementary Aquavits (flavored vodka shots) and given a gift certificate for our next meal there. All in all I say that more than made up for one nasty bug. 

Anyway, on to the food. I had the herring for appetizer which, well, tasted like you'd expect. It's pickled fish. But it was presented in a very interesting way. For entree I had a juicy roast beef plate, prepared to perfection. I left lunch feeling completely satisfied, which is a relief considering the disappointment I have felt with other Restaurant Week experiences.

yet another Restaurant Week review. 

i really did consider ordering off the menu for the sake of diversifying yelp's exposure to Aquavit. oh the things that i do (and the money i pay) for the sake of Yelp. but the RW menu just looked too damn good. 
sorry folks. maybe next time. 

try it. you wont be disappointed. 

unless you don't like mustard. 

not even joking. 

luckily, i happen to LOVE mustard. 

anyway, on to the FOOD: (please excuse my ugly iphone photos.)

meal ended with two complimentary gift cards for $24 each. uh, i was told that things that sound too good to be true probably are. but seems like this is common practice for them.

Scandanavian food, where have you been all my life?

My husband and I came here for Restaurant Week Summer 2010, and were pleasantly surprised by this impressive representation of Scandanavian food (Our first time trying it!).  The overall experience was quite pleasant overall.  The staff was accommodating in helping us to sort out a booking problem, and were friendly and helpful when it came to ordering.  The decor was lovely and modern.

Drinks

We tried the flight of 3 aquavits, since it is the restaurant's namesake. They're basically infused vodkas.  We weren't huge fans of vodka, but we wanted to try it anyway.

Blueberry-Elderflower - Pleasant and (very!) slightly sweet, but the vodka taste masked any blueberry or elderflower taste.

Mango-Lime-Chili - Tasted more strongly of chili than anything else.. I wasn't a fan.

Cardamom-Anise-Fennel - Tasted similar to absinthe, but without the bitter aftertaste.  Cleaner.  I might prefer it to absinthe.

Appetizers

Pickled Herring Smorrebrod - Delicious. I love pickled herring, and this was some of the best I've had.  The combination of ingredients complemented each other very well.

Cherry and Smoked Wild Boar Salad - My husband ordered this and thought it was just okay. Very little boar, apparently.

Entrées

Cold Poached Salmon - WOW.  I was so jealous of my husband for ordering this.  I've never tasted such perfectly-cooked salmon in my life.  I didn't even realize salmon could be this tender and so melt-in-your-mouth.  It was transcendent.  It was worth coming JUST for the salmon.

Roasted Asparagus Barlotto - It was good... but honestly my palate was spoiled by the salmon already so I couldn't appreciate this fully.  You know what?  Just order the salmon instead!

Dessert

Cardamom Pound Cake - The strawberries were good with the little pieces of meringue.  The lemon sorbet was good.  As for the pound cake itself... It was decent, albeit had strange texture.  I didn't mind eating it, overall.

Overall, we felt as if it was a good meal and left feeling very satisfied.  I look forward to returning!

4.5/5 for food, 5/5 for atmosphere, 5/5 for service

Food was great - I went for restaurant week, and found the menu to be quite better than any other restaurants participating in the promotion. Their herring salad was absolutely amazing. I found their grilled beef to be better than the salmon, and they have absolutely wonderful wine selection. I very much appreciated the impeccable service, and the atmosphere is one of the best I've seen in NY restaurants.

Yes, this is yet another RW review. I've never had Scandinavian food prior to dining at Aquavit so I didn't really know what to expect except that Scandinavian food includes a lot of smoked meat and seafood. Luckily for me, I really enjoyed my first time with Scandinavian flavors. The restaurant's decor, like their food, was a balanced mix of modern and traditional, and the service was impeccable.

For dinner I had...
... Amuse Bouche: SALMON TARTARE (smoked salmon topped with diced cucumber, cantaloupe and watermelon) Why why why must an amuse bouche be just one bite? This amuse bouche did it's job; it was so delicious that it had me looking forward to the rest of the food.
... Appetizer: PICKLED HERRING SMØRREBRØD (with Danish rye, truffled gentlemen's delight, trout roe) - WOW This was my favorite dish out of the whole meal. According to our sever, gentlemen's delight is the egg salad that topped the pickled herring. Why do they call it that? I have no idea, and I'm kicking myself now for not asking when I had the chance. All the flavors and textures worked SO well together and I loved the mustard flavor that added that extra kick to the whole dish.
... Entree: WARM ROAST BEEF (with smoked potato salad, summer pickle remoulade) - The beef was perfectly roasted, rare in the center and juicy. This dish also had that mustard bite which I loved, and the potato added the heartiness and starchy base that held the dish together.
... Dessert: CHOCOLATE BUDAPEST CAKE (with hazelnut praline mousse, apricots, vanilla ice cream) - Beautiful presentation. My favorite part of this dessert was the hazelnut praline mousse. It was rich but not too heavy. I like :)

All in all, my friends and I really enjoyed our dinner at Aquavit. Their regular menu is expensive ($75 for their regular prix fixe and $105 for the chef's tasting) so I probably won't come back unless it's for a special occasion.  BUT they don't slack on their RW menu and it's a ridiculously good deal for the RW price - definitely worth it. Unless you hate mustard.

Came here for dinner during restaurant week and I was pleasantly surprised by how much bigger my belly had gotten afterwards. For its portions, Aquavit gives more than enough food ESPECIALLY during restaurant week for anyone to walk out feeling like they can go straight home instead of to a late-night deli.  

I got the... 

Pickled Herring Smorrebrod
Cold Poached Salmon
Chocolate Budapest Cake

Oh, and a free shot from our waiter... I don't know if it was an addition to the restaurant week menu or whether it was because he felt bad for making us wait so long but it was free. Now that's classy.
What is Scandinavian food, you ask? Lots of raw meat and green leaves, or so I learned during restaurant week... Food, service and ambience were all stellar.

My father used to work at a Swedish company and he used to travel there all the time for business. I was not so lucky in the aspect and I am curious what Scandinavian food consists of besides meatballs. 

Finally, restaurant week granted me the chance to sample it for a reasonable price! 

For appetizers, we tried the herring sampler and boar salad. I was a bit scared to trry the herring at  first because it is basically cold fish. It tastes surprisingly good and there is very little fish smell. The wild boar salad was also great. My boyfriend, who doesn't like salad so much, was totally impressed. 

I got the Asparagus Barlotto for entree and my boyfriend got the roast beef. The asparagus dish tastes like creamy asparagus risotto but it uses barley so it is actually healthier. I got to say the dark green color make the dish slightly undesirable but again it surprised me. The roast beef is also good but I guess it is not very special. 

I really like their dessert, Budapest Cake, which is chocolate and hazelnut moose cake paired with ice cream. The dish I got, Cardamon pound cake, is good but nothing to rave about. 

The service is definitely 5 star and I really like their simplistic design. I am glad I got another great NYC restaurant under my belt.
If you enjoy Scandanavian food, Aquavit will never disappoint.  They do what they do very well.  If you're not particularly into this type of food, just avoid completely.

3.75

Scandinavian was a little of a shock to my taste buds.

I went with a friend for Restaurant Week. 

i got:
CHERRY AND SMOKED WILD BOAR SALAD
WARM ROAST BEEF
CARDAMOM POUND CAKE

friend got:
PICKLED HERRING
COLD POACHED SALMON
CHOCOLATE BUDAPEST CAKE

*the warm roast beef was really good. a little chewy but i enjoyed it a lot with the potatoes. i normally dislike potatoes but it was cooked so that it was hard but not undercooked. and it was a lot of food even though it didn't look like much at first.

** the herring was wayy too flavorful. and way too much for an appetizer. at least for me.

***the salad was good because the balance of sweet and salty was carried out by the venison (salty) and the cherries (sweet).

****the cold poached salmon was wierd.. maybe im just not used to cold salmon.. ever. and salmon with hollandaise was also very interesting. ALSO! if you have TRYPTPHOBIA.. i suggest you not to get this dish because there is a cluster of lentil that might freak you out. (my friend couldnt eat her food because of that).

This is NOT a review of Aquavit's restaurant week menu.  

You are, I know, like totally and amazingly shocked, because it would seem Aquavit only gets reviewed during restaurant week.  I guess we Yelpers are a stingy bunch.

But, wait. Don't get too excited. This isn't a review of Aquavit's food menu at all.  Just the bar.  

Aquavit's got a good bar. They've got good booze, namely, all kinds of aquavit. And some other stuff.  Namely, cocktails made with aquavit.  Oh, and lots of other stuff, too.  On my most recent outing, if I hadn't been having a "martini" (in which cucumber aquavit substituted for the gin-- and, hey, of all the bastardized martini concoctions out there, this one was damn fine, so refreshing and summery-- all my favorite gins were there.  

Amongst the advantages of the Aquavit bar are the following:

a) Scandinavian modern design.  More or less.  In other words, it's all nice and modern looking and feels oh so elegant. Wear nice shoes.

b) It's not crowded.  There's usually been enough room at the bar. There aren't a gazillion people there milling about the bar.  There are a few seats, where, if you're with a bigger group, you've more or less got your own little area.  It's nice.  There's space to breathe.

c) It's kind of an oasis in midtown.  Precisely because it's not overrun with obnoxious types (or, better said, I didn't notice if my fellow bar-goers were obnoxious, because I didn't have to stand on top of them, like at other places).  

d) For this kind of thing, the prices really aren't that bad.  The drinks are generously sized (and good).  

e) Decent nuts.  Who needs restaurant week when you've got cucumber aquavit/vermouth and nuts?

Food is fresh, quality Swedish, with slight influences from founder's native Ethiopia (works well, since many of these spices show up traditionally in Nordic baking.) Excellent seafood & salads. The green tomato soup, green salad w/ venison,  cured & poached salmon entree, & Budapest cake were all outstanding. Superb service. Huge bar, elegant modern decor. 
Personally, it's out of my everyday price range, but Restaurant Week lunch or a special occasion treat is great. Front room is more casual & lower prices. 
Very authentic (I have Scandinavian family & enjoy travel there.) If you've never tried this kind of food, you might like it if you enjoy neighboring cuisines (ie Baltic, Russian, East European Jewish.,etc.)

I got to Aquavit about 10 minutes early for a birthday dinner - they gave me the option of being seated or waiting at the bar.  I truly appreciate the offer to be seated (I hate places with the strict "not until your full party is here" rule), but chose to wait at the bar.  The atmosphere is wonderful - very spacious (unlike most places in NY) with a clean, sophisticated look and feel.  The bartender was excellent!  I only ordered water, but she explained the different aquavits to me and even gave me a sample of the horseradish aquavit (hmmmm!).  This courtesy truly started the night off right and made me anxious to try one of their cocktails.  I ordered the Spicy Mango Martini - soooo spicy, yet smooth from the mango puree - it hit the spot!!! My birthday friend ordered the Scandinavian Bellini - also refreshing and delicious!  

For dinner - I decided not to do the prix fixe and ordered straight from the menu.  I got the chilled green tomato soup and Swedish meatballs.  OMG - both were perfection.  The chilled green tomato soup was so fresh and soothing.  The Swedish meatballs were juicy and full of flavor - not to mention the added bonus of the generous portions and the potato puree, berries, and pickles that come with!  My friend ordered the Herring (which I didn't try - I don't do seafood) as the app and asparagus "barlotto " for her entree.  The asparagus dish was beautifully green, unique in flavor (this is a compliment), and very well portioned.  For dessert, we shared the creamiest chocolate pot de creme and got decaf coffee.  

It couldn't have been a lovelier evening - I would highly  recommend this place to anyone looking for a quality meal in the city.

I came to Aquavit recently for dinner.  They have a few areas for dining, with different menus.  We had dinner in the most formal setting, the main dining room.  Although Aquavit is an older restaurant in the timeline of NYC restaurants, the decor is not dated, very clean with simple elegance, and the dining areas are well separated.  We sat in a booth, which was spacious and felt private.  Service was very attentive.

The bar area seems popular, and Aquavit has a fairly extensive cocktail and wine menu.  We had wines with the meal, and started with some cocktails earlier: the bellini and grapefruit mojito were very well made.

In the dining room, there are two available menus: a 3-course prix fixe menu and a 7-course chef's tasting menu composed of items from the prix fixe menu, with wine pairings available.  We went with the tasting menu, and the meal went as such:

-- starting with an amuse bouche
Six small bites, mostly fish with unusual pairings, that were an excellent start to the meal

Beau soleil oysters
Three small fresh oysters that tasted of the sea, with a gentle sweetness and saltiness from the small diced fruit and caviar topping

Matjes herring
The richest dish by far, this generous portion of pickled herring was accompanied by a row of finely diced red onion and yellow beets, sour cream and chives, a soft-boiled quail egg, and a separate plate of cheese, fingerling potatoes, and sweet brown butter.  This was probably the most interesting dish of the evening.  Each slice of herring and a bit of the accompaniments was a taste I've never had before.  The cheese and potatoes were also excellent.

Seared diver scallops
Two plump, beautifully seared scallops, perfectly cooked, and came with gently sour sauerkraut and cauliflower

Pea crayfish
This was a substitution from the prix fixe.  Several small, tasty crayfish in a brightly flavored pea foam and meaty peas.  Very refreshing.

Lamb from Valhalla farms
The "main course" was a smorgesbord of lamb: medium rare lamb chop, dumpling, slice of sausage, and a small round.  The lamb chop was really the highlight, deeply flavorful, great texture, and cooked just right.  The dumpling had a great skin but the filling did not wow.

Raw milk alpine cheese
Soft and delicious!

-- insert a lovely palate cleanser here, a mini version of their popular Arctic Circle dessert, with a goat cheese parfait

Chocolate raspberry bar
A bar of rich chocolate covered raspberry mousse, with a bit of ice cream.  Not too sweet, not too rich, just right.

-- and end with four different housemade candies: a jelly, marshmallow, toffee, and macaroon

This was overall a very lovely meal.  While not transcendent, it is certainly an excellent dining experience and well worth experiencing.  I've never had Swedish food (unless one counts Ikea), and I was very pleased with the flavors.  I will probably try the bistro at another time.

This place is just lovely. It has space between tables, and very elegant but comfortable decor. Lots of clean relaxing lines, and pretty light. They don't rush you at all, and the service is excellent. 

I got the price fix menu. Smoresbord for the appetizer was amazing. The herring was something I'd never experienced. Salty, fishy and fresh all at the same time. It has a lot of mustard on it, which was an unusual but delicious flavor. For second course I got the asparagus barlotto. When it came, I said "it tastes so green!" (a compliment). It has a fresh taste all the way through and a great portion size. It did need something along with it though. By the time I was done, it felt like a side dish. It was good, but a little odd for a main course (which is why I'm giving a 4 instead of a 5). 

Dessert shared with a friend was silk like chocolate creme and decalf. 

I loved that they didn't rush you and the price fix in their "cafe" instead of the restaurant made the price very reasonable.

I've been to Acquavit half-dozen times now. Had I reviewed the restaurant after my first visit, I would have given the place a solid 5-star rating. Unfortunately, second, third, fourth, fifth, and sixth and possibly the last visit this past week all gave me diminishing returns on my hefty check. 

So, I'm cheap and tend to follow the "always order the second cheapest wine" about 75% of the times when wine compliments my entree. This rule hasn't let me down too often, and this time was no exception. We ordered the "Estate" chardonnay from Carneros, Cali. Extremely clean and crisp. Went very well with my oysters and sweetbread. At $75, it was the best bang for buck (among alcoholic bev) here at Acquavit. 

Now comes the disappointments. I always order the tasting menu every time I eat there. Why? I love herring...but I don't love herring enough to make a meal out of pickled fish. I love small bits and bites of my herring. I really do. There aren't many places in the US where you can find fresh, well pickeld/smoked/seasoned herring. Yet, Acquavit always was the place for unbelievably delicious, fresh, and mouthwatering herring samplers. This is no longer the case. My herring, which was accompanied by quail egg and red onion, was not tasty at all. I simply couldn't taste the herring. How is this possible? It just didn't taste like pickled fish. Unfortunately, I did taste the aftertaste you get when you eat poorly prepared fish. 

Disappointments continued... 

My scallops were overcooked and felt rubbery. 

My dessert - almond accentuated chocolate ice cream - smelled like it was pre-prepared and left, without being covered, in the freezer until a customer ordered the dish. 

Am I crazy for expecting better-prepared dishes when I pay over $200/person (incl. tip, drinks, tax) for dinner? 

Anyways, I still love the meatballs and smorgasbord at Acquavit Bar & Lounge. I may only visit the Bar & Lounge until someone convinces me the dining room's food has improved in quality. 

Gosh, I miss the delicious herring at the old Acquavit...

I can't believe I haven't reviewed Aquavit, which is easily one of my favorite restaurants in the city.

I came for Restaurant Week a few years ago and loved the menu. The Swedish meatballs were superb and moist. The herring plate was also a fun treat - but, admittedly, only if you like herring to begin with. (It _is_ quite... herring-y.) 

Our waiters were professional and attentive, and the presentation of all the dishes was great. 

This restaurant definitely has a modern, Scandinavian decor. It's not for everyone, for, I imagine, some people might be put off by the sleek, almost sterile vibe. But I found the decor classy and traditional, and it fit the presentation of the dishes quite well. 

Definitely a great choice for a nice occasion!

I came here during the summer restaurant week on saturday night and heard different reviews on the food.  I figured that it would be worth   trying it out.  I've listed what was ordered and how it tasted.
Food: CHILLED GREEN TOMATO SOUP (tasted like vinegar mixed with cucumbers), PICKLED HERRING SMORREBROD ( nothing special ), COLD POACHED SALMON ( nothing special), WARM ROAST BEEF (crap, tasted like leftover deli meat), CARDAMOM POUND CAKE (usual pound cake), BUDAPEST CAKE (Excellent!). The portions were small so ended up grabbing another meal elsewhere.
Service:  Our male waiter felt bad (we made these faces when trying out the soup and roast beef) and was surprisingly attentive. It could just be that my friend and I were the youngest ones there.  (Mix of late 20's and up)
Décor/Environment:  Was a bit on the warm side.  
 Overall I'm going to stick to the "probably not coming here again" side.

Came to Aquavit for the first time for Restaurant Week. The space is absolutely breathtaking with its tall ceilings and unique layout. The Restaurant Week menu gave diners a great idea of the food that Aquavit has to offer. I also really appreciate when these expensive restaurants also provide a restaurant week wine menu. I stuck to the vegetarian options with the "Barlotto" stealing the day. The service was a little scatter which I'm becoming accustomed to during Restaurant Week. Would definitely come to again!

I've been wanting to eat here for quite a while ever since hearing about the original restaurant Aquavit in Stockholm, thrilled to find out there was also a NYC branch as well.  Sadly exec chef Marcus Samuelsson has long since departed and broke his ties with the restaurant but knowing that shouldn't affect the experience in my opinion.  

You have 2 options when you book a dinner reservation, one is for the dining room that serves the exquisite 8 course chef's tasting menus or multiple prix fixe options, or the bistro located in the front for those who want a more traditional a la carte style 'you pick it and pay for it' dining experience.  I went with the bistro side as I thought the tasting menu was a little too much food for me and didn't want to spend the 3 + hrs going thru the whole thing.  Perhaps another time.

I opened with the steamed mussels appetizer in your typical white wine and garlic reduction, but seasoned with tomato instead of the usual french-style shallots.  Flavour was pretty good but sadly it looked like about a fifth of my mussels failed the 'open up and eat me' test and many of the ones that did open had little to no meat inside.  Now I know the chefs have no control over the contents of the mussel shells, esp when they are shut tight, and I thought the preparation was great, but the actual catch was a little poor for my meal.

Many of the entrees were a mix of your typical swedish style seafoods which entails a lot of cold fish and shellfish or your more traditional land based meats for the seafood averse.  I pondered for a sec ordered the Swedish meatballs, but I felt tacky ordered something I associate with the IKEA cafeteria so I decided to go with the Smorgasbord instead, which consisted of a selection of pickled herrings, sausage, smoked salmons & toast skagen.  While not the largest portions I found that I loved the pickled herring dishes a lot and the salmon was prepared near sashimi style as well.  After having what I felt was an undeniably swedish dish I washed the meal down with a selection of traditional aquavits (aka swedish style vodka).  With multiple flavours to choose from I picked a trio of traditional anise, coconut cappucino, and lingonberry (again the IKEA connection).  The anise tasted as I expect, almost harsh and medicinal, while the cappucino definitely had the coffee accents but I had no idea where the coconut was, and the lingonberry was probably my favorite with the tart acidity of the fruit represented well in the liquer and most well suited among the ones I tried.

Honestly I can't say this is the type of menu for everyone, but lovers of seafood and something a little different from the American norm should give this place a try.  I think it's Michelin stars are well deserved and if I go again in the future, then I'm plunging straight into the chef's menu and really see what is the best he claims to offer.

When you make a reservation you can either dine at the dining room or at the bistro. Dining room is formal, and do require dressing up. It Offers tasting menu and the atmosphere is more stiff than the brighter lit bistro. The bistro do not have any dress code but don't come here in T or sandals, most people eating in the bistro are well dressed. They also have a full bar but there is no reason to drink here unless you work nearby. I came here 3 times in the last 2 months, once for drinks at the bar and twice at the bistro. 

Bar: seems a little isolated since its not connected to neither the bistro nor the dining room, which is why the after-work crowd dominates the bar, and its a little deserted on weekends. Bartenders are very good and down to earth, will offer you free drinks if you are a regular, or have been drinking for a good 2-3 hours. 

Bistro: Space wise its not very big, but surprisingly spacious when you take your seat. Some people like the food and some people don't. personally I find the food to be very good. Scandinavian dishes focus on fish, and in Aquavit they seem to focus on Herring. The herring is fantastic but it is an acquired taste. Only order the herring for either the app or the entree but not both, because its a little overwhelming to have it for 2 courses. The meatballs is amazing, the cod is also awesome. almost all the dishes I have had are well executed. 

Service was very good, they greet you warmly and was accommodating with cancellations or changes. Most of the staff are very nice and knowledgeable about the food. However the second time I dined here our waiter was a little stiff, don't think he smiled once the whole night, and I felt like we weren't giving the attention we had the first time we dined here. 

I strongly recommend this place. come here during restaurant week if you want to be safe, and also they often have specials offers. Sometimes they will give you gift cards. Other times they have special events, like crawfish fest buffet for restaurant week prices. I don't think I will be a regular here because the food is not your daily diet food, but I will be back every once in a while just to remind myself of the wonderful experience I have had here.

Class. This place oozes with class. Well crafted. The interior/layout = fabulous, and you're enjoying well mixed cocktails at a NY Times 4-star restaurant...gets no better!

The manager also came over to check on how we were and struck up a conversation which was a nice touch. I'll def. be back.

Updated as promised!  This is a review for Aquavit's annual Crayfish festival. Sad to say, I still didn't try the Aquavit, but I did see it all about and it looked beautiful and delicious.  A fine dining place that has great beer, wine AND cocktails. Love it. 

Now, onto my main concern- the festy!  Warning: You gotta at least tolerate mayo and be in the mood for heavy Scandaniavian food to stomach this festival.  But I digress. My dining companion who's from out of town severly got lost so our 7:45 reservation turned into an 8:30...  yeah. Fortunately, the hostess was so sweet and understanding and took us into the Bistro at that time- no problem. 

The Bistro, as you would imagine, is completely different from the dining room. Still  sheek, and stylish but much warmer with warmer lighting. I almost feel out of Midtown and downtown in a NY hotspot.  You can get the normal bistro menu at this time; I saw some crossover from RW's dining such as the salmon, but also other ad hoc items which I think you can get only from the Bistro, without a tasting menu- such as the meatballs.   I was glad to see all the Aquavit's traditional favorites were on the buffet menu- which admittedly were at times better than the actual crayfish! 

I started with side one, before they bought out the eat and peel suckers!  Side one included (at least the highlights): Crayfish Skagen- I went up for this twice!  The only thing too! Creamy, but not too creamy- great taste- like a lobster salad, but with its little craysfish cousin.  Vasterbotten cheese- so unique, and sharp unlike any other!   Smoked salmon- not hot really, more like lukewarm, but good. (meh), Pickled Herring- I could only tolerate just one- you need to really love pickled herring.   Cheese tart- it was good but actually lacked in that strong cheese flavor; I almsost felt this was filler. I don't know how innovative that was.  Then, salad. I got the unhealthy kind too (yeesh- crayfish cesar salad...and some plain mixed greens... some).

Insert , crayfish.  These were a bitch to open.  Really- and it dawned on me that they looked like cockroaches with the legs all limp and about- cockroaches of the sea.  It makes me not want to eat them again because of the long- ongiong war I have with land roaches in my apartment.  Yuck. Moving along... As silly as this sounds, I almost missed out on the main event because I really couldn't  open any of them.  Lobster are bad enough but these are 20x smaller. Smaller than crawfish and darker too.  You can crack your labor away on getting the tiny claws but my dining partner instructed me on opening the tail.  Out some some tender, goopy crayfish.  Good--- and messy--and at one point, I punctured my thumb on a thorny part of the shell (which due to the oustanding service, I am sure they would have comped me for, but alas I kept quiet, drats)-- I'd say it tasted great, including the lemon/tartar-ish sauce it came with- and that it definitely needed those accents. Don't think I'd think much of crayfish solo. Honestly, don't know if I even liked the main event as much as tasting the buffet! 

Buffet side Dos: here come the starches!  Corn on the Cob with Taragon Butter- where was the taragon? I definitely tasted the butter, but no taragon.  There was Janssen's Temptation, which sounds like something from the Bible but was a shredded potato casserole- a little greasy but still good.  It wasn't as crispy as I'd liked.  Swedish Meatballs- burnt, succulent, the BOMB. Well seasoned- and ps I hate meatballs and don't ever eat grinded meat.  Ever.  Although I ate 1/4 of a meatball, it was damn good. 

Dessert: an assortment of here and there cookies that were unmemorable- also because I'd went overboard at this point at the buffet station and only nibbled. I'd had only really a good tasting of the "blueberry"- not strawberry cake, which was standard. 

Service- All fine and dandy. Just as good in the Bistro as in the Dining Room; I mean some of the busboy/waiters (in- betweens) weren't as professional or on point as you'd expect in fine dining but that's ok.  They still always folded our napkins nicely when we sat down, and bought me a new plate for Buffet Side 2 when  I asked.   In general, I was fine with the service.  They were never pushy- didn't push me to buy a drink which was great.

If you dined during RW Week, and got the coupon to come to this for basically, -$24 off, it's a solid deal.  I had one but my friend did not, but it still came to $70ish (plus his drink and tax/tip).  Overall, I'd give the crayfish festival 3.5 stars even though I stuck it with a 4 just because of my love for the Aquavit entreprise.   It wasn't anything way special, but still fun to attend.

GO CRAYFISH!

I'd give it 2.5 star only because the food wasn't that great. If you were going there for the decor, sure, why not. But a foodie like myself, I'd much rather go for the quality of the food and not to sit there for 2 hrs and not liking my food and staring at the decor. I ordered some type of Fish and it was so not memorable that I can't even remember what type of fish it was. It was a bit of a disappointment, considering that the price of the food there weren't exactly cheap either.

As a normally very frugal person, I decided to splurge and try this place out, and was happily surprised.  In the dining room, the host and waiters were extremely kind and helpful, offering suggestions about which aquavit flavors/cocktails would compliment which dishes.  The portions are haute cuisine -- I enjoyed my six bites of steak very much.  Ligonberry and reindeer made appearances on the menu, but it all still felt rather French in preparation and presentation.  If you are from the midwest (like me) and have trouble reckoning these factors, try checking out Smorgas, which offers fish, meatballs, and potatoes in forms and amounts you're more familiar with.  Still, Aquavit was an excellent departure from the norm of fine dining, in my experience.

I came here on a business lunch.  Our table had the chef's tasting menu, plus we ordered swedish meatballs to start.  The dining room in the back is so pretty.  I really loved it.  

The swedish meatballs were the best part of the meal.  They were juicy and flavorful, and the cream sauce was delicious.  The tasting menu started with a trio of herring served with cheese and a potato.  I discovered that I do not like pickled herring.  I had a really hard time suppressing the look of disgust on my face.  I don't think the fish was bad or prepared poorly, it just is clearly not my taste.  I will never order herring, lesson learned.

Next up was the cold smoked salmon on a potato cake with roasted pistachios, sour cream and caviar.  This was tasty, but I couldn't really taste the caviar and it just didn't seem that special to me.  I could easily just buy high quality lox myself to enjoy.  When I go to a fancy restaurant, I like to have something that I can't normally enjoy or prepare myself. 

Next was the Penobscot chicken breast which is stuffed with wild mushrooms and served with zucchini and tomato saute.  The chicken was moist and it was very tasty, but nothing out of this world.

For dessert, I had the Arctic Circle.  It's a goat cheese parfait with passion fruit filling and blueberry sorbet on top.  The goat cheese was incredible and the passion fruit was not overpowering at all.  This was the second to best part of the meal.  The blueberry sorbet on top was a bit too sweet though. 

The service was kind of weird.  The waiter kept standing next to our table waiting for a lull in our conversation before approaching.  It was just very awkward to have stand right beside your table waiting for you to stop talking.  But, of course, he was nowhere to be found when we wanted the check. 

I'll come back if someone else is paying and really wants to try it out.  Otherwise, I feel no need to try the rest of the menu.

I finally got to try Aquavit with my wife for my Birthday.  We made a reservation in the small bistro section of the restaurant.  Having wanted to try the restaurant for a while I was pretty excited.  

Decor:  When you think of Scandinavian design, all I can think about is Ikea.  This place was no Ikea.  Inside they do have a very minimalist brand of furniture, from the wooden paneling of the walls and floor to the simple benches and swivel chairs at each table.  The paintings are very marimekko in style (as pointed out by my wife), but you do feel very at home. 

Service:  Throughout the whole night the service was quite impeccable.  Our waitress was at our beckoning call all night and immediately made her appearance at our table when we sat down.  Nothing I hate more than sitting there for 10 minutes with no waiter.  We ended up with a couple freebies due to our own mistake of ordering the wrong drink, and a free dessert from our waitress' mistake of placing the order.  I felt taken care of throughout the night and the table was cleared swiftly and quietly.  

Drinks: Aquavit -- we decided to do a flight of 3, picking the mango lime and chili pepper, ligonbarry and ginger and lemon.  I only really enjoyed the chili pepper, as it had the taste of Absolut Peppar.  Honestly though, i could have had another beer and less of this stuff.  Not my favorite, but I appreciate the availability of so many types.

Food:  I decided on the prix fixe, which changed so it did have a few options I really wanted.  I had my heart set on the Bouillabaisse for my main dish, and by my own mistake, i picked the Chantrelle Veloute with pork belly.  My eyes saw pork belly and missed the Veloute.  Oh well, it was still excellent, but I would have maybe enjoyed something more.  The Bouillabaisse however was remarkable.  The broth stunning, fragrant and bursting with flavor.  The scallop was seared and cooked through and each shrimp was still plump and good.  My wife picked the barlotto, which was a barley risotto with white truffles and cheese.  It was rich and excellent, from my tiny taste.

Dessert:  My set meal had me chose the chocolate cake with fresh fruit salad and creme.  My wife picked the goat cheese pancake, but on accident they brought a brownie sundae.  Oops, we got to eat that too on the house.  The goat cheese pancake was like a crepe filled with creamy cheese, nothing wrong there.

Overall:  Each dish took a lot of attention to detail and nothing was missed.  The service was friendly and helpful.  While I might have ordered something different as an appetizer, I was still very happy and thus give 4 stars.

Giving two stars, I am being generous.

The plus : 
- the decor, very stylish... (but not comfy)
- the service was excellent overall, if not a little cold
The minus:
- the food. between the six of us, tryinf different delicacies, we could not find one dish that we thoroughly enjoyed.

Also, I have eaten way better salmon almost anywhere in the world, let alone NY. For a scandinavian restaurant, that's a shame !

An expensive disapointment.

One of our favorite restaurants of all time.  I found out about it because my wife is half-ethiopian, and even before it became uber famous, it's been a buzz in the Ethiopian community since Chef Samuelsson incorporates traditional Ethiopian flavors into Scandinavian dishes.

We come here often, and have had nearly everything on the menu.  We're on the mailing list, so we also come for their wonderful seasonal smorgasbords.

I don't really have any suggestions, because everything is amazing... but if this is a special occasion, here is my personal suggestion for getting best bang for the buck.

1) Get the tasting.  Period.
2) Don't think you'll enjoy the tasting, get the prix fixe.  Pick three courses with a amuse bouche or two in between.  Perfect date night.
3) Please try the "Herring Degustation."
4) The foie gras will evoke emotions you never knew existed.
5) My wife loves the Arctic circle dessert (kind of like a cheesecake that graduated with its PhD), while I love the more down-to-earth chocolate cake with ice cream (lame, i know... but it's great).
6) If you're around during the "Crayfish" festival, GO.

I'm not sure what else to say.  I can write pages upon pages on Aquavit, but who wants to read that... So I suggest to just go, enjoy the tremendous service, enjoy the delectable flavors, and leave with a happy stomach.

Aquavit is by far the most impressive fine dining experience I've had thus far. I recommend making reservations ahead of time and go when you're not in a rush - allow at least two to two and a half hours for dinner. There are two choices - chef's tasting and a three course prefix, but there are so many complimentary intermittent dishes, aside from the muse, that I don't recommend going when time is tight.

It's not a particularly romantic atmosphere, but make sure your properly dressed in business casual. 

I had the prefix by the recommendation of the waiter - crusted maine lobster, berkshire pork and coffee savarin for dessert. The lobster comes in a rectangle with a side salad of greens which had a floral taste - an interesting choice to mix cardamom in Scandinavian cuisine. Berkshire pork is apparently new on the menu, which is what I had as an entree and the serving is quite large with a portion of pork belly as well and a bit salty, but a dish I definitely recommend for dinner. 

The coffee savarin was so amazing - its a white espresso icecream on a circular slice of cake. They offer mixed berries of your choice and serve it to you separately on a plate. 

I really recommend coming here on a first date, its definitely impressive.

Aquavit is on the ground floor of the building in which I work.  I am spoiled having such a gem only a short elevator ride away.  I've enjoyed eating at Aquavit for years and was skeptical when it moved to its (now-not-so) new space.  I remember the intimacy and charm of the old space near the University Club with fondness.  It's true when people say this space on 55th Street is much more "Scandinavian" in a way.  It is tall and spacious with a well-lit frostiness to it.  This only highlights the warm service and excellent cuisine.  If you enjoy herring, Swedish meatballs, gravlax, venison, Arctic Char, etc. then Aquavit is a must-visit.  

The bar area has a nice lounge that separates the front dining room from the rear (more formal) dining room.  A great place for after-work drinks.  Joey and John are two of the nicest and skilled bartenders you will meet.  Heard they just started a Saturday brunch and will definitely want to try it out soon.  The restaurant has lost nothing with the departure of Marcus Samuelsson (although he was an incredibly skilled and gracious presence at Aquavit) and is as good as ever.

The best meal I've had in NYC!!  We went for lunch and enjoyed the prix fixe menu in the bistro ..  I selected the chantrelle veloute, grilled mackerel layered with mashed potato & spinach (sorry I don't recall the exact description of how it was prepared) and the creme brûlée.  I also enjoyed the herring sampler. 

As a Norwegian-American and active member of Sons of Norway, I am familiar with Scandinavian foods ... particularly herring. Aquavit took the familiar to the next level. Beautifully presented and each dish delightfully prepared. I was impressed with each course equally and enjoyed each bite.

not only have i had a front of the house experience, i also had a back of the house experience as i have trailed and worked for this restaurant.  (a trail is a cook's interview to see if you are able enough to work in their kitchen, etc).

being in the back of the house you get to see how everything runs it was definitely good to witness.  this new aged scandanavian-american restaurant is definitely a place to come check out.  

i did the pre-fixe menu and was very pleased with my meal.  could definitely tell that the food is well made and prepared with detail and care.  for the first course, we tried the herring degustation, warm king crab, and the wild mushroom and beet cassoulet.  for the second course we had had the scallops, angus beef and the lamb.  everything was cooked real and was very pleased with the meal.  

all in all, this place is definitely worth checking out if you're willing to spend a little.  this place is well known in new york and was definitely a great meal.

I have come here twice - the first time may years ago with my sister (a fellow foodie) and more recently, with my wife a couple of years ago - each time we tried the full tasting menu.

In short, I remember two things in particular:

1.  The food - the food was artfully conceived, artfully prepared, artfully rendered and artfully presented.  I remember feeling like we were being swept away on a high-minded culinary adventure rather than just a normal great meal.  The dishes were creative, fanciful, unobvious, and breathtaking to look at.  In both cases, I don't remember which specific dish spoke to me the most, but I do remember that the full experience was nothing less than delightful.  

2.  The service - the service at Aquavit was impeccible.  The wait staff was extremely attentive, polite and helpful.  With such contemporary sensibilities in the design of the dishes and the ambience of the restaurant, its nice to see some old world charm in the service. 

This is truly one of the most extraordinary restaurants in the city for pure foodies.   There are more romantic restaurants in the city, ones with more interesting decor, more grandiose themes, etc.   But for a pure food experience, Aquavit is king.

I came here for dinner a few nights ago.  I love the smorgasboard concept, so I ordered the Christmas Plate to try a little of everything.

Glogg - it's like a scandinavian version of mulled wine.  VERY sweet.  Be warned.  But it's warm, so it goes well with the cold plate actually.

Cold plate - I liked everything on this place - mackerel, herring, beets, apples, deviled egg, fingerling potatoe, small slice of cheese

Main plate - I really enjoyed the swedish meatballs, but that was about it.  There was a sliced up hot dog...eh.  There was a rolled up piece of ham with mustard...eh...and some onions...I should have just ordered the swedish meatballs main dish!!!

I did enjoy the dessert, which was a plum dessert with saffron ice cream and almond paste on the dish.

My date got the prixe fixe and I think he enjoyed his meal more than me.  Hahah!

This place is really cool - but I either ordered the wrong things or I am not a fan of this type of food.

Food was good but I find it frustrating when the restaurant's web site states that brunch is $48 pp and when we arrive it is $65pp.  Why can't the restaurant publish the correct info?  and not crazy about loud kids running around a restaurant .

This review is long overdue by about a year. I work in the building next door and have been stopping by for a drinks to unwind after work. This is a great place for sit down dinner or simply just some drinks / appetizers. 

Naturally the selection of Aquavit here is quite excellent (the restaurant is named after the drink). They have more than 20 flavors to choose from  - Horse Radish / Coriander & Dill / Fig are my 3 favorite s. Cocktail selection is quite excellent as well, spicy mango martini or the Manhattan are about as good as they get. 

The staff here are just great.  Service is prompt, efficient and attentive, but never over bearing. Really classy but chill type of environment. Depending on which nights you are here you'll get either Joey, John or Gillian. These guys are really knowledgeable on the vast Aquavit / wine selection, as well as the delicious menu . Really great group of people there.

Only downside to this place is they do really get busy sometimes - when you stop by after 12 hours of work and find out that your favorite bar is occupied that's just disappointing. Bummer.

Perhaps should give this 4 stars but I'm giving it 3 based on its comparison to my expectations.

While it's better than the swedish meatballs at the Ikea foodcourt, it was still Scandinavian at the core, which is better than British Food, but still...

I read that this place was Scandinavian with a "twist".  I'm thinking there needs to be some more "twist".

Went for restaurant week. What a relief to find that Marcus Samuelson, whom I always respected, was not responsible for this experience. The dining room was sweltering. The service was friendly but not proficient. Why were the servers reaching across my face? Most disappointing: the food was mediocre. They gave us cards to come back at a discount. I wouldn't.

Great Swedish cuisine.  Really think the deals are to be found at the bar and bistro seating, although the meal I had in the main dining room was ridonkulous, but pricey.  Very low key but classy place to grab a drink.

This place is clean, simple, and delicious.
I felt refreshed after my dinner.
It made me want to go to the Nordic countries.

even the reindeer tasted delicious!

I've been to the old location several times and loved the clean minimalist modern space.  I went to the new one with a friend for lunch, and liked the updated modern 60's lounge vibe.  We ate in the cafe, and chose from the limited restaurant Week Menu, but everything was outstanding!  The herring sampler is a must!  The vodka selection is extensive, and the innovative combinations will tickle your taste buds. Definately try Aquavit's full menu, as there are so many wonderful dishes not available for restaurant week. Portions are uber small and prices very high, but all worth it.

This review is for the restaurant week winter 2010 menu:

I ordered the goat cheese salad and the Mrs ordered the herring. Their herring is highly lauded, and we could not come here without ordering. Apparently the herring is great on the real menu bc she says the herring was alright. My salad was good. 

For dinner we ordered the Pork Belly and Celeriac barley. Both were great. The Barely tasted like oatmeal for dinner. The pork belly was unlike any I have ever tasted. For dessert, we ordered the two options, the hazelnut terrine and artic circle. Sweetness heaven!

For drinks we ordered the 3 aquavits. It doesn't matter what flavors they were, bc they were all terrible to me and the Mrs. We had no idea that aquavits were flavored vodka shots. Thankfully our host saw our malcontent and removed the charge from our bill.

For the evening, I was surprised by the portions. Usually at these high class restaurants, for restaurant week, they offer the dinkiest portions that leave you very unsatiated. I was 100% expecting that here. I was gladly mistaken. I left feeling full and content.

As an added bonus, they offer a $50 coupon for a re-visit.

This is my second time eating here, although last time was in the lounge area, and I have to say they really upped the ante this restaurant week. I was thoroughly impressed.

I'll start with the only oddity, which was the somewhat uneven service due to having two formal wait staff for the entire main dining room. This was fine at the start of dinner but we got more and more busboy service toward the end of the meal as the place filled up. I wouldn't complain about this, but they're frankly just not as good at introducing the intricacies of each dish and I found myself getting the waitresses for additional explanation.

Other than that, the evening was fantastic. The breads were unique and the butter tasty. They brought out a 3-part Amuse: smoked salmon, poached salmon, and anchovie. I later noticed that another nearby table only received one little dish for their amuse. I wonder if these were leftovers or they just ran out. Either way, all three were delicious with distinct flavors and beautiful presentation and definitely a great way to start the meal.

We had the steak tartar, which came with condiments (fresh shaved horseradish, capers, pickled red beets, Swedish mustard, chopped onions, smoked egg yolk) on the side, and glassblower herring, to start. The tartar was rather tasteless on its own, but worked well with some of the condiments. The herring was tasty but I honestly don't remember much about it.

We had the pepper seared mackerel and Berkshire pork belly for our mains. The mackerel was very peppery and overpowered the creamed cabbage it was sitting on, but flavorwise was exceptional. The pork belly was amazing. It was very tender and packed a lot of flavor in every bite. I found myself cutting smaller and smaller pieces to savor it. The skin was slightly caramelized, which was a nice treat. 

There were only two options for dessert but both were great. The hazelnut praline terrine honestly tasted like Nutella, but that's a good thing! The apple compote it was paired with frankly seemed like a second dessert, as the two flavors didn't go together, but again, that's a good thing. The Arctic Circle is Aquavit's signature dessert, a frozen goat cheese parfait with a lingonberry core and a scoop of vargtass (lingonberry + vodka) sorbet. The parfait was the perfect consistency and had an excellent flavor. My date litterally teared up a little while eating it.

Highly recommended, though I'm guessing you'll be hard-pressed to find winter restaurant week reservations at this point...

My friends and I came here during the restaurant week. It has a simple and small front door and I alomst ignored it when I passed by. But when I walked into it, it looked like another world. It clean and simple, no more decoration. I like the warm light there, it's neither too bright nor too dim. 

We choose the restaurant week menu. My appetizer is sth like "hot goat cheese salad". I really love the hot goat cheese! One of my friend ordered sth with raw beef. It tastes a little weired...

My main dish is fried fish and cabbage (sorry I forgot the name and I have to use such a suck name...). The fish is not bad, but not that good. Anyway, it tastes good.

Finally, the dessert time! I ordered a goat cheesecake with berry icecream (goat cheese again...). I love the goat cheesecake!

Wow, very impressed!!  Every dish that came out was delectable!  I can't believe I've waited so long to eat dinner here... this is one restaurant that's worth the $!  And, even the dessert was amazing.  I will definitely be coming back here.

In Short:  Good decor and a solid menu make up for friendly, if spotty service.  Portions are beautifully composed, but rather on the small side.

I met with a few friends at Aquavit for a get-together during restaurant week.  I ordered off of the restaurant week menu, and we dined in the more casual bistro room.  The decor of the restaurant is definitively updated modernism; think Ikea but with nice materials and less Formica.  Some of the paintings were a bit hokey (featuring the restaurants namesake liquor, for example) but once we were seated, the overall feel was calm and private.

Before the appetizers came out a plate with wasa-esque bread and a tiny loaf of fluffy white came out, accompanied by butter and a kind of salmony spread, which went beautifully on the harder bread.

For an appetizer I had pickled herring.  Having never had it before, I was unsure of what to expect and I was tremendously pleasantly surprised.  It had a lovely firm consistency that is often hard to find in a white fish.  The flavor was a bit acidic with hints of citrus and there wasn't even the faintest hint of the fishy scent and taste which accompanies less-than-fresh fish.  There were other little bits of things on the plate: stiff toast and some sprouts, but the piece of fish was about 2/3 the size of a pack of playing cards and the rest were gone in a mouthful.

For a main course I ordered Berkshire Porkbelly with mashed potatoes.  It came out standing like a tower in a vast wasteland of plate with only a few bits of foliage and starch to keep it company.  The top layer was unbelievably fatty, but somehow managed to be so without overwhelming the taste of the underlying meat.  The mashed potatoes were unremarkable and the other bits of flora were so minor as to not deserve mention.

For desert, I had a lovely series of three sorbets (it isn't on the restaurant week menu, but being lactose intolerant, I got an exception).  The flavors were good, and not overly sweet.  My friends ordered the Arctic Circle and while I sampled a bit and found it good, none of the three of them managed to finish the rich dish.  

While the food, if meager, was delicious, the service left something to be desired.  I asked for no ice in my water (never really been a fan) at the beginning of the meal.  The first glass came out ice free.  But then the waiter neglected to tell the busboys and all subsequent water had ice in it.  I am a bit picky, it is true, but the lack of communication showed a weak point in this otherwise great experience.  Furthermore, one of the dessert orders at my table came out completely wrong.  The waitstaff, however, were nice and did their best to be accommodating.  They simply lack the protocol to allow good communications.

I rather liked the food at Aquavit and found the decor to be good, if not awe inspiring, but a few errors by the waitstaff marred the experience.

Visited for restaurant week and the food was very good. I was surprised by how casual the dining experience was and how laid back the ambience was (lighting, seating etc in this case). I second other reviews who've communicated that this is top notch scandinavian. The cuisine is not for everyone so be sure ahead of time that you're aware of what's offered.

I ordered a bottle of wine (Rest. Week price of $24) Cabernet
Steak Tartar was excellent. The plate features white horseradish, a spicy mustard, chopped beets, egg yolk, chopped onions and capers. Excellent. Really.

The main dish was the berkshire pork belly w/ side of yukon mash which was also quite good and well presented but on the small side, even by haute standards.

The lingonberry sorbet finale was tart and yummy, a mouth battle of contrasting temperatures and sweetness.

All in all I was impressed at how reasonable the non-restaurant week menu was. I'd always heard that this place was very expensive. Expensive yes, but not for this caliber of restaurant.

The food experience was good, not mind-blowing, and the atmosphere is laid back and Diner chic. I would probably return for Rest Week Lunch, I'd love to taste the swedish meatballs.

All in all, a good dining experience, maybe just not worth the restaurant week trip.

Had the restaurant week menu on Friday night. The steak tartar appetizer was good, but not great. The fresh horseradish and smoked egg yolk really tied it together, but the actual steak would need to be better for a knockout appetizer. The peppered mackerel entree was very good. The fish was excellently cooked and the skin was perfectly crispy and complemented well by the bed of porcini creamed cabbage. The goat cheese parfait dessert was the highlight of the meal. The goat cheese--reversing from its usual role as the tart ingredient--was delightfully sweet and creamy, topped by the tart lingonberry sorbet. Of the Anise, Caraway & Fennel aquavit, the coconut & espresso aquavit, and the fig and cardamom aquavit, the anise was the best and truest to its advertised flavors. With good company and nice ambiance, this is a great spot for a nice, but not over-the-top dinner.

Yum!

I came here for a friend's birthday and to take advantage of Restaurant Week (which is only available in the bistro area, just fyi when you're making reservations online).

When we arrived, we checked our coats and we were seated v. promptly. We were each handed a menu which was a piece of paper in between 2 pieces of plastic held together by rubber bands (I uploaded a photo). Clever idea, if you ask me - easy to change the menu and you keep it waterproof and stain proof!

The restaurant week menu offers 3 choices of appetizer, 3 choices of entree, and 2 dessert choices. Amongst the 5 of us, we tried to divvy up the dishes so we could try all of them - we ordered at least 1 of each dish except for the celeriac barley (because none of us are vegetarian or interested in barley, though I'm sure it would have been delicious).

The appetizers:
1. Steak Tartare - delicious! It was a "deconstructed" tartare, meaning the chopped meat was in the center of the plate, simply sprinkled with salt and deep fried parsley. Surrounding the meat were the "condiments" and seasonings - like diced onions, capers, horseradish, smoked egg yolk, and pickled beets. I love tartare.

2. Glassblower Herring - wow! The plate was styled v. simply: herring in the middle piled with roe and a dollop of sour cream on the side. There were a few slices of red onion as a garnish as well. The fish wasn't fishy at all and the dish itself was really flavorful. The portion was rather small - but there was enough that all 5 of us got to have a sufficient taste.

3. Hot-Smoked Goat Cheese Salad - yummy! The goat cheese balls were breaded and then warmed, which made for a really lovely texture (contrast between the crunch of the breading and the softness of the cheese). The salad itself was a normal salad (micro greens with a soft vinaigrette). Really good though.

The main courses:
