1. Pepper Seared Mackerel: not bad! This dish was good, but not great. The fish was cooked well and I liked the crispy skin. It was served over creamed cabbage, which was the best part, I thought - full of flavor, great texture.

2. Berkshire Pork Belly: drool! I loved this dish. We ordered 3 of these, and it was a little odd because the portions of the belly varied greatly amongst the 3 plates. The belly brushed with a sweet and tangy sauce (like barbecue sauce) and came with a really smooth mashed potato. The amount of potato given wasn't really proportional to the serving size of the meat, however - it was so small that the bf swiped up and ate the entire portion in one swoop of his fork.

The desserts:
1. Arctic Circle: tasty! Wasn't quite sure what to expect with this dish but I was excited for the lingonberry (which reminded me of Ikea). It was a cheesecake-like custard with a scoop of lingonberry sorbet on top. The salted pistachios added a great crunch and I liked the combination of salt and sweet.

2. Hazelnut Praline Terrine: sweet! The plate had a super thin slice of a custard made with layered hazelnut and chocolate. It was almost like a mousse - soft, smooth, and really rich. Served along side was apple compote (tasted like tart applesauce) and a hazlenut sorbet.

Things to note: they offer a RW wine list (1 red, 1 white) with a bottle for half the price of the rest of the wines offered. They also have a few beers, ciders, and dessert/after dinner drinks. They also have ice wine! (Look it up if you don't know what it is) and they serve it by the glass as well as by the bottle.

The service was superb. Our water glasses were always filled, our empty plates were taken away quickly, our bread was replenished when asked, really commendable. If the food had been mediocre (which it wasn't) I could probably have been easily wooed and swayed by the attentiveness of the staff.

I definitely recommend you come here! Especially for Restaurant Week, as the prices are really worth the quality of the food.

gorgeous restaurant. even their less formal bistro is beautifully appointed and one does not feel like sitting in the middle grand central station (see oceana).
the food was excellent. if might not be for everyone, but with an open mind it is a memorable experience.
we made reservations by phone, but they failed to mention that their restaurant week menu is only available in the bistro section.
we were already seated in the main dining room and the server was so gracious that we decided to stay and try their regular fare. it was well worth it. the service was superb (with the exception of a rather strange and borderline rude man serving bread). 
both pork and fish were great. try arctic circle for desert. we are used to a french way of eating cheese before desert, so it was interesting to have a combination of the two in one dish. frozen goat cheese - yummy!

Had the following courses during the Restaurant Week:

* Fried smoked goat cheese balls and frisee salad w/apple vinaigrette
* Pepper crusted mackarel on a bed of sauteed cabbage. Filet was cooked perfectly. Cabbage was tasty. Not crazy about the red beet on the top.
* Lemon tart w/ shaved almond, candied orange peel, marshmellow, tear-shaped meringue. A bit too sweet for my liking.
* Arctic Circle - cold goat cheese log/cake with lingonberry sorbet and salted pistachio nuts. Very refreshing and sophisticated!  Perfect ending to a good meal. Definitely highlight of my meal.

$35 for a 3-course meal is a steal!

I'm new to Yelp and haven't written that many reviews, plus I'm not a good writer but I feel obligated to contribute as I've been reading everyone else's reviews... and I also realize that wow, I've been to many many restaurants in NYC throughout the years...... and I came across Aquavit as I was looking for a dinner spot today. The dishes, as I remembered, were exquisitely presented. However, the taste perhaps weren't my style as I didn't find them that memorable to be ranked as one of the best restaurants in NYC. If you've never tried Scandinavian delicacies, this is a great place to start. The atmosphere, as with many fine restaurants in NYC, is very elegant.

1st restaurant week stop!

Not much of a fan of the atmosphere felt like a fancy office, slightly austere. Service, however was top notch.

Appetizers: we ordered the Glassblower herring and hot-smoked goat cheese salad. The salad had great taste and texture. Though the herring had a nice presentation, it lacked some flavor. 

Dinner picked things up. I really liked my Pork Belly. it was laying on thin smear of whipped yukon gold potato. Wishing it was a bigger proportion. SO had the Celeriac barley, which frankly I barely remember now.

Desserts: we each picked the two options: the artic circle( goat cheese parfait + sorbet + salted pistachios) and hazelnut terrine (apple compote + hazelnut sherbet). Overall I feel dessert is where most places shine the best for RW. 

One big regret of ours: getting the Aquavit special. Littled did we know they were powerful vodka shots (not a fan of raw hard liquor)

worth a restaurant week visit!

Went to the Bistro with clients on Sunday evening. It was a little empty (well maybe because the Jets played the Steelers that evening) but the service was good and the food decent. The meetballs could have been a little warmer though (maybe the chef was busy too watching the Jets). Still a good place for a business lunch and dinner.

Aquavit is most definitely in a class of its own.

Yeah, I know, not many Scandinavian restaurants around these parts, but still.. it's really effin' good.

Everything... every single morsel and drop of food and drink was pretty close to perfectly-done. This past evening was my second fortunate experience dining at Aquavit, and I was really feeling blessed to be an epicurian in its Nordic temple.

Except, there was one thing that really burnt the shit out of me. So much so that an amount of my review is, unfortunately, going to be focused on it.

A really great friend of mine made reservations for restaurant week and we went. Unfortunately, Aquavit was no longer offering the restaurant week particulars, unbeknownst to us until our incredibly kind, incredibly charming, and incredibly apologetic (in exactly the correct, polite, and dignified manner) informed us of this catch. He really was the ultimate exemplar of a class-act server, befitting of such an establishment. The management should be proud to count him among the staff.

As it would be, we were kindly re-seated and accommodated under said particulars anyway, though we had even initially shrugged it off and started settling on the $85/person prix fixe or the $115/person chef's tasting. Server number one even gracefully handed us off to our second server and whispered a fairly audible, "please take *very, very* good care of these ones." My heart kind of melted at the sweetness of it all. Server number two was equally as fantastic. Attentive, kind, hands-down fantastic. The food and the drink, all of it top-notch, as dreamed of.

But then the bomb dropped.

Another server (let's call her "server three") came over to chat with our server (sweet, wonderful server number two), at the service station nearest our table, and, quite loudly, quite snottily, barfed out (roughly), "Oh, isn't it so NICE it's not RESTAURANT WEEK ANYMORE? I mean, can't you just TELL?!"

Word to the wise: if you're a server at a greasy spoon, don't trash talk any (kind of) patron any time of the year, ever. If you're lucky enough to pull the kind of gratuities serving at Aquavit, you really should have a higher level of decorum.

Server number two reacted with a really bitter scowl, as if to say, "shutyourfaceomgicantbelieveyoujustsaidthat" in an entirely non-sarcastic way, and audibly hissed multiple, multiple scathing shushes at her. Server number two's instant, unflappable save breathed some serious air into my otherwise seriously deflated heart.

Conduct unbefitting such an establishment from server three was, for lack of a better descriptor, leveling. Frankly, even if I was at a Michelin rated restaurant, I wouldn't want to hear that kind of talk. Even if I was our city's wealthiest patron, I wouldn't want to hear that kind of talk while eagerly eyeing a spectacular menu. It's just really very shitty and I hope she never, ever, ever, ever does that kind of thing again. We hear you, and we've judged you right back.

Regardless, this did not detract from the smart, clean-lined, smoothly-designed, efficiently-presented fact that Aquavit in food, drink, service, and ambiance (99%) is nothing less than spectacular. If every server was as kind and attentive and caring as the ones and the twos, I'd have petitioned Yelp to give out six stars.

I came here as a party of 5 during Restaurant Week.  After perusing the list of restaurants, we decided on Aquavit because of the great price point/value and reviews.  We arrived at 6:30 for our 6:45 reservation.  We checked out coats and were seated promptly, in the bistro area.  It's a nice big cozy open space, which I really liked.

We each ordered our own dish and shared so that we could have a taste of everything. Our bread "basket" came out on a stone and included this hard wafer that I was not particularly fond of.  I liked the salmon spread that came with it, though.

Appetizers
I think out of the appetizers, my favorite was the Swedish steak tartare.  Apparently, Swedish steak tartare is supposed to come with the meat in the middle with all the other ingredients on the side and supposed to all me mixed by the diners.  Oops.  Not knowing this, we ended up eating them all unmixed.
The goat cheese salad was good, but nothing spectacular enough to wow me. The caramelized walnuts were pretty good, and I liked the interesting crispy/crunchy texture of the breading and the goat cheese on the inside.
The glassblower herring was really flavorful considering its small portion. I feel like the side accompaniments like the roe, sour cream, pearl onion and all were lost in the flavor of the herring.  But then again, we had split this one piece into 5, so I only had a small bite to really taste. 

Main Courses
The Berkshire pork belly was really good.  Mine was a bit more soft and had the texture of pulled pork compared to the other two pork belly dishes we had.  It made for a hard time trying to cut in (it just came off in "mushy" pieces), but the taste was really great, and very moist.  I also tried the other pork, which was also good. The charred cipollini onion was not a particular favorite part of this dish, considering I'm not a huge fan of cooked onions (had a bad experience as a child), but it was good for a cooked onion haha.  The Yukon mashed potatoes were nice and creamy.
The mackerel was pretty good.  It was well cooked, but nothing spectacular.  However, I am a big cabbage fan, so I thoroughly enjoyed the bed of creamed cabbage the fish was placed upon.  My friend who ordered this dish is not big fan of cabbage, so I luckily got to eat most of his cabbage.

Dessert
The hazelnut terrine was really good.  It reminded me of Nutella that I love so much, but in a more creamy texture. I thought the hazelnut sherbet and apple compote combination was pretty interesting.  The textures and the combination of tart and sweet was surprising.  But yeah, I really enjoyed the terrine.
The arctic circle dessert was really good, too. I liked the cheesecake texture to it, and the salted pistachios were a nice relief from all the sweet.
I think both desserts were a hit.

We ordered wines with our meal.  The red wine on the Restaurant Week list was not available, but they had two others on the regular wine menu that were the same price, so we ordered one of each. We also ordered dessert and ice wine (by the glass, which is hard to find according to my friend) for our desserts. The ice wine was really good, but my friend said the French ice wine is sweeter and better (they only had Canadian at Aquavit).

The service was really good.  Perfect balance between tending to us enough times not to feel ignored and not coming too often to have it feel like an interruption.  I think all restaurants can take a cue from the Aquavit waitstaff.

I definitely recommend the Restaurant Week menu, as it is a really good value.  I would love to try the regular dining menu here someday when my money tree finally blooms.

Came here for an early business lunch around noon. They had extended RW, so I ended up ordering from that menu and my companion had their lunch tasting menu. Usually the tasting menu is for the table, but the chef was nice enough to allow us to be the exception. 

What we ate:
- They had a cracker-like bread, and Danish bread as part of their basket. Both were great in their own way. The cracker was hard and had a nutty flavor, and the Danish bread was almost like a quickbread and filled with seeds. 
- The amuse bouche was pickling herring with something like a cream cheese on top, pickled beet and cippolini onion. It was very attractive. It was small and had great flavor, but a bit rich.  One bite was definitely enough.
- I had Chanterelle Veloute as an appetizer, it came with pork belly and mushrooms in the soup and a popover biscuit on the side. The pork belly was delicious (how could it not be?) but the soup was way, way too salty and acidic. It honestly tasted like creamy pickle juice, it was a bit too intense and I really couldn't finish it.
- I had the Mackerel for an entree. It came with a beet, cabbage, and red wine sauce on the plate. The fish was good, but to be honest not outstanding. I was a bit disappointed that the beet was in a giant hunk on top of the fish. I understand it is RW and they have to make ends meet, but I would have been happy with a smaller portion and more impressive flavors. The sauce did not bring all the components together. Again, decent but not great.
- For dessert I had the praline terrine. It came with an apple compote and some kind of sorbet or ice cream that was terrific!  The ice cream tasted like it was made from yogurt and kind of like Pinkberry, but much more fragrant. The apple compote was DELICIOUS, and there was some hazelnut caramel on the plate that was really good as well. I really enjoyed with dessert and was impressed with the flavors and plating of it. 

My companion had the tasting menu, and I had a bite of everything :). This is what she ate:
- Pickled Herring - this was ok and tasted how you'd expect pickled herring to taste. It was good, but not exactly my cup of tea. 
- Duck Charcuterie - this was absolutely incredible and definitely the most memorable dish I had there. The flavor of the cured ham was great, loved the foie, loved the mustard, loved the pickled vegetables. Loved everything about this one. If I come back, it's going to be for this one!
- The Chatham Cod was delicious as well. The fish was moist, flaky, buttery  and seared well, it really tasted like a crispy hashbrown and had terrific texture and flavor. I really liked this as well.
- The Arctic Circle was OK - I'm not a fan of goat cheese and the bite I had of the lingonberry sorbet did not exactly stand out. I would say I liked my dessert more, but I will definitely come back to try their unique sorbet flavors.

We had a great Sauvignon Blanc to drink, and our waiter was great. The service was attentive and our water was always full. There were long pauses between courses, but perhaps that was to allow for conversation? Unsure.

I went with a friend after we somehow snagged a table during Restuarant Week at the last minute.  I was a little intimidated at first, going to such an iconic restaurant with really fancy food, but I loved the RW dinner I had.  I tried new ingredients (pork belly,) had old favorites (chocolate cake) and discovered I might actually like something I thought I hated (anchovy!)  The service was great and the generous gift vouchers to come back again to do the tasting menu was stellar.    

Perfect Restaurant Week experience!

My boyfriend and I dined at Aquavit for an early Valentine's day dinner. 

We dined in the Main Dining Room which was served a Prix fix menu. If you want a la carte, go to the bistro dining room. The Main Dining Room was very intimate and roomy. They had booths for 2 and conference like tables with huge black chairs for bigger groups. 

Before every course, the chef would provide amuse-bouches which were amazing and wanting you craving more of it. 

For appetizers, we ordered the Warm Maine Lobster (creamy and plentiful of lobster) and the Duck Pastrami (moist and full of flavor). For Entrees, we ordered the Nordic Choucroute (the scallops were heavenly!) and Berkshire Pork Three Ways. I personally didn't like the spicy black pudding but the pork was marinated, moist, and cooked very well that I overlooked that minor flaw. I would definitely recommend the Arctic Circle for dessert - not too sweet, a bit tart from the lingonberry sorbet. 

For the taste of the food, the service, and the ambiance, I would definitely recommend to go again for a special occasion or business dinner. The servers aren't quick to hurry you and give you the space you need to enjoy the meal and the dining room. After the meal, they did give us each a $50 coupon to come back and dine with them during a certain period.

Came here for the V Day.  They had the restaurant week menu which they apparently have all year around.  Maybe I am not a fan of the Nordic cuisine (though heaven knows I love my smoked fishes and Swedish meatballs), but everything we had just tasted pedestrian and mediocre. Appetizers included an utterly unassuming plate of greens you can pick up at your supermarket and piled on a plate in no particular order smoked salmon (see supermarket); Entrees were a super fatty pork belly slab and a tiny piece of fish that made me feel pity instead of hunger.  I did not finish my food, it was too unappetizing, even though I was starved.  My desert was frozen solid and every time I tried to cut a piece of it with my spoon, it slid off the piece of white sugary lard and banged with a loud noise into my plate.  So if you enjoy making ice sculptures, this might be your kind of thing. I did not care at all for my date's desert. Even the complimentary white bread was stale and possibly refrigerated prior to serving.  All in all - bad food.  Preparation took an unreasonably long time, I estimate we waited at least 20 minutes for the smoked fish and the salad and at least 40 minutes after we finished appetizers for entrees. They get a star for decent service and an interesting aquavit menu.  Ambiance was a bit depressing - they sport the whole socialist minimalism decor which makes you feel like you are having lunch in a government cafeteria back in 1975. Ok, I wasn't around then, but if I had to use my imagination, that's exactly what it would look like.  The kitchen noise was audible every time a door near us opened which kind of killed any chance at romantic atmosphere.  Remarkably enough, I had dinner here two years ago and I have absolutely no recollection of anything I had, which should have been a red flag to begin with. The total bill for two was about $130 with tip and a couple of drinks, thus in conclusion this place is ridiculously overpriced considering the subpar experience we had.

I've been to Aquavit twice now, each time for one of their special smorgasbords.  I highly recommend aiming for one of these events, especially if you want to get a slightly higher return on your substantial investment.

The first time I visited, I managed to stumble upon their herring festival.  Now I've grown up eating all kinds of herring for various occasions with my Scandanavian family, but this was so much better and fresher I can barely draw a comparison.  There were about twenty herring options - my personal favorites were the Matjes and the mustard varieties.  They also had fare that I understand to be standard for weekend brunch, all of which was excellent and is detailed in other reviews.  But if you love herring, this is THE time to go to Aquavit.  (And please pair some with the white cranberry aquavit - it is the best I have ever had.)

For my second visit, my father treated our family to the Julbord during the Christmas season as a way to thank us for hosting this year's festivities.  I'm now planning on hosting the next twenty years if the reciprocity continues.  The smorgasbord included the best of the herring offerings from my previous visit, but it also featured a wide variety of meats and fish that I hadn't seen the first time around.  The pate was fantastic, and the deviled eggs with caviar where the surprise hit.  I also really liked the mushroom cream soup - something I'm not used to seeing on smorgasbord lineups.  

The service both times was great, even though we wound up being the last table during the lunch seating each time (if you are a group of 6+ people, it seems to be difficult to get an early reservation).  They were even kind enough to set up a small desert table in the atrium just for us when they were switching the buffet area over in preparation for a holiday party.  When coupled with such outstanding food, it's this gracious service that will keep us coming back for special family occasions.

This was my first time to Aquavit, and certainly not my last.  I took my wife for lunch and we were blown away by how good the food was. The service is excellent. Our waiter Nate may have been the best waiter I have ever had.  This guy was a true professional. If you're thinking about it, take my advice and go.

I am shocked by some of the pointless comments I've read. Aquavit has not once let me down, granted, I've only been twice, but it is lovely. Lovely as far as atmosphere, excellent service, the pork belly is fabulous beyond compare, and the desserts are unlike any other restaurant in New York. 

Beautiful Swedish influences, without running wild with the menu. 

Highly recommended!

i was really excited to try scandinavian food, and i'm also a top chef watcher.

my friends and i ate in the dining room and did the prix fixe menu. here's the breakdown:

maine lobster: delicious. it came with a jus and i mopped up every bit.

pan-roasted pheasant: this was great but i almost wished i had tried something else.

arctic circle: i'm not much of a dessert person but this was great. not a fan of goat cheese either but when you eat this, you're not thinking "goat cheese parfait".

i don't typically eat in nice restaurants like this, so i wasn't used to the palate cleansers and other amuse bouches that came in between courses, but they were a pleasant surprise!

I ordered the lunch prix during NYC restaurant week. I had the Veal cheek blanquette, canterele veloute, and the hazelnut terrine. Everything thing was beautifully plated and tasted amazing. I also ordered a flight of aquavit. The wine pairing was also reasonable priced. The service was accommodating my date and I were a 1/2 hr late. We were seated right away. The booth was large for two people. I would definitely go back.
Wow. Spent a lot of money, but ended up eating a course of 8?9? Lost count. But ate for almost 2hrs! Best service. Amazing spin on scandinavian food.

Went to Aquavit for a late weekday lunch on a recent trip to NYC.  A comment from a colleague afterwards . . ."all the food there is really white (in color)".  True . . . but also really GOOD.

Food was superb (had excellent green salad, a barley risotto and shared a budapest cake), service was top-notch and the room is very beautiful in a spare, light wood, white light way.  Also, the wine recommendations were delicious and reasonably priced (the server offered two choices for each course).

Would definitely recommend it (for vegetarians as well)!

DELICIOUS!
My girlfriend and I went for restaurant week where you can try a 3 course meal (with optional wine), so we haven't had the full experience in the main dining hall.
But I was blown away by the great service, elegant dining room, and the food... my god the food was incredible.
I would also recommend classing it up a bit before dining there.

We will visit the main dining room as soon as we can afford it.

Delicious!

The setting is lovely and modern. The waiters were wonderful and professional and didn't even correct my awful pronunciation once. 

The food was amazing! The wild mushroom consumme was savory and full of barely goodness. The roasted pheasant had crispy skin and tender meat, plus delicious stuffing. 

A note about the dress: It's fancy in the dining room and slightly more relaxed in the front bistro. I want to strike "elegant casual" and "smart dressy" from the English language. You wanna be so specific about the dress (jackets preferred!) then just publish pictures of what you expect.

Oh precious 5 stars.  I give you away with SUBLIME memories of a perfect Saturday brunch at the Bar Room.

I don't even normally order eggs benedict because I can poach eggs myself at home.

But for only $15 the Eggs Norwegian was pure bliss.  Two perfectly poached eggs atop a crisp, buttery round of toast, generously heaped with high quality cold-smoked salmon (trust the Nordic to get that one right) and the most fragrant chervil hollandaise ever.  

I ate every bite, down to the last drop of sauce.

Many restaurants are guilty of heaping on sheer carbs in their brunch dishes because, well, it's little cost to them and it fills you up.  But the brunch dishes here are perfectly portioned with quality ingredients over quantity.  

Rest assured you'll be able to dine here and still fit into those clothes you're trying on at 5th Ave shopping afterwards.

I am an instant fan. From the apps, through the main dishes to the last drip of minimalistic coffee poured afterwards. I would have to go back a couple of more time to be able to actually say more about the food and the impeccable service in details. :)

This was my first experience with Scandinavian food. The staff was very helpful with menu selections.  There were many unfamiliar flavors, so it was exciting to try everything that came along. Overall, I enjoyed the food even if I wasn't always sure what I was eating.

The service was great and the atmosphere was perfect for a couple.

fig and cardamom aquavit = spicy and tasty!
cucumber aquavit = light and refreshing!
sipping 1 shot of each per person managed to knock me and my hard-drinking bf into a gentle pre-dinner buzz = A+

The mackerel with egg salad, mushroom consumme with poached quail egg and the perfectly cooked lamb entree were some of the most delicious and memorable dishes I have ever experienced.  

And the dessert.. oh.  I will lovingly slumber with thoughts of the espresso savarin and the banana mousse with walnut ice cream for years to come.

My absolute favorite? the creamy chanterelle soup with yogurt served with a mini brioche muffin. wow. double wow.

Only if you like Scandinavian food...

The ambiance is amazing, the service is impeccable and the food is of the highest quality, BUT the taste was just not for me.  I really enjoyed the experience and will always remember it, but next time I go, it will just be for the Aquavit's (flavored vodkas)

It was a birthday lunch celebration, and for my first time trying Scandinavian meal, I was quite excited.  Looking forward and settled in midtown east, and the surrounding was enjoyable to stroll down on Park Ave, I kept an open tummy to take in this full experienced. Beautiful setting and it was a crawfish feast luncheon they had offered.  Of course, being from California and we have plenty of live crawfish restaurant, and eaten in New Orleans; we decided on a 3 course.  We ordered 

HERRING TRIO three varieties of herring, vasterbotten cheese, fingerling potato
SWEDISH MEATBALLS potato purée, pickled cucumber, lingonberries, cream sauce
Beets, raw salmon corn chowder
Tomato and salmon'
ARCTIC CIRCLE goat cheese parfait, lingonberry "vargtass" sorbet, salted pistachios
BUDAPEST CAKE hazelnut praline mousse, chocolate ganache, orange supreme, vanilla ice cream
Chocolate mousse

Our meal was very colorful and enjoyable.  My favorite thing of the meal was our desserts.  We received an extra one for the birthday celebration.  Their desserts won me over, service was stable and in good time for lunch.

It wasn't the service, which was unfailingly polite and attentive, as befitting the reputation of the restaurant.  Nor was it the decor, which is impressively spacious and grand, and starkly modern.

It wasn't the price, which at $110 for a 7 course tasting menu - including 2 amuse bouche's, an intermezzo and petite fours - was more than fair.  Included in this price, was also a swab of spring onion infused whipped butter, which applied on the good hearty rye bread, was satisfying enough for a meal in itself.

It wasn't the presentation - Chef Marcus Jernmark's dishes were meticulously yet playfully plated.  Any shmoe who's picked up a knife or mandoline and attempted to hack away at an onion could appreciate the surgical precision that was necessary to perfectly brunois the onions and beets which went into a course of matjes herring.  

This is presentation at the Paul Liebrandt, Bill Telepan, Daniel Humm level playing field. "This is fucking whimsical" I reveled in a hushed voice as a beautifully presented and simply done farm egg was placed before us.  A house aged steak tartare was almost too pretty to eat - and indeed, I wish I hadn't, as the steak was off-putting - gummy, stringy and offensively funky from the aging process.

But what it was - a consistent imbalance of flavors.  Too heavy at times, like the clunky dish of cloying Prast cheese with fruit and nut bread.  Or the unbearably bland and oppressively opulent veal cheek blanquette.  The flavors of a  perfectly cooked scallop choucroute was stifled by an overwhelmingly strong side of sauerkraut.  

And at times, the flavors barely rose above a whisper.  The aforementioned Matjes herring could have been saved from mediocrity by a squeeze of lemon.  The salmon tartare, like that quiet weird kid that sits in the back of the classroom, could shine with a touch of salt and acid.

And at times, the food was flat out inedible, such as the aforementioned aged beef tartare - one of the egregious miscues i've ever tasted in my forays into fine dining.

Yes, Aquavit is a beautiful restaurant serving exquisite food, but as the saying goes - you'll not want to scratch the surface, for this beauty is only skin deep.

Yay, Aquavit was so good! My friend and I went for Saturday brunch, and it was such a great experience. I was a tiny bit nervous coming in because I had never had Scandinavian food before and I generally dislike brunch due to the huge food coma ingesting so much carbs always gives me. 

But Aquavit was perfect. Our waiter was this adorable skinny hipster with those huge non-prescription glasses. He was very soft-spoken and polite, helping explain the food to us Scandinavian neophytes and coming back  every once in a while to check up on us. The food itself was surprisingly delightful. To be honest, I don't expect very much from cuisines that originate north of Belgium, but I'm glad Aquavit helped prove my presumptions wrong. 

I ordered the waffle with vanilla ice cream and apple jam (I think that's what it was?) while my friend ordered the Swedish meatballs, and we had goat cheese croquettes to share. In addition, in accordance with the brunch special, we each had an elderflower mimosa. The croquettes were so, so good. I'm biased, because I love anything with goat cheese in it, but these were amazing. perfect crunchy texture on the outside, honey drizzled over, soft goat cheese - mmm. The waffle was fantastic as well. Not soft like the ones you'd get from an American pancake house, but crisp and toasted. The ice cream and jam went perfectly with it, and I savoured every single bite. And unlike the brunches I'm used to, this meal wasn't overfilling, which I was very happy about. 

In general - great service, great food, great atmosphere. The room was very well-lit and open, which is how a brunch place should be. The restaurant itself was part of a corporate-looking building, so the inside even looked a bit corporate, but I thought it worked. Highly recommended. The next time I'm back in NYC, I would definitely be interested in trying Aquavit again for lunch or dinner.

I went here for brunch with 2 girlfriends from out of town. I was really excited because I'm on a Scandinavian food kick lately. We needed to be in the area for an appt in the afternoon and there really isn't much fun stuff in midtown east.  We had a round outside of the bistro area. The bar area was nice, very modern and comfy. The drinks we had were really good (I'm always on the hunt for the most fantastic bloody mary and it came close). We moved into the "bistro" area. First of all, it's like eating in a cafeteria.  I wasn't impressed at all with the decor or the feel of the "bistro". We ordered the $18 brunch w/mimosa special. I had eggs Norwegian (poached eggs with smoked salmon). My eggs were so runny, it made me feel ill. I asked for toast to soak up the yolk at least. The waiter had the decency to be embarrassed when he said there was a charge. I said...that's okay. He then told me it was $12. For toast. Seriously? My friends meals were okay but nothing to write home about. Too bad because I was going to grab some friends to go back for the prix fix dinner menu. I'll stick to Smorga in the west village.

Flawless service. Atmosphere was a little stodgy -- but hey, I knew what I was getting myself into. I had really high expectations for the dishes, and I have to say, the kitche let me down. I'd take mom and dad, but probably won't go back.

Top notches again!  Who said the Scandinavians were cold?  Maybe, their fish, which was delightfully smoked and subtlety flavored.  Even their lamb was tasty.  The cuisines is on the simple and minimal side, yet, it works.  Service was in-line with their top ratings.  Staff was helpful and accommodating.

I really missed Scandinavian food, so I went here. Lucky for us, they had the all you can eat salmon & herring buffet for only $35. The service is top notch and the quality of food is world class. The salmon and herring dishes were delicious, Swedish style deviled eggs were awesome. I can't eat gluten, and they had no gluten free desserts, so they brought me sorbets instead (how nice of them!) the sorbets were amazing. I recommend making a reservation since it's a very popular place. Two thumbs up for the great service and food!

So, where you sit in the restaurant will significantly affect what you pay.  This confusing fact was brought to our attention when we reviewed our reservation.  If you are seated in the dining room, there are two tasting menus to choose from at $84/pp or $110/pp.  If you are seated in the still generally nice bistro, you can order a la carte or have a prix fixe menu at $35/pp.  Reviewing the menus, we noticed that many of the Scandinavian specialties were available in the bistro, and, further, the tasting menus in the dining room were pretty staid in selection and lacking in regional authenticity.  The choice was an easy one, so we changed our reservation from the dining room to the bistro.  

We decided to each have the 3-course prix-fixe at $35/pp and additionally ordered the herring sampler ($12) as an appetizer which was incidentally featured on the much more expensive tasting menu in the dining room.  Oddly, this appetizer was served as our second course, so I will give the rundown in the order in which we received the food:

First Course:  I chose the asparagus and leek soup over the mixed greens.  There was definitely leeks in this mostly watery, slightly creamy soup, but I could not pick up any asparagus at all.  The color was white too, which served to further highlight the missing ingredient.  Less than crunchy croutons were added, presumably for textural contrast, but the effect was lost.  They were probably swimming in my soup for too long.  Not the most auspicious of beginnings.  

Second Course:  Our appetizer consisting of three different herrings served with a lone fingerling potato and two triangles of vasterbotten cheese.  Said cheese was really delicious with a nuttiness that paired well with my Swedish pilsner.  Each herring portion was robust, and the three samples proved to be a lot of food for the two of us to work through.  Each portion was surprisingly tasty too.  The sour cream one was interesting, but I really took to the one enhanced with Dijon mustard.  There was a cuteness with the third selection involving bleak roe and a pearl onion.  A satisfying course throughout.  

Third Course:  We both opted for the Scandinavian bouillabaisse, insisting on making the meal as Scandinavian as possible.  How disappointing!  Another watery soup without any deep flavor.  The seafood wasn't cleaned very well either as I had no less than 3 moments where my teeth clamped down onto something crunchy and inedible.  The scallop looked well seared, but it lacked taste.  The mussels picked up no flavor at all and were a bit small.  Nothing worthwhile here at all.  

Fourth Course:  Kladdkaka.  While the first three courses came and went in a hurry, we waiting for nearly 40 minutes for this fourth course to show up.  We became really impatient, and couldn't understand the reason for the delay.  First we were rushed, and then we had to wait.  And for what?  A molten chocolate cake with a quenelle of ice cream, three sections of citrus, and three dots of citrus gelee?  Cruise food.  As staid as choices come.  

The service was really uneven beyond just the timing.  At one point a bus boy made a very quick motion to fill my mostly full glass of water and jerked the pitcher away in a hurry only to run off to another table.  I saw only the plop of an ice cube and he was gone.  How abrupt!  Nothing was explained when it was presented either, and no reason was given for the delay.  

Overall, charming dining room with a great view of the street, mostly lackluster food, and poor service.  And you can have it starting at $110/pp or $35/pp, the choice is yours.  I really couldn't recommend much here though, so I would pass all together on this madness.
Unique and delicious meal in a comfortable space with good service.  It doesn't get much better than this.  Can't wait to return to try the Swedish Meatball entree for lunch.

this review id for the bistro.
What a disappointment in every way!
The soup was served cold. A skin had formed on top from the cream. No sign of the asparagus it was supposed to taste like. I sent it back and got a green salad, which was fine but nothing special.
The herring appetizer was very nice.
Our wine came after we were almost done with appetizers.
The barley entree was so oily and salty, i had a few bites and let it sit.
The bouillabaisse was just creamy...no other flavors!
Would never go back! Yuk!
What a waste of money!

Have been here numerous times for special occasions.  Ambiance is great and food is perfect every time. 

Highly recommend the herring sampler with potato and a carlberg beer.  This is one of the few perfect dishes in the world. 

Fig and Cardamom Aquavit... oh yeah.

**CAFE REVIEW**

Although the menu has changed (albeit a little for the worse) over the years, the cafe/bistro is still on my short list as a favorite place to get a pseudo-fancy, well priced dinner.

I rarely order from the drink menu (I'm usually a beer and wine at dinner drinker), but their drinks list is great. The white cosmopolitan is deadly and a 'must' order for me whenever I go.

The schmorgasbord plate is my ideal meal at any restaurant, delectable bites of all the best on the menu. I miss the meatball, I miss when the potato and cheese were not one of the original nine bites, but sweet side additions, but this place still leaves me fulfilled.

For dessert, you can still ask nicely for the artic circle which is always a crowd pleaser (goat cheese parfait, with this amazing sorbet).

I'll agree that service can sometimes be a bit slow/spotty, but the servers at the restaurant have always been nothing short of great -- attentive, helpful, friendly.

I'm giving Aquavit 4 stars for food and atmosphere. For service they deserve 2 stars and even that might be too nice. The service was practicially non-existent during brunch. Our waitress spoke to us only to take our drink order and that was after we called her over. I'm not even sure I saw any waiters/waitresses talk to any of the parties in  the dining room.
My family and I went here for the smorgsabord, which is in the main dining room and is $48/person (w/ one beverage included). The food was very good. There were many different types of herring to try. If you do not like seafood (herring and salmon) then you won't be able to eat about half of the food served. There were some meat dishes - pork (very tender, my mom felt it practically melted in your mouth), sausage, and of course swedish meatballs (which I preferred w/o much of the sauce on them). I'd avoid taking any bread; most was very dry and even the delicious dill butter on the bread didn't help. For dessert there were small pastries, cookies, and fruit. The strawberry shortcake and banana bread were two of my favorites. I expected the banana bread to be dry because the regular bread wasso dry but it was very moist.

[dining room lunch review]

Man.  I was so excited to eat here.  May have done it wrong.

Misstep 1 - did not get any drinks.  At a place named after a drink.  shame on me.

Misstep 2 - ordered the herring degustation with the full knowledge that I have never truly enjoyed herring (my hopes were high).

That said, here is my review:

ATMOSPHERE: 5
This place is gorgeous.  Impeccably designed, clean, sleek, calm, fairly private and comfortable.  Downright pleasant place to be.

SERVICE: 4
Very attentive, polite, and even keel folks (though it was difficult to find someone when we needed the check).  Would have liked my plate of 6 herring preparations explained to me, especially when it seemed like our server spelled out everything else we ate.  My companion who made the reservation suspected the hostess of faking her Scandinavian accent.  True or not, I love that.

FOOD: 3.5
Agh.  The food!  I've never eaten Scandinavian food before (with the exception of my dad's preferred pickled herring on Ritz - does that count?).  So I was completely lost when it came to the menu.  I still get nauseous when I think about all that herring, but again, shame on me for ordering it.  Accompanying cheese wedge and fingerling potatoes were functional as palate cleansers, but the dish was just a lot for one person to process.  Octopus salad and Swedish Meatballs looked lovely, though I didn't try.  Cod entree was perfectly cooked with some nice asparagus and an undefined puree in a creamy fishy sauce and some (tasteless) raw grated horseradish.  SO rich.  Perhaps I would have benefitted from a sharp aquavit cocktail in this situation?  Other thing worth mentioning was the chive butter, served as a smear on a rock (yes, a rock).  couldn't really find a place for it on my already oversalted and overfatted palate, but dang.  that is tasty stuff.

PRICE: 3
It's...just too expensive.  For the loveliness of it all, I still have trouble getting behind a $50/person lunch (without drinks!).  Despite its class, Aquavit's food does not achieve the ecstasy that I expect a lunch of that price point to invoke.  At all.  

OVERALL: 4
Would be willing to give it another go, maybe at the bar or the bistro room, skip the herring, and prepare to drink.

Some people do not like Scandinavian food.  I am not one of those people.

I have wanted to go to Aquavit for quite some time.  I went to Copenhagen this past summer and when I had Smørrebrød for lunch, it was quite an experience for me.  You see, I am one of those people who inhales his food.  I usually make a plate of enchiladas disappear in about three minutes, and although i know it's kind of embarrassing, it's all I've ever done.  BUT, when I had Danish cuisine for the first time, with the first bite, I let the food tarry a while on my tongue.  It was strange.

AND THEN it hit me...when I eat spicy food, i can taste everything instantly.  That might be why DRINK Fra diavolo sauce rather than let it spend any time in my mouth.  I take, I taste, I swallow.  All gone.  Scandinavian food does not work that way.  The flavors are all very mild, but undeniably delightful.  They don't hit you like a ton of bricks.  You must invite them, allow them to appear, and allow yourself to recognize them.  No, this is not chicken tikka masala, but it's just white bread either.

I had mentioned to one or two of my friends a long time ago that I had a really strong desire to go to Aquavit.  Well, one thing led to another, and they INSISTED on taking me here for my birthday.  It should also be said that none of us have any money, so this was really an extraordinary gesture.

A few of us walked in and sat near the bar in the very heavy, yet sleek, furniture.  The special for the day was a flight of Aquavits with herring prepared three ways or something or another.  We chose to sample the horseradish, dill-coriander, and mango-chili-lime.  They were all really tasty and elegant.  As one of my friends remarked, the atmosphere of the whole place was "very civilized."

When we were seated, they brought out all this amazing bread and butter.  So i went into Dyson-mouth mode again.  Enough of that.  I had a midtown martini and the seared chatham cod.  The martini was refreshing and ethereal.  I ordered the cod because it's made with leeks and I love leeks.  The leek flavor was really pretty weak but the dish as a whole was just so rich and rewarding.  My friends had-if memory serves me right-Mussels, the Scottish Salmon Burger, Smorgasbord, and...and...memory fail.

But everything was good.

My friends are the best.  Thanks Karen S., Ben L., Ann L., Christina L, and Jami O!

Scandinavian Brunch buffet blew me away. 

Not sure how many plates of Pickled herring, Gravlax, Meatballs I had... Let's just say enough to give me a stomach ache later on that day. 

We had a couple of Aquavit shots as well. (One was the chili infused and had some serious  SPICE). They were ok.

This is one of the best meals I've ever had. We got the 7-course tasting menu, and while I don't really care for fish (except shellfish), I loved the smoked salmon, butter poached trout, and halibut with tomato plum sauce. I still daydream about that smoked salmon; it just melts in your mouth.
In addition to the fish, highlights were hay smoked sweetbreads, which were crispy and cooked to perfection, and the lamb that was done 3 ways: sliced with jus, dumpling on mustard greens, and sausage with mustard sauce.
We had opted to get the wine pairing, since it was a special birthday dinner, and they were NOT shy about the pours. These weren't little mini tastes, they really gave you a nice healthy glass with EACH course.
The service was professional, and the setting was elegant, but comfortable.

N.B.: Only a review of the Herring Festival.

One year ago, I went to Aquavit's annual "herring festival" and took careful notes on my cell phone about the myriad of herring preps on offer for my usual loquacious Yelp review. Then my phone deleted the note. So no review.

A year later, I returned, armed with an iPhone. No hiccups this time around:

Pickled ramp herring
Black currant herring
Creamy horseradish herring
Citrus dill herring
Tomato-vodka herring
Pickled rhubarb herring
Rollmops
Mustard herring
Glassblower herring
Matjes herring
Herring tart

This is one of those events where if a simple list of the choices doesn't compel you, forget about it. (cf., Yakitori Totto's menu). If you've never had pickled herring, Aquavit's celebration of it is probably not the place to start. You might just waste $38 on a foodstuff that is a distinctly acquired taste.

But if you *do* enjoy pickled herring, the smorgasbord is heart-stopping.

They didn't have my favorite prep from last year (one with sweet apple slices), but the ones on tap were more than satisfying. The mustard prep spared nothing in terms of sinus-clearing spice. The tomato-vodka one was smooth as silk. The citrus dill was creamy and balanced -- how Aquavit can manage to balance pickled herring at all is a minor miracle in itself.

Other amusements are also on offer. Reasonable Swedish meatballs are trumped by a pleasantly subtle hot-smoked brook trout, and both are overwhelmed by the best gravlax I've ever had (yes, including Russ & Daughters).  Two you'd-never-guess-they-contain-anchovy dishes are also great and additionally have phenomenal names: Jansson's Temptation (potato gratin) and Gentleman's Delight (egg salad)

Some desultory vegetation and indifferent breads round out the scene. Dessert mini-cookies are dry but tasty. Seriously, who cares? Mark your calendar for next year if the thought of all that herring turns you on. If you can't wait, you can check out Aquavit's famous brunch smorgasbord for your premium Scandinavian all-you-can-eat needs.

Probability of return within 1 year: well, 100% in exactly 1 year

Aquavit was our first stop during Restaurant Week, and for $35.00/person, it was a fantastic deal (their regular 3-course prix-fixe menu is $84.00).  The main dining room has a subdued grown-up ambiance.  Overhead speakers play jazz showtunes through a moderately dimmed space, and (on a late Monday night) the conversations were hushed.  The decor is simple and contemporary, though the wood paneling and muted color palette felt a little dated.

Perhaps my favorite part of the evening was the moment when our butter appeared, smeared atop a volcanic rock, and casually placed in the center of the table.  It was hard not to stare.  But then our trio of Scandinavian breads came by - a crunchy anise-seed cracker, a dense seeded brown bread, and a tender sourdough roll.  These sort of set the cultural mood and I felt prepped for a night of authentic Northern cuisine.

Our amuse was a gruyere cheese puff, very light, and the cheese, very subtle.  Then came my Matjes herring tartare, which was fantastic.  It was really more of a herring salad - the raw fish was mixed with sour cream and dill - around which tiny spoonfuls of minced cucumber, beets, sour cream, egg yolk, red onion and fresh bread crumbs were laid out for incorporation into the tartare.  Each bite was unique and intensely flavorful.  

The blackened perch was less exciting (I kept trying to ignore the flavor of carbon) but the warm new potato salad was amazing, especially when coated in the gravy-like brown butter sauce.  My meal finished with a plate of fresh berries, vanilla ice cream, and almond meringue.  Lovely!

Aquavit's quiet, mature atmosphere, excellent service and interesting, well-executed cuisine makes it a great spot for business meals, etc.  I'm not sure I'd return here for the everyday dinner after Restaurant Week.  Nevertheless, I'd love to track down other Scandinavian outposts in the city for more tasty, dill-laden cuisine.

Went there for restaurant week (lunch). Was originally seated in a puddle of water but one of the waiters kindly moved us to a more comfortable location promptly. Ordered the cedar smoked ham, duck confit, and local strawberries. Not a huge fan of the cedar smoked ham - probably because of the horseradish mustard...maybe I need to learn how to read. The duck was tasty, especially with the corn, cherries, and whatever greens they added and finally, the local strawberries were aesthetically pleasing and sweet along with the almond meringue.
Overall, pretty good but I definitely wouldn't pay the normal price.

RW Week Review

RW menu was good, a little small, but good.

The atmosphere is great. The presentation of the food is superb.

Matjes herring tartare was great (must have)

I'm not a big fan of duck, so that was out of question. I had the blackend perch... I was a little scared when it arrived as it looked like someone threw the thing in a volcano (think charred chicken). I was pleasantly surprised when I had a bite, very light flavor, really enjoyed it.

Dessert was ok, presentation great, but taste just ok.

Overall, this is the type of place I can see myself visiting for RW again, but not sure if I would go there for any other occasion, nothing jumped out at me that would make me return.

came here for restaurant week! ordered the matjes herring tartar, long island duck confit, and macerated stone fruits. friend ordered cedar smoked ham, blackened perch, and local strawberries.

herring tartar was good for the first half, but then it started tasting a bit too salty for my liking. i tried my friend's ham, and found it a lot more tasty than my tartar, and easier to eat, might i add... i had no idea how to eat the tartar, haha.

duck confit was cooked perfectly and was absolutely delicious. the perch was lovely too, and had a lighter flavor than the heavy duck. (yep, as you can tell, my friend and i nommed on each other's, hence why we got all different dishes :) ) still preferred the duck, though.

desserts were presented fancily, and were very good. i think the presentation at first caused me to declare it 'amazing' but on second thought, it was nothing too special.

overall, would return. they gave a $50 gift certificate for our next visit to the dining room!

I really wanted to like Aquavit. But the entree I ordered was a definite miss. My friend and I came here for restaurant week. The appetizers were not bad at all. The gazpacho was extremely refreshing and since I am a huge fan of cilantro and red onion, I enjoyed it. The herring wasn't bad either, but if I had known that the bread that's brought to the table comes with salmon mouse, I would not have ordered it. I thought the herring was ok- salty and fishy but in a good way. Now the entree... We both ordered the duck confit and it tasted a little too salty. The meat didn't taste fresh and didn't pair well with the corn that accompanied it. To be honest, it tasted like the salted duck my mom buys from Chinatown. The desserts also were not memorable (though that's to be expected).

It wasn't that the food was horrible, but we had high expectations. Our last visit for Restaurant Week was at David Burke Townhouse and everything from the food to the service was five star.

Went with 3 friends, to who are Swedish, to try Aquavit during summer restaurant week 2011. They had our reservation saved as 2 people instead of 4, so we had to wait half an hour for our table even though I called two days before to change the reservation number.  

I ordered the gazpacho, blackened perch, and the macerated stone fruits.  My friends order the cedar smoked ham, the eggplant dish, the duck, and the local strawberries.  The gazpacho had an interesting texture.  My Swedish friends both ordered the smoked ham and were quite happy with it, although they said the mustard was a little heavy.  The black perch met everyone's approval and the buttery, lemon sauce it came in was amazing.  The eggplant dish was a let down.  Besides the perch, I think the desserts won favorite course.  

Since we were eating at Aquavit, we decided to try the liquor Aquavit.  After waiting 20 minutes for the drink menu, we order the house fig and cardamon Aquavit and then two imported ones.  The fig and cardamon was my favorite, although my Swedish friends preferred the more traditional, imported ones.  

When the bill came, we gave them two credit cards.  They came back with a split bill for us to sign, the problem was that they ran our cards for some other tables bill.  It was cheaper for us, although I imagine the other table was not happy when they saw their cards charged with our bill.  

I would not recommend Aquavit because of their disorganization, unprofessionalism, and bad gazpacho.

Marcus Samuelsson is quite possibly my favorite "Top Chef Masters" contestant thus far.  That smile.  Those ears.  The accent.  What a cutie patootie.  Ever since he won Season 2, I've wanted to eat at Aquavit.  And though he has since left the restaurant to open his own in Harlem, my desire to try it hasn't waned.

A snafu with the website's online reservation system caused major complications with our booking...the details are tedious.  But I will say that because of the inconvenience, Aquavit's manager bent over backwards to make it up to us, ensuring our party of four was *extremely* well-taken-care-of, starting with a complementary Smörgåsbord and ending with complementary dessert.  The rest of the service we received at Aquavit was as superb and accommodating, a refreshing change from some of the brusque, gruff service we had elsewhere.

Right off I really liked the décor -- *very* Scandinavian with sleek lines, blonde woods, and light, cream tones.  Like IKEA's highly sophisticated older brother.

We started with cocktails.  Pops and I went with aquavit flights -- he's a sipping-liquor man, and I didn't fall far from the tree -- building our own with three selections from the restaurant's extensive house-made aquavit (a Scandinavian potato spirit, typically flavored with dill or caraway) list.  I had the grapefruit, coriander-dill, and mango-chili-lime, Pops the anise-caraway-fennel, horseradish, and juniper-lemon.  So smooth and delish.  Husband had an equally pleasing and lovely Aquavit No. 6 cocktail made with Pimm's Cup No. 1, cucumber aquavit, and ginger ale.  

Alongside the drinks arrived a slate tile with house bread -- crispbread and a tiny, soft wheat loaf -- and salmon-dill butter.  We also ordered the Steamed Mussels with roasted garlic, whey, oven-roasted tomato, parsley, and grilled bread.  I love mussels, but these were just okay: the sauce was flavorful, but the mussels were small and not as juicy as I like.  We also ordered a side of goat cheese croquettes to start, and they were absolutely wonderful: fried crisp with a soft, creamy filling and served with sticky, sweet thyme-honey.  The Smörgåsbord turned out to be surprise hit: fingerling potato, västerbotten cheese, gravlax with potato chips and hovmästar sauce, cold-smoked salmon with potato cake, sour cream, and red onion, crab skagen salad, dried beef with mushroom, herring terrine, and pickled herring.  I'm not big on "fishy" fish, so the herring wasn't my favorite, but I loved the cheese, the cold-smoked salmon, and the crab skagen.

For entrées four of us sampled:

Scandinavian Bouillabaisse with cod, scallops, shrimp, mussels, and parsley aioli.  It was rich and savory, but really stingy with the scallop (there was *half* of one) and shrimp.

Seared Chatham Cod with potato and leek stomp, grilled asparagus, shaved horseradish, white asparagus beurre blanc.  This was my pick, and it was excellent, with crisped skin and stomp smooth as silk.

New Jersey Sweet Corn Barley and sugar snap peas, goat cheese, and summer truffle vinaigrette.  I mocked husband when he ordered this, but I had to eat my words after one bite.  Resembling Scandinavian risotto, this might have been the best dish of the evening.

Moms ordered the Penobscot Chicken Schnitzel with summer squash gratin and chervil yogurt.  Diners absolutely loved the tender, juicy cutlet coated in the lightest, crunchiest coating of crumb.  But the squash gratin was heavy, dry, and flat.

The last surprise of the evening was the arrival of the "Arctic Eggs" for dessert: goat cheese ice cream -- shaped like little bird's eggs, filled with sea buckthorn fruit, and dipped in white chocolate -- sugar spun to look like downy feathers, crispy, thin milk chocolate cookies resembling a twig nest, and blueberries.  Quite possibly the most adorable dessert I've ever seen.  The goat cheese ice cream was tangy, creamy perfection.  

All in all, a great experience at Aquavit.  With food and customer service like that, tho, who could argue?

[15 Minutes of Fame: "Chopped: Chop on Through", Sous Chef Elise Kornack]

Maybe Marcus Samuelsson has become too busy with his new restaurant, The Red Rooster, but what a major decline here at Aquavit.  This had been such a favorite of ours for many years and we have been several times both to its original location and this one.  It had been a while since we had been back and we were all looking forward to the same great service we had experienced in the past.

Unfortunately, not to be.  The food itself is still quite good and we were not disappointed by anything that anyone in our group ordered.  But at a restaurant of this caliber and with prices too match, one is going for more than just the food and the overall experience was very disappointing.

Overall, the service was pretty bad. From the woman who checked us in upon entry who could barely say a word or crack a welcoming smile, to the waiter who took forever to take drink and food orders and rarely returned to the table to check on anything, it was very unpleasant. The restaurant itself was quite hot and uncomfortable and when mentioned to the waiter he shrugged and basically said, well it's summer and it's hot outside. We had to ask other servers several times repeatedly just to get him to come back with our wine. We were not doing a tasting menu or purposefully lingering, and yet this long torturous dinner lasted almost three hours!

I must preface this review by stating that I went to Aquavit during Restaurant Week, a week during which restaurants put away their most inventive and/or best known dishes in order to please everyone and still make money. The Swedish meatballs that Aquavit is known for? Nowhere to be found. The salmon? Not available.

While I can't gush about the food or service, I still had a nice dinner. The service was fine and the meal was enjoyable.

Appetizer: I couldn't finish my herring tartar but my friend loved it. It was probably great, but for someone who doesn't love seafood, probably too strong of a taste. 

Main course:  I thought the duck confit was prepared exactly as it should-covered in fat. The blackened perch, though, disappointed.

Dessert: Alright. Fruit and almond meringue or panna cotta. Eh.

The only course I really loved was the duck. Can't say I would recommend that any of my friends go here, at least not during restaurant week, considering the price.
So good.  Go for restaurant week or its pricy, but thats expected.  Great selection.  The duck confit with cherry jus... wow!

Went with a friend for Restaurant Week. The place definitely gets a 5/5 for decor and service alone; it was beautiful inside (somehow invoking Scandinavia without me knowing any direct references, also very spacious-feeling) and the wait staff were on top of things without being pushy. The food itself definitely fell more on the "unique" side of things. The herring tartar we got for an appetizer was amazing, and the cured ham (with a little forest of vegetables on top) was a close second. The blackened perch was actually somewhat light, unlike the roast duck which was fairly rich. Both desserts (fresh strawberry platter and the stone fruit platter) had great combinations of things and we couldn't decide which we liked better!

This definitely has the look and feel of a "fancy" restaurant. I'm not sure if I would come back for the full price experience unless it was a very special occasion, but I'm fairly glad I tried it.

My husband and I visited Aquavit as  part of the Summer 2011 restaurant week. At the end of the diner with got gift certificates for $50 off our next meal, which was a pleasant surprise. And, considering that Craw Fish Festival is coming up, we may be back.

We liked the atmosphere probably the most. The restaurant's dining room was rather quiet, in spite being filled to capacity, and decor was very Swedish chateau-like. Our server was very nice and when i mentioned that I am a big fan of Riesling, he walked me through the restaurant's selection and helped me choose the wine to accompany my meal. We liked the breads, the cheese puffs compliments of the chef and the interesting way the butter was presented - on top of a black rock (though, it melted and escaped to the table, so perhaps rock should still be positioned on some kind of a coaster?). My husband had the herring appetizer and did enjoy it, though when I tried a bit it was too strong of a fish taste for me. The herring appetizer seemed very similar to the Russian "shuba" (fur-coat) dish, only all of the same ingredients were scattered over the plate, separately. If I could suggest to the chef to try grating the ingredients, except herring - as it was already cut into the small pieces- and layering them on top of each other, I would. The outcome would certainly be better - less "fishy" and more textured.

My smoked-ham appetizer was good, but mustard really "blocked" all other ingredients of the dish (carrots, pickled cucumbers, ham itself), so if I could suggest to the chef to go easier on the mustard, I would.

For entrees my husband had the perch and I had the duck confit. Interestingly enough, the duck dish also reminded me of "apple-stuffed duck" - I traditional Russian dish. Only, apples were grated and not stuffed inside the duck :). It was served with barley, which was really well done, and overall the dish was very rich. The perch, which I tasted from my husband's fork, was very light, and overall we'd rate the dish as 'ok' (perhaps more potatoes in the dish would have done the trick? not sure). Both appetizers were berry-esques and I have nothing bad to say about them. My Earl Grey tea, freshly brewed in a small white pot, was excellent.

Again, our experience was very positive and we do want to come back for a craw fish festival and check out the Bistro. I took a pick at it on our way out and it seemed a little more loud than the main dining room with a slightly younger crowd.

I went to Aquavit with my girlfriend and two friends during restaurant week.  We each ordered from the restaurant week menu, which offered a three course meal for $35.  Although we didn't feel like sampling the aquavits, we did order a nice bottle of Bordeaux for under $40.  I would say that's a pretty good deal for a restaurant of Aquavit's caliber.

The decor is really nice in the restaurant: It has a 1970s Swedish minimalism quality (think sleak hard woods and sharp angles).  Additionally, they serve the butter for the bread on a volcanic rock, which is somewhat pretentious but I thought it was unique and fit the ambiance.

I had some sort of ham and vegetables with mustard appetizer.  My description, although apt, does not do the dish justice.  The flavors were all very harmonic, simple and delicious.  My main course was a duck confit with cherries and some sort of risotto-like carb.  It was fantastic.  The duck was cooked very nicely, and the flavors paired nicely.  Finally, dessert was utterly fantastic.  I had mascerated stone fruits (plums and nectarines) with a subtle fruit gelatin and long pepper ice cream.  Each simple part of the dessert combined with the others to create a synergy of transcendent flavor.  

Honestly, it was an amazing experience.

I would give the place an honest 4.5 stars.  My policy is that I round up or down half-stars for Yelp, depending on soft factors.  Since the tasting menus typically start around $80-120 per person, I am going to give Aquavit 4 stars.  Although everything was amazing, I am not sure it would be worth that loot.  If money is not an issue, I would definitely recommend this place.

I went here to end my tour of the July 2011 NYC Restaurant with high expectation and was nothing less than impressed. 

The decor, the service
and The Food was amazing. 

I highly recommend that you try the Duck Confit here. I've had duck confit elsewhere but this one was pretty high up there on the list of great ones. I also had the green tomato gazpacho which was has refreshing taste that was perfect balanced in flavor and texture. 

For dessert the wild berries and cream was a treat, the cubed sugar for my coffee  was a nice touch, and I must admit I am a sucker for well plated food composition.

I will not only return, I would highly recommend this place to anyone seeking to treat someone to a bite of elegance and flavor that they will savor.

I hover between a 3 and a 4 on this one but I'm going in for a 4 because overall this is a good restaurant. 

My friends and I dined in the Bistro which I really loved for its minimalist Scandinavian decor, like an upscale sophisticated Ikea. And of course, like Ikea, I wanted to have the Swedish meatballs. They were good... not breahtaking or memorable. I'll be dreaming about the veal meatballs at Ciano for years, but these didn't stand out. I also had the arctic eggs, which were good but I actually think not goat-cheesy enough. The flavor was a bit too mild. I think my favorite part might be the bread course, I really enjoyed the mini loaf with a little pot of some kind of tartare on the side. 

Service was excellent, and overall I had a good experience. I think that it's gotten a little too comfortable food-wise and could use some re-energizing.

Yup, restaurant week visitor here, and couldn't be happier with the menu or service, and we arrived for lunch in the middle of the rush. I had the tasty herring tartar, served like a painter's palette with dollops of color and texture, followed by the delectable duck confit and the refreshing berries and ice cream. I also tried several aquavits for the first time--a little too much like Jaegermeister for my liking, but it rounded out the experience. I'd long been wanting to try Aquavit--the restaurant week deal was the perfect opportunity.

This was definitely the WORST dining experience I have ever had. And I'm trying really hard not to be mean. You can tell this restaurant really really wants to be Michelin rated. But there are many reasons why it is not and will not be.

So many things wrong with this place, where do I even start? I'll start with the food, since I know people will have different service experiences.

Though we came here during restaurant week, my dining partner and I ordered from the regular prix fixe menu. The food was H.O.R.R.I.B.L.E.

For drinks, we ordered two flights of three samplers of their aquavit. And our waiter got our order wrong. But more on that later.

Let's just say the best part of the meal was the bread, hands down. And mostly because the butter came on a volcanic rock.

Appetizers: We started off with the Herring Degustation, which was interesting, but ultimately many of their varieties tasted the same. The Hudson Valley Foie Gras was disgustingly dry.

Entrees: I had the Roasted Porcelet Pork Shoulder. It was served in a pool of grease and basically inedible. It was also around 80% fat, and not the good kind of fat, and obviously overcooked. My dining partner ordered the Nordic Choucroute (lobster, scallops), which came in a nauseatingly overly creamy sauce. The lobster was tasteless and overcooked and the scallops were so rubbery you could practically bounce them off the floor. On top of that, both of our dishes were lukewarm/bordering on cold when they were finally served. I had one bite of my entree - that was literally all I could take. My dining partner beat me with maybe two or three bites.

Dessert: I ordered the Local Fresh Berries. This was the first time I have encountered a rhubarb dish I do not like, and I love rhubarb (I scour the farmers market for rhubarb when it's in season). My friend had the Strawberry and Meringue, which was dry.

Given the above, it's hard to believe, but the service was even worse than the food.

Our waiter was completely incompetent. Despite not hearing our orders and making us repeat multiple times (and if you know me, you know I am not a quiet girl), he still brought us the wrong drinks. He was exceptionally haughty and horribly remiss in both bringing out the food and clearing our plates. Our plates were never cleared in a timely manner, and when they were finally cleared, we still had to wait longer for the food. We sat with our napkins in our entree plates in front of us for at least 30 minutes, and the dining area was not even full.

Dinner ended up being an almost three hour ordeal. For three courses. When we barely ate the food. And we are both fast eaters. Absolutely ridiculous.

Beyond that, our waiter never even asked us how we were doing and how our food was. In addition, the restaurant manager was nowhere to be found throughout the night. We had to specifically ask for her. When she came, the first thing she asked was whether we had the RW menu or the regular menu. We answered regular, but were a bit taken aback. Why does it matter which menu we had? Bad service and bad food are unacceptable no matter if we just had an appetizer or if we had one of every dish on the menu.

We specifically told her we didn't want anything, but we just had to comment on the exceptionally bad service (we didn't even mention the bad food). I saw her pull our waiter away to talk to him, and after that, he completely ignored us for the rest of the night and never came around to apologize. Absolutely unacceptable. I am honestly disgusted by the service.

With our bill, we noticed the restaurant manager had comped our drinks. Another waiter handed us each a $50 certificate off the next visit, which they were giving to everybody. I had to exert a lot of self-control to not laugh in his face. Needless to say, we left the vouchers on the table when we left.

No self-respecting restaurant needs to bribe customers with $50 off to come back. Seriously. And besides, there is absolutely nothing that could compel me to return to this horrible establishment. Not even if they were handing out gold and granting free wishes. Nothing.

I would wish this hellish ordeal on nobody. Please save your money for somewhere else, anywhere else.

Oh don't hate me - I am NOT being too critcal with my review for this place.

Under the recommendation of a friend - I decided to take my boyfriend out for his first restaurant week experience.  Nice decor and I must say the lounge area was very interesting.  But with reservations at 9pm, we had arrived early at 8:50pm and were not seated until 9:20pm.  30 minute wait?  Seriously?  SMH.

The overall dinner experience wasn't fantastic but it wasn't horrible.  Our courses were served very timely.  

Appetizers were wayyyy too salty for our taste.  My boyfriend eats EVERYTHING like a vaccum and somehow he managed to stay clear away from eating my Herring Tartar which was - not our taste.  His Cedar Ham tasted like a Cubano - with no bread.  EHH.  

Entrees were amazing though so it definitely lifted my mood.  I had the blackend perch as my friend recommended was good with the buttery sauce and OH.MY.GAWD. - the potatoes were so delicious.  My boyfriend had the duck confit which was pretty good as well!  I was definitely happier by the end of that course.

Desserts - we both had the macerated stone fruits.  He loved it and I was so-so about it.  Maybe because I expected dessert to be sweeter than it was...maybe I just like sweet things...should go judge for yourself since there's only 2 options to chose from.

I really wish I had a good experience to agree with what my friend had said about this restaurant but overall I know, "Meh.  I've experienced better," as those 2 stars really indicate.  I'm just saying...

My family and I have been here several times, and my mom loves this place,
Since she was born in Sweden and Stockholm, myself, I think the food is very good,
great place, maybe a bit expensive but sometimes you have to pamper themselves.

Try some Swedish food, you will like it

I would have given 5 stars if not for two things.  First, there was an assistant waiter (for lack of a better term) who kept pacing back and forth around the area we were seated in and kept staring at us with a stone faced expression.  It was creepy and unsettling to say the least.  Second, the Swedish meatballs were not perfection. That might sound harsh but unfortunately with this being the only Scandanavian restaurant I've been to stateside, my expectations were high.

That being said, the house smoked salmon that was served chilled with a grainy mustard was phenomenal.  It was one of the most extraordinary bites of food I have ever had.  The fried goat cheese balls served warm with thyme infused honey was heavenly in its own right and I would go back just for that.  Amazing!

This review is of the bistro. The cocktails were excellent - we had the Manhattan and the Midtown Martini. Started with the swedish smorgasbord, which is a nice way to sample a bunch of things. Really liked the mustard herring. I got the restaurant week prix fixe (which is available to September 5, 2011) which seemed like a good value. The herring tartar was good and the scandinavian bouillabaisse was excellent, really good broth. Also loved the dessert, with panna cotta, stone fruits, and chocolate muesli. The flavor profiles of every dish were good, maybe a bit heavy on salt and certainly rich and creamy. Wouldn't eat here too often if I lived in NY, but it was a fun experience and would definitely recommend it.

This is absolutely one of the top 5 restaurant I have ever eaten at. Marcus Samuelsson is an absolutely incredible chef and you have to wonder where he comes up with some of his inventive gastronomical creations (just take a look at the Kobe beef dumplings with truffle tea). He apparently went from runway model to celebrity chef; this seeming non sequitur was a gift to anyone who enjoys incredible food. I have to admit that although the regular dinner menu is mind-blowing, when they have restaurant week specials, I was much less impressed with the café portion of the meal. Be prepared to spend for good food. Note that I am not rating the café in this review, which would merit a much lesser rating. This is for the regular dinner section of the restaurant.

Good Lord, there's a lot of Scandinavian restaurants in NYC nowadays.  Back when I went to Aquavit, years back, I remember going there for brunch, discovering that they didn't have brunch, and eating a fish & meatball filled lunch instead.  

It was a $55pp lunch, and it was A-ok. 

What I didn't like as much was the decor, which must have been based off  a 1960's person's imaginings of the future.

I came here for a business meeting.  Thank goodness the business meeting was extremely interesting, because the food certainly did not justify the prices and elegant venue.  I ordered off of the restaurant week menu.  I started off with the gazpacho, and it was my first time every having gazpacho.  This was pretty delicious--and cooled me down from the summer heat, but because it was my first time, I really did not have a dummy in which to compare it to.  Of course, the one I had at my business meeting the next day really blew me away, so I guess Aquavit gazpacho got a little downgrade there.  Just like our national debt.

I then ordered the summer squash gratin, which consisted of patty pans, smoked cremini, and chervil yogurt for my main dish.  While the dish tasted good, it was nothing special.  Personally I thought it was too lightly seasoned, and the food tasted as if it had been made in a rush; the spices were not perfectly marinated into the food; they had not penetrated through to truly form a complete flavor.  For my sodium and flavor loving tongue (bring on the salt and MSG!), it was too little to satisfy my cravings for tasty food.
