I finished off the meal with local strawberries, which included tarragon, almond meringue, and vanilla ice cream.  That was honestly the best part of my meal, because the strawberries tasted so fresh, and were perfectly complemented with the tarragon and almond meringue (and little buttery shortcake pieces).  The ice-cream was pure and delicious.  One of my favorite dessert dishes, probably because it scores high on the cost-benefit analysis scale of taste and healthiness.  Especially for dessert.

This review is of the Bistro. My friends and I were here both during the herring festival and crayfish festival. The food was good and the atmosphere relaxed. I'm sure the actual dining room merits its 4-5 star ratings, but the bistro doesn't. The food was good and consistent both times, and the service was friendly and attentive, but overall I was underwhelmed.

You know it's really good when you think and rave about it days after.

I came here for lunch on restaurant week on a warm summer day.  Service is top-notch.  Ambience is minimalist and relaxing and fairly quiet.  Food is amazing.  I had the apple gaspacho soup and a white fish with potatoes.  My friend had the duck which was pretty good.  Dessert is what I kept thinking about - Stone Fruit.  I don't know what it was or how it was made, but it was a very unusual combination of flavors.  Highly recommend the place.  I would definitely go back for another restaurant week.

Went for restaurant week summer 2011. 
It was really good. the appetizer, main and dessert was all very good portion. Least favorite out of three courses was dessert. but nevertheless, it's definitely worth checking out.

I went here for lunch and was only slightly impressed with the quality of the food.  I have fonder memories of the restaurant, and had eaten here twice before, but I believe Aquavit has changed executive chefs recently, and it shows.  

I ordered the herring trio to start and I gotta say - that was amazing.  I never thought I'd like herring but Aquavit has converted me.  The herring was fresh, so flavorful, and the accompanying cheese was sooooo good.  I'd order this every single time I come back to the restaurant.  

For an entree, I had the Swedish meatballs.  It truly pains me to say this and I know I might be sacrificing some credibility here, but I prefer the Swedish meatballs at Ikea.  The meatballs were dry and not very flavorful, the potato puree was runny.  The pickled cucumbers were unimpressive.  They were basically salted and peppered and then doused in some sort of watery liquid.  I'm a sucker for lingonberries though, and the lingonberry compote was on point.  

For dessert, I had the chocolate cake with dulce de leche cream and "citrus salad."  First of all, the citrus salad comprised solely 3 tiny slivers of grapefruit, orange, and some unidentified citrus.  So disappointing.  The dulce de leche cream was ok - the consistency was good, but the flavor was not really there.  The chocolate cake was tasty, but it was nothing more special than a warm brownie from any other bakery.  

The service was ok, nothing spectaular.  I guess that was the theme of the meal - ok, nothing spectacular.  I just expected more.  I may go back just for the herring though!

To be honest, when we first looked at the menu, it looked like we were going to be eating in a fancy Ikea cafe (Swedish meatballs)--but we were so wrong.  The salmon burger was fantastic and way better than we expected--and not pricy for Manhattan.  Awesome meal and place.

Came here for brother's 21st bday and had the tasting menu with paired wines. One of the best meals of my life--every dish was spot on. If you like bourbon, try the "Madison Ave Manhattan," which would make even James Bond jealous.

We went to that restaurant as a party of 6 for new year's eve back in 2005. While I personnaly could adapt to the starter all other guest just found everything self-indulging arrogant and just lacking of any taste. I must admit that come the trout with parmigiano pourred with broth I could but agree with them. Champagne served at the end was just . an insult

I came here with friends for the crayfish dinner
and none of us left feeling any thinner.
The food was tasty, drinks were good-
though we spent more than we probably should.
I was with a true Swede who said the menu was off
but it tasted great, and was fun- tip top!

BLOWN AWAY.

We've been on a fine dining binge recently to celebrate our wedding, going from Daniel to Le Bern to Gordon Ramsey and the like (all restaurants which never disappoint), but it was Aquavit that has recently topped our list as the tasting menu that unexpectedly blew the others out of the water!  Everything was so inventive, with an excellent melding of familiar and unusual flavors, presented through meticulous and artful plating.  The quality of the ingredients was awesome (and included the best langoustine we've ever had).  The portion sizes on the chef's menu may seem quite small at first, but with 2 amuse-bouches, 2 intermezzos, and mignardises to end, we were quite full by the end of the evening.  And the housemade selection of aquavits are to-die for.  We are looking forward to returning soon with friends!
I don't visit NYC over a Sunday without making time for brunch here. Scandiavian fare and flair. Will make a herring junkie out of you.

Great food and great service. The Sunday brunch, if it's still the same - is phenomenal.

I have to say, I really miss the old location on West 54th Street - I went there for Sunday brunch back in 2001 in the beautiful atrium, and it's a meal I haven't forgotten.  I remember the meal so vividly, and definitely ingrained the name Aquavit in my memory.

I was really happy to go back to Aquavit for dinner at this location two years ago, but wasn't quite the same as I had remembered it (at their old location) - which is why I'm giving it 4 stars. I would give 5 stars for their Sunday brunch.

Went here on a business lunch a while ago and was rather disappointed after hearing so many good things about this place.

First of all, the service was unbelievably slow. We were only small group, and it was after the main lunchtime rush, so perhaps the staff was tired or out for their own lunch break, but we waited literally (I counted) an hour for our food to be served.

The appetizers were delicious, especially the herring trio. But my main course was terrible--lukewarm fish is NEVER a good thing! Worst of all, the sea urchin roe was NOT fresh. Good sea urchin should taste salty-sweet and remind you of sunshine and wind and freedom. Bad sea urchin tastes bitter and foul and calls to mind an actual dirty, unwashed urchin who's been rolling in the muck at low tide. The sea urchin in my dish at Aquavit sadly fell into the latter category and was pretty much inedible. 

Dessert, at least, was delicious--some kind of very rich chocolate cake. Wonderful. But even that couldn't get the taste of rotten sea urchin out of my mouth, and the slow service on top of it all left us feeling less than satisfied.

Solid all around. The herring trio appetizer wins points for originality, although only the mustard preparation really worked (I'm not sure I really want my herring in cheesecake form). The signature meatballs were a winner and very seasonal - eating the meat, lingonberries and potatoes in a single bit felt very Thanksgiving-ish. The aquavits are fun, but somewhat pricey ($7 for a tiny shot) and of varied quality - fig and cardamom is the way to go. Service was a nice balance of attentive without being overbearing. 

Why just three stars then? Nothing really popped flavor-wise. This may be due to the inherent limitations of Scandinavian cuisine, but overall I want a bit more from a dining experience at this price point. The interior is also a bit stuffy and Ikea-ish for my taste. 

The less formal, more affordable bistro is definitely the way to go here. Not sure this place is worth more of a fuss or more $.

Without a doubt, one of absolute best meals I've ever had. 

I've been here twice now -- the first time was for the sadly-now-gone Smorgasbord brunch. Won't reminisce about it, but the selection of herring was truly phenomenal, and such a great deal at $48 pp. 

So on to dinner! My boyfriend brought me for a meal in the dining room last week; he hadn't been before and was curious to try Scandinavian food. More than certain the experience will have him hunting down more Swedish/Nordish/Danish/Finnish places in the city. 

Amuse-bouche was an adorable jar of celery cream soup with a delicate fillet of smoked salmon. We were offered a selection of three breads -- note, that means we got each of the different breads: a remarkably chewy/soft/dense/perfect dinner roll, a dry rye (?) cracker, and a dense, nutty brown bread. Loved them all. 

I could write a book about our entrees, so I'll just keep this short and useful by listing our favorites: DEFINITELY get the arctic char pot au feu (the uni cream is out of this world and you'll never experience eating seafood the same way again), the herring appetizer for the first course was scrumptious, and the rose hip soup for dessert. Sounds weird, I know, but the rose flavor is sweet and subtle, and I couldn't stop stealing my boyfriend's almond crunch ice cream -- after all, if I didn't eat it, it'd melt in the soup!

Service was a little stiff at first, but the waiters warmed up to us by the end of the meal -- like getting to know a new friend!

Initially, the difference between the old, familiar Aquavit and the hyperstylized, postmillennial version is a little jarring. The entrance to the restaurant's quarters resembles a bleakly modernist public square on the outskirts of, say, Göteborg, replete with scraggly trees and rows of abandoned marble benches. 

Inside, the bar has been greatly expanded into a long lounge area, where you can twirl about in high-backed chairs. The restaurant's homemade aquavits used to be stored behind the bar; now they're displayed along the wall, like pieces of art, in luminous square tankards. The dining room is small, even claustrophobic, by the standards of the grandiose old space, but the café, once part of the bar, now has a room of its own, appointed with simple butcher-block tables, pendulous sixties-era chandeliers, and orange cone chairs of the type you might see in the executive lounge of an excessively posh Scandinavian airline. Once you've adjusted to this new aesthetic, however, the food at Aquavit continues to be excellent; in fact, it's arguably better than before. After the departure of chef Marcus Samuelsson in April of 2010, former executive sous chef Marcus Jernmark is in the kitchen, making classic Scandinavian preparations like herring, gravlax, and contemporary twists like venison tartare.

HIghly recommend it to take clients or just because... GO!

Amazing!  Easily one of the top 3 meals I've ever had.  An incredible selection of flavors, textures and techniques.  This was my first Nordic meal and I was not quite sure what to expect.  My guest and I were completely blown away by the food, every single bite was basically perfect.  Deep layers of flavor, complex food without being to fussy.  Had a brief conversation with the chef at our table, he explained that they did not want the food to be to rich, but they wanted the flavors to be strong.  I'd say they achieved that perfectly.  We enjoyed this meal better than a few multi-stared Michelin places in Manhattan, i cant speak highly enough of this food and the place in general.  The tasting course was filled with lots of delicious, elegant ingredients like uni, truffles (multiple times), oysters and goat cheese, as well as some funkier ingredients that were as tasty like veal sweetbreads and herring.  They bread they serve is different and they each complement each other very well, heavy and light, soft and crunchy.

The meal started out with 3 amuse bouches, Goat Cheese pops with pumpernickel crumbs and a bit of truffles, excellent pungent, bright start to the meal.  An oyster cooked in I believe apple juice, with small tapioca style pearls, another great bite.  The last was one of the best bites i've ever had, a small cup of their smoked salmon, pickled cauliflower and a smokey truffle emulsion.  Incredible mix of crunchy, bright, vinegary cauliflower with deep, smokey, oily salmon, and a thick, rich base to bring it together.  Perfect food!

The first course was herring, my first time having it, but it is something I'll order it again for sure.  The dish was elegant, the fish was not oily, fishy or salty and was matched perfectly by the brown butter (foam?) and little potatoes.  The second course was bay scallops, another excellent dish.  Great texture from the crunchy slivers of the dark bread, thinly sliced radishes and other veggies.  The scallops themselves were deliciously sweet, and not overpowered by anything.

Course 3, a contender for the best of the night was an incredible mix of perfectly cooked sweet baby root vegetables with small crispy on the outside, juicy in the middle rounds of veal sweetbread, overflowing with black truffles shavings, outstanding dish!  Course 4, another winner, was the Nordic Seafood Pot Au Feu.  On my request and without any problem, they substituted this dish for the Cod dish that is usually on the tasting menu.  Delicious, delicate soft fish with a think and silky, deep rich uni emulsion, shrimp and a few more tapioca style pearls.  

There was a pallet cleanser of cucumber and lemon juice with sherbet, wonderful clean, cold, sip.  The 5th course, the entree, was a tie for the best plate, the pork shoulder with heirloom apples, brousel sprouts (the only bite of the meal I did not personally enjoy) and a truffle sauce that coated our tongues and the plate like paint, which was playful and incredibly flavorful.  Amazing pork dish!  The 6th course, a cheese, fruit and sorbet, was a great mix of temperature, flavor, and texture with the crunchy bread again.  We loved the strong funky cheese.  Next was a sweet intermezzo, a small jar of cold berry soup with huckleberries and a yogurt foam.  The final 7th course, the dessert, was a playful presentation of an egg in a basket, which was actual goat cheese with a milk chocolate coating.  Beautifully designed and equally delicious, perfect ending to the meal, not to heavy or rich.  Next up, the petit fours and a few small doughnuts with a caramel sauce.  The doughnuts were ok, but the petit fours were excellent including both a macaroon and a Macaron, which i though was clever.

Expensive but with every penny, 7 courses and about 7 small additional bites/plates plus amazing bread.  The food is playful and incredibly tasty.  Great attentive, friendly service.  They did not rush us, and the ambiance is relaxed and warm.  I cannot wait to return!
Nice tasting menu... unique space for dining, however, the restaurant is kind of like the New Giants Stadium... built for corporate use.  Nevertheless, the food was expertly prepared.

Lunch review only. 

So I heard the Bouillabaisse here was fantastic. I have some reading to do so I think, why not go grab lunch here, try the Bouillabaisse, and do my reading there. 

I arrive and immediately love the space and the freshness and modern feel to it. I get the menu. Bouillabaisse $28. Or 3 course Prix Fixe (with Bouillabaisse as an option) $35. Given the 2 other courses are on the menu for a total of $26, this is a 3 course that would have cost you $48 but together is $35. 

Now, most prix fixe options, when ordered a la carte instead, end up saving you at best a few dollars. Maybe instead of $40 it is $38, that sort of thing. So right away I am impressed that with the Bouillabaisse I was planning to order, I can get $26 worth of 2 more courses for $9, or the cost of an good extra value meal at Mickey D's.

Bread 
I believe it was Danish Rye. Delicious. Loved the butter with sea salt that came with it as well. 

First course - Gravlax
If you liked smoked salmon (and I love me some), you will love this dish. Very very generous portion and the salmon couldn't be any better. 

Second course - Bouillabaisse
Did not disappoint! Everything in here --- the white fish, the shrimp, the scallop, the salmon --- was perfectly. Great medley of vegetables and the sauce was flavorful but not too rich or overwhelming. So so good, highly recommend this if you at all like fish.

Dessert - Arctic Circle
I have never had a Goat Cheese based dessert before. I have to say - it was fantastic. Another good portion size with some nice gelato on the side. Lovely presentation as well.

Lunch Prix Fixe = FSGN = Five Stars Go Now!

Had a wonderful business dinner here. The food was excellent, with several dishes that tickled the taste buds in strange and exciting ways. Service was attentive; décor was warm and relaxed, with distinctive Nordic touches, e.g. a large deer antler as the table centerpiece.

The meal began with two amuse bouches - first a pumpernickel-flecked goat cheese lollipop, the creamy richness of the goat cheese nicely offset by the salty crunch of the pumpernickel. Then a beluga-topped sliver of raw salmon embedded in a tangy herb sauce. 

My dinner companions were uniformly pleased with their cocktail selections, many of which (not surprisingly) are made with aquavit, the Scandinavian-produced spirit. The grapefruit mojito was sweet and tangy with fresh pulp and just the right amount of acidity tempering the minty sweetness.

A trio of breads was brought out - one crunchy, rustic cracker; a piece of dark, dense nut-spice bread; and a sourdough roll. Butter was presented on a dark slab of volcanic rock.

I ordered from the four-course prix fixe menu: scallops with sea urchin and hazelnuts; fluke with heirloom egg, celeriac, and black burgundy truffle vinaigrette; and a medley of Nordic seafood with cod, prawns and sea urchin. Each dish was plated beautifully and featured bold, complex flavors. The fluke was particularly memorable, with the truffle vinaigrette mixing with the celeriac and egg yolk to create a delightfully complex flavor profile.

Dessert was a very good baked goat cheesecake with fresh figs, skyr, and port wine ice cream. Just when we thought the meal was complete, another set of dessert trays was brought out - homemade chocolate confections and mini-donut holes with an array of dipping sauces.

I have a newfound appreciation for Scandinavian food and would recommend Aquavit highly. Great spot for a date or business dinner.

I went to Aquavit a few months ago, this place is just so wonderful, the staff was very professional. I can't complain about anything. The food was excellent. I would definitely go back to this place. This place is very pricey but it is so worth it. Definitely the place to go for dinner.

One of the finest in fine dining in NYC. And Scandinavian fine dining? Not something taken for granted. But the prix fixe menu (4 options for each of the 4 courses) offers some of the best innovative food experiences ever to come out of that frozen peninsula. Salmon, caviar and the likes with all kinds of seasonal herb pairings, if you get my drift. And the wine list is great too, which is a rarity in NYC. Obviously be prepared to leave with a considerably lighter wallet, albeit a very full stomach.

Clothes: Definitely go the whole nine yards here. I wore fancy clothes: dress, stockings, makeup, boots, you know the drill. This is NOT a casual place.

Food: The food was elegant and well-prepared. I had meatballs and breaded goat cheese and bread and sparkling water and much more. I tried salmon for the first time, in this creamy buttery sauce. It was delicious.

Cost: Very, VERY expensive. A once-or-twice in a lifetime experience.

Dessert: Oh. My. God. The. Dessert. Was. Really. AMAZING! I ordered this chocolate brownie cake dish. It came with Rosemary ice cream dipped in white chocolate, shaped like an apple and the white chocolate outside was painted red to look like an apple. It even had a "leaf" sticking out of it. The "leaf" was a sprig of Rosemary coated in crystallized sugar. They brought extra desserts, even though all I ordered was the brownie cake thing. They brought sugared donuts for us to dip in different sauces, and they brought a plate of different truffles. I also had a pot of chamomile tea. Yummy!

PS: Eva W, are you SURE you went to the same Aquavit I did?

PSS: my first review for Aquavit just said "amazing". Are you glad I added this much more detail? Lol!
Check out my reviews for other places in Chealsea, Manhatten, NYC, NY like Bar Breton (French) and Dervish (Turkish/Meditteranean)

I will preface this by saying I went here during restaurant week.

Do you like to spend money on dishes that are given fancy names, but you are sure you make them with no culinary skills or "out of your way ingredients?" If yes, then this is your spot. For the appetizer I was served a slice of ham with a little bit of mustard sauce that was not only distasteful, I could not 'muster' the man in me finish it all. I then proceeded to order some meatballs, which were subpar with little taste. At this point, I wasn't hiding my disappointment in this restaurant: I needed a drink. I got a mixed cocktail, and in complete synchrony with the rest of the restaurant, it was pretty 'plebeian.' It was too sour for enjoyment, and like the appetizer I just didn't finish it. 

For my main course, I got a chicken dish which, finally, was decent. But let's be honest, this is Aquavit: a highly regarded restaurant with exceptional reviews. If the chicken was decent: then in my eyes it was bad. I could be a little harsh, but I will tell you that everyone in party was quite disappointed with the food. One the bright side, the service was good, and the waiter was very receptive to our changes in order etc. 

Bottom line: Will never go back and do not recommend.

A beautiful restaurant and has a very exclusive feel as soon as you enter. This should be a restaurant week choice if you are thinking to go, or one of those very special occasion places. However, if you work in the area and can afford it, it's great place to frequent. The food is beautifully plated and very tasty. Also this may be a great place for a marraige proposal. So with that being said...bring the AMEX.lol

This really wasn't the Nordic tour I had in mind, but it will have to do for now. 

One of the great things about living in NYC is that everyone always wants to visit you, and one of the great things about people visiting you is that it gives you an excuse to just be a little decadent every now and then...especially for dinner.

With that said, no one was visiting me from out of town and this was not a special occasion, but a random week day dinner with a good friend.  

We decided on the 4 course tasting menu, as opposed to the 7...seemed to much of a smorgasbord.  Started off with the Lobster and Peekytoe Crab (i enjoyed it); then the short ribs (really good, especially with the foie gras and pickled beet); amazing Nordic seafood (the urchin emulsion was a perfect touch); for desert I opted for the chocolate cake (predictable, but good).

Food: (2 4-course prix fixe menus, each $89)
~Goat cheese lollipop (3 stars): as the amuse.  This was rolled in a crust of rye bread on a stick.  Very cute, and the contrast between the crispy outside and creamy cheese was nice.  A bit too heavy on the the goat cheese though.
~Celery cream soup (4.5 stars): as the canape.  Smoked salmon and roe came in a bowl, and the cream was poured table side.  Flavors were wonderful, and the seafood fresh.  The cream complimented the saltiness of the seafood very nicely.
~Bread (4.5 stars): all choices came out freshly warmed!! The mini rye loaf was definitely my favorite.  It combined the heartiness of wheat with the mild sweetness of molasses, all with a delicious crust and nuts.  The sourdough was also delicious and came in a small roll.  The flatbread was also nice as a lighter alternative, with a myriad of spices in cracker form.  All came with brown butter, parmesan butter, and sea salt.  They even came around a few times to ask if you wanted more!
~Herring (5 stars): first course.  This was absolutely my favorite of the evening.  The herring was both smokey and sweet, layered with brown butter foam, parsley aioli, parmesan cubes, fingerling potatoes, a rye chip, and roe.  Despite having so many items on the dish, nothing stuck out like a sore thumb.  Definitely try this!
~These were the main highlights.  We also tried the gravlax, sweetbreads, pork, nordic seafood, salmonberry trio, and the goat cheesecake.  Of those, the pork and salmonberry were perhaps the weakest, with dessert being overall not the most outstanding.

I would definitely go with the seafood at this place, and the rye bread is simply the best I have had.

Wait:
~none for a reservation for 2 at 8pm on a Wednesday night.  Service was fine, and the decor felt very nordic indeed.  On the formal side.

I'm not sure if I would return, but this was certainly a nice experience.  They gave us small sachets of their glogg as we left.

Aquavit is one of my favorite restaurants in the city!

FOOD
Swedish meatballs (pickled cucumber, lingonberries, peanut potatoes, cream sauce)
-  I know meatballs sound ordinary, but they are delicious!  All the components come together, esp with the cream sauce
-  Lingonberries provide a sweet contrast to the meatballs

Gravlax (dill, lemon, hovmästar sauce)
-  Smoked salmon
-  The slices are served rolled together
-  Fresh tasting 

Herring Trio
- I've never really liked herring before, but I enjoyed the taste here.  There's not an overwhelming flavor


DECOR/AMBIANCE
Beautiful, high-ceiling space with neutral tones and interesting works of art on the wall.  Along the wall in the seating area by the bar are glass vessels filled with fruit and aquavit.  The background music is soft enough that you can talk easily with your friends.  People come here in business casual or more fancy clothes.


RECOMMENDATION
I come here after work for drinks and to catch up with good friends.  It has a relaxed atmosphere, so a great place to come and unwind at the bar.  The bar menu has reasonable prices, although the portions are smaller.  It's great for casual drinks or going out on a date.  I've also come with a large group of friends and had fun since it was easy to chat with everyone.  The portions were just large enough that everyone could share a bite of each other's dishes.

I was actually mad after this dining experience. 

I ordered a herring plate as an app. It was good. Not spectacular, but good. 

For my entree I ordered a Scandinavian smorgasbord with no description.  The damn entree had 3 fishes prepared EXACTLY LIKE MY APP. There were only two others tiny bits of food on my plate, and nothing mind blowing. 

My waiter never told me that I was basically ordering the same thing. When I brought it up, he was noticeably embarrassed. He stated I was right and it wasn't intentional, but a mistake like that shouldn't be made at such a high quality establishment. 

In fact, it was a joke. The food wasn't anything to write home about anyways. 

Snotty people, cold environment.

I feel cruel for giving Aquavit such a low rating, especially since the service was quite impeccable and also because I love all things Scandinavian (furniture, cosmetics, music, art, beer, cheese, oh my goodness I could go on for days!). I grew up spending my summers in Copenhagen and I have even had the pleasure of dining with the King and Queen of Sweden, so I consider myself having a finely tuned Scandinavian palate. For these reasons, I was more than mildly unimpressed with the tasting menu at Aquavit, although I say this out of fear of upsetting any faithful Aquavit diners or from scaring anyone away from expanding their palate to appreciate rewarding Nordic flavors. Ultimately, my dinner was fine and I tasted nothing close to insulting, but I got the feeling that the restaurant was trying so hard to be on-par with Daniel or Per Se and just couldn't find the means to match them. 

Some good news: the Gravlax was incredibly tasty and my cocktail that incorporated some acquavit and mushed strawberries put me in high spirits. I would love to give Aquavit another chance sometime, but frankly it is so high-priced that I am hesitant to make that "sometime" anytime too soon. I surely wish them luck in the future because I most desperately would like to see Scandinavian food succeed in New York City.

I came here during the restaurant week and was quiet a fan of the place! They even served butted on a rock, which was very unique. From the appetizers to the desserts you where kept happy all the time. 

Defiantly would return again.

I went for a business lunch, ordered appetizers and a salmon entree. 

I enjoyed the food, the service was great and ambiance was very nice.

I will visit them again in the near future.

I can't pinpoint why, but as much as I wanted to love Aquavit, there was just something missing. Oddly enough, I think that ambiguity is the exact reason why they are lacking a Michelin star. 

There are so many things fundamentally reminiscent of some of my favorite restaurants that I almost feel bad giving Aquavit only three stars. To start off, the service was incredibly fluid; never was a waiter crowding you, yet someone was always there to clear your settings at the most appropriate moment. The ambiance was notably intimate and upscale, yet also modern in a playful & unpretentious manner. That being said, there was a clear organization and flow during the entire experience. 

As far as the food goes, the menu is structured where you can either choose the four-course tasting for 89pp, or the seven-course tasting for 115pp; my friend & I chose the former. I really did appreciate the slight influence of molecular gastronomy on each course, but it just paled in comparison to Grant Achatz' work. The concept of higher-level Nordic cuisine is something lacking elsewhere in Manhattan, but I think Aquavit just needs a few tweaks. The food was good, but I walked out not even remembering what I ordered.

Recently spent 10 days in NYC and visited a lot of restaurants. Aquavit was unanimously felt to be the best by my family.  Relaxing atmosphere.  Fantastic food.
Fun to try the infused vodkas. 
Must visit again when i go back.

I came here for Summer '11 RW with a party of 5. I arrived on time while the rest of my party was a tad late and the hosts had no problem with me waiting in the lounge area. When we all arrived, we were seated in the back - round table style. I love the high seat backs of the chairs! 

I don't recall much about what I had that evening, which is not a terribly good sign as nothing was memorable. Perhaps it was because the RW menu wasn't the best representation of what Aquavit offers regularly.

We began with a personal bread plate; the unique bread basket was good although I tried not to load up on carbs. The rest of the food was interesting and definitely different to me as my palette is not used to Scandinavian cuisine. 

With that said, it was a decent RW experience. Wouldn't be at the top of my list, but not too shabby either.

My husband and I love to dine here every time we visit New York City. The ambience is upscale and romantic. The service is impeccable.  We always order the pre-fixes every time. I don't like the herring that's served with the 1st course, but my husband likes it.  The pre-fix main entree never disappoint.  This is definitely a must try if you like Swedish food or want to impress a date.  With drinks and tips, expect to pay around $200 to $300 for two.
Beautiful establishment but be prepared to be hungry after the meal. Place is all about presentation and platters are small. There were some snooty folks in there, including the waiter.

I have been wanting to eat at this restaurant ever since I saw Marcus Samuelson compete on the Japanese version of Iron Chef.   He has moved on to Red Rooster but this place goes on.

The Place is tiny with what seemed like 12 or so tables so you get very good service and it is not too loud.  The decor is very nordic with sleek wood tables and modern chairs.

The reason for coming was the food and usually when have high expectations one is disappointed but I was not as it was one of the best meals I have had in NYC and I have been to Le Bernardin, Oceana, Public, Gilt etc. 

I have to admit I love this type of food as does my girlfriend who has a sweet spot for northern/eastern european food.   That being said everything from the small cheese breads to start to the fluffy donuts that are as far removed from dunkin donuts as one can get it was amazing.  Usually we will share our food but the duck was so good by the time I looked over the plate had been cleared.  She also would not let me to touch the pickled herring.

Will definitely return to try some of the other dishes.
Just held a lovely dinner event in the private room.  Service was excellent.  Food was delicious and the space is very appealing.  I highly recommend it.

Facts:
- I did not come here during Restaurant Week. (menu wasn't limiting but food selections were sparse anyway)
- If one person orders from their extravagant side of the menu, the rest of the party had to order the same pricy side of the menu. (what kind of rule is this? the chef can't cook expensive food and less expensive food at the same time??)
- Waiter had an attitude problem. He sighed loudly at us and even rolled his eyes at one point when we realized we have to order from the same side of the menu due to their idiotic menu restrictions.
- Presentation is key. Being full after dining here is not.

To the pompous jerks who work here, thanks for serving us your foul attitudes and purely-for-show meals. You sure show us how unkind Aquavit can be to their patrons. Cheers!
had a great meal with friends...the place is more subdued than the normal frantic nyc place.

I don't even know where to start this review...my Acuavit meal was like an epic three hour dining experience, one that only New York City could provide. 

Amazingly chic modern decor, impeccable service, outstanding dishes, fresh cocktails...and flavored aquavit flights! It's a wonder that I remember the night at all!  

It's quite expensive and ideal for truly special occasions!
Wonderful ambience, great service and most importantly amazing food!

Had drinks and appetizers at the bar. Mushy gravlax. The meat on the  sliders was tough. Decent but not great herring especially given the price.  Great acquavit selections, so my suggestion is to go if it's the drinks you're in the mood for.

A friend of many years invited me here for lunch today for the wonderful herring festival. The food was great (especially the best-I've-ever-had rye bread, served as little 2" loaves), the service was fine and they accomodated our request to sit in the main dining room. 

However, someone involved in management of the room made a bad mistake: I told our waiter that my wife particularly loved rye bread and asked if I could have 1 or 2 of the small pieces for her. He misunderstood and said he wasn't allowed to give me the recipe, -- my friend and I laughed heartily and I said that I just wanted to bring her a piece so she could taste it. The waiter too laughed, said "Oh, sure" and left the table. He then did not return until we asked for the check and reminded him about the bread. He then looked profoundly uncomfortable and said he had made a mistake and would have to charge us for the bread, clearly having been told to do so by someone else. 

We said we'd pay for the bread, that we knew it wasn't his fault and that we felt that it was an extremely poor business decision on their part. Astonishingly, they charged $10 for four 2" pieces of rye bread that would be stale by morning and then gave us coupons for $50 off a dinner check! Can you say disconnect?

And so what was a 5 star feeling became a 2 star feeling (and review).

I've been to both private cocktail/dinner receptions as well as dined in their dining room and both experiences have been nothing short of exceptional.

Anytime I go to this caliber of restaurant I choose to do the tasting menu or chef choice because there are just too many good things on the menu to try and I can't just order 1.

Staff is always pleasant and attentive and I never feel rushed here either.

4.5 stars. 

I couldn't decide whether I should give this place a 4 or a 5, but then I remember feeling especially satisfied when leaving the place so decided to give it a 5. 


We ordered the prix fixe for dinner and asked for all the supplemental items. What I really liked about this place is that they served us mini dishes in between every course. The  waiter would say, "Compliments from the chef," for every mini dish and each time I would feel extremely giddy and special. 


Some memorable items. 

Herring (BEST DISH)
Long island duck breast with foie gras
Arctic bird's nest
Goat cheese parfait

I don't exactly remember what I had during the 7+ course meal but everything was beautifully made and delicious. I especially liked how they gave us a wrapped up mini meringue dessert on the go as we were leaving. 

I remember my wallet feeling a lot skinnier when leaving the place, but I had the biggest smile on my face. A great experience and longest dinner ever ~ 4.5+ hours.

Very classy restaurant with lots of interesting drinks.
Aquavit is really strong. It's almost like taking a shot kind of strong . Served in small glass. 
Course menu and it gets you really full and they gift you their famous warm drink for take home ( you have to brew it yourself ) waiters pays attention to detail but one of the source it was supposed to come with the dish was missing and we had to point it out. Very romantic inside.

This may have been the best meal I have ever had.  To start with we were an hour late for our reservation but called to let them know we were running late and they still got us in when we arrived.  The food was top notch from the first cheese bits through the final chocolate cakes they gave us as we left..

The corn soup they started with may have been the single best bite of the meal.  The gravalax and steak tartare first courses were both amazing with my wife and I loving both but not agreeing on which was better.  We had the Cod and Octopus for th second course and both were very well done.  The Cod was a little to salty for my wife but I loved it and the Octopus dish we both thought was great.

For the third course I got the Halibut and thought it was cooked perfectly and very well done but could have done without the beets but I am not a beet person.  My wife's nordic seafood dish was melt in the mouth good and we both thought it was the best we had for the third course.  For desert I can't say enough about about the raspberry cylinders.  I am not a desert person and I practically liked the plate clean.  Best desert I have ever had.  My wife got the lemon meraingue (SP?) desert and also ate every bite.

Service was fantastic.  They were attentive without intruding and very helpful when selecting our menu choices.  The place is expensive but well worth it for a special occasion!
Came during restaurant week and would recommend the aquavit no.6 with Pimms, ginger ale and cucumber aquavit. The pork shoulder was also very tasty.

Came here for restaurant week.  This year, it is their smorgasbord: herring, salmon, salads, swedish meatballs, custard, small cakes and cookies.  Sweetie, a herring fan, declared the matjes the finest ever.  The meatballs are also very good: flavorful, moist, nicely textured.  The serving arrangements are a little hectic -- a work in progress -- but the servers themselves are warm, personable, knowledgeable, and unobtrusive.   We really enjoyed it.

My boyfriend and I wanted to do something special for Valentine's so we decided to try Aquavit for something different.. from the moment we arrived until the minute we left, we were extremely pleased with the service, but more than anything with the food.   We did the pairing with wine and it was absolutely amazing and delicious.  Every bite and every sip was better than the previous one.  
They have different menus according to the season and time that you go; so they had a special menu for the ocassion but everything was well presented and the selection of food was delicious.  Our server, was also very helpful and professional.  He described every meal and came back a few times to make sure everything was the way we wanted. 
We left the restaurant with big smiles and hoping that we can afford to go back again.  I have to give them 5 stars (but keep in mind that the prices may be higher than other locations, however you pay for what you get.. worth every penny).

Interesting experience because I came here for RW 2012 lunch. I liked the fact that because the option is the buffet-style "Smorgasboarg" you can have as much (or as little) as you want. For a vegetarian like myself, this is a great RW concept! Instead of asking for the "vegetarian option" when the fish, chicken or steak option doesn't suit you, and having it be an unimaginative pasta, YOU CAN LOAD UP ON THE CORN BARLEY DISH...and go back for seconds! There was a lovely broc-cauliflower dish, an heirloom tomato salad, yummy potatoes, an assortment of breads and condiments....The shellfish eater in me was tempted, and so I tried the mussel soup (so sublimely sweet and savory) 

My dad and his wife enjoyed the herring and meatballs greatly. It's a VERY dainty buffet (don't let thoughts of Sizzler taint your vision) with a dessert selection as well. 

Now for the ambiance...they DO put you in this windowless room in the back that feels like it's saved for the "pedestrian diners" - so I have no idea what the REAL Aquavit Experience is like. 

It's not a RW experience to impress a date with a romantic setting, (and the service was....just ok...they didnt have to do much!) but its a cool way to try a grand variety of upscale Scandinavian cuisine for $24 a plate!  Everything tasted great.

This is a review for the 2012 Restaurant Week Smorgasbord offering. 

I usually have to strategize when it comes to all-you-can-eat type settings (to maximize the eating experience!) but in this case, I enjoyed just about everything. It didn't seem like there were a ton of options, but I found the variety to be more than enough.

The gravlax and the hot smoked salmon were amazing - and this is coming from someone who isn't a huge fan of salmon. My first encounter with herring was interesting- definitely very distinct, but not unpleasant. I'm not a huge fan of meat so The meatballs and pork belly were alright, but I'm not a huge fan of meat so I didn't have a great impression of them. The pork belly in particular struck me as a bit dry. 
I was pretty stuffed by the time I got around to dessert but managed to try everything. While the cookies were good, the panna cotta really stood out. 

I left pretty satisfied. A 4.5 if it were possible.

the restaurant week smorgasbord dinner was a hit in my books! i mean, who wouldn't love a smorgasbord of delicious food?? it's definitely a different concept for a restaurant week setting. but kudos to aquavit for making this a great dining experience without losing the class and elegance of the restaurant. although "buffet" seems to drum up negative connotations, this was more like an upscale, catered event. after you are seated and situated with your water & drinks, you are invited by the waiter to help yourself to a variety of options. everything is clearly labeled, and nicely organized. just to name a few- there must have been 4-5 kinds of herring, some gravlocks, smoked salmon, assorted breads and spreads, wonderfully cooked potatoes, potato salad, egg salad, greens and veggies, swedish meatballs, pork belly, a seafood veloute, and for the dessert table- panna cotta, carrot cake, chocolate cake, and like 6 jars of different gourmet cookies. all delicious, and all bite sized. i think if you try one of everything, you will be full. the service was one of the best i have experienced. once you are up, they clear your plates and you come back to a fresh setting of appropriate utensils each trip. the decor is very modern and classy, perfect for a special occasion dinner as well. i would love to come back for a full experience next time

I pretty much agreed with Alda C. review below. Due to a bad experience with RW menu 2 days earlier, I made sure I read reviews about the RW at Aquavit, which seemed pretty promising. So mom and I decided to get lunch here. We never had Scandinavian food, so we were excited. I'm not going to comment on the authenticity however. 

We pretty much tried everything and there were a lot more good than bad.

The bad (short list): breads, swedish meatball 
The good: pretty much everything. Herring was too salty for both of our liking, but I guess it is how herring should be. The potato was surprisingly good. Very simple dish, but gd. Pork belly was great, my mom commented on how little fat was left on the meat, yet it was still succulent. The salmon was great. Very creamy but not at all fishy. We happily finished our plate. Dessert was ok. I'm not a cookie fan, but their panna cotta blew me away. 

Service and decor: since it was buffet style (aka you serve urself), not much service but they were quick with filling water and providing utensils. Decor is simple and elegance. 

But boi, they know how to keep customers. They gave us a $50 gift card to use toward our next dining here (which I'm sure will happen). And apparently there's a crawfish fesitval coming up in mid August. Mom already said she will be bringing coworkers here. 

Left happy and would return :)

Here we go again...Restaurant Week. Please read this review based on my RW meal and not the actual dining room experience. So Aquavit decides to offers their smorgasbord instead of the usual three course prix-fixe.  This seems quite a special treat, considering the regular smorgasbord costs $32 and this would also be a cultural experience as well.  So, for my annual special day (:P), I decided to partake on a Swedish RW lunch.  As others have noted, do not expect a long table of selections, but everything arrives in small amount, for freshness and to look more elegant.  From one start of the table, you have a choice of three different types of breads (a round white roll, Swedish rye 'log', and a fennel crisp), then there are herrings and pickled salmon for you to load them onto the bread.  Lots of additional condiments are also available for additional flavorings.  In the middle section, you have the potatoes, salads, greens, dressings, and finally the meat section consists of the famous meatballs, corn and barley , and pork belly. You are welcome to go back for more plates and whenever you get up, the attentive waitstaff would take away your used plates and refold your napkins.  That's 5-star service for you.  

According to my mom, the pork belly was quite lean, but wasn't dried out. However, the meatballs do need a bit of sauces to revive their moistness.  Herrings are an acquired taste, but if you do not enjoy pungent and salty flavors, steer clear of them and just pile on more salmon.  

When you are done with the savory items, you will want to end on a sweet note with the six jars of mini cookies (oatmeal was the best for its chewiness and heartiness) panna cotta, and bite-sized carrot cake (though could not detect any carrot resemblance) and chocolate cake.  I was actually a bit disappointed by this pedestrian dessert display.  No Swedish influence whatsoever. Where's the torte? The Lussebullar? The Swedish waffles? And finally, while some parties received a $50 gift card for their next visit, we did not receive one. Wonder why...

They allocated the back area specifically for RW, which is understandably as diners have to maneuver around the floor to get their foods. It is more casual, which I liked, but you are also not getting the full Aquavit experience.  So, in conclusion, do the smorgasbord if you are into salmon, herrings, and meatballs, but skip it and pay more for a prix-fixe in the main dining room if you want the real McCoy.

This is a review for Summer 2012 Restaurant Week.

Had a truly wonderful dining experience at Aquavit. They have set up one of their private dining rooms as a dedicated Smorgasbord, which is a smart way for a high end restaurant to separate their Restaurant Week diners from their regular a la carte diners.  All of the salmon options were delicious.  Ask for the special Restaurant Week wine list. The server gave me $50 vouchers for a future visit to the restaurant, which is a nice incentive to spur a return trip.

(setting up the instruments)
At the door I'm greeted by a pleasant hostess.
Welcome to Aquavit, how many will be joining you sire?
I'm alone, so one please.

Are you here for dinner or for our restaurant week menu selection?
Uh.. Restaurant week.
Certainly, right this way.

(elegant jazz music playing)

I'm being whisked past this beautiful looking bar, with beautiful looking people sipping $14 cocktails. I feel like I'm being brought thru heaven but its not my final destination....

Here you are sire, enjoy your dinner. I'm seated in a small room that looks like a cruise ship. 

The waiters come and they are spot on. Folded napkins, forks, and in the best English voice I'm asked, Cocktail to start?
Uh. yes

Fine sire. Here is your restaurant week menu. Its a smorgasbord.
Wait a second, what??
Yes sire, a smorgasbord
You mean like all you can eat? Like Sizzler?
uh.. Sizzler Sire? Yes, all you may wish to partake. Enjoy and bon appetit.

(Banjo music playing)...
(I now turn into Larry the Cable guy)

HOWDY!
I look around, see quite people eating little danty things..
Well Golly! Lets grab a plate and get the party started!

I see a small table but everything is arranged properly.
What are these, holy smokes.. MEATBALLS in brown gravy!?
I grab about 15 of them, load them all on my plate. Head back to my table, I'm sitting next to two demure Asian woman.
I show them my meatballs and say HOWDY!
(looks of utter discontent flashed my way)
They also have pork belly. Pork Belly, think of cooked bacon. When you cook it down, the fat dissipates and the meat is thin. Pork belly is like a thick, cooked down bacon steak piece. Very decadent.

I go back. What is this, that raw fish? Nah.. Its Herring, White Fish and Salmon. All yer can eat! 
I'm not a big herring guy but the two salmon choices were really fresh and tasty.

I go back again.
Green salad, cheeses, and sides. Tater salad?! Lordy lordy! Wait a sec, these potatoes are brown inside?!

I see a cold, creamy soup with one oyster in clear coffee cups.
The Larry in me says: Well looky looky, cute lil soups. You don't think this one lil clammy part is gonna fill up big ol me? 
I grab 5 and one asian woman quietly throws up in her purse.

Dessert has these custard cups, different cookies and small cakes.
Yee Haw! My mamma used to call me puddin'. Well it started after she looked in my diaper. (Asian woman next to me is getting ready to perform hari kari)

So, $35 bucks to eat where Marcuss Samuelsson trained. Is it worth it, all you can eat? I'm thinking what I had last year at Bar Boulud was mind numbing.. 

Your call.

See ya'll later!

Scandinavilicious Restaurant Week experience! So yes, it's a buffet, very atypical of the slow, 3-course RW meal experience - perfect for someone like me who likes to freakishly control what she eats while also enjoying the art of shoving things in her mouth with insatiable hunger and urgency. Here's my take on the delicious Aquavittles I sampled on my FOUR (I was a Viking in another life) trips to the buffet: 

- Herring, served three different ways: My bro preferred the one in dill sauce; I loved the salty pinkish one with chopped onions. All good and not offensively pungent, as I feared.

- Salmon, prepared two ways: One was INFINITELY better than the other. The version topped with fresh dill was some of the best raw fish I have EVER had, while the hot smoked salmon was too smoked and lox-like for me.

- Creamy dill salads: Sampled a potato version and a shrimp salad tossed in their delicious creamy white dill sauce. The base is more tzatziki-yogurty than heavy mayonnaise-based stuff. Yum. And the potatoes are purple! 

- Mussels velouté: Deliciously light, frothy milk broth with tender mussels and cooked veggies, flavored with fennel, and of course.... dill. Loved this.

- Tomato salad and turnip salad: both vinegar-based and fresh. I sprinkled some of the incredible hard cheese from the buffet onto the tomato salad, and BAM. Even better. 

- Mixed greens with lemon vinaigrette and lingonberries: Really refreshing break from the salty deliciousness of the fish. I couldn't get enough of the salad - try adding the cheese to this, too... goes great with the 'lil berries. 

It's a crime if you don't scoop up the sauces, especially the creme fraiche w/ dill, and sample them with just about everything. So good. The pork belly and meatballs were enjoyed immensely by my tablemates, so give 'em a shot. Dessert was great, particularly the cookies (cranberry white chocolate nut, baby), but the panna cotta with fresh berries stole the show. 

Ambiance was beautiful, and service was impeccable. Plates and silverware replaced and napkins folded in the blink of an eye. AND a free $50 gift card at the end?!

Smorgasbord bliss.

I love Scandanavian food. They are nutritious, delicious, and finely seasoned. 
Due to the delicacy, on the other hand, I am only willing to dine at quality-proof places, such as Aquavit. So glad that I came with coworker for the RW lunch this year.  
$$ price at a $$$ place for the $$$$ food?! This is probably one of the best deal one could find in nyc. 

Aquavit serves a buffet style of Scandanavian food- the generousity of selection and the authentic taste really wowed me. From herring to salmon, meatballs to porkbelly, in addition to those light 'n beautiful desserts pleasant to both eyes and stomach...

Modern European decor, upscale ambiance, standard kind service... all was very attentive. 
We did dine in style.

Why does such immpecable food and service only possess 4 star? Well, like many others, I sort of feel with so many distinguishing restaurants in town, we need some unique personality/character to leave customers a strong deep impression, in order to reach out to the perfect 5 star.

Regardless, I highly recommend participation in their Restaurant Week lunch!!

Came here for Restaurant week yesterday.

Reservation was at 7. We arrived on time and were seated immediately. I think all the R/W people were seated in a separate dining room (weird). Surprised it was a legit buffet where you would have to get up and choose your food. Thought I could order whatever was on the menu and have a waiter bring it to me (I wish of course). 

Portions were good for me. I really only needed one bite of everything. For the $35 price tag, you get to try everything on the R/W menu. I've never had an experience like this and the food was different, so it was definitely worth coming. 

Everything was good except for the one herring I had (not sure which it was, but try them all anyway), the dessert was mediocre. And the entree options were somewhat limited. 

Bottom line: The appetizers were great. Entrees were okay. Dessert was disappointing, but still better than many establishments.

Overall, my bf and I left full and pleasantly surprised.

A must go for us.

Not impressed.  My expectations were clearly too high.  A trusted foodie friend has Aquavit on his list of must try places in NYC.  I'm assuming this place has gone far downhill since because my Aquavit experience was very disappointing.  Disclaimer, this was a restaurant week meal.

Food - Before arriving, I had done my homework and knew roughly what to expect.  I was not crazy about the buffet idea but it allows you to try a bit of everything.  Started with a bit of each of the herring, which I thought was all quite good.  Next moved onto the main course items: Swedish Meatballs - semi cold and not that great.  Pork belly - I love well prepared pork belly but sadly I was disappointed.  Served under a heat lamp (really) and again cold and not the seared outside, melt in your mouth inside experience I was expecting.   Mussels velouté - two ounces of semi dried liquid with undetermined seafood served in a coffee cup under a heat lamp.  Honestly, I had no idea what this was until I asked the waiter, tried and was disappointed.  Dessert - I guess we waited to long because several of the plates were empty and not refilled for the rest of the night.  What was left were a few jars of mediocre cookies.  

Experience - Again restaurant week, was served in a separate room from regular diners that was as dated as Tony Montana's mansion.  Waiters - not expecting the A team but the staff may have been trainees recently hired from Chili's.  Waiters interrupted date conversation multiple times to bring replacement silverwear or let empty plates sit in for extended period.  At least our wine glasses were always filled.

An excellent dining experience should include both inspired food and a quality atmosphere, mine had neither. I understand that at restaurant week prices, you may not get the full experience.  I expect about 75% of the full experience, if you enjoy then you come back for full fare.  At the end of the meal, we received a couple of the previously mentioned $50 discount certificates for a subsequent visit.  We left the certificates behind, enough said.

I had amazing restaurant week experience at Aquavit.  It's a buffet style with a generous selection of Scandinavian food.  The herring trios were a little salty but all delicious.  Gravlax was good and Mussels velouté was phenomenal.  Pork belly was a bit greasy but still tasty and juicy; i liked pork shoulder better.  Swedish meatballs were moist and flavorful.  I especially loved their sauce selections--make sure to try them all!  Dessert was ok.  The pana cotta loaded with berries totally blew me away!  Romantic ambience, impeccable service.

My friend and I came during Restaurant Week, and I was pleasantly surprised. Most of the other fancy places give you a tiny three-course meal and leave you still feeling hungry, but Aquavit instead offered a smorgasbord of many different dishes, buffet style. The food was amazing, and you could get as much of it as you pleased. However, I must admit that the dessert selection was rather pedestrian. The cookies and cakes didn't seem much better than their store-bought counterparts.

I've been to Aquavit twice in the past 2 weeks: once for restaurant week and once for the crayfish festival. I would give the RW visit a solid 3 stars, and crayfish fest 4, so think of this as a 3.5-star review really. 

Both times I went, it was for a smorgasbord setup, a fancy word really for an all-you-can-eat buffet. In that sense, Aquavit is one of the best RW deals around. Come hungry and eat as much as you like. Be warned though that most of the offerings are heavy and many are doused in mayonnaise. The best parts were the tomato salad, cheese, and smoked fish. I'm not a big fan of herring, but my boyfriend is, and he was very happy with the offerings. I enjoyed the smoked salmon and shrimp/crayfish salad. 

Going for the Crayfish fest, you get a 1/2 lb of crayfish before you can go up to the buffet. The crayfish were excellent, but there isn't much to eat on a crayfish. I came much hungrier when I went for crayfish fest, and enjoyed multiple buffet visits. It was a little disappointing that some of the dishes advertised on the Crayfish Fest promotional card we got at RW weren't present at the bar (I really wanted to try some Janssen's Temptation and my boyfriend missed the crayfish herring). The meatballs were a bit disappointing. Kinda dry.

The desserts are simple, but the cookies offered are excellent. The snickerdoodles were better the second time -- chewy and buttery, tasting like Cinnamon Toast Crunch in cookie form.

And finally, the aquavit itself -- I enjoyed it, but I still like flavored vodkas better.

In short, I'd say it's a pretty solid bet for RW, if you're hungry and enjoy Scandinavian food.

I came here for Restaurant Week, which was essentially a really fancy buffet. There was all-you-can-eat salmon, herring, salads, Swedish meatballs, and dessert, just to name a few items. I definitely enjoyed the variety (it was a "smorgasbord" after all) and the food was fresh. This is certainly worth your $35 if you come really hungry and ready to eat yourself into a coma. 

In terms of the food, I'm a pretty adventurous eater, so I appreciated the three different types of herring and two types of salmon. The hot smoked salmon was my favorite. It was perfectly cooked on the outside, a little raw on the inside, and topped with a delicious pickle/dill/mayo sauce. It was a very balanced morsel of fish. The hot food section was a bit underwhelming. I'm almost embarrassed to admit this, but I preferred IKEA's Swedish meatballs and lingonberry sauce over the ones served at Aquavit. The meatballs were dry and the lingonberry sauce was too tart for my taste. The summer corn barley also had a strangely tart taste, but that could have just been my taste buds. For me, the highlights were the pickled cucumbers and dessert. Those pickles were the perfect blend of sweet and sour, and was a refreshing bite to cut the heavier sauces of the other food items. Then, dessert. Oh dessert!!! The panna cotta with fresh berries was DIVINE and the chocolate cake was TO DIE FOR. The chocolate cake seemed more like a flour-less chocolate cake with a brownie-like consistency/texture. I was in heaven. I almost wish that I saved more room for dessert. 

Service was a bit strange. I think they were itching for us to leave, because I was on my fourth plate of food, and this didn't even count my fifth plate of dessert. Yeah...I'm pretty disgusting. In any event, I hate being rushed, so I'll have to knock that down a point. 

All in all, I think this is well worth a Restaurant Week visit. I think my experience was more of a 3.5, but I'll give Aquavit the benefit of the doubt.

Went with a group on business. The meat had a dark sauce that looked like chocolate, on it but once you cut into it it was delicious. The service was great but I did not get to try much else on the menu.

This was my second time at Aquavit - 6 years later and I still was not disappointed! The food and service was excellent, even though the chef changed since the last time I came here. The attention to detail, the finesse in the food and not to mention the great decor and mid-century scandinavian furniture - all in all a great experience! One that will leave me wishing we had such a place in LA, one that will sure result in another visit! But this time I won't wait for another 6 years...

Ok its really fancy sophisticated place!but really expensive!and we left hungry:)cause portions are really small!its beautiful unusual cute meal....but its not for people who really hungry:)if u want just come and enjoy and try something new its really nice place!but if u are really hungry -chose something else:)

Came here for restaurant week and took advantage of the smorgasbord. 
There was a decent variety of food but a lot of it was just sauces. If you like Scandinavian food, this place might be right for you.

The food was less than par. Nothing stood out. The meatballs were good but it was just upgraded IKEA meatballs. The pork/ribs were supposedly good. I think these two things were the only things people refilled on. You had your bread, random salads, assortment of fish, and that's about it.

The desserts looked pretty but none of them tasted good. I'm a sweets person and I didn't go back for seconds (that's pretty sad). The only memorable dessert was the panna cotta. The cookies were dry and unmemorable.

They gave out $50 giftcards to each of the guests so that you can revisit them for a second experience. I have yet to use my giftcards and it's been over a month.

Wow! Beautiful presentation, so complex, and totally worth it.  Service was tremendously good.  A fantastic wine selection and an interesting take on Aquavit spirits.  The ambiance was everything you'd expect from the Swedish- streamlined, elegant, modern and clean, with a great rolling ceiling in the lounge area.  Best Gravlax I've had in a while.  Chef Marcus Jernmark is certainly on his A game.  Desserts are also amazingly intricate.

We (a party of two) went for a casual dinner. I ordered halibut -- which was bland, but smoked salmon in sauce as amuse-bouche was very good. Their desserts are amazing, as well as petits fours. Overpriced, no doubt, but not bad. I'd go back just for the desserts.

I still think about this dinner and it's been 3 months. 

We were seated at one of their round tables where the black, high-back swivel chairs  which are slightly reminiscent of evil super-villain chairs. I felt like I should be stroking a white cat. That said, they were very comfortable for dining. 

The amouse bouche which came out at the start was a smoked corn chowder presented in a little sealed jar which they opened in front of you. A little puff of smoke comes out, and even before you taste it, you can smell that it's going to be good. 

Everything in between amouse bouche and dessert is great. Just pick anything. 

Dessert seemed to go on forever in the most amazing way. Our desserts came out and they were excellent, although I was so full at that point I, to my shame, could not finish my chocolate dessert. Then, just to rub it in about how awesome they are, they bring out a tray of tiny confectioneries like mini cakes, mini brownies and mini macarons. Of course, they looked so adorable I stuffed myself some more. And then, when the bill comes, they present you with two brownies to takeaway! OMG takeaway dessert so that I can satisfy my inner piggy at home later. And not two brownies to share with your partner, everyone gets two brownies! Hurray.

despite the fact that i am a BIT less of a fan since samuelsson's departure, aquavit is still amazing.

the herring, and the gravlax are the best in the city. the seafood is always fresh, and the fennel seed bread is amazing. the swedish meatballs, obvi, are still great; always have been.

BUT, i miss the interesting herring flavors they used to have; curry with apple, in particular, was my favorite. also, samuelsson's hovmastarsas with espresso was sick sick sick. if i could, i'd smear that sauce on everything i ate for the rest of my life. i miss the sunday brunch smorgas bord they used to offer (i ate gravlax by the boatload during those brunches). i also miss the arctic circle dessert. 

i'm not saying it's not good food now, but it's certainly feels like something is missing nowadays. not quite off, but not quite the enthusiatic 5 stars i would have given it a few years ago. i give it 5 stars squarely on the fact that the food remains of high quality, and the service is great; but i give it a little begrudgingly now. 

still, one of my top 3 restaurants ever.

oh. and not to continue this nostalgia too much, and i know it's been years, but i miss the charm of the old location. it was one of the best hidden surprises i've ever experienced in a restaurant.

Ate there this weekend with girlfriend and we each had the tasting menu with wine-pairing. 

The food and service were irreproachable. Flavors spanned the whole spectrum of gustatory elements, with the first plate's aroma  highlighted by its presentation.  The dish it was served on, a closed glass jar, was opened table-side to unveil a beautiful aroma of hay smoke. 

The carbonated beet amuse bouche was equally original. The quail delectable, and the wine pairings spotless.

Overall the meal was excellent and the service friendly and professional. 

Would not hesitate to recommend this for a sophisticated culinary voyage guided by a very capable chef.

I dined here last week and, after trying thousands of restaurants in NYC, this one is definitely going to be in my top-5-list. In my personal opinion Aqauvit is way better than many other high-end restaurants (i.e. Daniel).
The service, the attention to details, the quality of each ingredients are superb.
Everything from the appetizer (Mollusk tartare) to the main course (long island duck breast) to the dessert (chocolate and texture) was perfect.
I also enjoyed very much the cucumber-based cocktail (Aquavit N.6, if I recall correctly).
I was incredibly impressed by this restaurant and I will definitely suggest it to anyone who loves high quality food and environment, you will not be disappointed!

Yum.  The menu here is solid all-around, and its midtown location is especially convenient if you're trying to enjoy a post-workday dinner (or meeting someone who is!).  I made sure to try as many dishes as possible, all of which are full of flavor, and had complaints with none.

"Does your girlfriend particularly like Scandinavian food?"

"No, it's not that. The particular type of cuisine doesn't matter. She just like fancy food. It needs to be on small plates. And incredibly expensive. Then she's happy."

This was the conversation that my bf had with his colleagues in the week leading up to my birthday. He chose Aquavit because it has (in his words) "a snooty environment." We both found nothing snooty about the restaurant. The service was gracious, attentive, and welcoming. An incredible touch that Aquavit has is how they served both of us at the exact same time. Two servers would lay down our plates at the moment and when we were done, they would come by at the same time to whisk our plates away. It was a show unto itself.  

The new fall menu was out. They no longer have the 7-course menu, but the 4-course menu (plus lots of extras) for $85 pp was not an outrageous price for the level of service and quality of the food. We thought we got a very good deal for everything we got.

He had a Scotch and I ordered a grapefruit mojito for our drinks. I liked the bright citrusy flavor, but I thought the mint leaves were overly muddled. They were disintegrating and the leaves would get sucked up through the straw as i was trying to drink. 

They brought out some sort of delicious warm cheese bread that was like Brazil's pao de queso. Four delicate little round bites of fragrant and warm goodness served on a platform really, a bowl that was filled with little beans or something. 

A couple moments later, a waiter carrying a slate with rye, sourdough, and the flat Swedish bread came by. Ben and I elected to have both the rye bread and sourdough. The rye bread was in the shape of a mini-loaf and still warm. They brought out softened butter and flakes of sea salt. 

Next was the amuse bouche, which was smoked barley, mushroom, and paper thin slices of radish in a celery root cream sauce served in a little airtight container. Puffs of smoke swirled inside the container until they were released. 

For my first course, I had the steak tartar, which was incredible. I loved the contrast of textures between the tender steak and crunchy Dutch rye seeds. I adored the perfectly boiled quail egg that came with the tartar. Soooo cute! And delicious. Everything tastes better when they're miniaturized. Ben had the diver scallop tartar, which was beautifully plated to look like a the floor of an ocean.

For my second course I had the charred langoustine with maroon carrots and Ben had a cod dish. The langoustine was perfectly cooked. It was rich, unctuous, and still had the sweet taste of the delicate briny sea. Ben's second was absolutely amazing. I highly recommend that you get it. The cod was like butter. So tender and rich. I never knew cod could be a transcendental experience.

Third course, I had duck breast with foie gras and he had Nordic Seafood (a medley of lobster, scallops, and fish). More perfection from the duck breast. Cooked medium so it still retained with lovely red color, the breast was tender and juicy. I fell in love with the seared foie gras. It was so smooth and rich. I could feel tears of joy in my eyes as I savored the foie gras. 

For my dessert, I had the peach mousse and Ben ordered the "Chocolate and Texture." After having such a rich meal, I wanted a lighter dessert. The Chocolate and Texture was chocolate in four different ways. Because it was my birthday, the chef sent out a gratuit third dessert. We're savoring and enjoying our desserts, each bite being quite delectable. Even Ben who is not a dessert person, enjoyed himself. 

But this was not the end! After we finished, Aquavit gave us more dessert! First two little beignets filled with caramel and coated in cinnamon sugar. Then more little bites of beautiful dessert that looked like jewels against the dark gray slate serving plate. There were a tiny little macaron, fruit jelly candy, a square of lemon mousse, a chocolate chipped coconut madeleine, and other bites I can't remember. And just when I think it's over, they come out with a lovely little package of homemade kladdkaka (chocolate brownie) for us to take home. The kladdkaka was fantastic. The little cake was rich in chocolate, but light in texture and moist. I loved it.

I had a wonderful dinner here. Aquavit made my birthday a memorable one.

Awesome infused vodka and Delicious salmon. We were here for Restaurant week.

Return ? Yes 
Frequency ? Rarely

In my last review, I said that if the service were better, I would give Aquavit 4 stars.  Well, if was not only better but it was truly excellent.  Service was first rate.  Tremendous attention to detail.  

The chocolate cake was wonderful.  Only complaint was it was a bit too small.  Great chocolate flavor.  Served with excellent ice cream.  

Looking around the room, I felt I was in Scandinavia.  It was a wonderful trip.

Excellente!  We did the $85/prix fixe, everything was perfect, ambiance, food and staff.  The meal also came with a ton of freebie dessert tastings at the end in addition to the dessert that came with meal, awesome.  I also tried the Aquavit vodka tasting (3 flights for $17 - they make their own vodka flavors) excellent compliment to the meal as well.  Would definitely recommend checking out Aquavit.

I've been to Aquavit twice in the past few years and after each experience, this elegant and classy restaurant has proven its quality time and again.  

To begin, I am absolutely in love with the layout and orientation, and interior design of this restaurant.  It is one of the nicest places I have been to in the city as it is equal parts sophisticated and meek enough to feel homey and approachable.  The lounge and bar area are separate from the dining nooks, which are cordoned off in two sections.  When we had our company dinner here the other night, we were seated in the room at the front end of the restaurant, while another private function was being held in the room closer to the bar.  The noise level was average to below average, and each table was filled in a room that approximately accommodated 20 guests.  The service here is impeccable.  Aquavit might just have the best, most attentive, and inviting crew of all the fine dining establishments I've been to, yet.  On decor (a lovely contemporary motif), and service, Aquavit is an unflinchingly 5 star restaurant.

We ordered from the prix-fixe menu that serves four courses for $85pp.  Additionally, we were generously given some freebies (amuse-bouche, and desserts).  The food preparation and plating is notable, as the quality shines right off the plate, and everything is presented very exquisitely.  Taste-wise, I'm not sure I was head over heels for my Scandinavian fare although I did enjoy most of my dishes.  I noticed the same experience throughout each of my four courses - a lot of frothy and milky textures.  For my main dish, I had the Halibut which was a very clean and hearty piece of fish.  But at certain times, it felt slightly overwhelming and heavy because of the creaminess of the brown butter sauce.  For taste and overall impression on the food, I would give Aquavit 3 stars.

I just really can't get over the uncanny service and the gorgeous space, and for this reason, Aquavit ranks high on my most favorable NYC restaurants.

What an amazing experience this dinner was!  Just the fact that i am takng my time to write about it is a testiment to how memorable it wzs: both food and service. If you truly enjoy food, this place will make you happy and put a smile on yout face. I can only speak to wht we have tried, but i have a suspicion that its all pretty outstandig....so....we had scallops, pickled herring [ defibetely an acquired taste which we have, but not for everyonr],cauliflower, lobster... for main dishes we had halibut and wague beef...you will not miss with these choices.... this place is a reason to come back to NYC...

Another work trip brought me back to New York. I returned to Aquavit, as my last experience was so pleasant. The food had improved slightly, perhaps the kitchen is finding its groove. What I was looking forward to most was the delightful wine service and hospitality. The sommelier had recommendations based on what I enjoyed months earlier (she actually remembered!). As a pinot noir enthusiast, she surprised me with something unexpected and memorable. I can't wait to be back.

It begins with the bread service, that warm and buttery housemade rye bread that I could eat everyday, a few times a day. Then the amuse comes in a jar, smoke escaping while servers pour a delicate liquid on top of tiny morsels. From appetizers to dessert, dishes keep tantalizing our tastes buds. 

Presentations are gorgeous: the nantucket scallop with sea urchin comes in a wooden box complete with seaweed and seashells, and the little green balls are not peas, they are tiny cucumber balls that pop in your mouth, so refreshing. Some dishes looking like an intricate garden, on a slate, or in a bowl, all equally beautiful and delicious. 

The chef has a particular knack for all seafood. Desserts match perfectly, and they are not overly sweet, leaving you with a feeling of lightness even after 4 courses and some in-between. 

The cocktail list is attractive, and many wines are very reasonably priced. The wood tables void of tablecloths give the dining room a warm feeling, the atmosphere absolutely not stuffy for a fine dining restaurant. Nordic charm. The 4-course menu is $85, and it's good value. You can easily spend more and not have such a great experience in many restaurants, in New York or elsewhere.

I thoroughly enjoyed our dinner at Aquavit and got a chance to try some unique dishes.  I'm a fan of Aquavit liquor and got to try two different house made selections including the traditional caraway and hot horseradish.  Strong stuff, but a good complement to the food.  The dining room is small but well appointed with clean modern lines, though the decor was a bit dark for a winter's night.  The service was quite good with fresh silverware for each course and a manager overseeing the room coordinating dish delivery.  The pickled herring was fantastic as an appetizer.  It is served as a whole fish with all the troublesome bones removed.   The seared scallops were well prepared for the entree.  We ordered desserts which were tasty, and at that point we were stuffed.  Then came the complementary desserts!  We had to take those home.
