We also received one spice satchel each to make glog (scandanavian spiced sweetened wine) at home.

Beautiful restaurant, excellent staff, food was good but rather one dimensional.  We ordered the chef's tasting menu and while each dish was good and had some interesting elements, it was too much of the same, similar ingredients and techniques between each dish, rather lacking in proper orchestration/flow/excitement/contrast.  Dessert, however, was absolutely amazing and brought smiles to our faces (white chocolate 'egg' in a nest....mmmm).  I think anything the dessert kitchen cooks up would probably be just as good.  Would definitely come back on the merit of the dessert alone.

Good food but not great. Service is good but not great. Managers a little snooty. Walked past it twice before we saw it. Too highbrow for it's own good. Way too many great restaurants in Manhattan to waste time here. Go if you're curious but its not what it used to be.

Wow. This place was incredible. I came here though Savored's 30% off and I have to say the food, service, and ambience makes that 30% a major bargain. In addition to the pre-fixe menu, we received additional chef items that were not on the menu to make our dinner a 11-12 course meal. The service was impeccable and the waiter explained each dish to us - like how they do it on Top Chef. The only negative on the meal was that the Swedish Meatballs were not on the menu the night I was there. Overall though, definitely worth going to at $85pp for the Pre-Fixe when there's a special occasion to celebrate.

Good service, mediocre food, great atmosphere but i'm not the type to like expensive small dish meals-- that is more my mother.
I didn't know what to expect for Scandinavian Nordic food at all but i was willing to try.

Therefore, as a vegetarian, i didn't quite enjoy to the utmost last night. Service was great, the sommelier knew how to recommend, my cocktail was great (it was a cucumber flavored  martini that was not too sweet, just the way i like it) but i like to feel full after i ate and i wasn't that full.

The first course on the V-day menu was the scallop/ tomatoe raw dish -- my tomato was too sour but the scallop that boy had was good but not spectacular.

My second dish was a fennel salad-- again, a light vinaigrette was applied and it was nothing that was amazing that made me say "omg that was so great".

Third dish was the best-- barley with truffle taste-- i love truffle taste and this was no exception. It was warm too and i like my dishes warm.

My last dish before dessert was a mushroom, veggie dish which was salty and wasn't particular spectacular either. I liked it but didn't love it.

Dessert is usually my favorite but the chocolate tart/mousse dish was too sweet and had too much going on. THere were some crispy cookie stuff on one side, iced gelato/sorbet on another and it was just too much stuff and made the dish too busy, i thought.

Very good service but i just didn't think it was worth the price... it was midtown and too fancy for my taste.

Maybe the ala carte menu would be better? But thanks but no thanks....

The first time I visited Aquavit was during the summer Restaurant Week. Enjoyed the all-you-can-eat herrings VERY MUCH. The second time was for their regular lunch. It is on the pricey side, but I would say the food and service were worth it (loved their rye bread too).

Hands down, the most memorable dining experience I have ever had.  From the moment I walked through the doors, I was transported to a far away land of food and beverage.  The food was beyond perfect, the drinks paired wonderfully with every bite, and the service was spot on throughout the entire journey (my meal).  My dinner date and I must have been been categorized as "fabulous eaters/dinners" because the server brought us two desserts plus the complimentary spread of cookies and candies.  Amazing.

Came here for drinks after work recently. Had two glasses of the Sauvignon blanc, which was quite tasty, and a very strong Hendricks martini. The bartenders are great and appear to really enjoy creating new cocktails. 

After we paid our bill, our bartender brought my friend and I over two glasses of their house aquavit - one horseradish and one cucumber. Both were quite nice! I will definitely be returning. I really enjoyed the drinks and overall ambiance. I plan to make reservations for dinner here soon.

I am being a bit generous with my rating with this restaurant because how often do you get to review a Scandinavian restaurant? "Nordic Cuisine is my favorite!" said no one ever but the menu and presentation at this restaurant is actually surprisingly pleasant.

I had the fixed menu and lost track of all the food that was served as they throw in extra dishes throughout dinner. I wouldn't say the food was particularly memorable but if you are coming in not knowing what to expect (which is all of us, minus our Nordic buddies) then you will be pleasantly surprised. Service is also exquisite so a star for that.

My one negative comment is for the decor and ambiance. Yeah our  Ikea founding Northern brothers are practical with furniture and mastered clean designs but high office chairs for dining? Uhm not very romantic. Naturally, although I was here for a date everyone else was making business deals. (That said if you want to ogle hot men in suits then please consider it a positive).

Bonus: It is also a check off the Michelin Star Restaurants list.

Upscale, quiet, wood grain, calm and serene environment. Wait staff were superb: always there with just one look, and even before you look. Enjoyed the tasting menu with wine pairings-absolutley delish. Quail egg, herring, smoked salmon, one dish had roasted hazelnuts with roasted cauliflower and herring-a very interesting and favorable combo. Tried squab for the first time and it was cooked just right and tender. I cannot recall each plate because there were so many! Dessert was an artistic edible birds nest with goat milk ice cream nuggets shaped like birds eggs. One was covered delicately in silver foil. The blueberry glaze around the nest tasted as if it were immediately prepared. If you want to really talk to someone during dinner, this may be your place. Everyone is having light easy toned discussions, and the music around you is very subtle. A very streamlined interior with a straight edged crowd.

This is a stellar restaurant and the experience was out of this world. Service was exceptional right down to printing out all that we experienced on a beautiful keepsake with date and a little wrapped homemade Kladdkaka. For a different taste, like Scandinavian, you have to try this out.

This review is not about the food, but my experience of coming here to dine for the first time.  I made a reservation on OpenTable for 10:30 PM on a Thursday night.  OpenTable also had 10:45 listed as an option.  I received a call at 10:32 asking if we were still coming.  I stated that we were in a taxi en route.  She said thank you and we ended the call.  We show up at 10:42, and were told that the Kitchen was shut down...sorry.  Really?  Don't accept reservations at 10:30, call at 10:32 to confirm and then shut your kitchen down.

Favourite dinner spot in the city! Outstanding quality scandinavian food the chef creates a perfect dinner every time we are there. 4 courses for $89 and it's worth every penny. You can also choose only one or two dishes from the menu or sit at the bar and enjoy some yummy bar food alternatives like swedish meatballs.

Truly a great experience!

Came here with my girl friends for one of my final meals in NYC.
Food was great. Loved the ambiance. Service was great--they weren't too intrusive.

I first encountered this restaurant when needing a private dining room for a team dinner. Even though I worked a block away and walked past it every evening, I didn't even know it was there until the events team showed me a menu! 

The team dinner went very well - and they were right, we definitely did not need a four flight tasting of aquavit per person! One shot of that stuff is lethal! 

So, I have been back a few times since, both for lunch and supper. I like the meatballs, but haven't tried much else. The wine list is lovely, the cocktails are better. The service is  smooth and friendly, but the place does feel a little cold and sterile. It is good for a clinical work meeting, but I wouldn't go on a date here or a large group of friends for a hilarious evening.

very very tasty food
great service
super fresh ingredients
i felt like i was in someone's garden and eating straight from it.

This review is long overdue, but I did the Valentine's Day pre-fixe menu and every course was amazing. They were small dishes that consisted of fresh greens, fish and meat. We had the wine parring with it and it went perfectly with each dish. I was skeptical I would be full after the meal, but it seemed like the dishes were just right. That night, the cook even gave us some appetizers and liquors on house.

It was the perfect romantic evening with a great waiter that made it for an even special date.

My husband and I visited Aquavit over our anniversary weekend for dinner.  We had a special American Express pre-theatre 3 course dinner with choice of Broadway show.  The dinner was incredible!  Aquavit gives the dinner so many extras - crispy fennel seed flatbread, pickled vegies, Smoked cream of white asparagus soup which was spectacular! It was like opening delicious  little presents throughout the meal.  The waiter brought a clear sealed jar which looked smoky and asked us to open it.  A puff of smoke escapes to show that the quail egg and salmon roe was smoked.  Then the waiter pours the cool cream of asp. soup in the jar.  It was heaven on earth!  Each item was delectable.  We plan to go there again the next time we visit NY.  It was the best meal we had in NY and we went to other up scale restaurants that weekend and a previous weekend.  I highly recommend this restaurant for it's food and drinks, creativity, presentation, and great service.  I found the Aquavit cookbook in the library and have made a few things. I like to cook.   I would really like to find the Cream of Asparagus soup recipe.   We still dream about that meal!

thanks to restaurant week -

Loved their ambiance and atmosphere. it is a sophisticated place with good food. You won't regret to check this place out!

Came here for Restaurant week yesterday.

Reservation was at 7. We arrived on time and were seated immediately. I think all the R/W people were seated in a separate dining room (weird). Surprised it was a legit buffet where you would have to get up and choose your food. Thought I could order whatever was on the menu and have a waiter bring it to me (I wish of course). 

Portions were good for me. I really only needed one bite of everything. For the $35 price tag, you get to try everything on the R/W menu. I've never had an experience like this and the food was different, so it was definitely worth coming. 

Everything was good except for the one herring I had (not sure which it was, but try them all anyway), the dessert was mediocre. And the entree options were somewhat limited. 

Bottom line: The appetizers were great. Entrees were okay. Dessert was disappointing, but still better than many establishments.

Overall, my gf and I left full and pleasantly surprised.

A must go for us.

Been here a couple of times this summer for lunch, and love it.  It's very close to work, but I'd actually make a trip for it.  The food is very good, and the menu is quite unique.

If you're going for lunch, I'd actually recommend the Prix Fixe.  You have a choice of one of two appetizers and one of two main dishes, and you get a dessert of panna cotta.  You'll drop $42 for some excellent food (a couple of the best dishes on the menu are on the Prix Fixe), and the Prix Fixe represents quite a value: (you basically are getting dessert free).  Plus, they don't skimp on portions when you order off the Prix Fixe.  We paid attention to this: some of us ordered meatballs off the Prix Fixe and some of us ordered it a la carte, and the portions were the same.

The food here, as I said, is great.  Try the gravlax, which is delicious.  It's presented differently than usual; instead of thin slices, it's a small cylinder.  Very good, though.  Flavorful and smokey!  I had a tuna tartare at one point, and it was amazing.  Very well put together.  Nice texture with a crunch topping, but it really let the tuna flavor shine through.  The meatballs are just amazing.  The salmon burger is huge, but reportedly great.  The char looks good, too.

For dessert, the Cardamom Panna Cotta is tasty, and comes with the Prix Fixe.  Oh, and when they come around to give you bread, get the rye - it's something else!

I really want to go back and actually try some of the aquavit - they have a ton of different flavors on the menu.

Service is good and attentive, and presentation is beautiful.

This is one of my favorite lunches in Midtown.  It's a good value, and very, very good.  Do it, do it, do it!

About a year ago, during restaurant week, a friend of mine had a lackluster experience with the service at Aquavit.  He emailed the restaurant about it and they offered him a $100 gift card.  I jumped at the chance to try this place when he invited me.

First off, we were given great service for the duration of the night. We were greeted by the head of public relations for the restaurant. She was very pleasant. It seemed like we didn't go more than 5 minutes without being served an amuse-bouche or something we'd ordered from the menu. Among the highlights for me were pickled vegetables and quail eggs, the heirloom tomatoes with cheese ice cream appetizer, and a chilled corn chowder that was served in a smoky jar.  My entree was decent, Arctic Char with crayfish and broccoli puree. It was a small amount of food for an entree and I wished that I'd asked if the crayfish were served in their shells (they weren't).  

I enjoyed the cocktails with actual Aquavit in them. Both the White Negroni and their take on a Manhattan were enjoyable.  For Dessert, we were given a plate of assorted items. The cinnamon sugar doughnut stuffed with some sort of cream was the highlight of that course.  

My one complaint is that our meal ended up costing around $200 and I was barely full at the end of the night. This was with the maximum amount of amuse-bouches that not every table receives, 2 appetizers, bread, an entree, and 2 rounds of dessert. I really enjoyed everything though. Patrick Stewart was sitting in the next booth over from us. If Aquavit is good enough for him, it's certainly good enough for me.

Chef's menu was one of the best I have had in the city. Better than some of the three Michelin establishments in town. 

We came in rather late, and got a table immediately. Of the amuse bouche, the corn cream soup was the most memorable, but there were a few other good ones.

It is hot and muggy and the plural use of flash frozen garnish was perfect. 

My favorite dishes were the ocean char and the desert bird's egg nest. L was head over heals for he foie gras dish and the wagyu course.

It was all in all a great experience with excellent food.

I think if this restaurant was either a little bit further west, or a lot further south, it would have gotten a lot more recognition. As it were, it is worth the trip to East 55th.
This food is so fancy and refined compared to traditional Scandinavian food, I'd call it "inspired by" Scandinavian.

My new husband and i took our best man and maid of honor out for a post nuptials dinner.  I'm a fan of new scandinavian, and thought it would be fun to see how an old-school classic has responded to new trends.  Recent reports have indicated that aquavit has upped their game, but that did not come through on our visit.

We were greeted by a very sweet reservationist, who sent us to the bar while we waited for our friends.  The bar area was handsomely  spare, with saddle leather jacobson swan chairs/settees, blond wood, and decorated with  giant ice-cube shaped jars of fermenting aquaviit, downlit on a ledge that runs accross the room.  I was pleasently surprised to find a few tables of young hipster-types dining in the bar. I greatly enjoyed a fennel and caraway aquavit.

When our company arrived, i was reminded that the MOH was vegan, and coming off a 7-day fast (yikes). I quickly notified the hostess, who happily assured me this would not be a problem (phew).  We were seated in the one center table of the mostly empty room.  All other tables were typical four-tops set with wegner round chairs,  and a few booths.  Our center table was a large round Saarinen marble pedestal, with dramatic highback jacobsen swivel executive chairs.  It was so austin powers groovy that we were at first excited.  The set-up quickly proved impractical for how the restaurant served many courses.  

The waiter immediately informed us that the chef could adapt about 4 dished for a vegan tasting menu or a la carte ordering.  The fasting MOH felt she wasnt up to a full menu commitment, and planned to order a couple plates. The three of us wanted to try the 5 course summer menu ($95).  Waiter asked chef, and chef ok'd our request for a tasting minus one guest. So far so good.

Five rounds of amuse bouche, and delicious bread with whipped butter(s) followed.   First, a basket of various "chips" comprised of amazingly thin, transparent sheets of deydrated vegtables such as butternut squash. Very tasty, great texture and interesting.  The small bowl was placed in the center of the table, and was a long reach for each of us to access.  Next was a slate tray of  "lollipops" for the table to share. Skewers of radishs, pickled fruit,etc, on a plate too ungainly to pass, and which again, left us with an awkward reach to access. The skewers did not register as paricularly interesting, as didnt the shared tin can of pickled vegetables, pickled egg, and anchovy oil.   The spoonful of pickled fish in a bit of creamy sauces was better, and served individually, which was better yet. Most dramatic was the mason jar filled with smoke, with a corn salad at the bottom.  It looked, smelled, and tasted great.  The kitchen very generously made vegan versions of each, on the spot, for the MOH.

First course was a shockingly bland pickled herring plate served with a sparkling wine.  A couple of small, very lightly pickled pieces of fish lost in an ocean of cream sauce with a few boiled potatos.  The fish were so timidly pickled that their flavor was overwhelmed by cream!  Crazy stuff.

Next was a tomato salad, which was basically that...a plate of tomatoes, lightly dressed in a vinegar/oil, with a lone shaving of prosciutto and a dollop of mozzerella ice cream on the side. The cheese icecream did all the heavy lifting.  Otherwise, it was a plate of not quite in season tomatos.

Cubed Fois gras, with corn kernels, and a sauce of frozen buttermilk ladled table-side. Delicious, the textures and flavored married beautifully, although not much to look at.

Intermezzo of frozen shreded sorrel leaves followed, with prosecco poured over tableside.  Didnt find the clump of frozen leaves pleasent in the mouth, but it was more intersting and tasty than the tomato salad.

The main course was a cube of possibly sous vide turbot, on a plate of many composed elements....a ribbon of beet gelee, a pile of shaved frozen horseradish, scattered edible flowers.  It was very pretty, but again quite flavorless.  The turbot had exceedingly mild flavor, and none of the textural qualities one expects. It wasnt flakey, steaky, or silky, but more accurately mealy.  The frozen horseradish had no horsepower, the beet jelly no concentrated beetiness. 

Desert was an inoffensive bowl of berries, balls of cake and ice cream, followed by more shared, hard to reach plates of petit fours, cookies and such, which went mostly uneaten. 

Btw, the vegan was thrilled with her dishes.  

Service was perfunctory, verging on brusque. Granted we threw a lot of last minute curve balls at them. But while the maitre d' and kitchen made us feel at ease, even pampered,  the waiter exuded a weary disapproval, and came off as a bit of a sourpuss. He was also a bit sloppy with the hand-pour, with dribbles of wine and sauce dripping down the sides of dishes/glasses after each pour.  

All in all, i had to Aska myself if this was the center of nyc scandinavian dining. Acme again, and I'd have to say no
This place was fantastic.  The food was creative and delicious.  The service was impeccable.  Of course, it is not cheap, but if you're willing to pay, it is well worth it.

I came here this summer for the three course business lunch.  I started with the smoked salmon.  Absolutely delicious -- this was the highlight of the meal!  I then got the meatballs.  Frankly, I think this tasted very similar to the meatballs I can get at IKEA.  And considering how much I was paying, I was expecting more.  Perhaps more delicate plating, or some kind of distinguishing flavor.  I have to give them some credit for the huge serving.  I wasn't able to finish my heap of meatballs.  As for dessert, I mildly remember ordering something with mango. Overall, a mediocre, overpriced lunch in midtown.  The decor is nice, but unfortunately, also looks like everything is straight out of IKEA.

Fine dining with a nouveau Scandinavian flair. Tapas/taste style menu in a couple versions with wine pairings if you prefer. Preparation and presentation are exquisite and highly creative. Jazz music completes the setting.

LOVE LOVE LOVE.
there really isn't too much to say about this place. its fabulous, beautiful, innovative...we had a party of 6 and everyone enjoyed it. a must do dining experience.
An unforgettable experience. Every course had its own unique, amazing flavor. Aquavit is unlike anything I've ever had.

Mine is a dissenting view of a once charming and delicious restaurant.  We dined there on Sept. 25 and found ourselves in a nearly empty room [with fur-like throws on the backs of chairs to simulate diners out for a moment] .   The atmosphere was formal and hushed with a host who was so stiff he actually apologized  when we mentioned having seen a lousy play that afternoon.  As for the food, the grav-lox was insipid; lacking in taste, resembling a barely poached salmon strip.  My foi gras was surrounded with  a melange of veggie which were described  by the indiffererent waiter in a barely audible voice.  My next course was a favorite of mine, sweetbreads, but   rendered dry and devoid of taste, having been fried.  They too were requiring of a recital by the inaudible, rapid speaking waiter.  Overall, my food was dull and too precious.  The best items were the chef's offerings...Otherwise the evening was a great disappointment, and we sorely missed the flavors of the old Aquavit... There will not be a return visit.

Both the food and the service at Aquavit are extraordinary.  I went for a birthday dinner with friends, and after trying some of their very interesting cocktails, had the tasting menu.  It was full of interesting contrasts and unique and vivid flavors, and the 'arctic bird's nest' dessert was just incredible.  The staff were extremely attentive, and were delighted to accommodate the people in our group who would not eat red meat.   For all the hype about the newer Nordic restaurants in Greenpoint, in my judgment Aquavit is still the best in New York, and one of the most interesting of New York's great restaurants.

Celebrated our 10yr wedding anniversary there and enjoyed every minute (we were there for 4.5 hours). We ordered the Chef's Tasting menu with Beverage Pairing (instead of wine, 1 course had sake and the other beer). There are 8 courses on the menu but it ends up being like 15 courses because they bring out a lot of surprises. 

If you are craving something in particular, don't go here. BUT do go if you want to try many exciting and flavorful dishes. The food combinations are interesting and hard to describe- you just have to try it for yourself.

Everything was A+++ (food, service, and ambiance)
Serously, Woohoo! As GOOD as it gets!

This restaurant reminds me of a gifted athlete who keeps getting in trouble with the law. Just a few examples.

The bar is never crowded, possibly because it has uncomfortable bar stools. The lounge is also not optimized for hanging out and racking up large bills.

Aquavit's food pairs well with champagne. For a while, the menu offered a mind blowing grower champagne available by the glass. Now it has reverted back to second tier boring choices available at your local wine store.

This restaurant has terrific food. But it's not as much of a destination as it could be if it expanded its wines by the glass program and provided comfortable seating at the bar.

Sometimes you want to plan in advance and eat in a dining room but more often you want to eat at a bar with a friend on the spur of the moment without a reservation (maybe this applies only to Gen X). Aquavit is missing out on the latter market.

Amazing service and food. I brought my fiance here for his birthday. We did the chef tasting with wine pairing & they were very accommodating when we requested a table change. You will not be disappointed.

My favorite restaurant in the city.  I am 98% vegan, and the 2% of the time I am not I can be found eating here.  The herring here is among the best you can find in America.  The different sauces and styles, the potatoes that accompany them, the crisp breads, all add up to a savory, succulent feast.  

I also recommend flights of aquavit for which they are famous.  Unless you are rich, this is not your everyday restaurant, but this is the place for special occasions.

Aquavit has a great balance of great service and friendly atmosphere, without being uptight or pretentious.

It was an experience at Aquavit. A modern take on Nordic cuisine at its best. The Chefs tasting menu felt like it was never going to end. Food was great, staff was attentive and helpful. All the plates were very appealing. Definitely will be back.

If you can't find it here, you can't find it anywhere. That's how I feel about New York and what brought me to Aquavit. It's rare to find upscale Nordic food. I've lived in the Pacific Northwest which has a significant Scandinavian population, but no Scandinavian restaurants. I've also lived in Southern California where Scandinavian food mainly exists in the touristy Solvang which is mostly Danish.

When I mentioned Aquavit, every New Yorker replied, "I've been there, but a long time ago." The restaurant didn't look old enough to have existed a long time ago. The style of food also wasn't from a long time ago. I'm guessing Aquavit has changed with the times.

Because of the rare Nordic influence, I ordered rather traditional at the bar. I started with the sampler of three types of herring. I hate to admit this, but if I were blindfolded, I couldn't tell the different types of herring apart because they all tasted similar - just different types of highly fishy fish. The Swedish meatballs were just like the ones at Ikea. Just kidding. (I've never had Ikea meatballs so I really don't know.) Not kidding, the meatballs themselves were ordinary. The sides of lingonberries, potato puree, and pickled cucumber salad made the dish fun to eat and showed the delicate combination of contrasting acids and sweetness being presented. The contrasting harmony of tastes was most evident in the "Autumn Dashi" which was the best dish of the three. Although the dish used all earthy ingredients, the soup contained foie gras, sliced radish, kelp, and a ragu of oxtail. Mixing the earthiness from vegetable, animal, and sea can be a dangerous recipe which chef Marcus Jernmark cleverly avoids. Of course, I had to order this dish because it had foie gras. I do this on every visit to New York since the sustainable foie was banned in my home state of California.

The bar offers cocktails with a Scandinavian twist which mainly comes from infused aquavits. Like the dashi, the "Gothenberg Gibson" used kelp in the form of kelp aquavit. It was a tight, dry drink that was suitable for rye bread-like flavors. The "Madison Avenue Manhattan" used fig and cardamom aquavit to create a fuller, more satisfying Manhattan.

There were no earthshaking dishes that I would rave endlessly about, but I deeply enjoyed the harmonious combinations with detailed prep work in a satisfying, homey comfort food way.

Wow, had tickets to see the New York Pops at Carnegie Hall, so decided to do the 'theater pre-fixe'.

First of all, when you come it you are put in the mood with the beautiful Scandinavian design. The chairs draped with fleeces were a nice touch. Anyway, I've never really had Nordic food before, outside of very Americanized things like Swedish meatballs and gravlax. 

As other mentioned, they do bring out a lot of surprises. Before starting out, had a set of canapes: micro-radish with brown butter, a piece of black garlic, crisped seaweed topped with lobster and uni (and more!)... next was an amuse bouche, crisped tapioca with quail egg smothered in a celeriac soup. 

We had 2 first courses: the beet stained gravlax (topped with freeze dried foie gras!) are surprisingly sweet; and a herring covered in a bernaise that I can't do justice to describe. 

The main courses were also very nice: cod with scallops and the 'lambs neck' which had this rich cheese bechamel. It's amazing how the traditional herbal flavors (coriander and dill) are present in many of the dishes, but never overpowering. 

Finally dessert. Small pastries with a chocolate theme and also a creme brulee, both excellent. What probably put us over the top were the additional little sweet bites they brought out with the check. 

Overall a wonderful experience with great service. Hopefully we can come back and try other dishes next time!

A friend recommended Aquavit for their Christmas Eve Julbord. He spoke of a faaaabulous dinning room with fur throws and a warm cozy atmosphere. I wanted to go just hearing about this! However, even with a reservation we were put in a back room which felt like we were being escorted away from the adults and put in the kids corner. It was really odd and I can't say I was very happy about it. No dark candle lit room for us with fur throws. Instead it was a very uninviting "events room". I already felt turned off.

Since I am not a fan of crazy fish dishes I can't speak of loving the foods however, my husband and friend enjoyed a lot of the choices at the buffet. The glögg was the best thing I drank all night. I think I finished off three glasses of it. There was a celery soup to die for as well. 

I simply recommend going on a regular night and trying a few things. The $88/person buffet for Christmas Eve wasn't really my speed given our seating location and the amount of items I didn't enjoy, but if you're down for Scandinavian food I do recommend giving this place a try. 

Oh, we did order the Fig & Cardamom Aquavit as well as the Vanilla, Pear, Pepper Aquavit. Both were delicious but be prepared for the alcohol level. It'll practically asphyxiate you!

Great ambiance, incredibly attentive service, and even better food. The Bird Nest dessert is to die for. 

A must stop for NYC.

In my opinion, there's no better way to pamper yourself like dining at a Michelin starred restaurant. Aquavit was a treat. Unfortunately I was not hungry enough to have the tasting menu (looked fantastic though) so we got the a la carte. Before that they brought out a few interesting amuse bouches, including seaweed chips, and a celery soup that was delicious. 
I ordered the Scottish langoustine crudo as the starter. At first glance it looked a bit disappointing- some fennel and cucumber in a bowl. But underneath the greens was the treasure - a beautiful piece of langoustine and fresh sea urchin. I instantly wanted more. The monkfish main was also fantastic. It was perfectly cooked, and the octopus on the place was as tender as can be. Everything was also beautifully presented as it should be. 
Will be back to try the tasting menu next time.
Went to this place about a year ago and still have not been able to forget its incredible food. Simply amazing! The duck foie gras is out of this world.

I had dinner last night and can't say enough about how creative each dish was. We started with 4 complimentary amuse bouche that were terrific -- and what a nice way to start the meal. I had a first course of grav lax that was tremendous; my companion chose the herring which was equally wonderful. For the main course, we had monkfish and cod, both excellent. For dessert, an apple tart flavored with tarragon among other things. I've never had more interesting, fresh and flavorful food (and the coffee is awesome, too). Everything was beautifully presented and the staff was flawless. The portions are very small, but I was nonetheless very full when we left. It's expensive, but for a special treat, worth it.

Tasting at Michelin Star One restaurant was such a great experience. The food was superb so the layout and atmosphere were. 

Price tag doesn't concern me but the quality of accommodation is somewhat troubling me because we are deaf and we hoped this restaurant can cater and communicate with us thru pen and paper so we can understand the food the waitress explained. 

Regardless of lack of accommodation, the food was great and exceeded my expectations.

With the recent popularity of Nordic cuisine in NYC's dining scene (mostly attributable to newly opened restaurants such as Aska and Skal), it's easy to overlook Aquavit, a modest restaurant situated in Midtown East. For nearly three decades, it's been quietly serving up Scandinavian dishes with more than just a few modern twists; thankfully, the Michelin inspectors were thorough enough to award this restaurant one Michelin star for the past few consecutive years [1].

I came to Aquavit just one week after my visit to Per Se, so my expectations going in were already high. My dining companions and I had initially agreed beforehand to opt for the Seasonal Tasting, but upon being seated and given menus, realized that the courses we had seen posted online were completely different from the ones printed in front of us. A last-minute consensus was reached and we immediately decided to switch to the longer (and more expensive) Chef's Tasting Menu, which was a decision that none of us regretted.

Our meal began with a seemingly never-ending barrage of amuses: a variety of vegetables served on skewers, baked kale chips, a crisp cracker dotted with flax seeds, and the absolute favorite of the night: a smoked jar of tapioca pearls that was covered over with a foie gras and mushroom emulsion. By the time our actual first course arrived, it was well over an hour into the meal.

As for the actual courses - each was a creative and surprising plate, and nothing close to what I would have initially considered "Scandinavian". The Beet Gravlax was one of the most memorable presentations of the night, as the cured salmon formed a yin-yang curve across the plate and was dotted with shaved foie gras, pickled mustard seeds, and hovmästar sauce. While slivers of foie gras aren't my first choice of such an ingredient, the overall contrasts of textures and tastes encouraged bite after bite after bite as my taste buds attempted to make sense of what I was eating. The Sweetbread and Langoustine paired a perfectly cooked sweetbread with langoustine, complimented with a lightly smoked stalk of onion. And the Winter Dashi featured a myriad of vegetables with two pieces of melt-in-your-mouth foie gras, all enveloped in a clean yet savory dashi broth.

I could go on. I could rave about the perfectly-cooked Cod with Crones, the slightly controversial Squab with Apple (which featured the entire squab leg, including the claws), and the smartly selected cheese plate. But Aquavit's dessert deserves its own paragraph as it's one you won't encounter elsewhere: The Arctic Bird's Nest. The nest is made up of a crunchy, straw-like tuile that surrounds three "eggs". The eggs themselves are a remarkable product, made of goat cheese parfait and blueberry sorbet and finished off with a crisp white chocolate shell. The center of each egg has a surprise - a bright yellow filling of sea-buckthorn. The plate is finished off with garnishes of "snow" and chocolate "dirt", which rounds out a masterpiece of a dessert. Eating this dish was synonymous with destroying a work of art, but to leave it untouched would have been an even greater travesty.

In hindsight, I will say this: I was far more impressed with the food I was served at (one Michelin-starred) Aquavit than I was at (three Michelin-starred) Per Se. There's something about the food that pushes boundaries; that tempts and teases all dimensions of taste, flavor, and texture; that makes you remember in exact detail each and every bite, even many months later. And if that kind of experience isn't worth five stars, then I don't know what is.

--
[1] Congratulations to Aquavit for obtaining their two Michelin stars for 2015!
So happy I came here! Everything was quite balanced in flavor and texture. Had the chef tasting and there was no drought in presentation, style or flavors.

I want to give this place a more detailed review, but I fear that my memory is incapable of keeping track of the 20+ dishes we received. There were probably only 9-10 dishes on the tasting menu, but the extras we received from the kitchen (which are fairly standard from what I've heard and read) doubled that amount easily.

Food here is superb, chef is also incredibly nice, and it's a great place to celebrate a special occasion; I really, really recommend this place.

Incredible food, relaxing atmosphere, fantastic service! This was not only a delicious night out, but a delightful experience. We ordered the Spring Tasting menu with the wine pairing- everything was absolutely perfect and exceeded our expectations!

Went here for a business dinner last night. Unsure if my review will be fair as we were given a private room. 

I had sweetbreads for an appetizer. I was unsure what I'd get but it turned out great and included some white beets (and I am a beet fan!). Strip sirloin was an awesome entree. Mango dessert was equally good. 

The wine selection and service were impeccable. Downside?  Nyc prices for this standard will drain the wallet. :-)

I had lunch at Aquavit last Tuesday and was just blown over. I have been noted for saying that I just don't get Scandinavian food but now I am a believer. The fish was so fresh and flavorful. The smoked lamb tartar was inventive and packed with flavor. We had cod for our entree and it was cooked (sous vide?) to perfection. I live in the Midwest and was craving fish, next time I'm in New York this will be my go-to spot.

I've eaten here twice now and both times were amazing. From the decor, to the perfectly timed service, to the creative foods presentations, and of course the food itself, this is one of my favorite restaurants both in NYC and the world. That sounds like a platitude, but I mean it sincerely. If you have an opportunity, do yourself a favor and go!

This review is very late as I was at Aquavit with my wife back in October of '13.

We had a reservation via Groupon.  The arrival time was for a 9pm.  Upon arrival, we were told there were still diners occupying the tables and we would have a short wait.  After waiting for 20 minutes we were told we could eat at the bar.  The reason was the tasting menu offered at that time was taking longer for diners to finish.  They were apologetic.  We wanted a table and were willing to wait.  Another 20 min went by and they felt horrible, offering is drinks and apps.  We again turned it down and waited patiently.  Another five minutes passed and the manager came over to us.  He offered us drinks at the bar and to start eating our dinner there until a table opened up.  We agreed.

At the bar we were given a really good bottle of wine and 3 shots of their Aquavit.  We ordered our dinners there.  Shortly after our apps arrived.  We ate those at the bar.  We were then given a table.  We had our full meals with dessert.  

When I asked for the bill, the head waiter instructed us that the entire meal was gratis.  The manager and head chef felt horrible for our wait.  I was beside myself as was my wife.  What a generous offering.  I never complained.  We sat there patiently waiting for a table.  My only regret was not having enough cash to tip everyone.  I was counting on paying the full check and tip on my credit card.  I wish I could have done more.  

My final thoughts on Aquavit.  It's a great experience in Scandinavian cuisine.  The wait staff, bartender and chef are friendly and very professional.  I look forward to dining at Aquavit again in the future.
One word-spectacular. We chose this restaurant for our thanksgiving meal in 2012. Would go there again and again if reservations were not so hard to secure.

I received one of the most embarrassingly bad experiences in this restaurant that I have ever received tonight.  I frequently entertain business clients in expensive restaurants, and occasionally I ask a friend at the last minute to join.  Tonight I brought a friend to the bar to have a drink before the planned dinner.  The bartender and hostess told me that if I had the drink at the bar, thus delaying the start of my dinner that I would have to wait 45 minutes for my table!  Of course the restaurant was never full throughout the evening, it was entirely rudeness on the part of the staff.  I paid over a thousand dollars for the dinner for four that followed but I can assure you I will never bring guests to this terrible restaurant again.

The more I dine at high end restaurants, the more that I realize that Aquavit does it right.  At this price range, there should be amazing food and service and this place delivers.  They place your napkin on your lap when you sit down, the manager will often check to make sure that everything is to your liking, they will clean the bread crumbs from the table between courses, etc.  And most importantly, the delicious food always looks and tastes exquisite.  The restaurant is beautifully decorated, the high ceilings makes the place look huge, and the staff operate like a finely tuned machine.  This is one of the few places at this range that we are happy to pay full price for.

Overrated. A poor dining experience for the value paid. We dined here on Valentines Day which historically is every restaurants worst nightmare. However, Valentines Day should not be used as an excuse for mediocre food - that's expected during NYC Restaurant Week.

My expectations were high based on the 4/5 star reviews and beautiful presentation I've seen in photos. The set course menu was terrible. Almost every item was a chilled/cold dish and the dessert was sad. There was not one memorable dish. Where food lacks, service should make up right? Wrong. I got barely any attention from the staff, no description of what was plated, and was ignored by waiters. We wrote a long complaint on their comment card at the end of our meal describing our lackluster experience and left contact information. Again, our opinions were ignored. Save your money and dine elsewhere.

Disclaimer: Restaurant Week menu reviewed below. 

Pros: Superb Food including the Herring Tartare. Attentive and friendly service. Very interesting selection of "Aquavit" alcohol that tries to punches you in the mouth but ends up giving you a peck on the cheek. 

Cons: Not to much that I can think of, maybe the price could be a little steep without the restaurant week menu, but that really is to be expected in the concrete jungle of Manhattan.

Bottomline: The establishment was generous enough to give us a $50 gift certificate for our next visit, not knowing they have already guaranteed our return with great food and service.

We went to aquavit for the herring festival that had been an annual event for years. In the past it had a full table of various kinds of herrings.  This year the event involved four small pieces of herring. The other dishes were mediocre at best.This event is clearly over. Aqavit advertised and took reservations with no notice of the fundamental change and the actual service was consistent with that lack of customer concern. The service was remarkable. With the place half empty service personnel moved as if they had just been told they had just been fired. If you can get a mental image of a zombie serving staff you get the picture. If you want zombie service I highly recommend aquavit.

Great lunch spot in midtown west. I thought I'd hate it after reading the menu online but ended up loving it. I've gone back since. The salmon burger, which has been on the menu for a while, is awesome.

When was the last time you have Scandinavia cuisine ???

Thank for my MBA school reunion back to 2013 May and let me discover this hidden gem. Until today I still remember how I was pleasantly surprised by my dinning experience in Aquavit. 

We were seven people and ordered several dishes to try. Every single one came out like a piece of art work. Beautiful presentations, Unexpected textures and components. Unique aroma came out from a small jar full of fresh vegetables and caviars. Nowadays I still can't relate anything else to this jar. :) 

I definitely will recommend Aquavit to all the foodie fellows out there ^_^

Came back here recently - the food is EXCELLENT!  The three course lunch prix fixe for $48 is still one of the best deals in this part of town.  

There were a couple of underwhelming aspects this time around: the desserts were mediocre, and so was the service.  Our server might have been under the weather, but didn't seem very interested in answering our questions about the menu.  Anyhoo, on to the food -- they currently have their annual herring festival, which is actually pretty awesome.  I got the herring sampler, which has five different preparations of herring, each one more interesting than the last.  For the entree, I tried the sea scallops, which were fantastic, and a very generous portion (three large scallops).  Didn't do the prix fixe this time, but I was assured by my co-diners that the bouillabaisse is still wonderful.  Aquavit remains one of my favorite spots in midtown east.

Had the set menu w/ my wife. Everything was great. They even made lutefisk taste great. The Birds Nest desert is heavenly. If you like Scandinavian food and want a modern twist on it this place is a must.
Should have 2 Michelin Stars.  Dinner was well attended from start to finish.  Beautifully plated food.  Unique and creative flavors and aromas.  A truly wonderful dining experience..

Came here with a three-course dinner Groupon deal for two.  Thou we were 15 minute late due to traffic, we were seated right away.  They have a separated menu for Groupon and have 2 choices for each course.  They have an interesting cocktail selection and I tried the cucumber reviver.  Very tasty and refreshing for the hot summer.  The service was excellent for the night and the food was amazing.  Lots of complimentary treats and bigger then expected food portion.  There's really nothing to complaint about for the meal.

Aquavit 
 
Ambiance 
 
Close your eyes and imagine classy but simple, fancy but sophisticated, chic but with a "twist". This place has it all.  I can best describe it with this combination of words; exquisite seasonal Nordic cuisine.  What I'm trying to say is this. Even though it's a midtown restaurant where the norm is a "business dinner" or "let me take my out of town clients to a nice place", don't be fooled!  Does anyone in the US really know what Nordic cuisine is?  I mean really know?  No offense to anyone but I would say the answer by the majority of people would be a resounding "no".  I'll even go one step further.  Does anyone in the US really know what the Nordic countries are?  Ok, I'll stop here.  :)
 
Back to the review.  This restaurant still has the "expected" bar/ lounge area.  You will find the usual after work "finance guys" crowd reviewing the Dow Jones and Nasdaq day's events.  But please don't judge a book by its cover!  The crowd in the dining room definitely knows why they are there.  They know Nordic food.  They have that "experienced fine diner" look to them. 
 
Food
 
First of all Nordic cuisine has a limited option of ingredients, especially vegetables. I personally think it's an advantage.  I will explain why.  Everything they use is grown in a pure natural environment without the use of chemicals.  The ingredients used are dependent on the time of year.  The result is a "limited edition" of dishes based on what is available for that particular period that "fit" the time of year.  Nordic cuisine also has a knack of being able to keep food edible during seasonal changes without the use of commercial preservatives. Generations of people have passed this "art" of growing the right ingredients and preparing these seasonal dishes.  This style of cooking is so much more complicated than the styles used in Italy and France for instance.  Those countries have great climates with great soil.  Most if not all of their ingredients are available year round.  They spend more time working on culinary perfection rather than thinking about what vegetable will be available in the next couple of months.  Don't get me wrong I love Italian and French cuisine. Please don't throw stones at me.
 
I tried their seasonal tasting menu.  It was awesome!  Aquavit  is one of the places I would definitely recommend to try the tasting menu. Sometimes you can surprise yourself in a good way.  Their a la carte menu is American with a Nordic touch.  It looks ok but I would still recommend the tasting menu. 
 
Service
 
Their service is awesome.  They have great team work and a lot of energy. The staff really does care about your dining experience and of course they are very knowledgeable.  When serving Nordic cuisine you have to be knowledgeable about what you are serving.  I didn't select wine pairing with the seasonal tasting menu but our server and manager took care of that for me.  They recommended the best wines for each particular dish.  I appreciated that so much.  It is so important to me not to have feeling of  being "pushed" ... for whatever reason.  I've experienced that too many times.  Certain restaurants trying to "push" a specific tasting menu or wine pairing to their customers. 

Conclusion
 
If you are looking for a place to eat with somebody who appreciates the art of international cuisine, small small portions but huge quality and value with every dish, you found the perfect restaurant.  Some say nothing is perfect.  I say Aquavit in NYC is synonymous with Nordic cuisine perfection.

Amazing food here, and service and presentation of food was great too. 

Food wise, the foie gras 1st course was exquisite! Perfectly seared and so flavorful. 

I had the duck for the main, and it was just as delicious. Crackling crispy skin, and tender meat. 

Price was pretty decent for a 1 Michelin star too, so it deserves all 5 stars.

I came in for lunch and the restaurant was phenomenal. First off the atmosphere is like being in some trendy/mad bougie swedish living room - Ikea, this is not. Service was fantastic from start to finish.

I had the Scandinavian bouillabaisse for my main and started with the caviar and toasts. The caviar and garnish were really good, though I don't think it's something I would ever crave. The bouillabaisse was amazing. It's not a soup like traditional bouillabaisse; more like seafood with a sauce and foam. There was a wide variety of fish and shellfish, all of which were perfectly done and fresh as can be.

For drinks i had the Swedish 77 and their Manhattan. both were delicious well thought out drinks. I would recommend it to anyone down to pay the high price.

We got a private room for dining with a prix fix menu

amazing as hell i'd have to say

the foie gras was amazing... melts in your mouth.. and it is a HUGE piece too

entree we had salmon and pork belly

personally i liked the pork belly much better.

We had diner here yesterday and all I can say is that this is an amazing place!!!!! They go above and beyond with the food, presentation and service. Exceeded every expectation we had! Get the tasting menu if you go, worth every penny. Also get one of their mixed aquavit cocktails, just perfection!
great food.. good service.. one star michellin restaurant. great nordic cuisine restaurant

I'm a fan of smoked and pickled things, and this place has them.

I ended up trying a lot more than what I had expected thanks to a generous number of amuse-bouches between each course. My SO, who had never tried Scandinavian cuisine prior, thanks to her experience here, is now a convert.

The decor in the main dining room is very plain - the ceiling is actually classic office conference room, albeit with cute hanging lamps to try to distract from it.  The service was scattered, as a different person serves you as your meal progresses - too chaotic for my taste.  The food was way too much - I didn't even finish each course in the tasting menu and ended up bloated and over-stuffed anyway -- very unhealthy!  The food had a few (well, one) knock out item - the foie gras with novel accoutrements.  A few others were interesting, many plain.  It took too long for the courses to come out, or even start, and at this price point, I'd expect more efficiency.  And a nicer dining room.

Food was testy, but service was not up to the standards of what a two Michelin star restaurant should be. There are too many staff members walking around but not coordinating with each other about the needs of each table. And forget it, if you have certain dietary restrictions. They will bring you what you can't eat, a few times... I'd say spend your hard earned money on another two or three Michelin star restaurant, NYC has more than enough of those to be stuck coming back here.

Don't get the chef's tasting menu, this place creates amazing-looking dishes without regard to taste. The nest egg dessert is beautiful...until biting into it. Same with the sweetbread and sauerkraut dish, drowning a small piece of sweetbread in a quarter-gallon of cream. But then again, it's all about looks: gorgeously-arranged in a neat cylinder held up by thin apple slices and fruit that you'll never be able to taste after getting slaughtered with overpowering cream.

The amuse-bouches were the best dishes of the night and, not coincidentally, the simplest dishes. The rest of the menu is expensive form-over-function. This recently got two stars from Michelin, it shouldn't have gotten one.

PS: The cocktails were garbage. Just like the food, someone took a good-not-great drink idea and added two or three contradictory ingredients in the name of complexity and creativity but not quality.

I've had the chefs summer tasting menu here. From the moment I walked in I knew it was going to be a great dinner. The decor is unique and unlike most places in the city. We were immediately greeted with an amuse bouche. The cocktails were delicious. The tasting menu itself was very diverse and had a lot of variety. The chef came and greeted us in the middle of the meal to ask if everything was okay. The waitstaff was more than attentive. The meal ended with a desert called the arctic bird's nest, it was truly a piece of art. It looked beautiful but tasted even better! I can't wait to go back again.

Hands down one of the best dining experience I've ever had! Extremely tasty food and drink coupled with very attentive service make this a memorable evening for any of you seeking that!

There is construction going on on their street, which is probably quite damaging to the traffic coming through. Which may explain why such a superb Michelin-starred restaurant has a Groupon offer. My fiancé and I came here on the aforementioned groupon which entitled us to either 2 of the three course prix fixe or a la carte to the value of the voucher ($130). We went for the prix fixe and each ordered one of the 2 options offered for each course so that we could taste a variety of dishes. 

I started out ordering a flight of 3 Aquavit (the drink from which the restaurant derived their name). These are essentially tall shots of flavored Swedish spirits. We wanted to taste a variety of the dozen or so flavors. We went for unique combinations like horseradish; mango, lime & chilli; and grilled pineapple. Very interesting flavor profiles and a unique experience to begin the meal. Would be intrigued to try a few of the other flavors too. Ps at $17 for the flight of 3, I thought it was actually pretty good value too (as a single cocktail goes for a similar price)  

Onto the food:
To be honest, I am easily won over by superbly executed bread and butter- nailing this humble part of the meal really sets the tone. They came around with a variety basket of warm mini bread rolls to choose from and then a couple different butters too, including a delicious brown butter (which I've seen in desserts but never as a spreadable butter- it was sweet but delicious). I think I landed up having about 4-5 rolls. I was theirs to lose...

The apps were a salmon tartare with caviar and an authentic Scandinavian salted fish (cod maybe?) dish. Tartare was mind blowing but both plates we scraped clean. For mains, we got the the lamb chops and a fish dish. I remember the fish dish being really good but those lamb chops were outrageous. I have NEVER had lamb chops this soft before. As an Aussie, I appreciate I may be putting myself at the mercy of a sheep joke here, but I've had my fair share of lamb over the years and this was certainly the softest ever and up there with the best. 

Now onto dessert, which deserves its own paragraph. Wow wow wow. The eye test had me salivating as it was beautifully presented. One dessert had apple done a variety of ways and cardamom panna cotta. I unfortunately don't like cardamom, making this the only morsel left on our plates all night. However, this dish was more than forgiven by a white chocolate mousse half sphere that was so good it makes current-me jealous of former-me. The other dish had a dulce de leche "worm" (for lack of a better descriptive term) with sorbets, fresh raspberries and a range of other well presented offerings. For me it was all about the "worm" though. I actually said to my fiancé after dinner that if the dessert had been the white choc half-sphere and worm together it would've almost definitely been the best dessert of my life (with the possible caveat of maybe being too rich- if there's such a thing?!). We were so exceptionally satisfied with this meal.

But not them, they weren't done yet. Out come a couple cinnamon sugar rolled donuts which were yum and we thought a nice touch. We were happy campers.

But not them, they weren't done yet. Out comes one of their servers with a tray of Petit fours, chocolate truffles, biscuits etc (all really interesting flavour combinations too with combos of chocs- dark/milk/white, caramels, chilli, spices, nuts, fruits etc). We could choose a range of them, whichever we wanted to try. Some enjoyable bites and a really great finale to an exceptional meal. 

But yet again, they weren't done wooing us. With our bill came two small take-home packets of almond cookies. I had these the next day, and unsurprisingly these were tasty too. 

The one super small negative we experienced was that some of the waiters, despite being very attentive and helpful, had accents that made their descriptions of the dishes being presented, hard to understand. But if that's the sole gripe then you know this is one seriously special experience! 

If you've made it to the end of this:
1) congratulations
2) thanks for reading and
3) book to dine at Aquavit- you will not regret it!

I had been dying to dine here ever since I moved to Manhattan. Everything was incredible; I had the duck and it was the best duck I have ever had. The drinks, dessert and service were also great. This restaurant is perfection. My bf has never been so I made a reservation for our anniversary, can't wait to go back!

Solid fine dining choice. Elegant contemporary feel with some clear Scandinavian/Nordic touches to the design make this place feel sophisticated but not super pretentious -- while the dress code is smart casual, most people seem to be at least in business attire or dressy.

The food itself is pretty excellent taste of Scandinavian cuisine. For lunch, it's a decent deal for a 2-star michelin experience. The gravlax to start and the Scandinavian bouillabaisse were good. 

We got the pre-fixe but they were nice enough to let us choose a different dessert.

I'd come back again. I imagine this is the closest NYC comes to NOMA.

Two years ago, I had a tasting menu dinner paired with acquavit.   I was in heaven and it as by far one of the best dinners I've had in a long time.   Each course was a work for art and a beautiful gift to all my senses.  The service was well choreographed and the head waiter had the demeanor of one of those beautiful prep school boys who dressed and spoke well.  The acquavit was perfect for each course and highly enjoyable ... And no hangover the next day either!  They served some delicious Amuse before and in between courses as well as served us a tray full
Of dessert from which we can choose as many gorgeous little pastries as we wanted.  

Alas, then have changed their menu and the pairing is now paired with wine instead of acquavit and the service was inconsistent with different waiters serving each course and the food was also disappointing.  

I hope the here just having an off day and get their act back go where it was.

Outstanding food with remarkable service.  The value for the lunch prefix menu is excellent! Atmosphere is relaxing and not stuffy like most other michelin star restaurants in midtown.  Would definitely go back again.

I've heard about Aquavit before, but after seeing it get kicked up to 2 Michelin stars, my wife and I decided to take a Monday evening out to see what the fuss was all about. Neither of us really have had much experience in Scandinavian cuisine, so we were interested to see how this would come out. The dining room is very modern, along the lines of several other higher-end restaurants in the city, but the main dining room isn't large in and of itself. Service was very solid as well, although I did feel that some of the time between courses was a bit on the longer side (or it may have just felt that way after a longer day at work).

While there is a prix fixe menu, we decided to go with the standard tasting menu (there is also a seasonal menu as well). You start off with a few small delicious amuse bouches - a lightly salted cracker, a quail egg with an over-medium yolk, and the a savory bite of bread (I forget exactly what it was) that gives you a preview of the tastes to come ahead. Right off the bat, though, you get hit with two absolutely phenomenal smoky seafood dishes - the hay-smoked gravlax and the scallops topped with a smoky whey. While gravlax can be found on most brunch menus, it's never been anywhere near the quality of the salmon, which was so rich in flavor and perfectly prepared. The scallops may have been even better; I've never had many sliced scallops before - as they tend to be more prone to drying out - but they maintained their moist chewiness, and the whey (another food item I rarely encounter on my own) really adds a nice soupy depth to the dish, with the aforementioned smokiness that is a hallmark of Nordic food. This was followed by one of the most interesting foie gras dishes I've had - three small circles of terrine wrapped in sea buckthorn, which is a good deal more bitter than a tart fruit flavor (like apricot) that you might see paired with foie. With pomegranate seeds providing a sweeter burst of flavor, the dish really hits all sorts of different taste points on your tongue, making it a great way of using the creamy blankness of the foie terrine to paint expressive flavors on your tongue's canvas...definitely the most interesting dish I had here, and one that I'd love to try again, just to see how it hits the mouth differently each time. Next up was the sweetbread wrapped in thin apple slices and topped in a creamy sauce. I think the presentation was a bit big given that the sweetbread was a bit small, but the sweetbread itself was probably one of the best I've had anywhere, with the veal adding a real succulence to each bite.

At this point, we got a shot of house-made aquavit topped with compressed IPA fizz. I'd probably do shots more often if it was this stuff; the liquor itself wasn't that harsh, and the hoppyness of the fizz adds a nice twist to what is a bit of a sweeter spirit. If anything, it's a great way of clearing the palate for the main courses, the first of which was a charred langoustine with potatoes, almond, and cucumber tapioca. I've never had langoustine prepped this way, but the light char on top adds a bit of smokiness to what is otherwise a very succulent bite of the large shrimp, and the almond and tapioca add contrasting textures and flavors to the dish. Next up was a few slices of duck breast and a chard-wrapped duck confit, paired with multiple-colored cauliflower and served with a decadent black truffle and currant sauce, giving it a slightly sweeter flavor than your typically rich, musky truffle on its own. The duck was prepared perfectly, and the confit, while flavorful on its own, works really well when given additional texture from the chard. We then moved on to dessert - the first of which was a Danish soft cheese paired with a slice of fig and a swab of balsamic brushed onto the edge of the bowl - a nice combination that combines the tartness in both sweet and savory flavors. The nest egg that completes the meal is presented perfectly, and the flavors of the cinnamon nest / cookie works really well with the creaminess of the 'egg' (which even has a yellow citrus syrup in it) and the additional fruit flavors encircling the nest. Petit fours at the end were delicious but relatively standard.

For my first serious sojourn into Scandinavian food, I really enjoyed everything that was served during the tasting menu. With relatively friendly waiters - as well as servers who are very well-versed in explaining everything on the plate - it's a complete, and completely fantastic, dining experience. Absolutely a place I'd love to come again, especially because the tasting menu (at $135) is, while not cheap, very reasonably priced compared to other high-end restaurants in the city. Dinner did run a little over 3 hours, though - so keep that in mind if you're going to do the tasting! What seemed like a very reasonable start time (8:30 PM) put us out of the restaurant at nearly midnight.

We booked a table for the Julbord (smorgasbord) brunch. The restaurant is discreet on the street almost like a sidedoor next to the big entré of the building. The corridor in to the restaurant was small. The service was attentive and not "too much". We didn't order any alcohol with the food and it was no problem, no awkwardness like some places might give one who goes alcohol free.
The food, really fresh and the herrings was really good with different sauces. My favorite was the mustard sauce. The staff was there all the time to fold your napkin and clear the table when you go for the next food round. Julbord is like a 3-4 courses dinner/lunch.
The Scandinavian tastes was there and delicious. 
Not getting a 5 star from me is because of the dessert table. For example the chocolate balls with pearl suger tasted not chocolate, only suger. I understand it should be sweet because it's dessert but it was way too sweet for our table. The ris a la malta, I like it with the dessert sauce/saftsas but, Aquavit prefers without sauce.
I understand it's their way to present the julbord and not copy other traditional julbords nor restaurants. But but...oh well, it was really delicious food on the "fish table".

Hmm, but I didn't see the white fish named "lutfisk"....

YES! Highly recommend this now 2 Michelin Star establishment. 

You don't feel that this place is a that much of a Scandinavian restaurant, feels almost like an extremely modern type cuisine, similar to an Alinea on Chicago. They were very artfully creative throughout the courses.

Backing up a little bit, I made a fairly last minute reservation on Opentable after an event that my date and I attended. After a short bit of getting lost and searching for this hidden spot, we find it and are seated in a nice booth by the hostess after a few brief moments of waiting at the bar. 

My date and I ordered the full chef's tasting. You are at a two Michelin Star restaurant, one of the best restaurants in the world, we might as well.

The chef's tasting included the following:

1) Hay-smoked Gravalax - I love the smell of burned hay and taste of dry fish with trout roe :)
2) Sweetbreads and Sauerkraut - came with a fuji apple chutney and a sort of foam of blue cheese. Very good!
3) Black truffle and Barley - sliced black truffle on top of wild seat beans and barley with some pickled onions. So good.
4) Langoustine - I was able to eat this in one bite! So delicious! There were a few almonds and oysters also artfully meshed in the dish.
5) Elderflower and IPA - Unfortunately cannot recall what this one was
6) Striped Bass and Chanterelles - Incredible dish with kale on top and some salty type foam. 
7) Duck and Cauliflower - There was a lot going on in this dish, it was very delicious!
8) Havgus and Yellow Peach - Light easy dish with sliced peach and a few vegetables and cheese on top with candied walnuts. 
9) Arctic Bird's Nest - WOW!!! One of the best desserts I've ever had. I don't even know how to describe it. 

I very much recommend you do the chef's tasting if you have the time to do so, it was phenomenal. We went with a simple sauvignon blanc throughout but I wish I went with the cocktails. Nevertheless, everything about this place was top notch and they very much deserved to earn their second Michelin Star. Looking forward to coming back very soon.

Since 3.5 star is not an option, I went for 4 stars.  I didn't have the heart to go with 3.

Chef Emma Bengtsson's recent Michelin success brought me back to try her tasting.  The dishes have gotten more refined and the desserts of course were more elaborate than ever (naturally because of Emma's pastry credentials).  The seatings in dining room are very comfortable, modern classic decor with a nice touch of sheepskin and leather pays tribute to the north.  It was overall a pleasant 3 hour dining experience with attentive and friendly service but there were small details that fell short from my expectation of a 2 M-star establishment.  

The Scandinavian elements were consistently used through out the courses in different forms: smoke, berries, apple, sunchoke, cheese.....paired with rich proteins from the land and the sea.  The highlights to me were the sweetbread, the langoustine and the arctic bird nest dessert.  All the elements worked well and made each bite interesting. I don't usually love sweetbread, but it was actually my favorite dish of the night.  The composition was unexpected but really tasty.  I wish I could have more of the succulent and flavorful langoustine and forgo the boring scallop.  Scallop was good but not special, and personally, I like my scallop plump, not sliced (unless it's raw).  The foie gras was delicious.  Super creamy and decadent.  The bird nest dessert to me, won the points on innovation and presentation.  But I'm not a fan of plain sweet white chocolate shell, and the sprouts seem to be there purely for visual.  I know the egg had to be white to make sense but I would have enjoyed it more if the white chocolate shell is infused with a flavor that enhances the yolk, rather than masking it. 

What fell short was the complimentary confection tray at the end and the diligent but messy water service (think wet table).  My eyes beamed up when the waiter came with the tray filled with cute little confections waiting to be picked.  There were macarons, chocolate truffles, cookies and candied fruit.  I picked one of each thinking they have to be good coming from a pastry chef that turned executive.  To my disappointment, they all tasted stale and flavorless.  I was puzzled, why would they finish the delightful experience with these terrible freebies when the sour dough bread in the beginning was awesome.  I don't believe that the chef would serve these if she had tasted them.              

Here are some tips: Do not bother paying extra for truffle shaving on the duck.  The shaving was done inside the kitchen and could barely be detected.  If you choose to drink aquavit (which they infuse in house and you can see the jars down the hall), I personally prefer the clean, crisp, spirit forward ones over the sweet kinds.  It's a strong drink despite the infusion.  But the sweet ones tasted like cough syrup to me.

We were treated like nobles from the start we entered the room. It was four of us so we have tried four different appetizers, main dishes and desserts. Sous vide lamb neck was velvety smooth, pickled seasonal vegetables were delicious. There were lots of tiny treats before and after the meal. I can understand why they were awarded a Michelin star.

I don't really know what I was expecting, but it was more than what I got, seeing as this place is a 2 Michelin star restaurant.
I got the chef's tasting menu. Everything is very showy. The first thing that came to my table was a smoked potato leek soup, which was shown to us by reveling the smoke and having the soup poured over the potatoes - very theatrical for a dining experience. The next thing is the bread and in-house made butters (WHICH WERE THE BEST THINGS EVER, excuse me while I indulge myself with butter with a little bread). Then we had our first courses, the gravlox and herring. The gravlox was nice and light whereas the herring was EXTREMELY salty and fishy. Then there was the main entree, which was a herb crusted lamb with had great flavor but was surprisingly fatty. We ended up getting 3 of their desserts (since the lamb was fattier than it should have been). The desserts were honestly just alright. I'd say the bread and butter and gravlox were the best things.
Maybe if you choose to get the most expensive option it might blow your mind, but I really doubt it.

I was impressed overall with my experience at Aquavit. We ordered the Chef's Tasting ($135 per person) and it was very nice.

I don't want to ruin the surprise, so I won't go into too much detail. But order the Chef's Tasting over the other available options and you won't regret it. My favorite course was the scallops, but the gravlax and the duck were also excellent.

I will say, however, that the white wine at the bar was a rip-off ($15 per glass), because we later ordered a far superior bottle in the mid-$50s range. We also passed on the cocktails as none looked particularly attractive.

RECOMMENDED.

Maybe I have a high expectation because it is now michelin two star restaurant. I feel some of the dishes are very forgettable. Overall, I would like to say that  food is 3.5 star and service is 5 star.

We came here for a second visit thinking they still had their Saturday brunch buffet but that was a Mother's day special. Oh well. Their lunch menu was eqally yummy. Too bad they don't serve their birds nest dessert during lunch.  If I had an extra night during my trip, I would've went back just for dessert.

We had a total of four Akvavit drinks: tomato, horseradish, lemon juniper, and grapefruit [herb that I can't recall - (hey they were good pours)]. This was a fun way to start our meal, and each was delicious in its own special way. We ate two different appetizers of pickeld fish, both very delicious, and a Swedish Meatball which was a different category than anything I had ever had previously.

Decor is absolutely beautiful Scandinavian style, and the service was polite but a touch aloof.

We had the fixed New Years-menu. It was way overpriced. Nice place but it didn't feel like a 2-star Michelin-restaurant...
Food was good but not as amazing as I had thought. Service was good as well although they seemed a bit stressed, rushing the food. Probably to make in time for midnight. 
Any other night here is probably when to go! :)

Came here for Christmas Eve dinner, and it was a wonderful meal!  Aquavit was clean and festively decorated for the holidays.  As a part of the Christmas buffet, I got to try many dishes ... notable to me were the herrings in different marinates (lingonberries was extremely yummy as was the mustard seeds).  The salmon was also really delicious.  While the swedish meatballs were also good, as expected.

For aquavits, I only tried two the fig & cardamom and elderflower & blueberry.  Both were very good!  Will have to think of another occasion to come back here. I would imagine Aquavit would also be great for business power lunches and dinners :)
God I love this place.  Modern Scandinavian decor.  Fresh food.  It's a little touch of Noma and Copenhagen in NYC.

Went there for their New Year's Eve event. Even though service was excellent, the food felt like it was mass produced (the restaurant wasn't even full), and was mostly bland. The exceptions were the the 7x Colorado steak & the pear mousse dessert, both of which were outstanding. The restrooms were unkempt & poorly maintained, and reminded more of a bad neighborhood McDonalds, rather than a Michelin star restaurant. Unsure how this place was upgraded to two Michelin stars, when even one would seem too much.

KenScale: 8.5/10

Aquavit is a modern Scandinavian restaurant that has been around for a while. It gained critical acclaim during the era of the star chef Marcus Samuelsson, but has been somewhat flying under the radar after his departure. Recently, the pastry chef at the restaurant, Emma Bengtsson, took over, and the restaurant seems to be having a little Renaissance, culmianting recently in two stars awarded by Michelin. I visited the restaurant a couple of years ago, and I was more fond of their desserts than the savory courses, and decided that a revisit should be in order. Overall, I was pretty impressed with the refined flavor of the food coming out of the kitchen.

The restaurant has three options (three-course prix fixe at $85 per person, seasonal tasting menu at $105 per person and chef's tasting menu at $135 per person). I opted for the prix fixe and shared all six dishes with my dining companion. My meal was focused on various fish dishes. On my last visit, I was a huge fan of the herring dish, and this time the salty fish that came with peanut potato, red onion and sour cream was delicious too. I was more impressed, however, with the dry cured gravlax (salmon) that was just melting in my mouth, with a hint of coffee. For the main dishes, Icelandic cod that came with trout roe, celeriac and fennel was flavored just right (with no overseasoning), and the striped bass that came with salsify, baby kale and lardo was also expertly prepared with great balance of flavor and texture.
