Both dessert dishes that I ordered also turned out to be brilliant, with Fuji apple and caramel and dulcey ganache fully displaying the prowess of chef Bengtsson in pastry dishes, with refined (but not overly sweet) flavor and great texture to each element.

The restaurant's dining area is somewhat formal (with professionally dressed and attentive staffs walking around to serve your table), although you can still show up in casual dresses. Getting a reservation could be a challenge here, so I suggest booking in advance. The restaurant has a full bar, with some nice selections of aquavit (Scandinavian spirits) that you can sample (my best suggested approach is $20 for a flight of three). With all the accolades on Scandinavian/New Nordic cuisine in the world, I still feel like the taste of the region is somewhat underrepresented in NYC. Aquavit is a worthy stalwart that will give a nice experience exploring the freshness and versatility of the region's flavor.

I had the honor of visiting this Michelin star rated restaurant and I was impressed.  It was my first Michelin rated star experience and now I understand why these restaurants receive these prestigious awards.  I went here for lunch during a business meeting and had the Herring sampler (perfection!!!) a must try.  As a second dish I had the Swedish meatballs and they were very tasty and delicious.  This place is a culinary masterpiece.
Food was amazing. The service was hazardous is amazing. Knowledgeable and friendly staff and delicious food.

We had family dinner with chefs' tasting-menu and vinepackage. Food was excellent., but the serving was confused and not what i expect from G.M. Awarded places. Back i '97 i dined at the old Aquavit, which imho had a "grander" air, especially with the waterfall inside.. Strict and attentive serving, and more Swedish origin foods. I think the new aquavit would benefit from going back to basic ideals, Kosher-up on the Swedishness :-)

Aquavit was a great dining experience overall because it was so unique and different from other restaurants ive been to in the city. The bar and dining area are both gorgeous, and i joked that it looked like a classier ikea.

I had a flight of the aquavit because i was really curious about what it was. I think i had the blueberry, blood orange, and grapefruit flavors. They werent my favorite, but i really enjoyed trying them. My man and i both got the three course meal and were amazed by the creative and gorgeous presentation of every dish. The small meal additions compliments of the chef were all great too. The food was very good but i wouldnt say it was amazing. Im really glad that i had the opportunity to dine here because it was so special and unique. The chef came out too to speak to the table next to us. Power to the women!! ;-)

Absolutely wonderful experience.

This is one of the best restaurants in New York and has remained so for years.

We arrived and were graciously shown to our table by the very attentive and extremely well mannered staff. Both the maître d'hôte  and our waiter were very knowledgeable and accommodating.

The food was sublime. I wanted to take some pictures, but I thought it improper in such a lovely setting. 

I had never tried Scandinavian food but I left with a little glimpse of the depth and the flair the cuisine has. Simplicity belies the wonderful flavors and aromas in every dish.

Was looking to try this restaurant out because it has two Michelin stars and I got inspired to try out Scandinavian food after seeing a NOMA video online. The service, quality and decor were all top notch. I would say that the food, at least for my taste palette, is quite a bit salty. Half way through the tasting menu I had to ask the waiter to tone down the sodium. My favorite dish was a six-mushroom assortment dish and the dessert which was. I feel like a lot of people would appreciate this restaurant and cuisine, but maybe my taste palette just isn't meant for Scandinavian food ;).
worst experience ever. none of the dishes are good. Very disgusting.nothing else to say. How could this place even earn one star?!!!!!!

I have been here twice and was very happy each time.  It is very classy and very quiet, I love that you can enjoy a conversation with someone and not compete with anything or anyone else to be heard.  The food was excellent and the service impeccable.  The Chef's tasting menu was hard to finish as it is a lot of food and all of it delicious and the best presentation I have seen in years. Highly recommended.

As a Swede I approve very much! 
Our decision to have dinner at the bar turned into one of the more memorable nights we've had here in New York City. :)

Turns out that our bartender Joey made all of the house made Aquavit so we got a story about each of the flavors we tried as well as other fun anecdotes and stories related to the restaurant and the dishes we had. 
The food from the bar menu was excellent and gave a luxurious edge to classic Swedish flavors that I miss so much living here in the States.
The Västerbotten grilled cheese, the salmon burger, the meatballs and the gravlax all deserve to be mentioned since both Americans and Swedes in our group loved everything about them.

This is a quiet and pricey place with two Michelin stars. The food is great, but not having been to Scandinavia, I don't know how it compares to top restaurants there. 

They make their own aquavits, which are flavored vodkas. They have made ones that taste like horseradish, which goes really well with beef, Danish rye bread, and kalamansi, which is a variant of the lime.

The front room and the backroom are two very different experiences, but they are both sincerely amazing and well worth multiple visits. 

The back room remains one of my favorite first class restaurants in the world. As is often the case in the truly amazing restaurants, what sets this one apart is the service and the ethos. Marcus Samuelson, a Swedish person of African descent, puts an emphasis on hiring people of color and immigrants as servers and that alone to me (as a child of an immigrant) is deeply moving and compelling. What's more is that these staff are genuinely top-notch, in my opinion second in the city only to that of Per Se. They are attentive, warm, professional, kind, intelligent and able to answer almost any question posed to them regarding the food. If they do not know the answer, they will try to seek it out. 

The chef's tasting menu never failed to impress and delight in its creativity and brilliant execution. The many aquavit flavors also always hit the spot. 

The front room was also quite good for a quicker, less of an event meal. I used to love the Swedish meatballs, but they seem to have gone with the advent of a new chef, which is sad.

The most memorable fine-dining experience in 2014 in NYC goes to Aquavit. 

Service: A+
Plating: A+
Food: A+
Creativity: A+

Tips:
Try for a reservation well-in advance of your desired dining date.
Sample the house-made aquavit. But know that one sample is included as a part of the tasting menu.
Excellent for a romantic night out or a special occasion

Aquavit in a nut shell : over priced & overrated!!! I had the duck w truffles : no truffles to be found even if I had a microscope ! Tried my friends salmon & it was so dry ! At a restaurant like this your going to mess up salmon : really ? Now granted this is a Scandinavian restaurant so it's not generally the most exciting cuisine however at these steep prices it should be a lot better!!!

What an amazing, unbelievable experience. The food was top notch with flavors that were so different and unique, but delicious! The service was excellent and they served so many extras. Every time we turned around, the servers were dropping off another delicious treat at our table. The homemade truffles at the end of the meal put us over the edge. I can't say enough about Aquavit. I highly recommend this restaurant for a memorable meal you are not soon to forget!

Best restaurant ever !

The highlights of the chef tasting menu are the gravlax and asparagus, the sweetbreads with birch soup and the langoustine. I never had many different flavors in one evening.  The mix between acid and basic is incredible and always perfect. 

And all this without speaking of the best desert in town, the artic bird's nest. 

Great service rounded by a nice decor makes Aquavit a go to restaurant in New York. You will see me there for the winter menu again !

Did the spring menu w/ wine pairing. Food nicely presented and definitely filling/solid. Really did not enjoy wine pairing. Usually would chock it up to my lack of wine knowledge but the others in my party who know quite a bit more agreed was pretty subpar. Service was friendly but clearly the different servers, sommelier, management not on the same page and pretty disorganized.

Great food, service and atmosphere!

Came here for my bday and loved it. The atmosphere was intimate, upscale, but not stuck up. 

We had the seasonal tasting menu which consisted of four dishes and a dessert along with a complimentary palate cleanser in the beginning and extra desserts in the end. 
Everything was cooked perfectly and sauces were poured on the spot so you could smell all the different flavors. The Icelandic cod was especially well cooked - the meat was soft but resilient. 

Service was very professional and not overbearing.

Would definitely recommend trying it out!
Very pretentious menu but everything was delicious. The waiters stare at you while you eat though, which was kind of uncomfortable.

Lunch with a client 4/27

- Herring sampler: tart,pungent,delicious. Listerine needed post.

- Beef Rydberg: beautiful presentation. Beef could have been more tender , doused in too much sauce. Left me wanting something more. 

- Molten chocolate cake: meh
The tasting menu price went up a bit this year since it's now a Michelin Two Star restaurant. But the experience was great!

***Aquavit utilizes quality ingredients to deliver beautiful food showcasing intense flavors; Aquavit's modern cuisine is easily among the city's best and most ambitious***

Emma Bengtsson's Aquavit is a highly acclaimed Scandinavian restaurant that utilizes a lot of ingredients and flavor combinations found in Scandinavian cuisine to deliver a creative and delicious chef's tasting menu. While you might not be able to experience many high-end Scandinavian restaurants, there are many fine dining restaurants in NY, Chicago and SF, which offer fine dining tasting menus combining high quality ingredients and a talented kitchen to produce excellent food. Aquavit though feels a notch above a lot of those restaurants.

Aquavit is very ambitious and delivers inventive plates of food. Aquavit's tasting menu also feels reasonably priced.  It is less expensive than similar modern and ambitious tasting menus offered at comparable restaurants like Coi, Benu and Atera.

The tasting menu started with a series of bites like rye and tapioca crisps and crispy mushroom skin topped with other mushroom textures like raw mushrooms and a creamy and savory mushroom mousse. Another bread-like bite followed--blood pudding topped with bacon and the very-popular-in-Scandinavian-cuisine lingonberry jam.

Onion soup followed with leek ash croutons, cheese and a great aroma from smoked hay.  A very popular Scandinavian course came next--salmon gravlax. This was turned into a modern interpretation with salmon tartare, creamy panna cotta and shaved asparagus.

A very plentiful serving of shellfish followed consisting of excellent king crab, very soft scallops and mussels. It was served with beets, sea beans and kelp consommé. Unfortunately, the kelp flavor did not come across that much.

Very creamy calf's liver pate was wrapped with a wobbly and too sweet and tart green apple and cucumber gelee; this pate was garnished with raw cucumber and crispy croutons that helped mellow out the intense flavor of the gelee. A far more satisfying cucumber preparation came next--surprisingly distinct and modern cucumber powder dusted over pickled kohlrabi with a center of minced, moist, soft, and naturally sweet langoustine.

Roasted sweetbreads was the next course. The sweetbreads were moist, rich and creamy and had a smoky exterior. The sweetbreads were served with a medium cooked egg yolk, green strawberries and really pleasing, crunchy but also airy puffed buckwheat. A palate cleansing bite of oyster with horseradish and granite followed and then came the main fish course, which was moist mackerel with sweet and tart red gooseberries, charred cauliflower and a sweetness and nuttiness from pistachio powder and pistachio puree.

The main meat course was raw lamb, which had an excellent seasoned crust. There was also seared lamb belly, which had moist and tender meat to contrast a crispy and chewy exterior. The lamb was paired with great onion flavors from spring onion, pearl onions and charred and crispy leeks.

The cheese course followed, which was firm cow's milk cheese. It was similar to other salty cheeses but was also satisfyingly creamy. The cheese was garnished with a sweet, nutty and peanut butter-like hazelnut paste, bitter greens and mildly sweet raw peaches.

Desserts were impressive--green apple granite topped with intense frozen raspberry and a sticky and sweet toasted meringue as well as a cinnamon sugar beignet filled with pastry cream. The centerpiece dessert looked like something out of Atelier Crenn's kitchen, which produces all kinds of inspired by nature presentations. The dessert featured white chocolate egg shells filled with goat cheese parfait. The parfait had the tanginess of goat cheese but did not overwhelm the other elements in the dessert. The dessert also had a light, crispy and mildly sweet cookie nest as well as chocolate lattice, frozen white chocolate powder, and a tart blueberry sorbet.

Service was very good--polite, pleasant, organized, and polished.

As mentioned, prices are reasonable given the quality, generous portions and the kitchen's creativity. Aquavit features a contemporary and upscale dining room.

Aquavit is an impressive restaurant. Like a lot of Scandinavian cuisine, Aquavit serves bold and intense flavors as well as some strong flavor combinations. I can definitely see the intense sweet and tart flavor combinations turning off some guests. But if you do not mind that, I think you are likely to enjoy your dinner here and appreciate all the creativity and talent needed to produce some of the most impressive fine dining cuisine in NY.

I am not sure what the parking situation is, but I imagine parking around here is very expensive.

Oh so Scandanavian ... simple, elegant  food with clean fresh flavours.  If those perfect rooms in the Ikea catalogue had food on their tables then it would look like this. I'd always though it was the high levels of social protection and low levels of inequality that made the Scando countries the world's happiest. But perhaps its really the food.  And Abba.

Fabulous restaurant; well deserved two Michelin stars.

Service is fantastic; unpretentious, low key attitude. The food is simple, elegant, and holy god flavorful. This is full of food and flavors that you can't find in other places - definitely an experience. 

We did the Spring tasting menu and paired it with a bottle of lighter red wine that we chose. The wine itself was unique and paired with the food was pretty tasty. The best part of the Spring tasting menu has to be the Artic Char. It's just so, so good. The meal in it's entirety from the appetizers to the tasting menu to the breads - very filling and just unique in all of the flavors. The presentation is visually pleasing; each dish is colorful and beautiful in its own way. 

And let's not forget the cinnamon sugar beignets, chocolates, and take home cornmeal apricot scones. Wowza. 

Excellent restaurant.
Excellent spot to unwind with a well crafted drink after work if you are in midtown.  Go for the flights, just ask and you will not be disappointed.

Really amazing dining experience at Aquavit. Got the spring tasting menu, the food is absolutely tasty and flavorful, I can feel the intense flavor from Scandinavian cuisine, the food's flavor it's so strong and unique. Every dish is refreshing my mouth with their exquisite plating. And also it's definitely reasonable priced. Good service, clean and modern decor. Really nice restaurant. Absolutely worth Michelin 2 stars.
They gave us 4 Amuse-Bouche before the main dish start. And also highly recommend the dessert: Arctic Birds nest. You can switch it to your dessert in the spring tasting menu or pre fixe menu. It's an amazing dessert that you must try! 
And the location is really nice. Even there's a construction out there in the street. You can just walk there if you are visiting NYC right after shopping. Really amazing restaurant. Worth to visit!

And unforgettable experience. My friend and I decided to go all out and try the Chef's tasting menu. Neither of us had ever had Scandinavian cuisine before, so this was an exciting and new adventure for us. We came a little earlier than our 8:30pm reservation, so enjoyed a few exquisite drinks at the bar. 

The dining room had this subdued beauty to it. Scandinavian design was very obvious - from the paintings to the furniture to the accessories. Simple. Sophisticated. Streamlined. 

Throughout the meal, we were served these delightful amuse-bouche dishes, which not only served as palate cleansers but also gave us a sneak peek at the dishes that were to follow. My favorite amuse-bouche was the apple flavored ice that was served prior to the dessert dishes. It was so light and nice and cleansed the palate very well.

Gravlax and Asparagus: The gravlax was very well done. Not too salty. 

King Crab and Kelp: Served absolutely beautifully - it was presented in a fish bowl that evoked the sense of an underwater terrarium. The broth was amazing. 

Calf's Liver and Cucumber: Very fascinating and bold dish. Definitely make sure to eat the calf's liver and cucumber and croutons together when taking a bite - the combination of flavors and textures makes this dish a success. Otherwise, if you eat each layer separately, it might come off as too strong.

Sweetbread and Dandelion: One of my favorite savory dishes. The sweetbread was delicious and the accompanying flavors that surrounded it (egg yolk, green strawberries, etc.) complimented the dish so well.

Mackerel and Pistachio: Another one of my favorite savory dishes. I'm not normally that big of a fan of mackerel, but this dish was done extremely well. The flavors were in perfect balance and the mackerel was so tender.

Lamb and Spring Onion: Presented beautifully. The raw lamb and spring onion went together very well.

Havgus and Walnut: This cheese dish was very nice - nutty and paired very well with the walnuts.

Arctic Bird's Nest: Officially my favorite dessert in the world. Not only was it presented gorgeously, but the combination of flavors and textures made it absolutely award-winning. There were little gold flakes nestled among the eggs, which added to the luxuriousness of the dessert. But the most impressive part of the dish was the freshness and quality of the ingredients. The blueberries that were tucked into the nest were some of the best blueberries I've ever tasted. I could go on raving about this dish forever. 

As I mentioned before, this was an unforgettable experience for my friend and me. The food was impeccable (in terms of taste and presentation), the maitre d' was so kind, and the ambience was humble and beautiful. I am definitely planning on coming back to Aquavit. Compliments to Chef Emma Bengtsson and her staff for the two well-deserved Michelin stars.

Most reviews will talk about how fantastic the service and food is. I'll be brief on that note. It is top notch, among the best restaurant experiences I've ever had.

What really speaks for a restaurant is how they will respond to an unpredicted situation. I have a hip injury, which is rarely a problem in a restaurant. Aquavit did their diligence about food allergies, even calling us the day before our reservation, and this was our fault for not mentioning my injury. I found that the chairs in the restaurant aggravated my injury. I was going to "suffer" through it and not complain, but I quickly realized that this was going to be an actually painful meal. The problem was that the chair did not give my leg the mobility, so it put pressure on my hip. Within minutes of sitting there, I went from feeling great to feeling agony. They could tell and asked the situation. I almost didn't tell them, but my wife told them for me.

They would have been well within their right to do nothing. They had plenty of reservations, and moving to another table for this busy of a restaurant was probably a major inconvenience to their evening. They nonetheless made it happen. Soon after moving to the new table, I was feeling relief. After a couple drinks, the pain was gone completely. 

My advice to other customers is tell them if you have any orthopedic injuries. The chairs are not as forgiving as other restaurants. Everything else is top of the line and well worth it.

I had been to Aquavit repeatedly at its old location and loved it. The food was different and creative - I had meals there that were intensely surprising and wonderful, and that I can almost taste today in some cases they were so vivid. On our recent visit, the food seemed to aim for surprise for the sake of surprise. We did the tasting menu, and had a number of items that were rather nice, but most were weird seemingly for the sake of being weird. I do like interesting food, but it should be tasty, and this was largely not very tasty. I was sad, because I always thought of Aquavit for its new, different, strange, and yet delicious food.

Headline: Two Michelin stars well deserved. Novel, innovative and satisfying.  

Food: My Scandinavian dining experience was previously limited to Ikea. This was a step up, to say the least. Main courses complemented each other well. I particularly liked the fish dishes.... who knew they could extract so many flavors from herring? The horseradish aquavit was the highlight; just the right amount of zing. 

Ambiance/Service: Transported away from the noise of midtown through simple yet elegant interiors. Service was top notch; slightly pretentious but that's what we're paying, for isn't it?

There is a reason why this place is Michelin-starred. Outstanding food (tried the prix fixe dinner and substituted the dessert with Arctic Bird's Nest), and some best cocktails I ever had - Plaster, In the Clear, Havtorn (had a sip of Dusk to Dawn and it is good as well). Great service, friendly waiters (in spite of the black coats) and great ambiance. For every round of the prix fixe, there was something extra that was sent to the table "from the chef" - a delightful touch. Even the bread was so good. I had the Gravlax, the Norwegian cod and substituted the dessert for extra. We were told that the Arctic Bird's Nest takes a day to prepare - to get everything together - it's a beauty. Pricey, but that's understandable for the Michelin stars. You will not regret the indulgence.

Not-so-authentic Viking cuisine

Being originally from Denmark, I love Scandinavian cuisine. This is anything but ethnic food, but maybe that was what I loved so much about it. The food was absolutely delicious, truly a wonderful dining experience. The service was impeccable and the atmosphere was very comfortable and great for my date and I. I will recommend Aquavit to all my friends traveling to NYC. It was a delightful experience to end a perfect day in Manhatten. Well deserved two Michelin stars.

My husband and I got our Michelin restaurant cherry popped this past weekend, and our first was Aquavit.

Why I chose Aquavit: 
Culinary talents Marcus Samuelsson and Elise Kornack used to cook here; this Scandinavian restaurant was just awarded two stars by Michelin; and their current executive chef started as a pastry chef, and is a woman.

So how'd Aquavit live up to its fame and the luminaries associated with it?

Aquavit delivers beautifully presented and well-balanced meals. A particularly memorable amuse bouche was a morel soup topped with lingonberry broth. It was playful and unique thanks to the mix of sweet and savory, very umami. The Norwegian cod with white asparagus, baby fennel, and almonds was creamy yet light and everything you would want in a seafood dish. Really enjoyed everything we tried except for the dessert that I chose, the chocolate and texture. 

This dessert consists of chocolate mousse, sherbert, and crumble. It was, as with the amuse bouche and other plates, rather whimsical. However, I thought the flavors lacked complexity and sophistication. My husband's black currant and passion fruit meringue, sour ribbon, and sorbet was much more pleasing to the palate and showed more originality. The chocolate and texture dessert reminded me of something I had seen on Chef's Table, a dessert that accidentally came to be. Some unintended results are better than others...Mostly, the food was remarkable and worthy of all the accolades.

If you're a pescetarian, then this is probably one of the most pesceterian-friendly top restaurants in town. Whether you choose the prix fixe, summer tasting, or the chef's tasting menu, you'll have plenty to eat. 

Service was impeccable. Our charming hostess was so kind, and I loved watching her move about the dining space to mingle with the guests and attend to their needs. From the coat check person to the dining room service captain, everyone was super professional and detail-oriented.

In honesty, I don't really care for this type of setting; it's far too formal for me and I'd be lying if I told you I didn't feel uncomfortable. The sparse, Scandinavian-themed dining space feels a bit cold, and the small army of restaurant staff at your beck and call can make you feel both very important and very small. But Aquavit sets out to give you a refined dining space, exemplary service, and innovative cuisine and it achieves all that.

Recommended for gourmands who won't squirm in such a fancy place the way I did.
Great restaurant! Delicate dishes, healthy, new potatoes were beyond expectation. Nice wine too. Don't like the pork. Desserts were ok.

I strongly recommend the chef's menu with wine pairing, which will set you back $265 per person before tax/tip. Aquavit is one of those rare "special occasion" restaurants that is truly worth it. The decor is understated and elegant, maintaining focus on the food. Each course is meticulously crafted and presented (the executive chef, a relatively young Swedish woman, was a pastry chef). 

My father is a chef and extremely difficult to impress, but during the meal he would repeat words such as "phenomenal" and "this chef is a genius". You will not be disappointed.

It was fine. If you're looking for a business lunch or dinner, this is probably a fine place to go. If you're a foodie, some of the techniques and presentations are interesting, but the taste isn't fully there. I enjoyed the desserts the most. No doubt it's innovative, but with the amount of great restaurants in NYC, there are more meals to be had with the same price tag that will guarantee to blow your mind. 

PS. To all the ladies (and possibly some gents): if wearing heels watch out for the slippery floor. Totally had a drunk experience slipping without even having any alcohol :(

Dinner at Aquavit was my first foray into the world of the [two] Michelin-starred restaurant. To put things into perspective, I had no idea what an amuse-bouche was before dining here. So I've now learned a little, but you should read my review with this in mind.

My boyfriend and I wanted to up our usual restaurant ante for my birthday, and since we're headed to Iceland next week, Aquavit's Scandinavian-inspired cuisine seemed like a logical  and delicious choice. We were able to snag a 9:30 reservation on a Saturday night more easily than expected, and once we arrived, we noticed a significant amount of empty tables. However, an experience here can take up to three hours of one's time, so it was no wonder there were no more seatings after our arrival. 

We tried the chef's tasting menu, which comprised eight courses:

Gravlax and Sea Urchin- My first time trying sea urchin, I'm fairly certain.  I'm not sure I cared for it, as it came across as slightly bitter to me. However, my palette is very sensitive to bitterness, so I'd take that analysis with a grain of, um, salt. The texture was unique-- somewhere between fatty and creamy. The gravlax was understated and fresh.

King Crab and Rhubarb- one of my favorite dishes of the night. The crab was TO DIE FOR, especially when paired with the nutmeg butter. Hugely flavorful dish. It was all a bit on the salty side, but I like that. 

Calf's liver pate and cucumber - the most visually striking thing I think i've ever eaten, these were also some of the most intense flavors imaginable. imagine a core of oxtail, surrounded by the pate, surrounded by a clear gelatinous substance. I don't even know how to describe the flavor. Perhaps extreme savory tartness? The cucumbers and croutons were necessary in order to give the dish some balance. i'm still not sure how i feel about this dish, but it was an adventure in and of itself. I can still remember exactly how it tasted, weeks later.

Beef tongue and Nasturtium - Okay, I'm going to need some help on this one, if someone doesn't mind. First, it was a great dish. I loved the potatoes. The oxtail tongue (my first tongue) was nice and smoky. But one particularly interesting thing about this dish was what we called its molecular gastronomy bent: something (was it the buttermilk?) was frozen into tiny little icy bits, and then poured over the dish. It slowly melted into the food and became a sort of dressing. I thought it was a really fun presentation, and how cool that the dish is experienced differently from one moment to the next.

Mackerel and Pistachio, Lamb and Garlic Scapes- To be honest, as it's been a few weeks, I don't remember too much about these two courses other than that they were tasty.

Hogelundgaard (cheese) and fig with ruby port ice cream, walnut, and mustard flower - We loved the cheese/ice cream combination here. The sharp blue cheese flavor combined with the sweet, creamy, somewhat muted flavor of the ice cream was excellent.

Arctic bird's nest (goat cheese parfait, sea buckthorn, blueberry sorbet) - a true masterpiece. Delicious, delicious art. Crunchy, rich, chocolatey, tart, and there was literal gold in it.

As for the aforementioned amuse-bouche, they were plentiful and wonderful, and at least one or two made good use of the lingonberry. One particular palette cleanser arrived on a stylish log. Another was an oyster leaf and elderflower served on an oyster shell. Everything looked gorgeous. I wish I could remember more. 

We did not get the wine pairing as it was about an extra $100, but we did have two cocktails each. One was a lot better than the other. I think I got the Havtorn Special (rye, sherry, sea buckthorn, lemon) and the Dusk to Dawn (elderflower and meyer lemon aquavit, lillet blanc, aperol, sparkling wine. The Havtorn Special was much better. 

The service was super formal, perhaps a bit intensely so, but I suppose that's the kind of service that this kind of food demands.

I'm not sure that I'll ever have the pleasure of dining here again, but it was a wonderful experience.

Had the lunch prix fixe, one for each of us. The Gravlax has a amazing sauce though a little drizzle of it seems less than the perfect amount for me.  The meatball dish had a beautiful taste and plate arrangement. The lingonberry was very bright and special with the cream potato sauce.

The almond brittle in the vanilla savarin was very nice and bright.

Overall the service is good but not exceptional. The flaw in the salmon was the reason why a star was taken out for the Michelin restaurant.

Positive positive positive!

Our server was so nice and funny and the food is amazing! Def deserve the Michelin 2 stars and the price is so worth it (not too bad)

The Riesling to start was probably the best I have had for a while.

The shrimp salad as appetizer is a cold dish that's fresh and tasty. I had the Swedish meatballs as entree and my friend had the seafood dish. They were both amazing, from the actual meatball/seafood to the garnish!


Must come back!!!

Spectacular summer tasting menu. The food was delicious and presented in delightful ways. The service was fantastic. We could not have asked for a better meal. 

Tip: start with a flight of the house made aquavit

Overall: not sure what all the hype is, maybe I came on a bay in terms of choice

Tried the prefix menu

New catch holland herring: nice presentation, herring was ok. The sides around it were just ok 

Veal cheek with parsnip, dill: presentation was very nice, wish it tasted as good as it looked! Veal was very salty, meat was tender

Not worth the cost or the two Michelin star

Very nice place to have a formal dinner.  Just to not surprise anybody, (even though the prices are on the menu) expect to pay $700.00 for two people with the paired chef's tasting and 15-20% tip. 

The only critique I would give (to newbies like me) is that some of the more complicated dishes could use a description of how to eat them. I know this sounds silly, but it would have helped tremendously. 

I thought the pairing of wines was great, but some of the service timing could be improved. 

If I'm ever in NY (and have another big roll of cash) I would love to come back by!

Worthy of the 2 Michelin Stars it has, and having eaten at many restaurants of this service level, we were most excited about the unique flavors on the menu. The dishes really represented Scandanavia with flavors, herbs, fresh berries, fish, and venison from that region. The food was unique and excellent, and for a tasting course with 2 stars, the prices were VERY reasonable. There is an extensive wine list, with many upper end wines on the single glass menu you would rarely find 'by the glass'. We also recommend you try their long list of house made liquors.

I had the summer tasting menu, and it was all great. There could have been more range in the flavors, but it is Scandinavian and perhaps the palate is more fixed. The staff was a little overbearing, but they may have been training someone.

Where to begin?? This fancy Nordic restaurant has 2 Michelin stars, so I'm like ok.. This is going to be fantastic. When we're seated, I noticed how quiet this restaurant is, just about to the point where I can hear people chewing on their food. Next, the food. Small, micro-food that for the most part tasted kind of strange. I can't say that I truly enjoyed anything except for the stuffed leeks, blood pudding and the sourdough bread with homemade butter. Service was good. But it's kind of tiring to have to switch utensils after each plate. I'm like omg, every 10 minutes someone has to reach over me across the table to put down a new fork. Overall, I appreciate the effort into the food and presentation. I realize that it does take a lot of prep work to prepare this meal. However, I would prefer good ole NYC street food.

Preferred the "old" location. However, still pretty nice to have the opportunity to have really good Scandinavian traditional food in New York, such as Herring sampler, Shrimp Skagen, Gravlax and Swedish Meatballs. The new location is much less cozy than the "old" one, feels too strict and without any "feeling". Service ok. Will return only when cravings really hits you!

To begin with my wife and I have been to this restaurant numerous times in the past. Each time the service was most excellent and the food was what you would expect at a Michelin 2 star restaurant.

Last week we made our reservation through OpenTable. On Monday I received a phone call from one of the Aquavit reservation specialist to confirm same. I mentioned that we would have a service animal with us and was told that was absolutely no problem and they would enjoy having us as guests.

We arrived at our requested time and were immediately confronted by the manager with a request for our service animals "papers". We were happy to provide same. We were then asked "where is the animals crate". My response was that I am a lifetime diabetic thathas a service dog trained to alert me to any changes in my physical condition. Placing this animal in a crate would defeat the purpose of which the animal was intended. I was then told to place my service animal in a bag, which we did.

During my family's dinner we had a group of five Japanese man on one side and five Spanish women on the other that were talking so loud that we couldn't hear each other without raising our voices.

My wife decided to take a family photograph of us during dinner with her cell phone. She took two photos with the cell phones small flash and were immediately approached by an assistant manager and told that the ladies at the table next to us objected to the flash having gone off.

At this point I would like to say that nowhere in the restaurant was there a sign posted "no flash photography". The foregoing having occurred, my wife's dinner was ruined and both my daughter and I were embarrassed. I complained to the waiter, who called over the manager. The response we received was a verbal apology for what took place and that the issue we brought up would be addressed at the next management meeting. The manager offered us additional drinks which we refused. To add insult to injury, there was no adjustment to the bill for this outrage having taken place.

Bottom line, the food was acceptable and the service and management was deplorable.

I've only been to Aquavit a handful of times--maybe six or seven over the course of a decade--but the place constantly amazes me.  Amidst a constantly changing culinary landscape, Aquavit's managed to maintain an exceedingly high bar.  The wait staff is polite and knowledgable about their food, and the cuisine is fantastic.  There aren't many places to get Scandinavian food in the city since Hospoda closed, but this isn't a bad exposure to their fare.  The food is expensive, but not punishingly so--expect to shell out roughly $60 per person.  The chilled and octopus and prawn is fantastic, the chanterelle veloute really highlights the fresh ingredients.  The steak tartare was almost decadent with the egg yolk used to hold it together.  The best things, though, are their fish.  Go straight to the ocean when you're there.  Anyone can make a burger, and US steak is better than European counterparts and the French can outcook anyone when it comes to beef.  But what Scandinavians have perfected over the centuries sailing cold waters is how to prepare cod, char, and salmon (their gravlax is so light and fresh it's like inhaling saltwater).

I visited Aquavit last week for the first time. Since it has two Michelin stars I had somewhat high expectations. I would say the food is between one and two stars tending more to one. I had the lunch prix fixe. The gravlax was rather sweet and overloaded with mustard seeds. The Scandinavian Bouillabaisse contained some pieces of fish which smelled rather fishy - fresh fish does not smell fishy. The dessert, napoleons, was pretty good. The food was not awful, but not at all outstanding. There are several restaurants in New York serving better food with one or no star at all. I guess the ways of Michelin reviewers are rather opaque. My server was very nice and professional, but the atmosphere in general was rather cold and impersonal.

I know I should give 4 stars or more, and I don't take this lightly and have spoken w ppl who were at our table (5 of us).  This is a longstanding restaurant and food is still excellent.  But as a 2016 Michelin 2-star rated restaurant, the service was subpar.  

First of all, everyone at the table MUST order the same course.  They now only have 3 courses, and, NO, you cannot order Prix Fixe if your companion is ordering the tasting course.  With 5 ppl at the table, it was a bit awkward to navigate it, but we settled on Prix Fixe.  Our French friend found their wine menu good and found an excellent bottle.

Appetizers were excellent, especially the herring.  Their gravlax is great, but this time, the herring won.  The main dishes were all very good, but we were not wowed by the desserts.  

However, the service was inconsistent. There were 2 ladies at the table, but "ladies first" was really not observed, which was a little disappointing.  And three of us had the same main dish, but one of them was missing the sauce, which took a few more minutes before it was brought and poured over, which sort of broke the mood.  

At the end, they'll bring a tray of truffle chocolates.  The person who brought to our side of the table dropped one of them on the floor, but NEVER returned to replace what he had dropped.  Really??  The excellence of service was shown by the man who was in charge of our water.  He didn't miss which one of us was having water "with no ice," "yes, with ice" once.

Also I'm just not a fan of their décor since they moved.  It's very "conference room" and not elegant, warm, or comfortable.

Went for lunch - herring sampler was delicious and perfect.  Salmon burger was the best salmon burger I ever had.  Service very attentive and friendly.  Decor left something to be desired.  Dessert was good too!

Imaginative food flawlessly prepared-my family and I have been to Aquavit seven times and have always been wowed! As the Millennials in the group said, the atmosphere and service  is formal without being stuffy. It's like being in your trendiest and most gracious friend's dining room for a holiday dinner-except that it's always a special occasion at Aquavit. We always get the tasting menu. Favorites last time included gravlax and quail's egg with red beets, capers and mustard, venison and Brussels sprouts and king crab with bone marrow and goat's milk yogurt. The signature dessert - the Arctic Bird's nest- is delicious but almost too beautiful to eat. Fashioned of meringue with chocolate eggs and blueberries, it is simply not to be missed.

Except for the dessert, the theme of the tasting menu is "sour". Though many of the courses do have different flavors, the acidity dominates most of the time. Maybe I am not a big fan of sour food. 

The service level varies. Some people are very attentive, while some are somewhat careless.

The presentation of dishes are delicate and creative. One of the waiters is also very accommodative to my food allergies.

3.5 star. Although I dont know if it is common for scandinavian food, I have to say the chef is overly obsessive with sour flavor. The hight light of the dinner is the bird nest, which is far better than any dessert I have tried so far in all nyc michelin star restaurant (even 3 star ones). In addition, they do charge (a lot) for water. It is $9 per bottle.

Maybe it's just me not liking Swedish food. Had the 8 course tasting menu, the only impressions were salty and sour. 
I drank so much water that I went to bathroom twice during the 3 hour dinner.
One of the dishes, don't remember the name, was basically sauerkraut with some even sourer stuff. Tried hard to finish but failed.
The dessert "bird nest" was in a large portion, with 3 goat milk yogurt parfait balls which were also sour. With so much sour food, I wasn't to finish the dessert even though it wasn't bad.

We had a delicious and well thought out meal.  
Our party of 5 was seated at round table and served by a professional and knowledgable team.  
We had a few dietary restrictions that they accommodated quite well.  
I will be going back.  The menu and wine pairing was sublime.
I came for lunch . Order the prix fixe menu ,food is ok cuz I'm so full  ,can't feel much texture .planting is good.service is good. The wine tastes so good~~

Every dish has its own image. 
Food in here is not just food but art.
You are enjoying the wonderful pics and can't feel time flys.
This place will open a gate to new gastronome.
After that the environment is really nice to have a formal date. It makes people feel comfortable.

Love this restaurant. I came here with friends for dinner a while ago. Food was amazing, services was exceptional, reataurant was very spacious.

We ordered a lot of food, some of my favourites were the pigeon dish, the seared foie gras as well as their desserts!

I would definitely come back again.

Wow! This is amazing and I am unsure why I've never heard about it before. Went for the $50pp lunch and was blown away. The nicest staff, and the food is beyond special. The meatballs and the boullibaisse are not to be missed. Fresh and fun, this is what Michelin stars are given for.

I'm writing to amend my review a little. They did eventually send us a very generous gift certificate, with a more genuine apology included. Helps to make up for some of the sting from the original visit and experience.

This place is bomb. Went here for my best friends birthday and we were treated impeccably- borderline annoying. I didn't even mention to the staff that it was his birthday but they gave him a free desert. We had a late night meal, and they kept giving us free food, so they were probably cleaning out. Would def go again, but would go by myself. The decor was kinda blah and they seem to do a lot of private events. Great food, really an acquired taste.

Definitely in the list of most expensive meals to date, but the SO and I were fairly happy with our experience with Aquavit.  For dinner, Aquavit offers three menus - a 3 course prix fixe, a medium-sized tasting menu, and a full chef's tasting menu - the prices range from $95/pp to $145/pp.  Since we were celebrating our anniversary, we decided to go all out and experience the tasting menu.  They also presented us with champagne for our milestone!

Staff and service was impeccable here.  Everyone was very friendly, our table was always clean and cups were always full.  They took the time to explain all the dishes, as is usual with tasting menus.

I've attached a photo of the menu they had for our particular night.  Included with the tasting menu was a couple rounds of amuse bouche, palette cleansers, and petit fours... oh so many petit fours.

While we loved everything that evening, these few stood out to us:

- Rabbit and mushroom soup amuse bouche - the little piece of rabbit was tender and the mushroom soup - best mushroom soup I've ever had. Seriously.

- Salmon and apricot - salmon was so fresh and the "apricot snow" they threw on top of the salmon sashimi was quite the presentation

- Pelle janzon - venison tartar with what seemed like some sort of caviar and a quail egg in the middle.  A little on the salty side, but very fresh and a nice little starter

- King crab and baked potato - definitely not the kind of baked potato you're thinking of.  This is a delicate potato... "sculpture" with layers of white and sweet potato paired with the most delicious and juicy piece of Alaskan king crab.  The "potato skin" broth was flavorful and a bit tangy.

- Calf's liver and blackcurrant - tasted quite strongly of wine and thus I could not eat too much of the blackcurrant jelly.  The calf's liver/fois gras was very smooth and you actually get a large amount of it.

- Turbot (fish) and turnip - ever had cucumber foam? The tender and fresh turbot with the tangy strips of radish were something I've not had before and enjoyed thoroughly.

- Oxtail and truffle  - seriously, some of the best and most tender oxtail I've ever had.  See picture.  Such tender, much wow.

- 7x Sirloin (wagyu!!) and red cabbage - deliciously marbled (7 grade) wagyu slice with a tangy cabbage side.  SO good.

- Arctic bird's nest - the display is incredible - there's even gold flakes.  This is my type of dessert - lots of different tastes, textures, and flavors put into one dish.  There's fruit, blueberry sorbet in the center, creamy white chocolate goat cheese parfait "eggs" on top, and a cookie "nest".  This was an excellent end to our meal.

- Petit fours - choose as many as you like - our eyes were much bigger than our stomach at this point and we had to take some petit fours home.  Beware though and make sure you refrigerate your truffles and such even though they don't tell you you need to.  I found mold in my truffle the next day and it was a major hiccup to our meal.  They've checked to make sure this isn't an issue going forward and have been very nice in helping to resolve my issue.

Would definitely dine at Aquavit again for a special occasion!

I had the spring tasting menu, which was pretty good. The service was decent, although at the very end, our coffee/latte orders were forgotten. 

Food:
Lots of little canapes - all pretty good
Arctic char canape - good
Beets and goat cheese - pretty good
Lamb and lingonberries - pretty good
Monkfish and fennel - decent
Duck breast - very good
Cookies and cream dessert - not great
Dessert sampler - I had almost one of everything; good

This is by far the BEST dining experience I've ever had!  Perfection from start to finish.  The restaurant is decorated in a Scandinavian mid century style - very fitting of course and well done.  We were a group of 6, all couples and best friends which always makes for a great night.  We went for the Chef's Tasting Menu with wine pairing and the Sommelier paired the wines perfectly.  But the food, OMG the food - sensational food, A+ presentation, innovative menu, flavor explosion.  And your reservation covers the entire night, we arrived at 8pm and left by 12:30.... we were beyond full and close to food coma so called it a night, but it was a perfect one.
Ordered the spring tasting menu dining alone at the bar. Food was wonderful and would absolutely go back. But why is everything plated on rocks?

I think it's good if you like Nordic food.  The dessert was very good.  We were in the private room which was sparsely decorated.  Most of the menu choices weren't my favorite but I think it's more of a foodie place.

Amazing dinner! My husband and I came up from D.C. to spend our weekend celebrating in NYC. We own the Aquavit cooking book so decided to actually have a meal there. 

The restaurant is very beautiful, warm and quaint. We were greeted as soon as we sat down with a glass of excellent rose to congratulate us. We decided to go with the Spring tasting because of the ingredients they had (plus I liked everything listed). We started off with two small bites from the chef, Duck Confit with apples and a small salty bite with caviar (I forget what it was!) but were amazing!! We asked for the wine list in preparation for our first course. Then we got a small mushroom soup with rabbit rillette. Also amazing! Our first course came and I had run out of rose and NEVER got the wine list, which was a little annoying. We like enjoying our dishes with wine. So we had to sit there staring at our scallop while we waited for our wine, not ideal. The waiter recommended two amazing white wines. I hate Chardonnay but his recommendations were pretty on point (hence, I actually enjoyed the Chardonnay!). 

The scallop was good, not in love because I hate cucumber and it was cut in a weird way (I would've preferred to have the whole scallop instead of small and big chunks cut unevenly).  Second course was Mackerel and fava beans = amazing. My two favorite courses were the Halibut and the Lamb. Lamb was cooked PERFECTLY, and the Halibut was AMAZING. Depth of flavors with the Halibut including bacon, yum. By then we had switched to red wine for the meat, cheese plate and dessert. I thought their wines by the glass were pretty good and prices were reasonable compared to other Michelin starred restaurants. We had a cheese plate and conclusion was: don't order the cheese plate, not worth it. 

We had heard that the standout dessert was the Artic Birds Nest, and we asked to replace our dessert for it and whoa! it was great . Presentation outstanding and the flavors amazing. We had dessert with one of the best espressos I've had in a long time. So definitely order coffee. 

In conclusion it was an amazing meal. The service in the beginning was not the best but by the end of the night they made up for it as we got to know our waiter and increasingly felt more at home! Honestly the canapes, the soup and the palate cleansers were OUTSTANDING while the food was pretty good. We will definitely come back and recommend it to anyone visiting NYC. Thank you for a great night!
Tried winter tasting menu a while ago. Great ambiance, elegant servers. Sauce was perfectly seasoned, and presentation was neat. However, the chewy lamb was not comprehensible.

This has got to be my favourite restaurant in New York. A lovely atmosphere and friendly staff complete a wonderful dining experience. I have visited a few times now and thoroughly enjoyed the experience. I would thoroughly recommend.

I really wanted to write a review about this Princess Cake because it's my all time favorite cake  (and from LA to NY it has traditionally been my b'day cake)  and it's so hard to find here in New York City. When I read the other reviews here about the Princess Cake at Aquavit, I got REALLY excited. I really thought how could I go wrong since this place seems to be super elegant high-end Scandinavian food - they must have their Princess Cake down. So, here is my review. Whomever said this was the best Princess Cake that they have ever had CLEARLY has never had a 'real' Princess Cake. This was literally one of the WORST cakes I have ever had in my life. It was for my 50th Birthday party and I didn't even finished my slice, I was embarrassed that my guests had to eat it, and half of the cake went in to the trash. At $68 something dollars a cake, it's a shame. The thing is this restaurant is stunning inside, and the food looks incredible - and I will go back one day for the food. But the cake was an utter disappointment. It didn't even taste remotely like 'real' marzipan on the outside. It was too thick and hard and The cake inside did not have the layer of raspberry inside and what can I say, there wasn't one good element about this cake. There used to be a Scandinavian cafe in Columbus Circle (can't remember the name but they have since closed) now this place had quite literally one of the BEST Princess cakes I have ever had. My recommendation is that if you love this cake as much as I do, I would make sure to try before you buy.

I came to Aquavit last November, and I still think about it all the time.
I had never tried Scandinavian food (the cafe at Ikea doesn't count), so this was an eye-opening experience for me. I also opened a button on my pants by the time I got to dessert. The portions aren't massive, but the prix fixe menu will fill you up quite nicely.
My first course, gravlax, was exceptional. 
My main course was a lamb stew. If I'm ever on death row, let it be at Sing Sing so there's a chance I can get this meal again one last time. 
Throughout the meal, you're given several little amuse-bouches that reminded me of Kristin Chenoweth. Tiny, beautiful, and full of flavor. And there are cheeses. Cheeses for days. 
Service was impeccable. Professional, polite, never overbearing. Our server helped us choose an excellent wine pairing for our meal. 
The decor is somehow severe and soft at the same time. I was sitting in a handsomely cruel yet gloriously comfortable office chair that was covered in some kind of soft blanket which I can only assume was once a bichon frise. I wanted to steal it. If they ever sublet the dining room, I'd move out of my apartment.
I had a chocolate cake dessert experience, which was followed by a round of chocolates, which was followed by a complimentary little baby muffin wrapped up in plastic to save for the next day when I'd eat it at work, eyes glazed over, thinking about the previous night's meal.

My wife and I came to Aquavit for our fifth anniversary and we each had the tasting menu. 

We came to Aquavit a day after eating the best meal of our lives at Le Bernardin and so we had a very high bar and high expectations. They were certainly met. For my part, I loved both restaurants and would return to either - but I loved Le Bernardin more. My wife, however, would rather return to Aquavit, and that should tell you something about how good Aquavit was. 

The menu at Aquavit is more of a sampling, because between each course we received something different and new. Each course itself was also like an experiment, with vivid plating and sudden and unexpected flavors. Some of these experiments worked REALLY well, and some of them would have been better if they'd held back a little. 

For example, one of our courses was the sirloin with onion and bordelaise. I cannot adequately describe to you how good this was - in particular whatever they had done to the onion. I could have eaten only this course and considered my money well spent. 

For an example on the other end, the Arctic Birds Nest was vividly plated and exciting to look at, but the taste didn't live up to the previous courses or to its own presentation. 

We found the fried bits of one of the appetizer courses unappealing, and the oysters were simply not to our taste (though done excellently). Every other course was a revelation and super exciting for us - we really really enjoyed the whole meal. 

You almost don't mention the service as these Michelin starred restaurants because you know it is phenomenal, but there was a real warmth to the service at Aquavit that went above and beyond. It really made our experience that much more enjoyable, and it definitely won my wife over. 

I should also add that my wife has an incredibly bizarre food restriction due to a medication she takes for a brain tumor. She cannot eat anything carbonated (no champagne, no soda, etc) and we wouldn't have realized that carbonation would be used in any sauces or foams, but the restaurant caught that quickly and prepared my wife's meal slightly differently to avoid even the risk of her not enjoying it. This was very endearing as well. 

Phenomenal job, and we will absolutely want to come back. I hope you get your third Michelin star.
Elegant and thoughtful food.  Excellent ambience and service

Stellar food and great service. I really enjoyed the creaminess of the shrimp skagen for my appetizer. The only thing was, I wasn't a huge fan of the bread it was sitting on -- I would've preferred something contrasting the texture of the shrimp. 

I got the pork belly as my main and it was divine. The layers of it were perfectly made and the berry sauce was just the right taste and texture. Can't wait to come back to try some of the other things, all of which looked fantastic. 

Atmosphere was a tiny bit stuffy but I enjoyed the fine dining experience at Aquavit.

4.5 Stars. Really had high hopes for Aquavit and it didn't disappoint. The tasting menu was fairly priced and well rounded. The sirloin was really flavorful... only gripe is that there was so little of it... I pulled an Oliver Twist and begged "Please, Sir, I want some more" but alas! these Swedes would have none of it....I was, however, offered a complimentary meatball :(  The sweetbread was so so... Rest of the courses were very good. The venison tartare was really good. Also... must not forget the Arctic Bird's nest dessert. It looks like a hot mess but tastes pretty good. 

The service was very good. I really applaud the fact that Aquavit embraces diversity in its waitstaff. I saw an older Indian gentleman who was serving bread (delicious rye by the way) rare to see in Michelin ranks... reminded me of my father.  

The Fig and Cardamom Aquavit is superb. It felt like drinking an Eau de Parfum

I hadn't been here for lunch in a while so when a business lunch came up I figured it would be a good place. They have a beautiful dining room and are very accommodating. I had the shrimp skagen with bleak roe to start which was good. I then had the meatballs. They were good but not great nor nearly as good as in Sweden. I found them slightly chewy and would have preferred them less well done.

My wife and I went here for anniversary last week and the staff couldn't have made it a nicer experience. The food was perfectly prepared and unique. Our favorite part may have been dessert where a few surprise treats found their way to us.

Great great great! Second time here. The food is very consistent. Delicious as always. Meatball was awesome and can't have enough of their cookies at the end.

We did the lunch prifix, around $50 per person, come with an appetizer, a main course and dessert. 

Will come back!
Spectacular dining experience. The venison tartar was probably the best thing I have eaten. The service was truly impeccable.

Why #Aquavit restaurant is rated 2 Michelin stars?

The entire Michelin-star rating system is complicated including not only the food but also the service, setting, and comfort of the restaurant.  For example, I'll still rate Ledoyen in Paris, Benu in San Francisco, or Per Se in NYC as the 3-star Michelin restaurants.  On the other hand, @GusSouzaNYC and I were shocked that Alain Ducasse at the Dorchester London served us an over-cooked lobster.  So, let me break down #Aquavit further (in 0-3 stars scale):
Food: 3 stars
Setting: 2.5 stars
Comfort: 2.5 stars
Service: ??

Here comes the problem - the captains are all knowledgeable and I appreciate the diversity.  However, the runners are clueless with the menu.  I would never recommend a runner to hold two plates in one arm (or hand) as the restaurant was not IHOP.  Other critics mentioned about the servers in black suit as stiff as they were in funeral.  I totally disagree.  The climbing to the next Michelin star may require some trainings to the runners.

Nowadays, we can throw away the traditional French hospitality guideline.  When you sit down, you will notice the minimalistic on the table settings.  The setting is not stuffy or classical like Epicure in Paris.  Chef Emma Bengtsson knows how to manipulate the freshness of the produce (fish or meat) with interesting combination of different berries.  For a moment, I thought that I was dining at Matsalen in Stockholm. The fresh tomatoes, blackberries, peas, or meyer lemons are all having their own distinctive fragrance and aroma which have blend effortlessly with the produce.  It is undeniable that the ingredients and cuisine are stemmed from "nature" - a motto is also from Mathias.  

The wine pairing was impeccable - yeap I said it.  For 10 course dinner less than $155 per person, this is a steal in NYC.  After the Beard House dinner on 6/29 and tonight at Aquavit, this restaurant may soon be promoted once the front service has been fixed.  Now....shall we try the Aquavit London?

This is perhaps the most underwhelming meal I have had in New York. I was so excited to come here for a work lunch, given how many wonderful reviews I read heard about this Michelin 2-star establishment.

For the prix fixe, I had the tomato with bacon soup for an appetizer, cod for my entree, and finally a strawberry dish for dessert. To sum it up, the food was all for show and completely lacked in substance. The soup was similar to any tomato soup that you can get at fast takeout lunch spot. The cod dish was complimented with an incredibly bitter sauce made from watercress. Finally, the strawberry dessert was actually just strawberries drizzled in a syrup. 

Someone at the table opted for the Cornish hen for his entree, and I was seriously outraged when I saw the dish. Cornish hens are already tiny to begin with, and this dish only used the thighs of the hen. (What in the world did the restaurant do with the rest of the hen?)

One of the worse feelings is leaving a restaurant feeling hungry, and that's how Aquavit left me feeling. 

Understandably, the corporate lunch is perhaps not the best representation of what Aquavit can offer. However, I was so unimpressed by the meal that I think the chances of me returning are highly unlikely.

Been eating at the restaurant since it was on 54th St. Class all the way. I miss the Artic Circle dessert though which is no longer on the menu. Lunch is great (herring sampler is yummy) along with the salmon burger. Dinner is exquisite. Best duck I have ever had (had plenty in Paris -and the French are known for their duck!!!). Love the intermezzos as well. Service and food deserve 3 Michelin Stars (not 2 which it already has).

Now my absolute favorite restaurant. Ever. From the amuse bouche to the dessert, everything was phenomenal and far exceeded my expectations. The amuse bouche was gorgeously plated and I was SO impressed by the deliciously unique flavor combination in such a small bite. I can't wait to go back and try the tasting menu. 

Pros:
- No issues getting a reservation a week in advance.
- Amazing flavors, portion size, presentation, service.
- Reasonably priced. I went with the prix fixe menu and ordered the smoked salmon appetizer, duck breast entree, and chocolate dessert. 
- The smoked salmon looked like one of those typical fine dining dishes that actually look like art, but would taste really odd. I honestly didn't expect too much after seeing it, but even the vegetables were pickled and seasoned to perfection. 
- The duck breast entree was even more delicious. So soft and tender with a crispy skin. The only duck that I've had that I consider comparable is EMP's famous lavender and honey duck.
- I love chocolate itself, but usually dislike anything chocolate flavored. I don't know exactly how to describe it, but the ice cream tasted like actual chocolate, not too sweet and just the right amount of bitterness. The consistency was on point as well. However, I thought the buckwheat added a bit of a strange texture since it was somewhat sticky, though the contrast was nice. 

Cons:
- None. 11/10 would recommend!

Since our wedding ceremony at Aquavit in 2012 we celebrate our anniversary here every year. It was amazing 4 years ago and when you think it couldn't get any better, it still does. I fell in love with everything about Aquavit when I first walked through the door and to this day I get extremely excited when I visit here on our anniversary. I hope they will continue to evolve with time but always retain what's so amazing.

Very underwhelming, particularly given the prestige and the price. $500 + ought to be special. And nothing on the summer menu was memorable or remarkable and not even close to enough food or courses to be considered either a tasting menu or a dinner. 

On top of that, the service was disinterested at best - dropping dishes on the table without descriptions or explanations. 

And for a Saturday night, the place was practically empty. Now we know why. 

First time, last time.
Covers the expectations with 5 stars in all aspects. From fun drinks, to food, wine selection, service and ambiance. We had an spectacular dinner

I went there last month with my brother to celebrate his birthday. We both chose their chef's tasting menu. It was 11 courses of small plates all together.

The ambiance of the dining room felt austere, clean, and contained sprinkles of melancholia. The waiters were dressed in black suits; I couldn't remember seeing a smile from their faces. The whole experience was surreal, in a good way.

The plates were evenly divided between meat and seafood - four plates of meat with venison, foie gras, sweet bread, and sirloin duck, and four plates of seafood with caviar, king crab, oyster, and red snapper. Each plate was presented beautifully, however, some lacked flavor. The egg nest dessert was one of the high notes of the evening; chocolate eggs filled with ice cream was a surprise. The two cocktails I ordered were also delicious. Their bar menu alone was worth the visit.

Aquavit is worth a detour for anyone looking to celebrate a special occasion.

As expected at a fine dinning restaurant, the service was excellent - although a bit overbearing. The server to patron ratio was a little absurd. The wine selection was fair at best and the ambience was sterile and reminded me more of a hotel lobby then anything - a lot of white and very little that added to the experience. 

The food was something to be forgotten. The first course started with a tomato water that had a resemblance to salad dressing. The remaining courses were not only forgettable but disappointing. I kept thinking the next course would be an improvement, but sadly it was not. There were some dishes that were interesting and delicious. The venison steak had an incredible texture and taste, and the "bird's nest" dessert was a creative and delicious dessert that was aesthetically pleasing and the most palatable dish of the evening. 

Overall, this restaurant was not worth the cost, and the experience was extremely blah.
Took my fiancé here for her bday. Service was too notch like robotic perfection. Food was outstanding. Cocktails were amazing. The duck was by far the best I've ever had. Almost cried

This is mediocre, pretentious food in microscopic proportions with astronomical prices.

Imagine previously hearty Nordic cuisine "refined" with pretentious sauces; presented on too many Japanese ceramics; served by Prada-wearing, overly many wait-staff planted in a Jacobsen style decor and you'll have Aquavit.

Had the prix fixe menu and we were greeted with two canapes:  a microscopic, mediocre onion souffle and a microscopic potato topped with roe in a "witty" mini crate of small raw potatoes.  We were warned not to eat the raw potatoes as the skins were a little "jarring."  Don't worry we won't as the canapes were little better than the frozen stuff served at corporate events.

Then came the matjes herring first course.  Some little herrings die and go to fish heaven.  Others end up in jars on a Safeway shelf.  And the elite end up as the expensive First Course at Aquavit.  And the difference in quality is as minuscule as the portion size.

We had the Long Island duck breast as the Second Course, the first and only reasonably sized portion. Served rare and big, the duck meat itself was very high quality but the preparation was uninspired.  In other words, I can, at home, roast a better duck.  Especially if it's a high quality Muscovy as this one probably was.

And now for the best course of the dinner:  The entremets which consisted of a basil sorbet served as a float on sparkling dry apple cider.  That was actually inspired and very, very good.

The Third Course offered a very dry cake with a slab of chocolate, no better than from Godiva's.  This was only somewhat alleviated by the traditionally and pretty good French petit fours.

Absolutely incredible experience and one that I will never forget! The quality of presentation, both within the food and the servers was top notch and very well executed!

My boyfriend and I got the chef's tasting menu - a variety of dishes hand-picked by the chef, all of which had unlikely combinations of food that surprisingly went so well together! Some note-worthy plates were the venison, 7X Beef, and the Arctic Nest. The truffle sauce that we got with our venison was on point and honestly made me melt into my seat - it was THAT good. The Arctic Nest was also very tastefully decorated and looked like an actual bird's nest - so beautifully crafted together!

In addition to the chef's tasting, there were many in-between dishes, a variety of breads (which I made sure to go easy on) so overall, I'm pretty sure we had about 20 different things! But these guys are so skilled in the craft of food that they made sure all of these were perfectly portioned so it wasn't over-filling nor overbearing.

As mentioned before, service was top notch and the presentation was very well executed - a job well done because my overall experience here was just delightful throughout. It's definitely one of the much finer things in life though so prepare to break the bank!!

I felt a bit shamed to say that last time my dinner at Aquavit was left a bit underwhelming, as I was not completely stuffed towards the end of my tasting menu; so when my friend asked me for their lunch prex-fixe, I was a bit hesitated upfront. I am so glad that I did give a try, as each course from the set indeed impressed me.

It was very simple between the two of us, as we could each get a different dish. Out of all dishes, my favorite was the Swedish meatball. How could they manage to cook the meatball so tender, that the inner was about medium, while the outside was perfectly done? Taking one bite would definitely be a journey for your palate, during which you could experience completely different textures, and only left to say - oh can I get more? Dessert, on the other hand, served as a perfect ending, that you could feel the apple crisp gradually melt in mouth. I simply could not find a better deal in this neighborhood, that serves a better meal, while maintaining a legit bill.

Their holiday seasonal menu also looks attractive to me, and I'm planning to revisit for sure. 2017 Michelin list will be out in about two weeks, and I would not be surprised to continue to see Aquavit taking a spot. After all, New York City is still new in Nordic food and Aquavit is legitimately setting the standard. Very well done.

Food: 4.5/5
Service: 4.5/5
Cleanliness: 4.5/5
Atmosphere: 4.5/5
Price: $$$$

We dined during lunch for their prix fixe menu. Though it was 2 years ago that we visited, the prix fixe is still available today! You can click here for their lunch menu. À la carte menu is also available. Aquavit was a refreshing experience for us not because it was a Michelin 2-starred restaurant, but because of its unique cuisine. We weren't too familiar with the Scandinavian food scene let alone a fine-dining Nordic cuisine, so we didn't really know how much we would like it.

At $52 per person for lunch, it is quite expensive, but given that it's a 2 Michelin starred restaurant, I think it's well worth the splurge - especially when the restaurant is hard to book!

Having looked at the prix fixe lunch menu online, I have a feeling that they haven't perhaps updated their menu... or it's still the same all these years! I definitely remember ordering the Swedish meatballs while my husband had the Bouillabaisse. Swedish meatballs is probably what they're most well known for (one of anyway) so the lunch prix fixe is one of the best ways you can enjoy the dish for a more affordable price.

When you think of Swedish meatballs, one of the first things that probably come to your mind is... Ikea and their Swedish meatballs. Don't let that fool you, because the meatballs here are so incredibly delicious! I would re-order this in a heartbeat! Everything was well cooked and the cucumbers were a refreshing touch to the dish. I highly, highly recommend!

My husband opted for the other choice - Scandinavian Bouillabaisse for lunch. Having a seafood base, this colourful dish is highly recommended by hubby as well. I just asked him about his experience with the Bouillabaisse and he replied saying that it makes his mouth water. The pickled tomatoes keep the flavours in check while the light foam provides a well balanced and smooth bite every time.

I really enjoyed my dessert, though there wasn't anything too surprising or unique here.

Somehow, the waiters got mixed up and we were presented with another dessert - someone's birthday dessert. Though it was neither of our birthdays, the waiter let us enjoy the tart :). I pretended that it was my birthday. It was nice to know that you can have complimentary dessert on your birthday!

Aquavit is a Michelin 2-Star Restaurant in the heart of Manhattan having one of the highest ratings on all food/hospitality websites and guides. Not only does it have 2 stars from the Michelin Guide (for many many years, including 2016), it also received 3 stars from The New York Times and Forbes as well. Here is a full list of all achievements and press articles on Aquavit.

I highly recommend Aquavit especially for lunch if you like fine dining, a fan of Nordic Scandinavian cuisine, or just a plain foodie like me. The prix fixe can be expensive or affordable depending on your wallet, but the food you won't be let down - it'll definitely be well worth it. Aquavit's atmosphere is both casual and formal at the same time which allows anyone - tourists, locals, businessmen and women, families - to dine comfortably. I would definitely want to revisit the restaurant for dinner and their seasonal tasting menu!

Service is definitely top notch - nothing to mention here!

No question the food is outstanding, and a soothing Nordic atmosphere, but we had the most arrogant service we have ever experienced at a restaurant of this caliber. We were made to feel badly about having some special dietary requirements; were mockingly told that yes, cheese is vegetarian; ordered black truffles which never arrived; seemed to have run into a problem by the end of the meal about being told what dishes from the tasting menu we were being served; and were kept waiting for 15 minutes, until virtually the end of the meal, to see if our requested bottle of wine (2nd bottle) was still in stock. Overall, felt a significant damper placed on a special occasion. Very unfortunate.

Herrings was ok . A Chance to sample herrings with different herbs, but it is what it is, pickled herrings. 

Cod was a huge disappointment, small bites of cod was scattered in a bowl and piped with quite a bit of dill emulsion, making it quite a oily dish. I believe the cream split. The fish is not extra fresh for such acclaimed restaurant thus the taste of the fish didn't come through, just quite a salty fish (bits) with lots of oil. Feel a bit sick after. 

I stayed on for dessert and had three 1.5cm spheres of average ice cream topped with different fruit slices. 

Been having meals in Michelin stars restaurants, this experience has been the most weirdly disappointing. I did expressed my disappointment and saltiness of my dish. The gentlemen who served simply said, well people do have different preference.

Well done Michelin for your selection, no wonder I stopped believing in your recommendations, unless I just want to impress in a very formal and expensive setting without much concern about the quality of the food and satisfaction of the customers.

Very good chef's tasting menu. Strong acidity balanced by saltiness or light bitterness with hints of sweetness carried the theme of the meal. There was no "comfort food" flavor to be found, the flavor layers were complex and often times edgy. Fragrance was highly featured in the menu, almost every dish came with a distinctive smell, an often overlooked part of the dining experience. Loved the pairing of sole with savory pork. Adding white truffle to beets with venison was such a delight, never though truffle would go so well with beets. Big love.

This is without a doubt the absolute best restaurant in New York City. This is where my husband and I always go if we really want to treat ourselves. 

We have been to Aquavit five times and have always left feeling amazing. The food is unbelievable, the staff is outstanding and the overall feeling in the place is just great. 

This place is really reasonably priced considering how outstanding experience is all-together. 

I would recommend this place to anyone! Please do yourself a favor and go immediately!
