My girlfriend and I loved this place. We wanted the fine dining experience in NYC no gimmicks and aquavit was absolutely 5 Star. My girlfriend is so perfect for these things because she has no shame about asking our waiter a hundred questions about the food and honestly some of dishes were so different that it really helped to know what we were eating and detecting the different tastes. Some of the dishes in our pre fixe really required some lengthy explanations but the food was even more enjoyable when I was told the ingredients and cooking process. 

The staff was great. After we were done eating we talked with one of the staff at the front for a few minutes, really genuine guy, and he took us on a quick tour of the place, I thought that was cool. Real deal eatery with a small army of chefs in the back, I highly recommend if you're looking for fine dining. Bill after tip was $330 for 2; we went with the mid range menu option seasonal pre fixe and we don't drink alcohol.

One of the best seafood restaurants in NYC.  The amount of care and dedication the chef puts into the food preparation and presentation is beyond comparison.  It's a bit pricey, but worthy of the hype.

I came here for lunch and was not disappointed in trying Scandinavian food for the first time in NYC. I did my own three course meal and everything was so delicious. I tried the Raraka, the Halibut, and then the apple crumb ice cream which was so good. The waiter answered every question we had on the menu and detailed each dish.

My wife and I had dinner at Aquavit last night, and it was just fantastic. 
We chose the Chef's tasting Menu, and we were not disappointed.
Every item on the tasting menu was excellent and absolutely delicious !
The service was excellent, and everyone was very nice and attentive.

We highly recommend this restaurant. Definitely well worth the price.

Ramiro and Gelnda

This was the visit since the last one in 2011 (I guess they revamped the whole restaurant at least once as it looked very different).  We waited at the bar area which is very clean and spacious, then proceeded to the dining area.

We decided to go with the 3 course-98 dollar menu with herring, duck breast and chestnut dessert.  What they do, however, is that they add refreshers in between dishes so that you won't feel like having 3 course but more like 5 courses.

Of all things I was very impressed with duck breast.  Herring was good and chestnut was pretty good.  Lastly they give petit four at the end in which you can actually choose however many pieces you can have.  We were also given a recipe and pouch to make holiday liquor.  

Service was definitely up to the standard of Michelin and ny times review.  Would definitely recommend this place for special occasions.

My boyfriend and I were so excited to go here on New Years Eve and booked a reservation few weeks in advance. The Yelp reviews looked great and we were excited at the thought of a 9 course $275 prefix meal to ring in 2017!

What. A. Horrible. Mistake.

From the minute we walked in, the vibes were off. The staff was somewhat aloof as they took our coats; the overly large entry room with a bar in the way back was a confusing sight. The crowd gathering in the restaurant, was also a bit confusing in general - I won't get into that - but we brushed it off to try and enjoy the last evening of 2016. Shortly thereafter, we were brought to our seats in the dining room. We looked around, and then at each other in disbelief. The display of the room looked as though they were about to throw a very dismal birthday party for someone in a dingy nursing home. There were about 10 tables in our area, all situated in a totally random places, all totally bare with a just plain white table cloth and a white napkin. No flowers, no pretty decorations. Some dull colored low air balloons (mustard yellow and gray balloons to be exact) sat in the corner of the room and one dead or fake Christmas wreath hung gloomily on an otherwise empty off white wall. There was actually a large painting frame on another wall ... but the frame was completely empty. I immediately told my boyfriend we should leave right then and there, but it was too big of a move to make at 10pm on New Years Eve.

Our courses started to arrive, and at each course, the waiter either quickly rushed through what we were being served or just put the plate down and scurried away. It seemed like the staff had been hired a few hours before the dinner - I have no idea how other reviewers are saying they were "too polite" or "too serious". At one point in the night, we thought we saw them exchange a few smirks at each other - I can't be totally sure- but the joke really was on us. The food was mundane, a 4/10 at BEST, the best course being the first complimentary dish of fried goat cheese. The rest - not worth ever thinking about again. At one point, they served a slimy Black Sea bass followed quickly by a short rip covered in what tasted almost exactly like A1 steak sauce. So I guess that's something to think about. 

At midnight, the staff passed out crappy 2017 hats and noise makers, to make the night even more low class and cheesy, if possible. Then, a few minutes before midnight, the entire dining room (again, the crowd was very weird) was ushered out to go watch the ball drop in Times Square (it was being projected on the wall in another random room). We stayed at our table and chugged our wine instead.

People have asked me why I didn't complain during the ordeal - my answer being there was nobody to complain to; nobody in charge; nobody who knew what was going on. I still can't be sure this wasn't just a bad dream. 

At least it is funny in hindsight! Happy 2017!
Only the best! Wouldn't expect any less of a michelin starred restaurant. My courses and paired wine were superb. A little pricey, but worth every penny.

We returned to Aquavit for the first time in 18 years and found it to be even better than before. Every course of the three course menu was excellent and pairing courses with Aquavit was fun and reasonably priced. The pre-dinner cocktail (Like Herod) was amazing.

Excellent food. 
But really the only thing that stood out (read: remember after 1-2 years) is the chocolate edible nest egg. Maybe worth coming just for this dessert (one of the BEST of all time I've had). All the other courses paled in comparison. 
Do they have take out instead? I'd gladly pay extra for a to go box of just this. Look at the pics. You'll understand (ie looks amazing, tastes even better)

***UPDATE*** ...5 seconds later

Posted and then updated after looking at pictures myself. Probably one of the 3 best desserts I've had in my life.

This restaurant has delicious food. It taste even better than Jean Georges 3 MS. The interior design is not very nice ( maybe its just for me). Overall, a highly recommended place for a romantic dinner !

We did Feb 14th price fix menu for 2013. It was the best meal i have ever had. At one point i asked if the chef was married. The decor is simple but classy although a bit dark. We were seated promptly. Each plate better than the next. This restaurant is definitely in my must do again list.

I've enjoyed many pleasurable evenings at Aquavit however, tonight was the worst experience imaginable. I hosted a table of 7 guests at 6pm for Valentine's. Service was the worst I've ever received, a vegetarian was served meat after telling them he needed a vegetarian menu!! Throughout our dinner, plates were placed incorrectly. We had a vegan and a vegetarian at our table- both ate things they shouldn't have eaten due to the negligence of the staff. We were also served a bottle of bad wine!! After all these incidents, not once did a manager come to apologize!! 
I'll never waste my time at this establishment again, There's too many fantastic Michelin star restaurants in town!!

Great food, really. It's a true work of art. The concept of the northern European flavors reminded me of the textures and flavors of simple Russian food only with high end execution, creative presentation and in an unusual mix. I could taste each ingredient by itself and could appreciate how the meal came together. 
I am not always a fan with fancy restaurants but felt like this was unique because of the variety of flavors and unusual ingredients.
We did leave hungry, though - after a 5 course meal. Portions are tiny.
The decor was nice and intimate. Many families - grown kids and Their parents; a few dates. 
Bathrooms were blah. Felt like a hospital bathroom. Clean, but no charm. Just blah.
The space is surrounded by constructions and is easy to miss when walking around. 
Staff kept trying to upsell dishes. Our table was very close to the staffs table and I swear - I felt like they were hovering and listening to our conversation all night. Not like we were saying anything interesting or had anything to hide... but still. Didn't feel private. I think that would have been better if we sat further away.
Overall, worth a try. Also, have a big lunch before.

Food 4/5
Service and food presentation 5/5!

Came here alone and ordered the chef's tasting. The server was very attentive and made sure that I didn't feel left alone. The presentation was such an art. Love it! Also the price was very reasonable comparing with other 2 star restaurant. Food wise, the beef tartare was definitely the highlight. Enjoyed every bite of it

not we're talking, this is were james bond villans eat.  delightfully modern atmosphere, and comfortable lounge and dinning areas.  meetballs are huge win, so is the raraka.  great desserts, and overall awesome experience
Not bad, ordered 3 course dinner but it turned out to be 11. there were small dish/dessert like dish were served between main dish. portion was pretty good and it was fresh. staff was friendly.

The best Michelin star restaurant I have been to. The food and service is fantastic. Food presentation is very creative and the complimentary transition in between courses is amazing. The atmosphere is outstanding, light music and fine decoration

Presentation is really outstanding and the food quality is impeccable. The cod is very delicate yet leaving a sharp, salty aftertaste. 

Service is perfect but highly expected from a restaurant at this level. Price is in line with similar restaurants.

I came here for a special occasion last year and my companion and I each did the chefs tasting menu, and we left so full. Each dish was beautifully presented and delicious. The dining room was beautiful and very well laid out. The service was spot on, the wait staff was lovely and everything was perfection. Please make sure you carve out enough time to enjoy this dining experience as we got there for our 9pm reservation and didn't end up leaving until midnight. It's absolutely worth it for a special occasion.

Probably the best meal of my life, and I've been around awhile! The service was amazingly good. The servers are extremely professional and nice. It was supposed to be a 3-course pre-theater dinner, but the dessert alone was 3 courses! Lots of extras, unexpected treats. Dinner wasn't cheap, but it was totally worth it. I would love to go back next time I'm in the Big Apple.

The chef's tasting menu at Aquavit is the best tasting menu I have ever tasted, with just the right amount of food and perfect progression. I didn't really see much Scandinavian influence, but it must be pretty on par with those sought-after restaurants in Scandinavia right now. You can spend hours refreshing the reservation page for noma (now closed), but the easier thing would be to get onto an E train and walk through some scaffolding into this gem of a restaurant. Foie gras ice cream is literally the most bougie thing I've heard, but the result is a freezing cold scoop of cream that releases an intense richness as soon as it touches your tongue. The most unforgettable dish for me was the sea vegetable covered trout, and I particularly enjoyed tasting the two flights of akvavits with my date. As we retreated into our normal lives eating regular ice cream by the pint, Aquavit felt like a surreal experience as if we had an affair but with each other. 10 out of 10.

My fourth time at Aqvavit and it was disappointing. The chefs sampler menu used to be amazing but it has gotten too weird...! The wine pairing this time was less than ok and the entire experience was not as fabulous as the other three times I've been. It is definitely not worth the over $800 for two people....
The food was good but not exactly out of this world. And the service was not as attentive as I would expect. Also, I felt like server was talking down to us.
Fantastic cuisine. Eclectic staff. Genuine Swedish kitchen is badass. Ambiance: clean, elegant, sleek, effective. Emma is certainly one of the finest chefs around. Many mahalos ;) Aloha.

My husband and I dined here during a weekend getaway.  We arrived right on time for our reservation.  As noted previously, there is construction in the building plaza, which makes the restaurant sign easy to miss.

I have to say that each dish was a work of art and outstanding.  We ordered the chef's tasting menu, which ended up being quite a few courses with all of the "snacks" in between.  We were told that the experience should take 2 hours and 15 minutes.  That wasn't going to be a problem.  We did have a show to get to within 3 hours but were assured we would have enough time if we didn't dilly-dally.  The moral is to not go here with any other plans that evening.  Everyone was extremely nice and service was excellent.  It's just that the timing could be better and we also wish we had a more consistent server.  We were late for our show even rushing through dessert.  Our server also seemed to change halfway through dinner without introductions, which was odd.  We loved the dining room set-up and how tables were not cramped.  

Memorable dishes were the 7x beef, which completely melted in your mouth, and the venison, which was tender and flavorful.  All dishes were visually stunning, especially the arctic bird nest dessert.  White asparagus was used throughout a few of the dishes and was placed artfully on the dishes.  Caviar was another ingredient theme that was nicely done.

We tried an aquavit flight of 3 from lightest to darkest: cucumber, blueberry, and blood orange clove.  The blood orange clove was my favorite.  Getting the flight was a great way to sample the flavors.

We loved this experience and the food was marvelous.  We didn't leave hungry.  We recommend telling diners a realistic time frame for the chef's tasting menu of three hours rather than two hours and fifteen minutes to avoid any rushing.  I would definitely return and highly recommend.

Took my wife and daughter to Aquavit for dinner to celebrate Mother's Day and could not have been happier with the experience. The Chef's Tasting Menu is among the best tasting menus that I have ever had.  (We have been to Aquavit previously but had always had the prix fixe menu). The dishes were all wonderful and standouts include the 7X (Wagyu) Beef, the Halibut and Sea Lettuce, the Foie Gras and Rhubarb and the Caviar and White Asparagus. Perhaps the most impressive was the Arctic Bird's Nest for dessert. The presentation was beautiful and the mix of flavors and textures made it an outstanding dessert.

The service was impeccable and our server Diego was very friendly and helpful.

Will definitely look to return!

I have eaten at Aquavit in its various incarnations several times over the last 10+ years. The food is always creative and inventive and worthwhile. Thursday was no exception. However. . . 

1) This is not a restaurant for picky eaters, and the menu available on-line by "googling" "Aquavit menu" is not even close to the limited menu that is current. Since the on-line menu was similar to ones in its past incarnations, I did not investigate further and was surprised by the actual fare.

2) The service was problematic. In our case, perhaps because of #1, the servers were dismissive and impolite and seemed to enjoy playing jokes on the two of us. 

As I said, the food is interesting, but the overall experience was definitely not. I do not plan to return. . . which seems to be what Aquavit wants.

A sublime experience: service is smooth professional and friendly. Each entree is art and wonderful. For example the cod entree is an "aquarium" of diverse and piquant flavors. Herring is special beyond all expectations with sweet and tart flavor and textures. I would eat here every night and not miss another.

I would like to see more from a two stars Michelin. The chef menu start like only god will know how she cook the 7xwagyu beef and other starters so perfectly. But after the first four courses she goes down and down and some dishes are too salty. The hot smoked salmon is with no sense in the middle of the menu and the venison is really salty. But overall you should come to try.

My husband and I had lunch. We had a 3 course lunch; I had Gravlax for starter, Scandinavian Boullabaisse for main and Black currant for dessert. Everything was delicious, and the reputation and Michelin stars so well deserved. Serving was discrete, and throught the lunch we were offered 2 different kinds of Scandinavian bread.We would definitely go there for dinner one time

This was my first time having a 2 star or above Michelin restaurant or a Scandinavian restaurant and now I wonder why I waited so long for either. I had one dietary restriction before we began our chefs tasting journey and all accommodations made by the chef were absolutely amazing. The sweetbreads and calfs liver and cucumber dishes absolutely won the night as most flavorful and unique dishes. All dishes were presented wonderfully and the ambiance was incredible. The artic birds nest is probably the most aesthetically pleasing dish I've ever seen and the taste was just as good. The experience is worth the price tag.

4-4.5 stars. I was very excited to come here since it has an acclaimed female chef. I was overall very satisfied with the food, but I don't know if it would necessarily rise to level of 5 stars.  

Space
The space is very minimalistic but beautiful if that's your style.

Service 
The service was fantastic, the waiter was very helpful and gave great recommendations. 

Food
We went during their herring tasting and having never tasted a herring some of us just ordered a jar of it to share (dill flavor). I was pleasantly surprised by how good this tasted but it was definitely salty and I don't know how much I could've eaten.

For my appetizer I ordered the Raraka, which was amazing and all the flavors were perfect

For my entree I ordered the salmon burger, which was huge. The salmon was extremely juicy and the remoulade was delicious. It came with yummy potato chips as well.

For dessert we shared the chocolate, which if you like banana you should order this.  The portion was very small, however and I don't know if I'd order dessert again.

Overall, we had a fantastic meal and I'll be back eventually.

Had the best lunch I have ever had at Aquavit. They had a special lunch smorgasbord for midsummer. The selection of herrings, smoked fish, cured meats, salads, hot entrees, and desserts was absolutely phenomenal. The highlight for me were definitely the herring paired with aquavit as well as the prinsesstårta paired with a delicious Madeira. They have the smorgasbord several times a year and I recommend it.

The Chef's tasting menu - 19 separate servings - is worth it. My wife and I went for our 20th anniversary as part of a trip to New York. If you can afford it, this is a must-visit. We don't drink alcoholic beverages, and for the two of us we spent $500 (including tip and taxes).  The presentation, service and taste are all at the top level.  There was only one item that was not up to the overall standard: the strawberry tart near the end. It just didn't have the same wow factor. I would recommend skipping it. I have a mushroom allergy and the chef was able to make superb substitutions for the two items that needed it. My favorite item was the venison tartare, but many were a close second. The experience took a full 3.5 hours. I can't imagine it taking any less than 3 hours even with rushing through the items: make sure you plan for a long dinner!

The food is sublime, the presentation whimsical and beautiful, the service first class and the experience top notch. 

The tasting menu is the way to go here. It will take almost three hours and feature something like 18 courses when you take into account all of the off-the-menu surprises as well as well as the written menu. 

Even though the menu changes very frequently, the arctic bird's nest is always there and it's always the best way to end a meal at Aquavit.
I had the tasting menu at lunch. The food was amazing. Well worth the price -- excellent service and wines. A truly delicious meal. Enjoyed Arctic char, langoustines, and berry dessert
Came here for my birthday and boy this place did not disappoint. Beautiful food, excellent wine pairing and exquisitely crafted. Service was impeccable!
Really amazing food and service.  Very classy and multitude of flavors.  Worth the two Michelin stars.  We took the tasting menu. Three and a half hours of paradise.

Aquavit is an extremely trendy Scandinavian restaurant. As someone who is not well versed in Scandinavian food, the menu was a little bit challenging to decipher, however the wait staff is very knowledgeable about the dishes. I've enjoyed all the dishes that I've tried at Aquavit and thought that the presentation of the dishes were superb. (Definitely deserving of its 2 michelin stars.) My recommendations are to try the rye bread they offer and to save a little bit of room for the cookies they offer at the end of your meal.

Really good experience. I came with my friends for her birthday, and I was pregnant that time so I cannot eat undercooked food. We three ordered the testing menus, so the kitchen made some adjustments for mine dishes. Even though I cannot eat caviar or some beef, the chef used other cooked meat for mine meal;my dishes still kept at a high level, it was worthy. 
I used to have another testing menu at Gabriel Kreuther while I was pregnant, and they also avoid undercooked food for my dishes. But that was really bad. They almost changed most of my dishes to vegetables. 
So I feel like Aquavit really pay attention to every customer.
Besides the food, the service is really good.
Amazing food, excellent service and a sommelier who clearly loves his job - great night with some wok buddies!

Made a reservation for my eldest's 21st birthday. We thoroughly enjoyed the 13-course tasting with wine pairings. Food preparation and presentation was exquisite....loved the imagination and freshness of all components associated with each fish. Wine pairings were adventurous but well balanced. Perfect evening for a very special occasion

Food lives up to its reputation. Had the smoked trout and it was smoky, savory with a touch of sweetness. The Swedish meatballs were better than the ones I had in Stockholm - the sauce was not too creamy and the jam was very tart. Staff are are quite attentive and pleasant.

I really liked how they didn't clear my plate until my friend was done eating. Many restaurants rush to clear plates when some but not all are done and i find it quite rude.

Will go back again.

TBH I wouldnt necessarily give this place 2 mich stars...its more of a 1 star to me.

The service is impeccable so i will give it to them there. 

The food though good was not amazing and the reason i say this is that alot of the dishes have a pickle/fermented taste to them. Personally i hate pickles and anything that slightly taste like pickles.

We went here for dinner and had a fantastic time.
We opted for the Chef's Menu and the sommelier helped us choose a nice bottle of rose to compliment the dining experience.
Dish after dish we were surprise by the flavors, the textures and the smells of the food - it truly is an experience.

The staff was always attentive and catering to us throughout the dinner.

If you are looking for a place to have fabulous dinner, this is it.

Cheers.

I don't know shit about Scandinavian food, but I'm guessing Aquavit offered something of a skewed introduction to the cuisine. My mom and I went for a weekday lunch, and we were pleased to find how much we enjoyed herring, at least as prepared at a Michelin-starred restaurant.

The place was fancy, with a beautiful entryway to a beautiful dining room flush with chandeliers and vibrant plants. The design wasn't over the top lavish, but it was thoughtfully done, probably in the vein of a "Scandinavian design" Pinterest board. The tables were laid with textured white tablecloths; all the dishware looked precious and artisanal. Aquavit is in midtown and offers a lunch prix fixe, so I'm guessing it's a popular spot for business meals. The atmosphere was right for it, calm and upscale but not romantic. It wasn't full on a Tuesday, either, so I'd guess reservations can be made on reasonably short notice.

Service was immaculate. Our waiter Nestor (sick name) was a true professional, attentive and warm without being informal. He got plenty of help from a robust staff that made sure all our needs were taken care of before we fully noticed we had them. We wanted a couple of glasses of wine with our meal, and Nestor helped us out. We had a Herri Mina white blend that went well with our seafood-heavy meal.

The food was outstanding, starting with a bread service of fluffy sourdough and dense, nutty Danish rye with quality butter and sea salt. The lunch menu offered a $58 three-course prix fixe, with two options for appetizers and entree and one for dessert, as well as a more extensive a la carte menu and a $105 seasonal tasting, which would have required table participation. We opted to go half prix fixe and half a la carte, and this worked out quite nicely. I liked that the prix fixe seemed to include some of the best dishes the restaurant had to offer.

We started with the gravlax (prix fixe) and the herring sampler (a la carte), and both were tremendous. The gravlax--apparently not smoked but cured salmon--came in delicate briny little chunks mixed with dill and bursting bubbles of trout roe, topped off with asparagus, dill foam, and tiny new potato chips. Light and delightful, with a lot of interesting textures. Whether you're in it for the Scandinavian experience or just to maximize deliciousness, the herring sampler is a must order at Aquavit. It was a gorgeous platter of five types of herring--matjes, glassblower's, lingonberry, mustard, and horseradish--served with priest cheese, fine chopped red onion, and a little salad of lettuce and potato. I had no idea pickled fish could be so appetizing.

Our entree course brought more incredible seafood, in the form of a Scandinavian bouillabaisse (prix fixe) and a fillet of striped bass (a la carte). I'm not sure what made the bouillabaisse Scandinavian, but it was a remarkable dish, one of the best entrees I've had in recent memory. There was plenty of seafood--cod, halibut, mussels, shrimp, and scallop--along with cauliflower, peas, pickled heirloom tomatoes, and a fennel aioli. Every individual element was perfectly cooked, from the creamy scallops to the delicate cod to the peeled, juicy tomatoes and the al dente peas, the best peas I've had in years. The striped bass was also a strong dish, the bass meaty and flavorful, served with artichoke, fresh heirloom tomatoes, and a zippy arugula paste.

Before our dessert, we got a nice sweet preview: a wooden box stacked with tiny fresh baked cookies. We ate them up and they were all great, but I especially appreciated the salty chocolate chip. The prix fixe dessert was a strawberry rhubarb crumble with vanilla ice cream and it was pretty phenomenal. The strawberry and rhubarb were both lovely--strawberries are one thing, but it must be hard to make rhubarb so irresistible, crunchy and tart in the best possible way--and they came over a dense buttery cake that was really its own event. We supplemented this dessert with little scoops of black currant and sea buckthorn ice cream and apple sorbet. This was the weakest part of the meal. The apple sorbet was the best of them, bright and refreshing, but it had a big chunk of ice in it; the ice creams had a gummy texture that I didn't love.

No matter, this was a wonderful meal, with top notch service and food. I'd recommend Aquavit if you're looking for a special lunch in Manhattan. Now I'm curious to see what ordinary Scandinavian cuisine is all about.

Maybe this place was overhyped, but I was just not a huge fan. 

The herring sampler plate was lovely to look at with all the different types of pickled fish but all I got out of it was sour. Yes, I know they are pickled but I was hoping the sauces or toppings or something would balance the sourness or make the flavors more interesting. 

The general atmosphere was also quite cold...

Don't think I will be returning.

Do not eat here. No matter how many Micheline stars a place has, it doesn't give them the right to charge you 50$ for tap water. Especially without telling you beforehand.

Also, what's with the green tomato leftovers in every dish? Recycling ingredients much?

Overall it was a disappointment. 
We had the chef's tasting menu. 
Some courses were good and creative and others like the desert were far from the standard of a 2 Michelin star restaurant. 
The seasoning, sides and style were very repetitive.
The service was really good except from the guy serving the bread who was extremely mean and rude. 
Nothing was really bad, far from that but at $600 for two persons and 2 Michelin star I was expecting way more. 
Definitely not as good as other 1,2 or 3 stars restaurant in the city and way overpriced.

I have confused feelings about this place. It's underwhelming in a charming way - but I suppose that is all of Scandinavia. 

If you've been to Agern then Aquavit will seem a bit more understated and flat out plain at times. The interior is intentionally left minimal and space isn't rather large. The service was impeccable though forced smiles can get boring for a length of the Chefs Tasting Menu. Some of the highlights of the meal were Venison Tartare, Wagyu Beef - the Paté was excellent, and the Sweetbreads with Chanterelle was delicious. Note there is no chicken on the tasting menu.

I must say, this was quite the experience. The food was excellent, and the seasonal tasting menu was full of various flavors, colors and textures, despite only being 5 course. It still took us around 2 to 2.5 hours to complete.

The menu included:
- Tomato and rapeseed Swedish pancake and pork belly (starter)
- Spanish mackerel and Heirloom tomatoes
- Scallops and succulents
- Arctic char and snowpeas
- Malt and radish (chef's inclusion)
- Lamb and Cabbage
- Lingonberry Kombucha (to clean the pallet)
- Huckleberry and almond dessert 

In my opinion, well worth the $125 price point. The waiter was very friendly, but since we were one of the last reservations I felt a bit rushed throughout. If the waiter has to ask you whether you feel rushed, the answer is probably yes. I would have also enjoyed a bit more of an explanation of each dish and the significance. I was very difficult for me to understand the central theme in the menu (or maybe there wasn't one??).

Sensational cuisine! Flavors I've never experienced before. Service was impeccable, sommelier knowledgeable and chef utterly creative. Words can't describe the justice this place deserves. Should be 3 Michelin stars.

I would've liked to pay around a $100 less than I did for that experience. At close to $300/person (seasonal tasting and wine pairing) you want everything to be spot on. There were a couple courses that I just didn't enjoy at all (they were difficult to even eat past a bite) and 1-2 pairings that were very blah. Nothing was THAT exceptional. But the service was friendly, you certainly leave full yet not unsatisfyingly so. Overall 3.5 stars.

I chose to eat at the bar with my cousins to celebrate my birthday and was the first to arrive. I immediately love how laid back and chic it was, tucked away in a corner. It was interesting to see the huge jars of aquavit lining the wall. I felt completely at ease while waiting alone for them to arrive. The bartender made me a lingonberry cocktail first while I was waiting and it was really good. I ordered the Swedish meatballs and my cousins ordered the duck and fish, which we all enjoyed.

My partner and I went to Aquavit for an anniversary dinner, and overall, I thought the food was very good and the service and hospitality outstanding.

We were one of us to sit down for the night, and even then, they did not rush us or slack off at the service even though getting to be very late towards the end of our meal. All the different very servers genuinely seemed to enjoy their jobs.

The food was outstanding, and I would describe the tasting menu as light and refreshing. Nothing really rich and heavy like Italian pasta sauces and things like that. Everything was cooked expertly. 

The wine pairings, in addition to being a very good value, were varied and didn't stay too much in one region of the world. I think that's a special skill to match Scandinavian food with Old World wines and New World wines.

Overall, of course there are a lot of food options in New York but this was a very special meal. Not crazy expensive considering its two-star status.

I would give 5 stars for our experience and taste of food, but 1 star for how the management handled the matter when I called them the next day after getting FOOD POISONING 6 hour after dining at Aquavit.  
My sister and I were treated to a birthday dinner at Aquavit by a friend, and we really did have a lovely experience and loved all the food on the menu.  We were all raised in Sweden, so the twists on traditional Swedish dishes was fantastic and we all LOVED it! Service was wonderful as well. 
6 hrs after our dinner, I started violent vomiting, which fortunately only lasted a couple of hours. My sister and friend encouraged me to call Aquavit the following day.  I agreed that it was a good idea, to prevent anyone else from getting ill and just give them feedback.    The person that answered the phone was very apologetic and promised that a manager would reach out to me shortly.  That evening, no one had called me back so I tried again and the person I spoke to this time began questioning me and instead of apologizing or thanking me for the feedback she only focused on that it could have been something else, and that food poisoning from fish usually takes longer to break out.  Our friend's husband ended up calling them back and they were promised a gift card and special treatment next time.  

I completely understand that it's probably not a common experience that someone would get food poisoning while dining at this fine establishment, and I wasn't blaming them, just very disappointed about how uncaring and unresponsive the management was.

Aquavit proves you don't have to be French to be top notch. The food is exquisite and the service is first rate.  I wouldn't call his restaurant authentic though, fushion would be a more apt term, as our meals were prepared with daikon radish and squash, so they definitely add asian and new world flavors to the food.

My friend and I tried the seasonal tasting menu. I also did the wine pairing. Every course was first rate, inventive and fresh. While the wines were good, i wouldn't recommend the wine pairing.  i just wasn't wowed over and would recommend simply purchasing a bottle or ordering by the glass. The wine parings were Gamay, Tocai, a Legrein and a Riesling, While they were ok, they just didn't add that wow factor to the courses. Do yourself a favor and look at the wine list and select something you like and stick with it.

The one oddity about this restaurant it is incredibly hard to get a reservation, and I had to book a month in advance, but dining we saw the tables 1/3 empty. This is not the first restaurant I've experienced this phenomenon at and its a bit puzzling.

Bottom line, is if you've tried the high end restaurants such as Daniel or Italian such as Felidia Aquavit and looking for something a little different, this should be on the list.
One of my favorite Michelin restaurants. Theses 15 courses are totally worth your night and your money. Amazing food and first class service！

I've been here three times for lunch so far and it's always been a fantastic culinary experience. My favorite dish is the cod - deliciously sublime! I also loved their crawfish and the herring sampler. However, if you don't like fish, I guess you won't enjoy yourself. They have Swedish meatballs, which are good, but not as great as other dishes. Finally, I like the Scandinavian decor of the restaurant  - superior design!

I have been going to Aquavit for many decades, even dined there one weekend twice because it was so fabulous.  We were there this past weekend, and it has changed dramatically.  First, no more a la carte menu.  Second, the restaurant is now in what was the bar.  Third, we had a seriously pretentious server who assumed we normally dined at a fast food restaurant and  were clueless. Fourth, the food was good, but not sublime.  Some of the mezzo courses were actually bad.  They finally sent over another server to try to save us from the one we had.  He did work hard to try to save us.  I just long for former days when we had a true dining experience.  Bottom line - the food is good, but they have lost their luster.

What a wonderful three and a half hour 10-course Chef Tasting experience from start to finish! Excellent-creative cooking and attentive service. 
We enjoyed every dishes on the menu! Couple of them really stand out, the exceptional venison truffle (so creative), and the freeze foie gras dish just blew my mind! Shout out to Chef Emma Bengtess!
Delicious delicious delicious. The restaurant manages to make the simples of foods into a gastronomical feast. I can see why this is one of the top restaurants to visit in NY!

The chef's tasting menu here was like a dream! Every dish came out looking not only very artistically plated but tasting great!

I really enjoyed the kristal caviar and white asparagus dish. Also on the menu was sweetbread and morels. Sweetbread isn't a very common ingredient and so it was an interesting experience for us. And yes, the arctic bird's nest lives up to the hype. It was crunchy, nutty, fluffy, soft, sweet, tarte and the consistency of the dessert was a perfect recreation of a bird's nest. I really enjoyed the play of texture and appreciated that so much thought went into one dessert. Also, doesn't hurt that Bengtsson is one of two American female head chefs with two michelin stars. :)

Dinner service was about 4 hours as we were given quite a few amuse bouche sporadically, between plates. 

I noticed quite a few guests ordered the smaller tasting menus or maybe a la carte. But since it was our first time there, we were ambitious and hungry too. No regrets there!

Being a Swedish person living in NYC I'm very lucky to have a restaurant like Aquavit to go to whenever my craving for food from my home country comes. The meatballs are excellent, löjrommen is absolutely delicious, Skagen is great, gravlax spot on etc. I love this place thanks a lot to the whole team that you are so good!!!

Went her for a company xmas party. We had a private room and paid $200 pp for a three course meal. No amuse bouches. No cookies at the end. Just the three courses, no frills. Food was average. Bread was good. Other options available in NYC for that much money.

The restaurant took our credit card number months in advance and warned us to arrive on time -which we did- but they made us wait because people were still eating at our reserved table. We waited about 10 minutes, and they did not even offer us a free glass of water for the wait. I went to the toilet to wash my hands, and saw, to my dismay that it was filthy. I couldn't believe it. This is a very expensive restaurant, and this toilet situation was a bad omen. I told the hostess that the toilet was disgusting. She said she would check it. Later on, I went to use another bathroom, and to my utter disgust, it was filthy too - overflowing trash, toilet paper all over the place, some of the tiles were loose, I almost fell, the sink had not been cleaned who knows how long. I'll spare you additional details.
So should I talk about the food, ambiance and service now? It is irrelevant. Imagine how the kitchen looks like if these toilets are not maintained properly. Ugh. But if you decide to eat there, be prepared to say goodbye to a lot of money, and perhaps to catch something if you use the toilet.

Came here for dinner and was not prepared for the culinary adventure I was about to embark. Each dish was artfully presented and had an enormous range of flavors. Each bite was a different experience completely confusing my tastebuds in a very good way. Definitely recommend if you're feeling up for a unique foodie experience!

A very lovely restaurant with friendly staff
We went there for three courses pre fixed menu. All the food was delicious. I love the little tomatoes in the seafood dish. They looked cute and tasted extremely good. The dessert was a perfect conclusion to the lunch.
Highly recommend this restaurant! I think it's even better than some 3 star Michelin restaurants.

Another excellent restaurant that I wish I can rate with 4.5 stars. Beautiful ambiance, friendly, corresponding and well coordinated staffs, and artfully delicious dishes are among the many great attributes of Aquavit. My wife and I came to Aquavit to celebrate our 5th wedding anniversary. Although at first glance, the Michelin 2 stars restaurant looked average and ordinary at its front entrance on a cold December night. However, once we walked passed the front door and velvet curtains, the warm welcoming sight within immediately and gentlely embraced us like a long lost friend. The receptionists at the counter warmly and charmingly smiled at us and kindly took our coats. At the moment we had arrived a bit early then the reserved time, hence we decided to hangout at the lounge area. To pass time , I ordered the AdultCircus cocktail and a cucumber/pineapple nonalcoholic beverage  for my wife, which she absolutely loved it. Soon afterwards, we were informed that our table was ready and our journey of a wonderful and exciting Swedish dinner had thus began. 
Our long (3.5 hours chef's tasting menu) culinary journey commenced with two small appetizers: Seaweed and Mussel and Swedish pancakes and pork belly. Both dishes were not extraordinary but simple, nothing fancy but hearty. The fluffy pancakes with pork belly(bacon really) and the mussels with rich broth gave us a warm welcoming. Our next small dish was two tiny round dark brown balls fried crunchy. And honestly if we weren't told it was venison and truffles we would not have guessed it in our life time, but then again how often would one gets to eat deer meat? Next we were served with two seafood dishes, caviar and sea urchins! The Kristal caviar, topped with elderflowers, had a great presentation and its rich savoury taste was well balanced with a sour sauce. And the equally delicious sea urchins came on a toast stick. Afterwards by taking a short break on seafood, we were introduced to a wonderful smoked beef tartar that was covered with a crunchy shell that would release the smokes upon breaking it. After the red meat, seafood came back with an amazing Norwegian king crab and apple. The dish consisted two equally long cylinders: one was king crab meat   and pork wrapped by a sheet of apple. It was the most delicious seafood course of the tasting menu. Next was foie gras and red beet, delicious, creamy, savoury and at first we had thought this was a dessert, panna cotta covered in jelly. The next three dishes were, halibut and chestnut cream, excellent pairing, squab and buckwheat, half grilled and half fried tender and juicy, and finally 7X Wagyu beef that had melted in our mouth. All were wonderfully prepared. Since the last three dishes had covered the sea, sky and land, now it was time for dessert. Havgus and fig served as a transition between savoury and sweet with baked cheese and fruit. Then our server brought out two small dark chocolate covered ginger ice cream pop to prepare us for the climactic and signature dessert dish - Arctic Bird's nest. This artistic beauty was an epic to behold and a sublime representation of life and hope. With chocolate noodles as the nest and white chocolate with custard fillings as bird eggs, this ultimate dessert was too dear to eat. 
Aquavit had lived up to its Michelin two stars with well executed and presented dishes and excellent coordinated staffs. The only complaints we had was the epic time consumption (3.5 hours, that's 21 mins each tapas sized dish) and most importantly the dishes were overall too salty. I dont know if the extra salt was put deliberately for tasting menu or it was just the way how the chef cooks, but either way it's unhealthy and hence I can't give 5 stars.
P.S We were told there was a surprise for our anniversary celebration at the restaurant, but nothing happened, weird, maybe the staffs forgot about it.

The service at Aquavit is impeccable. There are rotating people who explain each dish and your water glass is never empty. They even escort you towards the bathroom.
We also loved the decor. Very minimalist. 
We did the Chef's Tasting menu, which honestly for us was so much about the experience itself. It is such a pleasure to try all of these unique dishes. Some standout dishes for us were 1. the first amuse bouche- the Swedish pancake with salmon tartare and dill powder. 2 the second amuse bouche, the mussel with cheese 3. The king crab and apple and pork (my favorite by FAR) 4. Halibut 5. Arctic birds nest. 
Some interesting things to note about some other dishes (again, not bad, but definitely unique): 1. The foie gras comes frozen (liquid nitrogen possibly?) amongst some beet leather, candied beets and some sort of yogurt. The frozen aspect takes away the typical creaminess found in foie gras. 2. The squab legs comes with the claw still attached so if that is something that may bother you, consider yourself warned. 

Overall it was a wonderful experience.
My husband and I went here for my birthday last year. I cannot say enough about how exceptional the food and staff were. The experience was worth every penny.

Another food adventure to a Michelin rated restaurant, and it did not disappoint. We did the chefs tasting menu with the wine pairing this time. Each and every course (total of 14) was extravagant and sumptuous. 

Upon leaving, We received an envelope with the date, name and description of each dish we had. This is the only reason I can list them here; I would've never remembered the 14 whopping courses I had. The service was impeccable and the ambiance was exactly what I would imagine to be the epitome of "Scandinavian chic". Very minimalistic with architecturally sharp light fixtures. The mood was romantic and our servers had a sense of humor which was nice. 

The only reason I am giving 4 out of 5 stars is because of the wine pairing. Although some of the wines were incredible with the dish presented, many of the wines were ports: quite thick, syrupy and heavy. Towards the end of the meal It was hard to continue tasting because I was becoming uncomfortably full from the heavy port wines- but of course I had to troop on and continue the tasting until the end. I am sooo glad I did! The arctic birds nest dessert was sublime! The other courses that particularly stood out to me were: 7x wagyu beef and truffles, foie gras and rhubarb, venison and endives, and the goats cheese and nettles. 

My only recommendation is to skip the wine pairing. 

Otherwise- it was a beautiful dining experience.

DO NOT RECOMMEND

Total price for group of four with tasting menu and drinks: $833 before tip.

Tl:dr overpriced and underwhelming

As soon as we walked in something felt off. Service was cold and awkward, and we had to wait 20 minutes past our reservation time for our table to be ready. 

Once seated, the ambiance seemed strange--the lighting too dim and the music incorrect for the environment and a bit loud. 

The service was terrible--not because they were trying to be rude, but it seemed like the restaurant had simply hired the cheapest staff. They had a hard time pronouncing the dishes and all seemed very nervous. 

The food was nothing special and FAR FAR short of a two Michelin star rating. Our group of four often shared dishes that some simply did not wish to finish. Almost all felt uninspired and used unnecessary cooking techniques that did not come off well (frozen foie gras) and some even had flavors bordering on offensive (heavy smoke on venison tartare). 

The caviar was the one dish I will miss--an intriguing story of texture and flavor that continues to change for a while around the classic briny salt that pervades much of Scandinavian fare. A great introduction that deserved a meal to match. 


Extra note:
The staff seemed like they didn't want to be there, and over time we began to feel the same. No one at any of the other tables was having fun, and we felt kind of scammed out of our money when we left. There is no way this place retains two Michelin stars.
Fantastic two Michelin star restaurant. The food was expectedly outstanding. I would go back for sure.

Aquavit - Michelin 2 Star - worth every bite and dollar bill escaping my bank account. 

Our family went to Aquavit for the Chef's Tasting during lunch time. Not knowing what to really expect, we were blown away rather quickly. 

Note to the friendly Yelp friends, DO THE SEASONAL TASTING. YES IT'S WORTH THE EXTRA CASH. Don't be skimpy with this! 

Amuse Bouche
Scallop and Sea Urchin
Artic Char and Kavring
Turbot and Sunchoke
Duck and Honeynut Squash
Blood Orange and Honey

Total per person: $105.00

Price point is fantastic. Literally worth spending 2.5 hours over there. 

In addition, some great things I've noticed that makes them a Michelin 2-star: 

- Timing of the food: before we started, the waiter asked if we were on a time crunch or if we were here to enjoy the food. We said the latter, and the timing of each plate was impeccable. The reason I state this as a positive is the way they make sure each customer is curated to their own schedule. We had one couple who came an hour later then us yet finished right on time with us. Another family was here but they had barely ate their 4th course (of course, having wine pairing does ease time even more...) 

- Man, that Scandinavian furniture doe - no wonder i love Volvo interiors so much. There's so something so elegant about the way the chairs and tables are designed. Cleary designed to emulate a modern living room in the middle of a cold winter, Aquavit has a done a fantastic job with creating such a beautiful vibe. 

- Immaculate service. Attentive and focused, super kind and always making sure everyone's food was plated and sat at the same time. Beautiful choreography that all Michelin restaurants should attain. 

- Surprises even after dessert - a nice wooden box of fresh baked cookies. UGH why are we so easy to please? Coffee and cookies after a nice meal is literally a feeling that everyone needs to understand. 

Aquavit is easily recommended with conviction. There is without a doubt that anyone with the time or special occasion should dive into the beautiful world of Aquavit.
I went to this restaurant with my fiancé many times. We loved it. I can't wait to go there Valentine's Day
Been here a few times for lunch. Food is quite average but service is good. Nice and quiet ambiance too. Will come back but not the top Michelin star restaurant you can find in Nyc

Long known as one of Manhattan's best Scandinavian Restaurants, Chef Marcus Samuelsson making a name for himself and the space near MoMA during the late-1990s and early 2000s, it was not until former Pastry Chef Emma Bengtsson took over the kitchen in 2014 that Aquavit captured its second Michelin Star and although some may say the Food has never been quite the same since Samuelsson departed for stardom a lunch on Thursday indicated that there is still a lot to like about the place.

Officially located at 65 East 55th Street for nearly three decades, a lounge up front and muted dining room to the side given splashes of color by wall art and flowers, it was just minutes prior to a 12:45pm reservation that coats were checked and diners led to a linen-clad four-top, the collection of leather banquets and sleek chairs providing comfortable seating over the course of nearly two hours.

Presenting a truncated lunch menu in comparison to dinner, a three-course prix fixe and seasonal tasting menu offered in addition to a la carte plates including Aquavit's famous Swedish Meatballs and Salmon Burger that are not offered in the evening save for at the Bar, it was after settling in with greetings from a youthful captain that decisions were made, a total of ten plates divided into three courses tallying just $65 per person exclusive of Beverages.

In many ways a unique Restaurant despite its traditional underpinnings, Samuelsson's childhood as an Ethiopian raised in Sweden and Chef Bengtsson's Stockholm roots befitting  a classic sort of cuisine that stands in stark contrast to the global obsession with "New Nordic" ideas, it was after a brief delay that two types of Bread including dense Rye stuffed with Sunflower Seeds were joined by four Appetizers, the trio of Fishes all cured or smoked in-house and highlighted by Salmon Tartare beneath Dill, diced Apples and Trout Roe while the "7x Beef Tartare" placed hand-cut Prime Filet lacquered in smoky Mayonnaise beneath crispy Potatoes along with briny Capers.

Deferring much of the order to two friends who'd dined at Aquavit prior, their choice of a Herring Sampler proving far better than anticipated save for the slices overwhelmed by Horseradish, it was after a prolonged wait that Water and Bread were refreshed along with share plates in anticipation of entrees, the $28 Swedish Meatballs tender and rich alongside traditional condiments while Sausage with Sauerkraut and Mustard Seed Potatoes was a bit too pungent bite-for-bite, a far better balance of flavor saved for Dumplings called Kroppkakor featuring mashed Potatoes stuffed with Allspice, Onions and Pork.

Dining slowly and enjoying the serenity of the room, something less and less common these days that makes Aquavit an ideal place for catching up or talking business, it was once again with fresh plates that a trio of Desserts was presented, the prix-fixe "Apple" an elongated strip not dissimilar to Sticky Toffee Pudding in texture while "Coffee" and the specially requested Dinner-only Arctic Bird's Nest were both textbook examples of how to balance sweetness with bitterness while adding  intrigue by way of crispy Grains and fresh Berries.

Well worth the trip. Recently came here for my wife's birthday celebration. Had the seasonal tasting menu with wine pairings. Food came quickly in perfect presentation, made for a very fun and fast 2 hour dinner. 

My wife loved the trout and I loved the turbo. But all was just perfect. 

Service is impeccable, you'll enjoy the perfect full service dinner.

Probably my all time favorite restaurant in New York. Impeccable service, and impeccable cuisine. My husband and I were regulars at Aquavit London while we lived there, and were excited to visit Aquavit NYC as soon as we got back. Needless to say it did not disappoint! There wasn't a single dish in the Chef's tasting menu that we did not enjoy!

I have dined at Aquavit a number of times and have enjoyed myself. I will not be dining there again.

I had a reservation last week: two for dinner at 8pm. Unfortunately, early in the day of our reservation, my dinner companion was clearly coming down with this season's virulent flu. Coughing, runny nose, sneezing, sore throat, the works. As he had never been to Aquavit, he wanted to keep our reservation and go anyway. In my view, he was just spewing germs and going out to dinner would be at the very least highly inconsiderate to both the other dinners and the staff at Aquavit. I called to cancel our reservation early in the day and explained why we were cancelling - I was abruptly reminded of their cancellation policy and charged $100.00.

I was aware of their cancellation policy when I made the reservation, and they were in fact following the letter of their policy. HOWEVER, I would expect any better establishment to make an accommodation in this case. Particularly when we could have well kept our reservation but chose not to as a courtesy to others. At the very least, perhaps a credit against a future visit? Aquavit chose the wrong thing here in my view, putting a small cancellation fee above an opportunity to provide the right kind of service - respectful of the patron, the staff, and its dining population. I don't care about the fee, I care what it represents - a careless disregard for participating in a community trying to stop the spread of a particularly deadly flu.

Came here for Valentine's Day.  It was the highlight of my stay...the very best that I had in Manhattan.  And, it brings to my attention that there are differences between 2 star Michelins in different cities.  A two star Michelin in New York City is a high bar.  

I found the food here transportingly good.  It is what I'm always looking for - to be blown away.  Such a hedonistic, satisfying experience.  My husband preferred this to Le Bernardin (3 M stars).

Chef Emma Bengtsston succeeds Marcus Samuelsson.  She did such a beautiful job on Valentines day...with the menu and its execution.  I see now that she is not only extremely talented but also gorgeous!  Beautiful and talented, love it! :)

They have a fun and varied selection of Aquavit and we put together a flight.  We liked 2 out of the 3.  We enjoyed the Horseradish and the Anise, Caraway and Fennel.  The one we didn't think lived up to its description was the Juniper and Lemon (I think!).  It was very lemony with not enough juniper and tasted a lot like limoncello...I had asked the sommelier for recommendations but my husband was curious to try what grabbed him  -always a risk :D

Trio of oysters.  Beautiful.  The picture does not do it justice.  They were arranged on salt with small, smooth stones strewn about.  Like a Zen garden!  Of course, the large dollops of caviar were delightful and romantic  but there were varied textures too.  Little sorbet balls on the one...Just to excite the senses.  The classic pairing of champagne, from Champagne was perfect.  Nice and dry, the perfect complement to our oysters.

The wine pairing selection for our meal was amazing.  The sommelier told us that the staff has a lot of fun with this.  They do a really fantastic job here.  The wines complement the food so well.  The pairings were creative and exciting.  Rather notably small pours.  

Next we had the langoustine and apple.  This is where the high quality of the food and its preparation really started to shine.  It was just so delectable and delicate and flavorful and served at the perfect just warm temperature.  Comforting and satisfying and it had and intensely concentrated grilled or smoky quality too it.

The salmon and red beet with some colorful radish was shaped into art, a beautiful rose.  I love gravlax so much and I make it home often with the best fish that I can find.  This is better!  It was marbled and just superb.  Tasted delicious.  In terms of balance, we thought that there was a little too much acidity.  But we still loved this dish too.

Halibut and Tomato was the zenith of the tasting menu.  The menu says halibut and tomato - yes, and with chunks of sexy lobster with a fabulous texture!  The seafood was swimming around in a slightly rich, light, airy chiffonnade or frothy emulsion ;) Warm and sensual, delicate purely satisfying dish.  This was paired with the highlight from the tasting menu, a 1999 Chenin Blanc.  Full bodied and thick, oakey, and interesting pairing.  Not my favorite but as with everything else, nice choice -adding to our enjoyment of the dish.  Very exclusive, very limited edition.

Duck and Lingonberries was dramatic to look at.  The intense color of lingonberries was beautiful and reminded me of the deep intense color of blood.  The wine was Franck Balthazar, Syrah, Selections, Cornas, Rhone Valley, France 2015.  It was an amazing pairing that complemented the duck to perfection.  We both thought that the bouquet actually smelled intensely like duck, just by itself before the meat even arrived!  It's a meaty, meaty selection. Thoroughly enjoyed this pairing.

The cheese and red port was actually a whipped cheese-themed creation.  Very savory and with a little baked cheese crisp on top.
Creative take on the cheese course.

Next we had strawberry and tarragon mousse-type creation, with dabs and dribbles of this and that.  What we really liked was the wine pairing.  The server said it's nicknamed ambrosia.  Well it was very nice as the meal was coming to a close.   Donnafugata, Muscat, Ben Rye (there is an accent on that e), Passito di Pantelleria, Sicily, Italy 2014.

Beautiful touch, another classic chocolate covered strawberries+ off menu.

We got 2 goodie bags and our menus and to my great delight it was the biggest Macaron (ha ha the "Manhattan" macaron that I've ever had.  It was made with whole wheat flour maybe?  Because it had some texture and inside a fresh filling with layers of fruit and chocolate paste and in the very center a giant liquor infused blueberry.

It was really the most perfect end to a scrumptious and very romantic valentine's day meal.

Service was good but not perfect.  Not as good as Dovetail!  They got overwhelmed towards the end.  We were in the rear dining room at a round table for 4 which was great.  Also next time I would try the dining room in front.  It has maybe a fancier decor.  

I had a beautiful time with my Valentine XO

Best in town. Wonderful food, try the birdnest dessert. Joey is the best, most creative bartender in NYC. Great decor, smooth and clean, bright,open, never loud. Pricey is the only issue but expected for such perfection. Go and enjoy

Our dining experience was on Friday, March 2nd. This was our 3rd and will be our last time at Aquavit. We celebrated our engagement on one visit and this evening was our 10 year wedding anniversary. The previous 2 times were outstanding, but this time was VERY awkward and unpleasant.

The food was interesting and clever, but nothing stood out as phenomenal. Often the dishes were overly salted and/or sour.

The servers were robotic. I feel like they are frightened for some reason. Perhaps the management has changed and they are under duress. On previous occasions the servers were professional but accessible and warm. 

Quite honestly, we could not wait to leave. We felt like we were in a Physics class praying for the professor to announce a break. It is terrible that we spent $500 and 3 hours to have such a substandard experience.

We wrote an email to them and they never replied. They obviously could not care less.

I visited Aquavit for dinner with co-workers. We were all impressed by the gorgeous minimalist and sleek interior. The dishes were interesting and the artistic food presentation is absolutely stunning. It was a great experience and although I enjoyed the Scandinavian food, the typical meal set here is not enough to satisfy my voracious appetite.

Exquisite preparation of distinctive food in an elegant spare room where you can converse in a normal tone of voice and will be served attentively. Are you looking for something different from French, Italian, Indian, Chinese, steak or "comfort food?  Do you want to be able not to shout to your party of 6 or just your partner? Can you be happy not surrounded by celebrities?Then Aquavit is the place for you. We had the seasonal tasting menu, 8 small, beautifully presented dishes, each delicious in a way you won't find elsewhere, in a relaxed ambience with a knowledgeable but unobtrusive waitstaff.  Being Scandinavian, seafood is featured, but there are plenty of other choices à la carte. (If the tasting or seasonal menu is desired, everyone must  choose it.) It was my birthday, so a small hemispheric marzipan princess cake appeared. Save a little room for the best after-meal petites fours in New York, to be chosen à la voluntée from a large tray.  And start with a flight of 3 Aquavits in lieu of a cocktail.

Our experience at Aquavit was absolutely phenomenal. We came in on a cold December evening while visiting the city from Seattle and splurged on the chef's tasting menu. It did not disappoint. The dishes were diverse and complex, from the welcome amuse bouche to the artful bird's nest. The whole evening was an experience of brand new flavors for me. The wait staff went above and beyond to make us feel comfortable (our first Michelin star restaurant experience) and gave us complimentary glasses of champagne to celebrate our anniversary. I cannot even put into words how special this night was for us. The food was so amazing and different, but it was the service and the people that really set Aquavit apart. As we were about to leave, our waiter pulled away from the busy dining room to find us in the lobby and personally thank us by name for coming in. We got little goodie bags to go with bread and the menu of what we had that evening. We will tell anyone who listens to GO TO AQUAVIT.

I had the pleasure of dining at this fine Nordic place. The decor and pre fixe dishes are exquisite along with their dessert line up. I met the chef several times. Did I forget to mention this is a Michelin Star spot? Definitely pass by with a few friends, significant other or by yourself. Host are great!

I haven't been here for a while (baby and all), more than a year.
After eating here recently for lunch, made me realize how much I missed this place.

Executive Chef Emma Bengtsson is such an amazing chef with all the creative/delicious/beautiful dishes coming out of her kitchen. Aquavit, along with Atera, Agern, and Aska, really got me hooked on Scandinavian/Nordic cuisine. 

Trying the seasonal tasting menu recently was such a treat, truly evoking the feelings and images of spring, which included salmon tartare on a delicate Swedish pancake, oysters/caviar, langoustine/rhubarb, black bass/white asparagus, duck/honeynut squash, and even the dessert, which included wild strawberries. That complimentary pork sausage/sauerkraut was so good, going to ask for it on the next visit.

Excellent service.

Highest recommendations. 
Can't wait to come back soon.

: 10 calendars
This Michelin two star restaurant is excellent. My best friend has her birthday here. We ordered two lunch tasting menu and the lobster, sea bass are great!

BEYOND DELICIOUS.
Wow. I have never been quite so blown away by a place. This is a flawless restaurant in every way. The presentation of the dishes is so uniquely beautiful and the tastes are flavors I've never experienced. The tasting menu fills you up to the brim and is very decently priced! FIVE STARS.

Don't let the very small portions to fool you into thinking that you will not be satiated and full at the end of whatever meal option you choose. That's what I was worried about when picking the Prix Fixe meal because it "seemed" to only offer an appetizer, main entree and dessert. However, that's not the case. There are many additional food options that you will be given "on the house" that's not part of the Prix Fixe option which fills you up in no time

Pros:
1. Excellent service
2. Many "on the house" food offerings
3. Very relaxed, quiet and serene atmosphere
4. You will be full even if you pick the Prix Fixe

Cons:
1. The food isn't necessarily special and delicious or out of ordinary to justify the $$$$ price tag. I ordered the Icelandic cod which was described as "gently" poached. Well it was a bit bland for my taste

Dined in here in Oct. 2017 as an anniversary celebration. It was a truly excellent experience! The ambience is elegant and nice. It was our first time to try scandinavian style food and it was so great! The waiter welcomed us with champagne for the anniversary. Then goes the stream of delicious food. We enjoyed the night with Aquavit!

We were really looking forward to this restaurant to celebrate a special occasion. The food is a wonderful combination of fresh ingredients and Nordic minimalism. The service, however, is not what one would expect from a restaurant awarded two Michelin stars. The courses were wonderfully prepared, explained and finished table-side but no one asked how we enjoyed them. We also felt a bit rushed to place a drink order, despite having to peruse quite an extensive wine list. Overall good experience but not special.

The portion is bigger than we expected. My chef friend and I love this place. The environ is not cold at all, and the staffs are so welcoming. We enjoy every moment there. Highly recommended for their black bass, and their desserts are delicious!

Next time we want to try their salmon burger.

This is one of the restaurants that proves that not all Michelin star restaurants are fake news. The service was beyond excellent (really, one of the best - 5 stars). The place is beautiful, and the ambiance is nice, though a little bit too formal for us (but nice if you want to impress someone). We got the chef's tasting menu (it is expensive, but I think that worth the experience. It is all tiny portions, but they serve around 14 dishes), and the food is overall a 5 stars, but let's go through the menu:

(1) Swedish pancake and smoked salmon (5 stars): it is a great starter. The pancake was on point and the smoked salmon delicious.
(2) Seaweed and mussel (3 stars): not my favorite. It was delicious, but mussels are not my thing. I little bit salty. 
(3) Caviar and Sunchoke (5 stars): I always think that caviar is a waste of money  until a try this dish. The contrast between the black caviar and the white foam is beautiful to see and to eat, bringing different textures in your mouth. 
(4) Sea Urchin and Pine (4 stars): I never tried urchin before, and really like this dish. 
(5) Venison and Truffles (5 stars): one of the stars of the night. The dish looks like a beautiful grass field. When you break the "this field", the venison and the truffles are in the bottom. It is a delicious dish!
(6) Norwegian King Crab and Chamomile (5 stars): Another excellent dish. The crab was amazing! 
(7) Foie Gras and Clementine (3 stars): I still couldn't decide if I'm a fan of foie gras (I have already tried different dishes, ways of cooking it). In this way, though beautiful and interesting (the foie gras has a texture of dippin' dots ice cream), did not work that well. It was not bad, but I would never order this in a restaurant. 
(8) The Halibut and Chestnut (4 stars): the halibut was very good, but not that memorable.   
(9) Squab and Bergamot (5 stars): It is a shocking dish to see, though beautiful arranged. The squab leg came with the best piece of the squab. The meat was delicious! 
(10) 7X Wagyu beef and malt (5 stars): the con of this dish is that it is so small and I love a great chunk of meat (no puns intended). The meat is delicious, the sauce and the crunch stuff wen't so well with the beef. Really enjoyed it!
(11) buttermilk blue and gingersnap and the citrus and honey popsicle (3 stars): great dishes to prepare your mouth for the star of the restaurant. But nothing that special. 
(12) Arctic bird's nest (6 stars!): This is might be one of my favorite desserts ever! The dish looks like a beautiful bird's nest that you only see in fantastic books/shows. Every detail is beautiful! On top of it, it is extremely DELICIOUS! You have the experience of all textures and flavors in the same dessert (fruits, chocolate, vanilla - crunchy, creamy, fruit textures). Perfect way to finish an amazing meal!

We also try the aquavit, a swedish liquor. They have many flavors! The chilli one was one of my favorite and interesting so far!

What makes me very happy and emotional with this restaurant is how far you can go to value ingredients from your country, and I think that their purpose was achieved!

Great food for a great price! I really enjoyed the authentic-tasting food. I'm rather new to Scandinavian food and my point of comparison is the meatballs at Ikea, but the food here really blew me away. I would definitely come back again. It also has two Michelin stars!

The atmosphere is nice and classy - they have these dining chairs that are akin to a villain's chair in a James Bond movie that make the experience more fun. 

Lunch time is less crowded than dinner time and I was able to make a reservation an hour before, ignoring their website disclaimer that reservations should be made weeks in advance.

I have been dying to go to Aquavit for years and finally last night I made it. I've always admired Marcus Samuelson and eaten at his restaurant C-House in Chicago and Red Rooster here in NY.
I really wanted to love Aquavit. We did the chefs tasting at 200 pp and it was underwhelming. There were many cured and smoked fish plates, all delicious but not very memorable.  Their squab and sweet bread plates were both incredible and there was a fish roe ice cream sandwiched between tuile cookies which was divine. 
The killers of the meal:
1) the oyster with caviar. Nothing fancy. The oyster was horrendous. It tasted like the smell when you pass a dirty grassy stagnant lake
2) the Colorado wagyu. Restaurants need to ask how you want your meat cooked. This was medium rare at best (which I'm not a fan of) but even worse it was the chewiest most rubbery piece of meat. I did not eat it. When I explained my discontent I was told "well it's not real Wagyu bc it's from Colorado". I've eaten plenty American Canadian and even real Japanese wagyu in my life. This was chewier than a skirt steak.
3) the dessert is pathetic. The birds nest is poor quality chocolate shreds, and sorbets. 
They brought a complementary hazelnut mousse as compensation for the terrible meat course I sent back. This also needs to stop. Bad dessert does not compensate disastrous courses at a two Michelin star dinner. Our dinner was $400 + a bottle of wine. The least they could do is compensate the wine.  Needless to say we will not be returning.

A quick dining experience at the bar.
Scandinavian styled interior design, Scandinavian everything. The butter infused with sea salt (assumably) was superb. 
Tried one of the most popular cold dishes (shrimp Skagen). Saltier than I expected, but very fresh.

Scandinavian cuisine is the theme for this place, and it's a magical winter wonderland of spins, twirls, and culinary might. I almost didn't get the chefs tasting menu, as they are quite strict about their dress code. I immediately ran out and bought pants and non-sneakers just to have this meal. Im so glad I did!  

The bleach roe (Löjrom?) amuse bouche is quite spectacular! I immediately got the sense of a dairy farm from the rich, creamy texture of it all. The buttermilk froth made it even more apparent. The bleach roe gave a salty taste that tied everything together. 

The Limpa  herring ice cream is phenomenal! Sweet, savory, salty, and everything I would want for an ice cream this weird. I think the wrapper is a little gimmicky, but it surprisingly makes the experiences better, as if unwrapping presents for Christmas. The herring is there but it's never over powering. The ice cream has some sweetness but doesn't go overboard. The baking spices they brine the  herring in gives the overall feel a gingersnap-like context. 

The Spanish mackerel itself was delicious but potato purée was just ok. Felt like filler to me, but the mackerel was a treat! 

The king crab chamomile was a great, unexpected combo. The sweet, herbal tea flavor of chamomile, along with the curds and almonds give this floral, creamy overtone to the king crab. The gelatin they have in this dish blends well, giving a sense that Im in the ocean rather than outside of it. The crab itself was good and the right texture, but I wish it was smoked or charred just a bit more. The grilled aspect does this, but I don't think it was strong enough. It was still a great dish though.   

The diver scallops with green strawberries are a stellar pair. The strawberries had the firm texture while the scallops are soft. Savory with sweet. Tang with mellow fishiness. The consommé gives it a melted sorbet profile that works well in enhancing the fruity and fishy flavor. The roe sprinkled on top gives it another depth of flavor with the umami profile. I'm glad they don't have to use MSG lol. The dry ice smoke only enhances the fresh feeling of the scallops. 

The sweetbreads and wood sorrel was not at all what I expected. But once I took my first bite, I was all smiles! The playful use of texture and temperature truly paint a picture of a husky dog, clumsily trotting through a snow covered forest. The sweetbreads is robust, low toned and gamey, producing this warm yet soft element. The gem lettuce provided the refreshing crisp of a crunch along with the bright refreshing feel. The frozen wood sorrel only enhances the hot cold interplay, but giving a middle toned depth of earth and floral. Truly a delightful experience when eating this. Make sure you have each element on the spoon. 

Goddamn the presentation of the duck was good! Cooked just right, had some gamy flavor that wasn't powerful, and the skin was crisp to perfection. The sautéed veggies surrounding it made it even better! It almost felt like I was eating some type of duck burger (no cheese in this case). If they make their entrée just like this, then I highly recommend you order it if you're not doing the chefs tasting menu. It was so good, I forgot to sip on the broth they brought out along with the meal. The broth had this leafy green, warm tone that wrapped everything in a blanket. 

The goat cheese and strawberries could not have been further away from my expectations. What would normally be bright, acidic, and high toned sweet was the opposite. The crust and crumbs were made with digestif spirits and spices that anchored and tamed everything from flying out of control. Every bite felt like a plane lowering in elevation. I was delighted that the chef made it this way, rather than a typical strawberry cheesecake. It also was quite possibly one of the most beautiful presentations I've had that didn't involve gimmicks, props, or theatrics. I want to frame the pictures I took of the dish somewhere in my house to remind me of the elegance it fostered. 

The basil ice cream is a sensory treat across the board. The flowers they bring with it transport me to a jardin in versailles. The sweet floral smells only enhance the basil sorbet bar. The white chocolate outer shell helps create the illusion of ice cream, with its buttery flavor. The candied basil and sea salt only further push the pleasure boundary. 

The arctic birds nest is a sight and experience to behold. It's a lot to take in, and with every bite you get closer to fully grasping the magnitude of how awesome it is.
