The only real problem I can see is cracking away Into the art piece of a meal. There's no real practical way, other than removing the "eggs" on top and cracking them separately with a spoon. I'm not gonna try describing this, as there's too much to analyze, but there a wonderful balance act of berries, chocolate, and honey at play. 

What an experience! I absolutely recommend making a reservation here.

Amazingly coordinated dinner experience! I never had to ask for or wait for anything. My every question or desire was anticipated. We opted for the chef's tasting menu, which perfectly went from fresh and light to a heavier finish. We opted to get bottles of wine instead of the wine pairing and gave a price range. The waiter stayed far below our budget, never tried to up sell, and we had the best bottle of wine ever. (We are currently trying to figure out how to get our hands on more of that wine). The whole experience was ~4 hours, we never felt rushed, and the place was fancy but never felt stuffy. Fantastic restaurant and fantastic food.

An NYC institution with amazing, super-stylized Nordic cuisine. The focus here is on fish but the Swedish meatballs are great too. Have only been here for lunch (and this is the ultimate power lunch), so no comment on the namesake liquor.

Another feast for the eyes, palate & stomach. I'd never tried scandanavian food before. The ingredients are simple yet the balance mixes for crazy experience. Jelly with foiegras looks like dessert but it isn't! Every course is an adventure full of flavor waiting to be discovered as one bites into it. Presentation is as beautiful as the taste of each dish. Service is impeccable. Aquavit is 1 of New York's landmark must eat must visit restaurants!

Astonishing detailed service is one of the features. From the Allergy inquiry to customer time restriction, many detailed questions will be politely asked in order to provide a nice dining environment.

To start, I had the sweetbread. I always love veal meat. Most restaurants choose to stew sweetbread. This place fries the sweetbread slightly, serves with grilled scallion and mayonnaise sauce.

As for the main course, we tried cod, duck and Wagyu beef. Beef is my private recommendation. Although duck and cod are also nice choices, but I prefer dishes with strong flavor. The beef itself has a high quality. More importantly, blueberry jam and mayonnaise sauce(maybe mayonnaise, since it has a sweet and salty taste) are provided. These two sauces enhances the strong flavor in the beef. 

The desserts have great appearances. For example, "bird nest" and the chocolate cake are just made be like the scene in fairy tales. However, the tastes of them are really mediocre. Especially the chocolate cake, the strong bitter taste surpasses the sweet taste in the sorbet and cream.

This was an OK experience. 

The dining experience felt a bit stuffy and tense. The waiters did an okay job of serving us, however the hostess was awful. She seemed annoyed the entire time from greeting us till the end of dinner. And at the end of dinner, she kept glancing at our table as if waiting for us to leave.

The food itself was good! Nothing that truly blew my mind, but for a prie fix, I actually felt that I got a good amount of food that made the $$ worth it. Throughout the meal, they offered little bites and bread (with some really good butter)so you really do feel full after this meal. 

For the first course I ordered the salmon. It was a cold preparation, with delightful textures and flavors throughout. The food wasn't anything exceptional (again, I'm grading this on par with other 2-Michelin star restaurants), however it was a fresh way to start the meal. 

The second course was the bass. The bass was simply seared with some vegetables, sauces and a foam. The bass was very flavorful and prepared very nicely - extremely tender and flaky. There was a substantial portion as well. However, the pairing with the broccoli rabe (which in my opinion was much too bitter) was a poor choice. 

The third course was a rhubarb dish with honey. I really enjoyed this dessert, though I think the granita they added on top really didn't do anything to enhance the flavor. The ice cream was really good and the rhubarb worked well with the dish. 

Overall, I would not recommend this restaurant for a 2-michelin experience. If the environment wasn't so tense and the hostess didn't look annoyed when we were greeted and when we left, then perhaps I would recommend this place. Again, the food was above average but the service was a bit lacking (for what you might expect at a 2-michelin).

This was my first time with Scandinavian fine dining and due to our anniversary, we splurged with the Chef's Tasting Menu which is 10 listed courses, but when all said and done, was 15 plates of food plus bread, some candy and a small pound cake and caramels to take home - that made 19 items!  That was a long dinner!

The place is divided into two dining areas, and we were seated in the front room at a window with view of the street.  The decor looks right out of Scandinavian Design and is contemporary and restrained.  It's pretty quiet.

The favored spirit of Scandinavia is aquavit and, in the spirit of the evening, I tried some.  They have quite a list of aquavits including a large selection of house made varieties, each one made with a different blend of botanicals.  I tried the S.O. Anderson, from Sweden, flavored with caraway, aniseed and fennel.  It's served chilled and neat, and tastes like a bite of rye bread that bites you back!  I enjoyed it.

They have a nice wine selection and we picked a 1/2 bottle of Bordeaux which was fairly priced.  There's so much buyers remorse these days when you order wine and then check your smartphone app for the retail price.  None such remorse tonight!

As course after course came out, I was impressed by the level of cooking and artful plating.  The theme throughout the meal were flavors of caraway, dill, and vinegar, but at times, the featured protein of the dish was made to take a back seat due to strong herbaceous elements.

After a palate cleanser of house made fermented plum tea, the first appetizer arrived - osetra caviar served over thinly sliced potato and yogurt, and enhanced with micro herbs.  I found the osetra to be overwhelmed by the other flavors - good thing we did not upgrade to the more expensive caviar.

The highlights of the meal were:
*Oyster and Elderflower - 1/2 shell with a foamy elderflower mignonette.
*Crayfish and Krondill - Lump crayfish, mangalista pork coppa and pressed rye bread.  Yummy.
*Turbot and Marigold - Beautifully poached fish, beet "scales" and herring roe beurre blanc.  Wow, beautiful and delicious.
*Mussel and Anchovy - A tasty bite.
*Duck and Apricot - Probably the tastiest dish of the night.  The duck skin was impossibly crispy yet the breast meat was medium rare and moist.
*Wagyu Beef and Chanterelles - American Wagyu beef, chanterelles and beef tallow hollandaise.
*Goat Cheese and Strawberry - More like a savory cheesecake, this was tasty.
*Basil and Yogurt - Small popsicles enhanced with smoked sea salt and chiles.
Arctic Bird's Nest - Artful plating at its most artful.

Not as successful:
King Crab and Chamomile - A beautiful dish for sure, but the crab was lost.
Scallop and Grape - As pretty as an ocean-floor still life, disappointingly I found the flavor of the protein was lost.
Sweetbreads and Wood Sorrel - Imaginative plating with wood sorrel "snow" but I would not have buried those beautiful caramelized sweetbreads under all of that greenery. 

Note to food photographers - the room lighting is definitely not optimal for food pictures - yellow and dim.

Very nice food and service, totally a good choice for occasions like birthday or anniversaries. Only thing it's the Inside of the restaurant is smaller than I thought it would be. Also their breads are soooooooooo good.

Aquavit, in one form or another, has been around for a LONG time. In one of it's primes, it gave rise to Marcus Samuelsson, whose cooking and restaurants I love, but I'd never been to Aquavit...

And I was a bit leery about dining at Aquavit. It's fancy, it's been around forever and it's in Midtown. This combination scares the heck out of me. Midtown is the breading ground for the walking dead of fine dining. But Aquavit manages to surprise.

The service is flawless. It's exactly what you expect from a top-tier restaurant. The hostess is coordinated with the waiters and are anticipating your needs as a diner. Special occasion, business meal, date, etc. They know what they're doing and will tailor the experience as such.

As for the food........ I'll add a lot of dots here. It's hard to dislike a place when the service is so good and the meal is wrapped with little amuse bouches and champagne toasts and take home breakfasts and oh my, oh my! But really, a lot of the dishes.... the technique is there, the sauces are perfection but most of the proteins were hammered! The sweetbreads were cooked beyond recognition. A duck that great up on the wrong side of the tracks was draped in luscious sauces with Chiffonade on one arm and Julienne on the other. It was good enough to make you WANT to forget that the protein was so tough.

So did I enjoy Aquavit? Yes, very much so. I could go back any time (sadly I probably wont, maybe in like 6.5 years). The service was stellar. The space is beautiful and a bit Swedish and homie...... And the meal was good. I'm happy I came here before this restaurant either closes or joins the hordes of the Midtown expense account zombies.

I don't have enough good things to say about Aquavit.  First of all, from the moment we entered the restaurant the staff was as polite and responsive as any restaurant I have visited.  And this continued throughout the meal.  The tasting menu and wine pairings are not cheap but it is a great place for a special meal.

Let's start with the table.  The setup inside is sufficiently spacious that you do not feel overwhelmed by other guests.  There are a few floating tables in the dining room but even those have reasonable privacy.  when we sat down, the host asked us about cocktails and volunteered to have our food start a little later so we could enjoy them.  This degree of thoughtfulness and concern continued throughout the meal.

We started with a plum tea amuse bouche that was lovely.  A sweet kombucha basically.  And the bread choices were fantastic.  The danish rye was what everyone went for but I tacked on an oat and sunflower roll as well.  For cocktails, I had the Odin's Spritz while my wife had Fawns Lavendula.  Both were excellent and unlike other drinks we have had.  BTW, the aquavit selection here looks amazing and the bar was hopping all night.  It would definitely be fun to do a shorter dinner and sample some at the bar.

Our first real course was the caviar on creme fraiche with dill and onion.  It was awesome though I will say the creme fraiche stole the show and overwhelmed the caviar just a bit.  The blini was delicious but a bit hard to cut.

The oysters with elderflower were lovely, even if it was just my second or third time eating them. You can't go wrong trying them again at a place like this.

We loved the crab and chamomile course which had some fermented kohlrabi.  I could have eaten this as a main and been very happy.  The pairing here with the Falanghina was excellent.  

Next up was the scallop which was paired with honeydew, baby cucumber and pistachio and a chateauneuf de pape blanc.  You know it is a good course if it has honeydew and my wife still likes it.  

The sweetbread course was also fantastic, maybe even ahead of the caviar or crab. The sweetbreads were super crispy with sorel granita and some creme fraiche.  A cofermented rose from CA complemented this incredibly well.

The herring ice cream, yes that's right herring ice cream, sandwich was just fantastic as well.  I had never had it before and took it down quickly.

With their take on a lobster roll (open face crayfish on danish rye toast) was great and paired with a beer from Illinois without hops but instead ginger, carrottops and dandelions.  We didnt love the beer but enjoyed the food for this course.

The turbot course had golden boots, horseradish and fish burre blanc paired with a very bready Sake from northern Japan.  Good but not enough to displace the caviar, crab or sweetbreads from the top 3.

We then got a quick break with a mussel before moving onto the duck and apricot.  It had onions and plumcot and was quite tasty.

Our final savory course was the wagyu which had beef fat hollandaise, mushrooms and currants.  This was excellent and probably displaced the crab though its a close call.  

We moved onto the end of the meal with some goat cheese cheesecake with strawberries and a digestive biscuit crust, a basil yogurt popsicle covered in white chocolate and salt and the arctic birds nest--basically dark chocolate twigs with goat cheese robins eggs covered in white chocolate and blueberry sorbet.  One of the most interesting desserts we have ever had.  

This 3 hour meal was amongst the best paced we have ever had, with outstanding service throughout.  About the only thing that wasn't over the top amazing was the wine pairing.  We knew the regular pairing (vs the premium one) would take us to different places and less traditional wines and they all paired very well but there were few which stood out.  The whites up front were the best if I had to have a glass of one on its own.  If we did the tasting menu again, we would probably try the more traditional wine pairing.

I had the chef's tasting menu with reserve wine pairing.  For the tasting, you would get to have caviar, foie gras, king crab, venison, wagyu beef, squad, turbot and various types of desserts on top of the Arctic Bird's Nest dessert.  You may think it is not worth it to spend close to  $500 per person on dinner, but I think the experience is worth it. 

The only issue is that you may want to consider if you want to add the wine pairing, as they give you a relatively generous pour, and at the end of the tasting menu, you would have had finished a couple drinks.  So if you are a light weight drinker, you can get very tipsy.  However, the wine pairing does enhance every course.  And we did not only sample wine, we also sample sake, whiskey, etc. with some of the courses.  And for every drink, they would explain the origin and history of each drink.  I regret not taking pictures of each bottle as I would love to get some of them to add to my collection. 

Each course features a special presentation, for the foie gras with red beet, the foie gras is frozen using nitrogen, the temperature and texture are not how foie gras is usually served to me.  I like the king crab in apple broth, the crab meat was fresh and the taste of apple was delightful.   Another course that I liked was the caviar with elderberries.  The venison was definitely not my cup of tea, but it was good that I tried it to know that it is not the kind of meat I would like.  One of the courses had an odd/unconventional presentation - the squab, I was not sure why they placed the leg on the plate. 

In addition to the courses, I also enjoyed the amuse bouche and appetizers.  

I was waiting all night for the Arctic Bird's Nest, the presentation was exactly like I saw in pictures, but the taste was not what I expected.  I ended up not liking it that much.  At the conclusion of your meal, you will be presented with a candy box where you could choose what mini sweet treats you would like to sample.  

About 2 hours later, we left satisfied.
This is the ultimate comfort food restaurant for me.  The food of my childhood, served up as haute cuisine.
Seriously the food  are perfectly on point, I like everything, food and services ,the cocktails   are very good.. I be back  again for seasonal tasting

Aquavit has restored my faith in finer dining. I had gotten bored with the same flavors at many a restaurants. I came here for a lunch on a random Monday and was not prepared for the tsunami of flavors that was about to displace me. 

I started with the 7X beef. The combination of quail egg, horseradish, and löjrom roe created a cascade of emotions, mostly pure joy and utter satisfaction. Next up was the scintillating salmon burger, which I could not stop from swimming upstream towards my mouth. For dessert, I had their Arctic Bird's Nest which was as beautiful as it tasted. Each bite had a different splash of texture and high flying flavor.

The space was immaculate and the service worthy of their two Michelin stars.

I've gone to Aquavit for a splurge lunch plenty of times and I've always enjoyed the meal. Pricey, true, but a luxury in a beautiful room with beautiful food. Tonight, on my way home from a late meeting, I was beat and thought--let me indulge. No reservation, but they accomodated me at the 'lounge,' three seating areas near the bar. As I sank into the cushy chair, I thought, this will not be so bad! The bar menu was expensive with lots of small dish offerings. I settled on a Norwegian King Crab roll on a potato bun with remoulade and trout roe. At $28, not cheap, but hey I figured it sounded on the hearty side. Hah! I kid you not when I tell you it measured maybe 4 inches, probably 3 inches. I didn't know they could make a "bun" this small. It was the size you'd expect on a tray being passed butler-style at a wedding. After 2 bites it was gone and I was still hungry. I ordered then the confit sunchokes. They were a smallish bowl of fried tasty fritters though the raita type sauce was over-salted. Still hungry, I opted for dessert, which I rarely do. I got the fig with almond cake and gelato and other intersting things. It too was tiny though delicious--still super heft tag at a whopping $18. With a diet coke and a cup of tea and the tip (which I was happy to give; the service was pleasant even though I wasn't at a table), the check added up to a whopping $90+. It was insane. Maybe, blame the bar menu, but I don't remember feeling so thoroughly ripped off when I came here last for lunch. The crab roll in particular was a total joke.

Aquavit is one of my all time favorite restaurant! I first heard about the place from someone I used to work with. My boy friend at the time was Scandinavian so I thought it would be nice to go there. Yes, it is on the pricey side, but you don't need to have the chef tasting. You can sit by the bar and get the a la carte by the bar. Everything is delicious. From the swedish meatball to the smorgasbord, it is delicious. My boy friend and I were fighting over the pickled herring when we first went.

If you decide to go for the chef tasting, bear in mind, you will be spending a good amount of coin. However, you are not only paying for the 13+ course meal, but also the experience. Being a picky eating pair, my boy friend and I were able to tell the waiter to exclude the things we did not eat. If I were to say something "negative" about this, it would probably be that the chef tasting is two hours long. Our reservation was at 7 pm. The chef tasting did not end until 9 pm and we were falling asleep. However, that is our personal problem since we are the type of people that are in bed by 9:30 pm. 

I can go on about how amazing this place is. The one sad thing is is that they no longer have the milk punch. It was this delicious elixir that they garnished with a dehydrated grapefruit dipped in meringue.

This place came recommended by several people, so I thought I'd give it a try for a birthday dinner. Made a reservation for 6pm on a Friday night and it was relatively empty when we arrived. Most people started arriving around 7:30pm. We opted for the Chef's tasting menu (10 courses + 5 small bites).

Compared to other spots in NYC, I think aquavit is one of the best michelin-starred restaurants in the city. Every dish was good and unique. And because it's Scandinavian, it holds a special place in my heart (I was born in Denmark... and they serve an amazing Danish rye bread here!!)

I won't go into details for each dish but some of my favorites were:

Caviar in cream: similar to an egg caviar, it was delicious
Scallops: love how refreshing and fresh this course was
Squab: very unique dish and the flavors were well executed
Arctic Bird's nest: no wonder this is their specialty--the crispy texture of the nest and the ice cream "eggs".... amazing

Dishes that I thought were average...

Oxtail and foie gras: I thought the foie gras was too overwhelming that it overpowered the oxtail flavor
veal and sweetbread: the sweetbread was served in crumb form from dry ice. the veal was deep fried and very chewy like gum... not sure if I liked that, haha

If this is your first time at Aquavit, I'd highly recommend going with the Chef's tasting menu because you really get to try the dishes that they're known for.

Dining at Aquavit was truly a great experience. After embarking on a few vacations and traveling to try some Michelin Starred restaurants, I can definitely say that Aquavit has earned its standings.

My table and I ordered the tasting menu and every single dish was extremely enjoyable. All the flavors and textures were layered perfectly as I would expect from a restaurant like this and they made all the root veggies extremely enjoyable--especially when paired with their protein such as perfectly cooked halibuts or a butter poached lobster.

We also ordered 2 Aquavits and the wine pairing. All of the wines were well selected for the tasting menu--I was even impressed to see they snuck in a local wine, which I wouldn't expect from restaurant like this, but it was nevertheless very enjoyable. I really appreciated how Aquavit wasn't stuffy like many other higher end restaurants I've been to and it was just an overall comfortable dining experience.

Out of many of the "higher end" restaurants that I went to, I really enjoyed Aquavit and appreciated something different from the common French and Italian cuisines.

Group dinner last night so chose from a set menu. Steak was "mass wedding" quality (medium well at min, I was not asked how I liked it even though there were only 12 of us dining). Very poor I thought. Put me off thinking of returning for myself in future.

The restaurant was named two stars by Michelin and three stars by the New York Times. The chef is Emma Bengtsson, and she definitely has so much talent on cooking. 
When we step into this place, I could feel the meticulous attitude towards details, those elaborately decorated ornaments and moderately lit atmosphere lights. The usher will put the customers coat away in the lobby and wait until he has sat down, which is the perfect service.
For a Michelin restaurant, the main course is the most important because it reflects a Chef's understandings and creativity in cooking. I ordered a lobster burger with plenty of meat and strong soup, but it wasn't so much that it dripped, but what I wanted to say was that this lobster burger was also eaten in some other restaurants, although it was delicious, but the cooking methods and ingredients didn't give me a refreshing feeling, which was the only defect in beauty. I have an idea is to consider mixing lobster meat and beef, which might make the taste more interesting. What makes me shine at the moment is dessert. It's very delicious and very memorable. It's a really good work.

Swedes are known for there understated reserve. Nothing over the top. Take only what you need. This cultural mindset permeates what is billed as the top Scandinavian restaurant in New York. The dining experience is understated and reserved. The main dining room is small. Just the right size. The decor is tastefully minimalist. The vibe carries through to the cliental. Conversations were muted. Diners seemed restrained, as if the experience brought out their inner Swedish-ness. The menu offered three options: a chef's tasting menu, a seasonal tasting menu and a prix fixe with three choices for each of three courses. The wait staff was attentive but not overbearing. A delightful amuse-Bouche was brought out in between each course. The food was understated. Subtle flavors, modest portions, and tasteful presentations left the palette and stomach satisfied but not to excess. We enjoyed a homemade aquavit and, it being the Christmas season, a delicious glogg before our first course. Herring, bass, and duck were our favorites. Deserts were delicious too. 
The bill takes a toll. This is not the place to economize. We left the restaurant and stepped out into the Christmas  -decorates streets of Manhattan satisfied and happy, having had a thoroughly Swedish experience, minus one star only for the lack of joy and life in the overly restrained dining room.

It's not just a meal, it's an event.

Each dish with a story and a complexity that will have you think about it for a long time. 

Wore a blazer, jeans an a nice crisp white button down collar with black loafers - well dressed by any LA standard. But this is NY and I was underdressed to the norm. Men: Wear a suit with a tie.

A Taste of Christmas! 
Monday, 
I enjoyed an excellent Christmas lunch at Restaurant Aquavit on  65 E 55th St. In New York City. 
The first plate consisted of small samples of delicious herrings, heavenly gravlax, devine skagen, cheese pie and potatoes beautifully displayed in a circle. 
The second plate carried Swedish meatballs of course, a tasty glazed spare rib, exquisite Christmas ham, mouthwatering red cabbage with the famous Janssons temptation served on the side. 
A Carlsberg beer and Icelandic schnapps enhanced the lovely experience. 
A marvelous Saffron custard and a little glögg ended the eating orgy. 
This is the perfect Christmas gift!

Had to go to this restaurant I didn't even want to go to because the restaurant has a secret $50 per person cancellation that they don't tell you about (illegal). Decided to suck it up and just go and as expected it was overpriced and not worth the money. Also found a hair in my food which the manager wouldn't refund me for. Delicious!

This place is amazing. It definitely deserves its Michelin Star rating. The ambience of the restaurant is great and the service is phenomenal. The food was so delicious. They have the warmest bread rolls. We had a three course meal, and every dish hit the spot.

Rarer for cuisines other than french, japanese, or contemporary american to earn Michelin stars so I was excited to try such a famed Nordic establishment (first opened in 1987). Their service was impeccable. I've always believed the best service is warm and helpful but not overbearing. For example, you don't feel interrupted in your conversation with your dinner companions when they change flatware or glasses, almost just magically appears in front of you. No minute detail was missed. The extra level that Aquavit brought was the great conversation with our server and sommelier who suggested we try a little flight of their in-house aquavits. How could we refuse the experience of sampling aquavit at Aquavit? See photos to see which aquavits we selected. Additionally always exciting when the servers and somms are clearly passionate about the food and want to comment on the subtlety of a certain flavor in a dish or the notes in the wine without any pretension but rather with genuine appreciation. 

We opted for the Chef's Tasting and I'm so glad we did. We'd actually been watching the menu for Aquavit for a while and decided to make a reservation when each course on the menu truly excited us. Each dish had distinctive presentation (bird's nest dessert as many Yelpers have noted) and tasted better than it looked. The waygu is possibly the best waygu I've had (impressive, having tried many waygus in Tokyo & Kyoto). If you're not as familiar with Nordic cuisine, you may not like the bitter, acidic or vinegar flavors of some of the courses. For me none of those flavors were overpowering and actually complimented the dish. 

Tip: If you have certain ingredients you really dislike (goat cheese for me), you can request that they substitute a different dish or ingredient for that course. They were extremely accommodating. 

Note: Having now dined at many Michelins winners in NYC, I'll say the sweet spot is two-star Michelins. The three-stars are always exorbitant, disappointing and too pompous for my taste. The one-stars are where you can find surprising gems but are definitely hit or miss especially in regards to service. The two-stars are consistently amazing experiences and always places that I would go out of my way to revisit.

This is my first time having Nordic/Scandinavian food. For the Chef's recommendation I feel like overall the taste profile of many dishes were tilted toward sour(pickled) and salty. I drank a lot of water because of this. The Squab is by far the best dishes (first is the leg, second is the breast I think). Soft, juicy and meaty. The Halibut fish dish had a balanced profile. The rose infused pickle in the crab dish/app was a very interesting taste. The first app dish with porched qual egg in the center was great, taste and texture. The bird nest, the desert, was a piece of art. Great service and atmosphere and everything.

I deducted one star due to the over tilt of flavor profile that heavily tilted toward salty-pickled-sour in many dish. The cider we had at the beginning kind of making the sourness lasting through to 3-4 dishes. Also the herrings moose ice-cream sandwich was a bit too fishy+salty, probably to Asian like me. 

Overall, a very interesting and some what positive dining experience.

So there was nothing really wrong about this place but the overall experience of it did not account for the hype of a two star Michelin restaurant for 2018. Personally for me it just lost points in comparison with my other fine dining experiences. The highlights of our meal were the Swedish meatballs and the shrimp Skagen. Also, their Aquavit flight was quite interesting!

I like this restaurant and enjoyed the food.  The service is very good - what I would expect from a high-end restaurant like this.  I can't give it 5 stars, though.  The prices are obviously very high, and so are expectations.  The food was very good, but not up to what I expected, especially for the price.  I still recommend Aquavit, though.

Incredible from start to finish and absolutely worthy of 2 michelin stars. Did the elaborate tasting menu and was not disappointed. Probably my favorite tasting menu that I have ever done at any michelin star restaurant including in Europe. 14 courses of pure bliss. If you are looking to stray away from the normal french or sushi themed michelin starred restaurants and go on an absolute gastronomic journey for 4 hours than this is the place to go! The flavors were extremely complex and left you truly savoring each bite. Service was top notch. Bravo Chef Emma Bengtsson! Will be returning.

It is a great space. The staff are attentive
and Service is excellent. The food here is good but not the best Nordic food ever. Overall it's still a 4/5 experience.

Came here for a lunch with a client, so, no pictures :( 

We only had an hour so we opted for their 3-course lunch priced at $58. 
First was a lobster salad, second was pan-seared salmon, third was a chocolate dessert with lingonberry (hardly found outside of the Nordic countries). 
Their bread is outstanding and we also had a few amuse-bouche passed out that were delicious. 

Service was flawless. All of the plates were delivered to each person at the table simultaneously. The lady in the front remembered everyone's jackets. 

I will be back for their dinner service or their longer tasting menu for lunch.
Wonderful, love the pork and nice service. Lunch price is reasonbale for michelin two stars

Michelin stars are difficult to rate because the price is so disproportionately high.  The food was great and the wine pairing was also nice but one was enough to share between two people.  I did not enjoy the actual alcohol called Aquavit.  You get the two-Michelin star experience, fun and interesting food, very formal atmosphere with impeccable service and a take home goodie on the way out.  Whether it's worth the price is completely subjective, just depends on how much you are looking to spend.  We had fun but we're also fine with splurging for the night.

Took my husband here for our annual Christmas dinner and we were both blown away. The restaurant has a beautiful dining room, consisting of tables and some booths. We were seated in the booth section, and were brought drinks menus and water immediately. 
We settled on the seasonal tasting menu, which lay in the mid-range of prices at $155, between the prix fixe, and the longer tasting menu. The menu contained one meat dish (pork), which I asked them to adjust to a pescatarian dish, which they happily accommodated. The tasting menu then consisted of 5 courses, with additional little things thrown in. 
Everything was presented beautifully, and we really appreciated the little complimentary things that came out. All dishes were sensational, and I loved the chocolate tray that came at the end, in addition to the dessert. 
They also gave us little bags of breakfast bread to take home. Utterly delightful, and would love to return. Highly recommend for a splurge dinner, or just because.

True definition of perfection. The Valentine's day pre fix was really unforgettable. Every dish was so precise & elegant. The combinations of flavors were next level. We really enjoyed our meal & will certainly return for another great dining experience.

Long known as one of the best Scandinavian restaurants in town. The Chef's tasting menu can take three to four hours, and the food never stops coming. Little extras are served between the listed courses, and every dish is work of art and full of delightful flavors, delicately balanced.  Extraordinary creative and delicious combinations of ingredients. The fig and cardamon aquavit, scallops with green strawberries, and arctic bird's nest ice cream were all outstanding. They are also very generous with extras, from the amuse-bouche to the chocolate truffles after dessert and the gift bags of blueberry pound cake. The service is friendly, efficient, and unobtrusive, and the dining room, modern, spacious, and quiet. Perfect place for a business lunch.

The chef's tasting menu here is such an exquisite culinary experience, with subtle and creative flavors! I'm a huge fan of anything torched or smoked, so of course loved the sea bass and oyster dishes. The highlight of the meal for us was their dessert course - arctic bird's nest. There are so many dimensions to this dish (texture, sweet/tartiness, temperature, fruity/milky flavors). 

The only minor thing to note is that if you do not like goat cheese, mention "goat and sheep's milk cheese", because we made a note to avoid goat cheese and was served sheep's milk cheese. 

Overall we had a great experience!

We were in NY for a week and dined in multiple 2* and 3* restaurants in April. Aquavit was good, but the weakest of our trip. We had the seasonal tasting menu. On the plus side the food is unique, with interesting combinations that you don't find else where, and with one exception was perfectly prepared. Its worth eating here to try something different. On the minus side, one of our dishes, pork collar, was ridiculously salty; the first bite and you wondered what's up, but we gave it a second and third choice; it was ridiculous and we wondered if anyone in the kitchen is tasting what they are serving. The staff were very apologetic when we mentioned this, but the dish should not have been served. Diners on an adjacent table had the same problem. The other areas where Aquavit fell down where a rather lifeless dining room, with too many hovering wait staff, a robotic sommelier who seemed to be following a script, with timed (30 sec) presentations of bottles, and ridiculously small pours; the performance was notably weak compared to Marea and Le Bernardin where the sommeliers and wait staff seemed genuinely interested in sharing their advice and knowledge. I'm glad we went to Aquavit, but we won't repeat for a while.

I picked this restaurant primarily because it was very close to our hotel; it has 2 Michelin stars, so that as a good indicator that the food would be to a high standard. 

Since my guest and I had to catch a show at the Met Opera, we opted for the 3 course meal. In all honesty if I had to pick my courses again I would've chosen what my guest had (stating this laughingly). As this was our first time here, I wanted to see the specrum of the dishes offered to get a feel of the Nordic cuisine displayed here.

The food itself seemed to be overly seasoned/pickled; I'm not sure if that is supposed to authentically represent Nordic cuisine but to my palette it seemed that way. The best way I would describe our dishes was that the plates were beautifully presented and aggressive in flavor. I myself chose the foie gras (red currant, grilled cream, almond), sea bass (morels, cauliflower, rye), and chocolate (malt, banana, walnuts). My guest had the egg (truffle, hazelnut, potato), duck (leek, onion, black garlic), and citrus (bergamot, ginger, kumquat). Along with our meal we had non-alcoholic grape juice selections that were quite excellent.

Like I stated earlier, the plating and service are immaculate here. I just can't bring myself to rate this 5 stars as I never had a complete "wow" factor while dining here. The particular high point was my guest's duck dish; it was unbelievably moist and executed perfectly. One of the staff explained that it was cooked with an initially cold pan with a low temperature. Of course, the textures and temperatures of every other dish were well orchestrated but I think if some nuances in subtlety in flavor were brought into each dish it would make the courses lighter and more enjoyable.

I would definitely come back here to try the full tasting menu when time is not a factor.

I cannot even begin to express my utter disappointment with this sorry excuse for a restaurant, not to mention a so-called two michelin star restaurant. Compare this to Per Se, Eleven Madison Park, or any of the fine establishments that I have been to and this place cannot hold a candle to the other amazing places to eat around NYC. 

Let's start with the dress code. I called in to the restaurant the morning of our reservation to enquire about what we should wear and was told no jeans, no sneakers, and dress shoes and shirt required. My brother came in from out of town and we had to go out to buy him a pair of dress shoes just for the dinner. But...lo and behold...customers all around us were in sneakers, jeans, and polos. So if you're planning to go, seriously free feel to wear whatever you like. 

Let's move on to the front desk. My wife and I arrived earlier than the rest of my family. No one offered to take our coats, seat us at the table, or even offer us a drink at the bar. While I wouldn't care if this was just regular dining establishment, I expect far better service from a restaurant that charges a MINIMUM of $150-200/person. 

Nevertheless, we finally were seated and offered sparkling or still water. I asked for good old regular NY tap water as I do at all of the michelin star restaurants that I have been to and have never been denied. However, at this ridiculous restaurant, they insisted I get bottled water. Again, this is not a problem at per se, jean georges, joel robuchon, french laundry...but at this place apparently tap water is below them. 

My father also had trouble reading the menu and so he turned on his cell phone light to read the items on the list. He was immediately scolded and ordered to turn it off. I presume this was to avoid bothering the other guests, but a) it was extremely rude and b) no alternative light source was offered. When we requested an alternative source of light the stupid waiter just pushed the tiny candle towards my father which was little to no help. Honestly I was shocked and appalled. I demanded a second candle for him or to at least read off the menu items which he did so begrudgingly. My father shouldn't have to apologize for his poor vision and the ridiculously poor lighting and it is the job of (once again) a two michelin-star restaurant to provide better service and accommodate their guests. If I were to go to the Olive Garden down the road I'm sure i would get better service.

With respect to the food, I will try to be more fair. Many of the dishes on the seasonal tasting menu were inventive and well-plated. For that I give my kudos to the chef and kitchen staff. However, I personally wasn't a fan of some of the "fishier" dishes like the herring or cod but I understand that it may just not work with my palate. 

I have already belabored my point enough about this restaurant and its service. I cannot in any way rationalize how this place garnered a two michelin star rating given my experience but either way save your money and go somewhere else. Don't be fooled by the fact that you can easily get a reservation same day as there is a very good reason for that and if you are set on trying it, at least keep on the look out for a groupon deal which I recently noticed was soon-to-be-available.

To celebrate my 100th review, I decided to try another one of NYC's Michelin star restaurants. Aquavit has two of those bad boys. Reserving a month out I arrived on a Wednesday night at 7:30pm with a party of 4. A friend and I arrived early and we were escorted to the bar to the wait for the rest of the party. The service and positivity of the place was probably the best I've seen in a long time. My friend and I tried a Singapore sling and snowmelt, two very well made drinks. The rest of our party arrived and we were seated. We all did the pre-fix which was a little pricey for a small three course. Little did we know that this place served so many additional complementary things. They initiated the food with comp trout roe bites which were phenomenal. Even their bread selection was extensive. For the appetizer I had the egg and a few of my friends had the foie gras. My fiancé tried the herring. All were good, but the foie gras was especially tasty. You can tell that duck is certainly their specialty. We were then given a pork loin mini slider to cleanse our palate. I had the bass as my entree, it was delicious. The cod was a little fishy, but the citrus flavors balanced that out. The duck on the other hand was again my favorite dish. Before desserts came out we were given another palate cleaner - a hibiscus soda cream bite. The desserts were good. We had the cheese plate and the chocolate with duck fat infused ice cream. A little salty, but very interesting for sure. At the end we were given another comp spread of various dessert bites including truffles, brittles, and more. Upon leaving they gave us a comp to go lemon cake. My initial thoughts of price went out the door, they literally just kept giving us things to eat. The value is phenomenal and our sever May was wonderful. I would 100% recommend this place, especially if looking for an incredible dining experience.
Amazing restaurant!  Food was outstanding, and the "aquavit" drinks afterwards were memorable.  Would recommend this restaurant to anyone who desires impeccable service and brilliant food.

Didn't even eat there-but tried calling to discuss a reservation cancellation/rebook and was hung up on. Not like an accidental hang up either. Jeezzz I don't want to spend my money here and you don't either if they can't even be polite enough on the phone!

A long time favorite but we never made it for the herring fest before. The herring tower plus delicious brown bread and butter was spot on. We also enjoyed a flight of House made aquavit. Service was very attentive. Didn't have room for dessert.

A subliminal experience from beginning to end. Incomparable culinary creations, impeccable service, classy ambience...and very high prices to match all this. We were seated in the lounge while waiting for our table, in very nice high chairs, and offered house made aquavit. The dinner that followed was nothing short of spectacular. Every dish was a culinary adventure, and the service was impeccable.

We had the seasonal menu, added a cheese selection, Bird's Nest dessert. And the horseradish aquavit, wine, glögg, and coffee as for beverages.

It was not cheap at $446 total, but worth it still.
Top Nordic restaurant in town. Two thumbs up. Absolutely gorgeous food, and good service.

Amazing experience. Everything was meticulously placed and every bite was fantastic. Allot yourself some extra time if you're doing the tasting menu, it took our group around four hours but it was definitely worth it. 
The best part of the meal was definitely the birds nest dessert but almost all of the courses were a hit. Aquavit (the liquor) is something that they make in house and while I did not enjoy it, it definitely cleared my sinuses.
Had the venison carpaccio and cod. Clean, minimalistic plating. Tasted good. Uncomfortable chairs. Would go back.

At this newly reopened space, ethereal design food and service meet. The bae menu which is in effect currently offers stunningly updated Scandinavian classics.
Ate:
Artichoke char cauliflower and sandrflord sauce
$34
Spectacular taste flavors and presentation with seamless service. A true dining gem.

In the middle of this incredible dinner experience you will close your eyes for a moment to say thank for Chefs like Emma Bengtsson of Aquavit. A Scandinavian fine dining restaurant  which has become a Manhattan institution.
It was an absolute privilege to have been invited last night to be part of a select group to experience the exceptional menu designed by Michelin Star Chef Emma Bengtsson before the grand reopening of Aquavit tonight.
When you have to say Oh My God a few times in the middle of a bite or take a moment to close your eyes and say thank you for Chefs like Emma, one has hit the jackpot of a culinary experience!
On Halloween night my treat was the Chef's tasting menu. From the very first sip of wine, the first canape, to the detail in each presentation and the exceptional service you know why they have 2 Michelin Stars

The treats were:
Gravlox with chamomile gel, house smoked salmon. A note of this spoonful  delight leaves you craving for more!
Shrimp skagen along w Langosteen in a malted crisp topped with oyster sauce. I've never had a skagen before and this was absolute delight. its was like eating a piece of delicious cake.
Caviar: imperial ostera caviar from China served on a bed of crisp brioche, house beurre blanc and potato crisps. I said OMG like 7 times as I ate this and kept saying OMG when they came ot ask me how it was. I'm still smiling about this deliciousness!
Live diver Scallop with lardo foam and chanterelles. mmmmmmm!
King Crab : kelp creme fresh and mussel stock and pickled green tomatoes
Sea buck tartine. The perfect intermission.
House  butter w dill baguette .
A nice crisp shell on the bagutte. You taste the dill immediately..butter had the right amount of salt and silky smooth.
Venison: Nasturtiums (edible leaves)
aged Beef fat, flat bread made w wheat, water and caraway and fennel. The venison is from New Zealand with a
tarragon emulsion. WOW! DOUBLE wow! I can never eat venison prepared in amy other manner. The layers of taste was just incredible  and needs to be tasted in person!
Halibut: I called this Halibut Heaven! This was perfection! It was served with kohlrabi prepared in three ways- Baked, Roasted and Fermented and pickled. There is a kale crumble on top of the kholrabi and the fish. Glazed w miso palm puree and elder flower w muscle foam. WOW!
7X Beef.  Topped with black truffle, charred onion cup w grape seed crumble with fermented truffle, buck wheat soy jous and collard green
I closed my eyes for a moment after I ate this. :)
This is when sadness sets in a little as you know when the desserts arrive the experience is nearing the end...
Priest Cheese with organe marmalade and caraway with flat bread.
Rose hip soup with almond ice cream and a sweedish cookie. Light and perfect. Love the presentation reminiscent  of a rose hip tea in a kettle.
Arctic Birds Nest..this is the Chef's signature  dessert. I've had this on a past visit and it did not dissapoint. Its served with shaved frozen yogurt and I took my time savoring and making this experience  last as long as possible.
Board of pettine  desserts; Vaccum cleaner, goat cheese and honey macaroon and lemon organe tart
(Vacuum cleaner as it is filled with a whole bunch of goodness from the kitchen.)
This was a perfect little touch to end the tasting. 
Wow! What an amazing dinner! I'm still amazed with symphony of flavors and  layering.

What a delicious night! We chose the chefs tasting menu. Everything is phenomenal and for a great price. There were a lot of small snacks in between meals. For the time being there is no wine pairing menu but don't let that stop you from trying all their cocktails. Very intimate space and the other dining area is also cozy. Beautiful kitchen with wide windows. A new favorite. My favorite dish would have to be the Dover sole. Thank you Chef Emma!

Went here with a friend to grab a bite in the lounge on a Saturday night. The newly redesigned lounge provided a very low-key and relaxed dinner, which was actually very enjoyable.

To start off, we went with an order of the crab fritters and spiced mayonnaise and the gravlax.

The crab fritters were decent--definitely meaty, and had good flavor overall, but didn't blow us away.

The gravlax was much more memorable as the fish was so fresh and paired deliciously with the rest of the ingredients.

For our mains we split the swedish meatballs and the pork schnitzel. Both of these dishes were outstanding and were really moist and flavorful--I would give an edge to the meatballs, especially because they paired so well with the pickles, potatoes, and lingonberries.

For dessert, we split a slice of the princess cake, which was the perfect sweet ending to the meal.

We also enjoyed several different drinks--there were definitely a large variety of flavors--can't say any of them really impressed, but they were good nonetheless.

Overall, this place serves up some very good food and ordering a la carte at the bar can actually be very reasonable--especially for a 2 Michelin starred restaurant. Service was top notch and food/drinks came out quickly. Definitely not a bad option if you are looking for a nice dinner out in the city.

Dinner reservations were made 3 weeks in advance.  Upon checking in, I was concerned about security of my exclusive coat with no ticket given. We were seated at the worst seat in the restaurant near the hallway even though the restaurant was half empty. I sat in a draft. I notified the waitress, and the waitress was fully prepared to offer me a "wrap" to cover my beautiful new dress and jewelry instead of moving us to a better table. I traded seats with my friend, and then I  got a full Birdseye view of the kitchen and their helpers for the entire evening. How romantic is that??? The no thank you scant portions of the foods, including the one tiny flavorless dinner roll, were extremely disappointing. Wine glasses were scantly poured, and the Wagyu Beef was stingy served with 2 leaves of underdone spinach, and some sautéed union peels. Mediocre is a kind description. I left the restaurant hungry. The service was "cold," and the prices were exorbitant! On the way out, we were given bags of rock salt as a parting goodbye. Really??? I will never return to this disaster restaurant! We deserve a refund. Just don't go!

Love the sea food and beef at Aquavit. The environment is pretty lovely but unfortunately since the restaurant is on the ground floor, there isn't any skyline view.

Also, I was surprised that a Michelin 2 star restaurant doesn't have a superb bathroom. The cleanness is not up to my expectation.

Never had Herring before, but my experience here has made me rethink herring as a main ingredient! For that alone, I would give Aquavit five stars. 

I went to Aquavit yesterday for lunch having no prior experience with the place other than the glowing recommendations of my friends. 

When we arrived the weather was quite bad, but as soon as we entered the restaurant the ambience blew away any earlier feelings caused by the dreary mess outside. 

The food was excellent: they had a Herring Festival fron what I can recall. And it safe to say there is good reason for.this restaurant being awardex 2 Michelin stars.  

I would love to visit again.

My SO and I had the chef's tasting menu with wine pairing and it was amazing. Each course  took something simple, such as a small piece of incredibly tasty crab, and added a supporting but not overwhelming cast of flavors. The wines were from small vineyards, and a running theme that night was vineyards founded by people who changed careers, such as one from  a former mechanic in Sardinia. Service was superb, friendly and unobtrusive. Tips - the setting is fairly formal, men will be more comfortable if wearing a jacket; dress well. Also the price was equal to the quality, so be prepared. Budget a fair amount of time - I wouldn't want to start the chef's tasting menu on a weeknight later than 7 as it took almost three hours. Finally, if you will indulge me, this meal reminded me of the multi course  tasting menu at the departed La Belle Vie in Minneapolis, and that was  my favorite meal anywhere - it was that good.

First, the service was excellent and really makes you feel as if you are in a high-end restaurant. Now the food was disappointing. We had the 3 course lunch menu and ordered different items so I got to try a few things. I like the amuse bouche of smoked salmon. It was one of my favorite things here. My first course were the scallops and they were delicious. It went downhill from there. My friend had the trout which was so incredibly fishy. I wished there was some sauce to cover the fishiness of it but nope. Next I had the lobster which was a supplement of 15 dollars. It's hard to mess up a lobster. This lobster was nothing to write home about. It was pretty small considering the supplement and not that tender. It also came with parsnips I believe which didn't compliment it at all. 
My friend had the halibut. Again, I've had halibut at other places that was tender and flaky. This halibut was rubbery and overcooked. It helped eating with mashed potatoes to have something creamy in a bite. 

Last was the birds nest dessert that I was very much looking forward too. It was another supplement of 15 dollars and it was the biggest disappointment of the meal. I didn't like it at all. It was overly sweet raspberry sorbet. It was so sweet I could only take a few bites. Not much on the plate was available to break up the sweetness. Some chocolate and the nest which tasted like nothing. There were also white chocolate eggs with cream inside. It was so lacking in taste and white chocolate really? Everything about the dessert was the opposite of scrumptious. It was awkward and excessively sweet. 

Even the bread course was uneventful.

This was my first experience at a Michelin star restaurant and it did not disappoint. The staff was extremely friendly and knowledgeable. We did the chefs tasting with the wine pairing. By the end of the night I could barley move I was so full. My favorites were the Live Diver Scallop and the Arctic birds nest but everything was delicious! It was my first time having caviar and surprisingly I enjoyed it! Highly recommend.

My friend and I go out every month for a dinner at a different ethnic restaurant.  For the holiday edition, we decided to splurge on Aquavit.

We walked in and were immediately greeted by pleasant and professional staff members, they took our coats and directed us to our table.  The decor is refined in a crisp and clean way.  The tables are spaced out enough that conversation at regular levels is possible.

We were lucky to have Douglas for a waiter, his knowledge of food and personality added to our evening.  We selected the eight course tasting menu and left ourselves in extremely capable hands.

They provided additional little bites on top of the eight courses.  Gravlax elegantly presented on a spoon, foie gras tartlet (such a remarkable presentation of foie gras, truly the essence of the foie gras), potato crisp with caviar, langoustine tartare in a taco, two types of bread (the dark one was astounding), an almond ice cream intermezzo, and a final tray of brittle, marshmallows, and macarons.  These were just the extras and they were all perfect.

The main events included a diver scallop, Osetra caviar with potato crisps and creme fraiche, cod with potatoes, cold smoked venison, king crab leg, beef from a Japanese breed of cattle raised in Colorado, a cheese course with dried sausage shavings, and the arctic birds nest dessert.  I could go on and on about each of these dishes but suffice it to say that their wasn't an off bite in the entire evening.  Every single item was expertly conceived and executed.  The food was expertly sourced and extremely high quality.

The drinks were also excellent.  Linie Aquavit with carrot juice cocktail was a great way to start our dinner.  Douglas recommended a 100% Grenache from the Rhône region.  It was stunning, remarkable nose.

The entire staff worked seamlessly together and were all knowledgeable about the food.  Also noteworthy is that they were all personable.  Aquavit has earned its two Michelin stars and is deserving of consideration for the third.  Highly recommend this place.

Good food and an interesting experience. 

I ordered from the 3-course dinner menu: venison, hen of the wood, and arctic bird's nest. Each course was flavorful, was presented well, and fit their wintry forest motif. 

The arctic bird's nest seems to be one of their most famous dishes, and it was the most elaborately assembled one that I had that night. Three eggs with a very thin white chocolate "shell" and a goat-cheese parfait "yolk" inside. Takes some finesse. 

There were 5 amuse-bouches that acted as mini-courses: hibiscus tea, bread, gravlax, ice cream, petit fours. 

Although it didn't detract much from their food, Aquavit doesn't always strike a perfect balance between taste and concept. The fennel marshmallow is unusual, but it doesn't taste any better than an ordinary marshmallow. The nasturtium leaves on top of the venison appetizer ultimately don't add much compared to ordinary garnishes. 

The biggest criticism I have is that Aquavit's theme is largely an illusion that falls apart easily upon closer inspection. They describe themselves as a seasonal Nordic restaurant. A few menu items are authentic Scandinavian--the gravlax, for example--but most aren't. Mangalica pork? Hungarian breed. 7X beef? From Colorado. Montana trout? Yup. 

Pacing was maybe slightly slow for a 3-course menu. That's in part because there were several mini-courses, but there was still a bit of a pause. Gives you a chance to talk though. 

Service was fine. Efficient coat check (didn't need a ticket, probably because I had a reservation). Slight wait at the bar though I had a reservation. 

No published dress code. I'd say half the men wore jackets and most of the rest wore business casual. 

The bathrooms are ordinary but fine. The paper hand towels are luxurious.

Very disappointing experience! Rude and unprofessional staff, I wanted to cancel reservation even before coming, after I asked lady on the phone about the price, she said "all the info is online" and just hang up! 

We were surprised how can a service at two Michelin be that bad, until we met this passive aggressive manager (no wonder only 3 tables were occupied ). 

If you read the bad comments below, its all about awful service.

If you want to feel the real Michelin star or even nice experience, avoid this place!!! There are plenty other worth $$$$ money restaurants in NYC!!!

We thoroughly enjoyed our visit to the bar here for dinner. Had some fun trying the flight of aquavit but the real winner was the smoked peach cobbler cocktail (so strong, unique and aesthetically pleasing). We couldn't decide between entrees so we ended up starting with the gravlax (which was super fresh and served with a tasty horseradish sauce) and then finishing with 3 entrees: the cod sandwich, the pork schnitzel and the Swedish  meatballs. If you've had schnitzel or meatballs before, you're probably thinking they can't be much better here than at IKEA...but you're so wrong. The flavors they melded together in these dishes were quite amazing. We had great service and enjoyed the quiet atmosphere of the bar. Would definitely recommend the bar if you're looking for a less expensive Scandinavian meal.

Simply put: one of the best meals I've ever had. Every dish is aesthetically artful, well-composed, and delicious. Modern Scandinavian at its best. The ambiance is upscale without being stuffy and the service is impeccable. The dining room has clean lines and the wood tones offer just the right amount of warmth. Well-deserving of its accolades.

Great service and plating execution! This is a two star Michelin restaurant and they took simple ingredients like potato chips were escalated to a different level. The tartare dish had so many elements that meshed well together. The bread was flavored with smoked salt and was so good! Will say that the last three courses were not my favorite. I thought the cheese course was quite boring and did not like the cheeses selected. The dessert presentation was great but didn't love the flavors. The chocolate was too rich and needed another element to offset the strong blueberry taste. The restaurant also gave each of us some smoked sea salt to take home which I was excited to use. However my dog went through my suitcase and decided to taste test it instead. Someone got to enjoy it!

Came here hungry and left hungry. I had the diver scallop and it was a single scallop. Then the halibut which was very good but super light and not filling. It was dead in the restaurant, only one other couple so the staff was hovering the entire meal, it was awful. There was only one type of bread and it wasnt memorable too. There are many better restaurants.

This place was awesome. I had a sample of different flavored Aquavit to start off. Loved the dill and cucumber most. Dinner was roasted endive and cod both excellent but the ultimate experience was the birds nest desert , the little eggS were frozen goat cheese, the nest delicious and twigs chocolate yummy with a dab of blueberry under the eggs. 10 stars. Fine dining at its best.

We came here with a reservation for lunch. Once we checked our coats in we were seated immediately. I tried the aquavit flight (3qty) of fig, raspberry, and I forgot the third one. They tasted good but I would have preferred a cocktail instead. For lunch I chose the three course option. I had the driver scallops, pork, and chocolate cake. The flavors were amazing with a beautiful balance of umami and subtle hints of sweetness throughout the meal.

I've heard many good things about Aquavit. It was one of the michelin starred restaurants I haven't got the opportunity to try. We came here for the Valentine's Day Prefix and don't think we will ever return. The service was ok at most. They had no idea what we had reserved or had already paid for, we had to keep reminding them which took away from the whole experience. There was nothing special or outstanding about the food. Our favorite part was the dessert, so rich and interesting in flavor. We forgot about everything else. Overpriced for what we got. I feel is one of those places that got popular and then simply is living from that fame without caring too much.

Aquavit is a stalwart on the NYC fine dining scene. This two-Michelin starred Scandinavian outpost delivers a refined experience while remaining congenial. Its recent renovation showcases the clean aesthetic of Nordic design that we admire, setting a lovely atmosphere. On a snowy New York evening, it seemed particularly apropos. The cuisine at Aquavit is deliberate and precise, presented in a creative way. Flavors are typical of the region, light and fresh, showcasing the ingredients. While the food was enjoyable, it was somewhat imperfect to our tastes. Wine list is well-selected and the service was proficient and hospitable. The experience is more classic than cutting edge, but it's an enjoyable meal. For lovers of Scandinavian food and seafood particularly, a worthy destination. Probably a 3.5/5, but rounding up for the pleasant sensibilities.

Atmosphere
- Serene and elegant, on the quieter side with well spaced tables and a quiet luxe sensibility.
- Recent renovation very well done; high ceilings and sleek Scandinavian design that retains warmth.
- Bar area is worth a stop before/after dinner. There are a few seating areas with low slung lounge chairs. Nice space.

Food
Aquavit offers both tasting menus ($155-$225), or a three course prix fixe ($115). Most of the cuisine is presented in a very creative way, and takes a refined approach. It's a high quality experience, and the food is typically Nordic - fresh and light. Quite enjoyable overall, but with some ups and downs. We enjoyed:

- Matjes Herring (danish rye, pear, cured egg yolk): When you get the perfect bite, it's well balanced with the yolk mellowing out the fish and pear lending some needed crunch. However, the proportions are off, leaving a number of bites just fish and rye, which gets a bit monotonous. This does have a 'fishy' taste, though remains refined.
- Halibut (kohlrabi, pear, elderflower mussel foam): Nicely presented, and elegantly balanced. Again the 'fishy' sensibility peeks through, but is not overwhelming. The dish feels more substantial than a typical fish dish, given the heft and firmness of the fish. Well cooked.
- Mangalista Pork Collar (rutabaga, plum, barley): A more robust dish. The pork was exceptionally moist, and well-employed acidity lent good counterbalance. Very nice.
- Chocolate (lingonberries and salted caramel): The cool presentation belied a rather lackluster flavor and generic chocolate cake, other elements not prominent enough.
- Arctic Birds Nest (blueberry and goat cheese - $15 supp.): A hallmark of the restaurant. Again really cool presentation, and the interplay of textures was unique. Tasty, concentrated berry flavor went nicely with the goat cheese. Worth ordering this nontraditional dessert.

Beverage
Began our evening in the chill bar area, which was sparsely attended on a snowy evening. Make it a stop before or after your meal. We enjoyed the Apres Ski (sparkling wine, pine, rhubarb, fennel - $21) which truly lived up to the name, with a subtle pine flavor peeking through. It set the mood.

With dinner, we enjoyed the 2016 Domaine Gouffier Cremant ($19) with our first course. It's a solid value selection, though a bit overpriced by the glass. The wine list at Aquavit skews toward French options (with an especially good selection from Burgundy both whites and reds), but has representation across regions. While the list leans toward pricer options, it's not hard to find a quality bottle ~$150. With our meal, we especially enjoyed the 2015 Dujac Fils & Pere Chambolle-Musigny ($245). 

Service
- Generally good, our waitress was thoughtful and attentive, plus had a welcoming personality.
- Bar area similarly welcoming and kind.
- Somm was a bit standoffish and just ok.

One of the best meals I've ever had. Got the chef's tasting menu with wine pairing and put my trust in the experienced hands of the team at Aquavit. 

Completely wowed from beginning to end. Excellent service, cuisine and libations. Outstanding.
I had the herring and cod in two course lunch for $65. It was an amazing experience and both dishes were perfect. The servers were also very knowledgeable and courteous.
a very good restaurant, top notch service, nice room and as long as you like their unique cuisine you cannot go wrong here.

Between a 4 and a 5. The food was great. Was it two Michelin Star great? Probably not, but for the price we paid and the fact that it was takeout it definitely delivered. For $125 (incl tax) you get an obscene amount of food for two. We feasted on three different types of herring, potatoes, cheese and bread, eggs, shrimp, gravlax, meatballs, sausage, more potatoes, and a variety of accoutrements like lingonberries and pickles. 

Everything was packaged perfectly, and some of the food stood out as incredible. My favorites were the cheese, gravlax, meatballs, and the shredded potatoes. The gravlax was an unreal portion - there was easily a quarter to half pound of the best I've ever had served with lemon and sauce. I could have been happy with that alone. 

Reheating directions were easy and simple for the hot dishes, everything was packaged perfectly, pickup was easy, and all in all it was a fun, unique, and filling takeout experience. Thanks Aquavit!
Get the aquavit flights and gravlax for sure but shockingly the steak tartar is the most amazing I've ever had!

Long due review. I dined here back in December 2019 and I was impressed. 

Excellent service and food. We ordered their three courses menu and had the following, herring and scallop for the appetizer, cod and halibut for entree and their signature dessert, bird's nest. Their halibut hands down is the best I have even had. It was soft and the sauce is buttery which paired well with the fish. I have dined at Eleven Madison park and had halibut, I wasn't impressed at all. The next highlight is scallop. It was cooked perfectly and fresh. Bird's nest is soso to me. In no doubt it is a masterpiece in vision but no resonation in favor.
A two Michelin starred resturaunt doing a $16 week day to go lunch. Totally worth it. Fresh and healthy nordic food. Very easy to order and pick-up.  Went over to the park and had a lovely picnic.

During COVID, we really enjoyed their picnic basket for two! Overall, best picnic food I've had for sure. The duck pastrami is a game-changer for me.. somebody please tell me where I can find that!! The amount of food was ultra generous for two people, we ended up taking a ton home, including all of the amazing desserts.

Some misses were the soggy potato chips, and a mix-up on our aquavit flavors (despite them calling earlier in the day to say they were out of certain ones and have us choose new). Drinking the aquavits out of the tiny bottles had us feeling like we had raided the hotel mini bar I also wish I knew a bit more about the daily variety of the menu, i.e. what the cheeses and pastries were.

Also, social distancing could have been better. They just started outdoor dining so I'm sure they'll optimize, but I wish they had a hostess stand outside, or at least someone greeting and directing traffic. The people there for outdoor dining were confused about where to go. It was cramped in the foyer where I had wait for my take out order, with people waiting for outdoor tables and waiters/waitresses shuttling back and forth.
I got Aquavit delivery on Tock to celebrate crayfish festival and their portions are both generous and delicious.

I am not one to give a bad review, but these times call for saying something. I ate here on Friday night and I was overwhelmed by the restaurant's lack of commitment to social distancing guidelines. My friend and I were sitting in a tent when it started raining and the staff packed ALL the restaurant tables under the tent! They could've easily apologized and given us our food to go and it would have been a better experience. We would've gone somewhere else had we known this was their solution to the rain that was forecasted and the reason we asked for a table under the tent. The tent was so crowded that the staff couldn't even properly walk through the tables. The servers were hovering over the table making us feel extremely uncomfortable. I understand that these are difficult times, but this restaurant claims to provide a fine dining experience. I cannot believe their disregard for the safety of their customers and their staff.

This is only for COVID outdoor dining and their crawfish dish too. 

Overall the experience was whatever. The crawfish was pretty disgusting. It was clear that they had attempted to cover a potentially smelly seafood taste with some sort of essence? It tasted like I accidentally got soap in my mouth. To me, it was basically inedible. I'd recommend you never getting the crawfish. If you had put it in my mouth during a blind taste test I would've said soap. 

However, the quiche, the crudités were both honestly really amazing. Best quiche I've ever had, but don't listen to me as I've had quiche maybe 5 times in my life. 

The desserts were underwhelming as well (sea buckthorne and frozen yogurt). Try something else y'all. 

Everyone was separated very well and the outdoor space was nice but as with any outdoor space be wary of flies.  I would love to go here again when in door dining is back as I'm sure it would be a better experience. 

I'd want to go back when indoor dining

Excellent restaurant in a beautiful garden setting. Excellent dining experience. The food was delicious and interesting. The service was fantastic and the staff are all very knowledgeable about the food they were serving. definitely worth a visit if you are in NYC.  Finally, One of the best Michelin 2 star I've had. Worth the michelin stars standard .
This is the  many  time we visited this place. Excellent
Food is amazing service is really good. It's a wonderful experience to dine in this Michelin two star restaurant.i love it .

After hearing about Aquavit for years (mainly because of consistent rave reviews from a former colleague who visited on multiple occasions), I finally got a chance to test it out for myself tonight. While they do offer indoor dining now (which through the window looked to be terrifically done--good spacing, a literal wall between 2 occupied tables, limited capacity) we decided to make use of the outdoor dining option that's hidden from the street and in an elegant, partly tented area.

Pros: food is AMAZING--I mean that for all the dishes we had, even the bread basket that we had to order separately--worth every dime; servers are super friendly and provided great dessert recommendations, they really went above and beyond; appropriate COVID precautions and spaced out seating 

Cons: towards the end of the meal, there was a completely random temperature drop that had our teeth chattering behind our masks--but obviously, this has nothing to do with the restaurant itself, just the unpredictable Fall weather. 

I would definitely return here, and would even be amenable to dining indoors sometime when it's no longer possible to eat al fresco.

We went here for a birthday celebration and the restaurant accommodated for that which was a great surprise. The food was fantastic, as my girlfriend is from Stockholm Sweden, she enjoyed the appetizers of the shrimp skagen and the many course of Swedish meatballs. The desserts were fantastic and traditional and our princess cake was the Icing on the cake for the experience. The atmosphere was great even when we were sitting outside in October. Next time we come though we want to create a reservation for the in dinning. But I do have to end with this, if you are looking for great authentic Scandinavian food in the states and know what that food entails, please make the effort to visit this wonderful restaurant. But if you do not know what Scandinavian food is, please choose another place.

Three weeks into the reopening of NYC indoor dining, the majority of other diners here apparently still feel more comfortable with the outdoor seating.  Admittedly, the beautiful decor and fully visible, glass-walled kitchen can only be appreciated from the spacious, limited seating, main dining room. Table distancing is used instead of plastic barriers to meet Covid rules.

Service from the helpful, masked staff was excellent, and each of my individual plate's taste and presentation demonstrated the chef's sure hand.  My only problem was that my technology failed me with the Covid-era QR menu, quickly solved with an "old-fashioned" replacement (disposable paper).

Unfortunately, while they looked amazing, I decided to pass on the aquavit creations.  Maybe next time, when I don't have to drive 200 km right after my meal.

I am so looking forward to returning soon.

2020 10 22. M2.

wedding anniversary, took my wife to Aquavit this past weekend. It was amazing, food tasted delicious - we had herring trio and scallop crude as starters. As a main course we both opted in for fish: seared halibut and poached trout - but were properly prepared and tasted great. As a desert we shared arctic birds nest, also definitely recommend. 

Highly recommend this place, their staff also deserve 5 stars.

If you are looking for some high end dining experience during COVID, definitely choose here! My gf took me here for my birthday. The decoration here is very minimalism yet elegant. The place is intimate. It doesn't host many people so this place is quite, which is perfect for me. We tried their prix fixe and it's such a nice dinner for me. Their lobster bisque is the best. Possibly my best COVID period dining experience so far

My boyfriend made a Saturday dinner reservation for 5pm to celebrate my birthday. We booked it 3 weeks in advance. We were concerned due to updated covid-19 guidance on restaurants the week before Thanksgiving. Luckily, this restaurant is still open for indoor and outdoor dining. 

We arrived around 4:50pm. First guests of the night! We were a tad bit early, but they escorted us to their lounge area. As we waited the waitress came over and offered us water. We also ordered a flight of 3: Juniper & Lemon, Mango Lime & Chili, and Coriander & Dill. 

Our table was ready and we were escorted to our table. We had a seat inside the restaurant next to the window. The waiter/waitress would pull the chair out for me everytime I returned to my seat from the restroom. The service is overall excellent. They are all courteous, patient, and attentative to make sure we enjoyed our overall dining experience. 

We decided to go with "Seasonal Tasting." The menu set include: lobster, foie gras, duck, and artic bird's nest. I am allergic to crustaceans. Therefore, I was able to substitute lobster for scallop crudo. 

We also ordered Tarte Flambee, Swedish Meatballs, and princess cake, Chateau Yvonne glass of red wine, 2 cocktails, a cup of coffee, and a cup of capuccino for dessert. In addition, we received a complimentary appetizer in the beginning. It was a potato croquet on rocks. They also gave us the Sourdough, danish rye, and cultured butter as we waited for our appetizers. As a complimentary dessert, we got white chocolate truffles & gingersnap cookies. 

Our favorites were the following: tarte flambee, lobster, foie gras, duck, swedish meatballs, and artic's birdnest. 

It was such a special night and a memorable dining experience.

Delicious Scandinavian fare!

I ordered delivery through Tock.

I was excited most for my crispy pork schnitzel, which was perfect. The potatoes on the side were a nice surprise - cooked and sliced beautifully and absolutely delicious. I had the Danish rye and butter on the side, which was seedy, soft and even a little crusty. The seasonal pumpkin pie was a treat and honestly stunning, too.
