Delivery was wonderful! Everything came packed extremely thoughtfully. I wish I could try the house aquavits, but that'll be for next time.

What a delightful find!  I can't say that I've ever dined on Nordic cuisine before, apart from Swedish meatballs at Costco, but my experience at Aquavit was fantastic!   The décor is modern and elegant with simple lines, like a much, much higher-end Ikea.  We were adequately spaced out for proper social distancing.  The wait staff was extremely accommodating.  I ordered the tasting menu, not immediately realizing that it was supposed to be for the table.  My dinner date could not eat lobster and would not eat foie gras.  He was provided with other options and there was no fuss about it.  Every dish was phenomenal.  The lobster was a delight with the fennel balancing the rich shellfish bisque.  The foie gras was mind-blowing!  The last time I played with liquid nitrogen was a college chemistry lab, when my lab partner splashed it in my eye (I luckily still have great vision in the eye).  Never had I thought to use it on foie gras.  The fresh figs, almond and sour cream were a delicious base complimenting the richness of the frozen foie gras fragments sprinkled atop. This was a truly novel presentation for me, and I loved it.  Not gonna lie, I probably would go out raiding and pillaging like the Vikings of old in order to procure the dish daily.  The duck, served with the sweet lingonberry sauce, was tender and juicy.  The dish did come with beets, which probably would have been a nice earthy contrast to the sweetness of the lingonberry sauce, but I despise beets (I know, how uncivilized of me).  I enjoyed the dish just fine without the beet.  The star of the show by far, was the artic bird's nest dessert.  A nest made of dried honey cushioned eggs made of goat cheese parfait, blueberry sorbet and yogurt with a rich berry and chocolate sauce filling the bottom of the nest.  Upon cracking the "egg" there was even a yellow center simulating yolk.   What fantastic dedication and attention to artistic detail!  It paired perfectly with the anise, caraway, fennel aquavit, compliments of our waiter.  Speaking of aquavit, I would go back again, just to enjoy all the offerings.  I had a flight of three with my meal and fell in love with the horseradish aquavit.  I'm sure my poor spouse grew tired of my effusive gushing over the surprising perfect blend of flavor and spice.  The fig & cardamom aquavit was a dessert in and of itself.  My one and only complaint regarding the experience, is that it was quite chilly inside the restaurant and I had to drape my long, down, winter coat over my shoulders to be at a comfortable temperature.  Eh, perhaps, it was part of the Nordic theme.  Overall, it was a wonderful experience that bears repeating.  I highly recommend the restaurant.

I went here for my birthday dinner at the end of October and they nailed it!! We were able to sit inside at that time but they also had an impressive amount of outdoor seating available. The service was impeccable and everyone was safely spread out in adherence to covid standards. High quality bathroom soap (which is a weird standout but super appreciated when we're all washing our hands so much). 

We didn't do the tasting but instead tried a handful of items from the a la carte menu. 
You have to pay for the bread basket but it's absolutely worth it, super quality bread and butter. Mushroom soup was phenomenal, as was the tartar with a pleasant crispy element (sunchokes). Both the Swedish meatballs and the Icelandic cod were brilliant, classics prepared perfectly. We went a bit overboard with the desserts, including the princess cake covered in green fondant (great but I skipped the fondant part), kladdkaka chocolate cake with dulce de leche ice cream, and s'mores which was our favorite.  They also gave us cake pop doughnut bites at the end, much appreciated! 

You should try the aquavit since it's the drink that the restaurant is named after. Comparable to vodka infusions, they have a handful of classics on the menu and some rotating seasonal options as well.

Fine dining at its finest. A laid back Michelin star restaurant on the upper east side. The blue ambiance brings a sense of calming. 
The oysters were fresh and with a hint of lavender, interesting yet refreshing. We both ordered white fishes. My fish was poached and a little bland. 
They gave us complimentary doughnuts for desert! Deli

Ever since we visited Stockholm and Copenhagen last March, I've been dreaming about the food. Since it was our anniversary weekend, we decided to splurge a bit and order their Smörgåsbord for Two. I placed the order online and it was ready to go at my pick up time. 

The Smörgåsbord for Two includes 3 types of Herring, Gravlax & Hovmästar Sauce, Shrimp Skagen, Cheese & Potatoes, and Crispbread. We also ordered a Princess Cake, which is a full sized cake and it took us 3 days to finish it. 

The gravlax was phenomenal and definitely on par with anything we had in Stockholm during our stay. The shrimp skagen was not as good as X's brother's gf's, but she's a wonderful cook, so I won't fault Aquavit. The Princess Cake, was definitely better than any I had during Fikas in Stockholm. 

I can't wait until the pandemic is over so I can go eat inside Aquavit.

I pre-ordered a $150 Valentine's Day gift box four days in advance, and told the recipient when to expect the delivery. On the day of the delivery, 15 minutes before the scheduled delivery time, Caviar sends a text saying that the order was cancelled because the store was closed.

I'm sure the food here is delicious, but I just don't understand how a restaurant could close without warning, when it's supposed to be delivering Valentine's Day pre-orders?

I never write reviews, but this was the best meal of my life. Have wanted to go here for years, and it did not disappoint. Perfect service, perfect food, wonderful ambience. Great social distancing during COVID. Hope to be back soon one day.

I'm giving this restaurant 5 stars overall for excellent service and great presentation of food. I enjoyed every dish that I had with the exception of one (details below) which was just personal preference.

Here's what we got and my rating for each:

LÖJROM - 4.5/5 [fun & elegant presentation, great taste, loved the condiments and toppings that came with the set. My bf preferred caviar's taste, but this was very cool to try]

MATJES HERRING - 2/5 [we both LOVED the sauce and thought it was spectacular and unique. the herring itself was very salty and fishy though and hard to eat]

DIVER SCALLOP - 5/5 [incredible. nothing to change, this dish is perfect]

WAGYU BEEF - 3.5/5 [tasted very similar to the wagyu beef flavor that I've tried at other restaurants throughout my life. this dish wasn't bad per se, it was just not as unique as I would have liked, but ultimately still very tender, flavorful, and delicious to eat. the flavors are quite common for an asian palette though]

ARCTIC BIRD'S NEST- 5/5 [absolute artistry and a beauty. loved the egg which was white chocolate + ice cream? there is even something golden in the middle which represents the yolk. loved this dessert]

SWEDISH MEATBALLS (add-on) - 3/5 [pretty good, but not stellar. glad to have tried it here though]

COCKTAILS:
UPSTATE PICKING - 5/5 [one of the best cocktails we've tried. super unique, just a perfect blend of everything on your tongue]

tasting set of 3 aquavits - 2/5 [hard liquor is not for us....we learned this when drinking these 3 shots haha]

overall great experience - thank you aquavit!

There's a reason why Aquavit exits for so long. Everything here is perfect and so on point. Definitely get their birds nest dessert . The best dessert I had last year. I'll definitely come back again!! The dining area is beautiful. Don't go for outdoor. The indoor door is too nice to miss!

We dined at Aquavit initially not realizing it was a Michelin 2-Star restaurant. We immediately recognized why this restaurant is so highly rated. Service was exceptional and every course was truly outstanding. The only complaint (and it's a minor one) is that, even by Michelin Star restaurant standards the price of the wines (both by the bottle and by the glass) was a bit steeper than we'd expect. Otherwise, the food and the whole dining experience was well worth the premium price.

This place offering delivery. Food is absolutely amazing.
I'm glad I found this restaurant.
Highly recommend to try.

I Loved this restaurant! You Must try the Grilled Diver Scallop, Swedish Meatballs with the pommes puree, and of course save room for dessert we went with trying the princess cake, so light and delicious  ! The dover sole honestly had way too much of a butter taste for my liking but was still very good ! 

The decor is very calming and soothing and the staff  very friendly , knowledgeable and accommodating. 

Great authentic experience  for a Michelin restaurant without feeling stuffy and over the top will definitely be back for another visit

Can't believe I didn't submit this draft review for Aquavit!  We dined in pre-COVID, for dinner on a late Friday night, and until this day the dinner was visually and palatably memorable!  There's ONE word that can describe the entire experience: IMPECCABLE! Service was polite, friendly and attentive. The restaurant is spacious and beautifully designed. Most importantly, the food was aesthetically appealing to look at, with a witty plating style, and DELICIOUS. I loved each and every amuse bouche, as they all had interesting flavor combinations that I've never sampled before. Definitely returning again for the impressive presentation, tastes and service.

The food was excellent, and the waiter was very polite and informative.  Cod and halibut were amazingly prepared, and the cook on the cod was perfect.  The ramps were really flavorfully prepared.  I thought the truffle and strawberry butter were lost to the strong flavor of the duck and would rate that 9/10, and the artisanal cheeses were too salty and heavy for my taste.  I'd rate that one a 6/10 (though that one would just be my tastes).  All other dishes and the canape were 10/10.  That's what earned the 5 stars, because I think the food is the most important part.  

But I got the wine pairing, and was disappointed that the sommelier seemed less than willing, especially as the night went on, to share why the food and the wine were paired.  The sommelier volunteered plenty of information about the process of making the wine, but not about what made it a good pairing for the food.  I was far more interested in the latter because it would tell me what to look out for, as a relatively inexperienced fine dining customer.  I had to ask for this information, and it seemed the sommelier was a little reluctant to answer that question at first, kind of seeming to want to leave the table before providing that explanation.  It got worse as the night went on, with the sommelier asking me why I thought the pairing was good, and saying that I could tell on my own.  I wouldn't go as far as to say it was "rude" - there were no insults or anything like that - but it was unhelpful.

All considered, I would return when the menu changes, and hope to have a different wine pairing experience, or skip the wine pairing.

One thing I notice at these Michelin starred restaurants is that the server makes the whole experience nice and delightful.

Presentation of the food was gorgeous and so flavorful. Lots of unique and interesting flavors that I didn't have while in Scandinavia.

Very memorable and excellent from beginning to end! 

For sure will be back when in NYC if they have an opening that is!

I would give 4.5 stars if I'm allowed to. It's a great restaurant, but I have some minor complaints. My partner and I ordered the tasting menu and they did not ask me how I want the duck cooked, they later gave me something that's more cooked than I expected. Despite that, the crispy skin of the duck was amazing, and I liked the course. 
The server is a nice guy, but when I left for the bathroom and left my napkin casually folded as a square, the server came and shook off the napkin in the air, and re-folded it into a neat triangle. This would have been nice if they backed off a few steps, but the server did it right at the table and my partner was still eating. It was a small table, and she found it rude for someone to shake off a large napkin right in front of her when she's eating. Then later, for one of the appetizers, my partner finished a bit earlier before me and the server attempted to take her plate away while I'm still eating. I ordered tea and the server forgot to press the lid of the teapot and the lid almost fell off. All those minor details that make us slightly uncomfortable. It was still a good experience overall, but would certainly be better if they could work on the details.
Beautiful food, Beautiful Wine, Beautiful Service.  Rare that a michelin tasting menu feels like a value.

They have two Michelin stars, but I would not be surprised if they get a third soon. This was one of the best meals we have had!

As other reviews mention, the service is phenomenal and the restaurant itself is beautiful inside with a great view of the kitchen. But the food here is really what sets this restaurant apart.

We did the 5 course tasting menu (they had an option for 7 courses which added langoustine and venison). The first bite was an amuse bouche, a smoked mackerel tart (very creamy and not at all fishy) with cup of basil seeds in a green tomato water. It sounds strange, but was delicious. It kind of reminded us of tomato basil mozzarella. They also gave us two types of bread (which is as good as everyone says in the reviews), one was a loaf with different seeds (I think pumpkin) which was nice and crunchy on the outside. The other was a dinner roll, but nicely salty and the perfect texture. Both were served warm with decadent butter.

The five courses were caviar, halibut, black sea bass, duck and dessert. The caviar course was surprisingly good, it had three types of caviar, split peas and pieces of squid. It was very refreshing and a nice combination of textures. The second course was the halibut, served with picked onions, white peaches and lingonberries. It was gorgeous to look at (looked like a bouquet of flowers) and the flavors were so light and fresh. We really enjoyed it.

The third course was black sea bass, served with a mussel hollandaise sauce and turnip. The turnip had seaweed salt and a buttery breadcrumb topping. The mussel sauce was the best hollandaise I have ever tried. We even used some of the bread to wipe the plate!

However, the best course was the duck. Extremely crispy skin on both sides with a super tender and perfectly cooked, flavorful interior. It came with a zucchini and yellow squash side which was quite enjoyable, I think it had a peach sauce on it. Dessert was the arctic bird's nest (the pictures don't do it justice, it is really a work of art, so pretty you don't want to eat it) which was very good, but a bit too sweet for me (the eggs are white chocolate with goat cheese filling). As we were celebrating a birthday, they brought out a princess cake which is a white cake with a marzipan exterior, raspberry frosting and raspberry jam in the middle. It was delicious and the perfect end to the meal.

They bring out two chocolates (with poppy seeds and elderflower) and two mango jellys as a gift from the kitchen after dessert. They also send guests home with some of their smoked sea salt.

Each course was delicious and perfectly constructed. Every ingredient was there for a reason and the flavors and textures blew our minds. We were smiling the whole meal, excited to try each course. I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a memorable and utterly delicious meal! They also have a separate bar menu for those looking for a more casual option.

Came here last night for the three-course prix fixe dinner. Excellent food and service.

Docking a star (I would give 4.5 stars if I could) only because I wish the menu had been more explicit in that the first course (we ordered halibut and venison) would be raw/almost raw. Sadly I'm not a tartare/sushi fan, though my companion loved it so I gave him my share.

For the main entree we ordered lobster and duck breast. My lobster was absolutely divine, cooked to perfection with delicious mushroom side. I tried a bit of the duck -- it was good too, excellent texture and right amount of fat.

Dessert was phenomenal! Got dark chocolate with cherries , loved that there was an interesting mixture of texture and flavors concentrated in one dessert. We are still talking about it!

We had to cancel our reservation 13 days earlier our due to a flight cancellation from our country. We understand the penalty for not showing up. But as many of us are flexible due to COVID, businesses should also be flexible and take into considerations situations that are not under the customer's control.

Dress Code: I wore brown suede dress/office shoes, dark blue jeans, a t-shirt, an a blazer and it was fine.

Wow, not only were all the dishes pretty, they tasted amazing! I really enjoyed the "tea" they first brought out. I put it in quotes because it was more of a fruit drink than tea. It was sour, in a good way, and really set the experience for me.

My favorite dish was the duck and green strawberry. The duck must have been soaked in brown sugar, I think, because the skin was not only very crispy but sweet. It really complemented the dish.

I got the additional supplement of cheeses, and It wasn't anything unique. I'd recommend you get it only if you're a cheese person in general.

Overall, I had a great experience here. The ambiance was great, the service was on point, and most importantly, the food was amazing. Check this place out!

Summary: several of the dishes in my prix fixe were disappointing and made me question Aquavit's 2-star status. My favorite restaurants in NYC are Jean-Georges and Gabriel Kreuther, which similarly have 2 stars each and I don't think Aquavit ranks among them. The dessert (Bird's Nest) was the saving grace of the meal

We ordered the following:

Lojrom supplement: this was sold to us as 'scandinavian caviar' but it tasted far closer to roe than 'typical' caviar. The waffles it came with were good, but overall this was 3/5

Matjes Herring: this was a cold dish with very salty/briney fish. This might be more of an locals/authentic type of dish but even then, I would expect to have some nuance/complexity in the flavor profile, like some fattiness to accompany the taste. But it was if I ate tough sashimi dunked in a jar of salt and it overpowered the other dressings in the dish. Again, it's fine if we were seeking to enjoy authentic scandinavian food but this was a 2-star establishment so we were expecting something more nuanced and BALANCED in taste. 1/5

Swedish meatballs (from the bar menu): frankly, did not taste much better compared what we could get at Ikea. 2/5

Diver Scallop: this was the best savory course of our meal. It had this sweet-ish, creamy corn sauce (if I remember correctly). 4/5

The 'wagyu' beef dish (which cost extra): shame on me for ordering 'wagyu' in the US (whole 'nother story... but in general all 'American wagyu' is not remotely similar to Japanese wagyu and is probably only 5-10% more marbled than a typical American steak) and at a Scandinavian restaurant but at the time it looked more compelling than the other choices. I could have cooked a better steak myself. The meat was tough, overly done, the miso sauce sucked and was uninteresting. 1/5

The dessert (bird's nest): this was INCREDIBLE. This was the saving grace of the meal for us. Not only did it look beautiful and creative, it also tasted quite good. Photo attached would speak better than whatever I could come up to describe it. 5/5

Besides the food, the service and atmosphere was exceptional. 

We walked in with high expectations and really tried to give the benefit of the doubt during the meal and it was not until afterwards that we re-assessed and realized that it was disappointing.

What a disappointment to receive special order of crawfish. Michelin restaurant with such great reputation served not freshly made crawfish but also half of it wasnt fully cooked    its shame how you handle your costumers and in same time ask to pay not small $$$ Being pregnant i really need to make sure i eat fresh and fully cooked food , so definitely didnt order seafood leftovers  which couldve affect my health and health of my baby . So in end had to throw it away to be safe.
About packaging : No utensils to open crawfish or even napkins . After taste of being scammed ,quality definitely not worth the price or your health.
Sad to say but will not recommend or come back ‼

Without a doubt, one of the best meals of our lives.  
It's no wonder they have earned 2 Michelin stars.  The service, wine pairing, presentation, attention to detail, flavors, and ingredients are second to none. 
While I can't say whether the bar menu is worth the visit, and a few other reviews have some grumbles, the Chef's 9 course tasting menu, some with multiple wine pairings per course, is 100% worth your time. 
Wine pairings truly let a sommelier strut their stuff. Knowledge of a wines linage, terroir, and quality-to-price ratio are nice, but finding funky unique wines to pair and accentuate the delicate flavors of this meal show true talent. 
We sought out special dining experiences on our trip to NYC, both in unique food, and chef's showing their talents.  Compliments to everyone working in Aquavit.  The execution of our experience was flawless. 
It's not cheap, few 2* restaurants are, and you'll have to judge for yourself if the juice is worth the squeeze, but for a special occasion, that you want everything to be perfect, look no further.

This place is like art! We came here for dinner this Friday and the service was superb and very very professional.

They have the dining room option as well as the bar dinner option. The dining room option is more formal and you get to try their tasting menu. The bar dinner option is more casual. We opted for their bar dinner option, which requires $25 per person as a down payment which goes towards your meal as part of the reservation, whereas the dinning room option requires $50 per person for down payment. 

Potato and Leek Soup - we got this as the first course and it was SOOO good. I loved how they present the ingredients in the bowl and then slowly pour the soup on it. It came with leek, chanterelles, and hazelnuts. Definitely my favorite out of the 3 courses.

Duck Confit Pot au Feu - it was so tender and soft and yet the skin was nice and crispy. It was cooked to perfection. Loved it! It came with celeriac, cremini mushrooms, and carrot.

Skate Wing "Schnitzel" - it's so soft and salty. It came with apple, capers, and trout roe.

Pumpkin Semifreddo - a lot going on in this fall dessert. It's like a party in the mouth. This is actually my second favorite out of the 3 courses. It came with salted caramel and pumpkin seed brittle, and was decorated with tiny flowers.

Cappuccino -  they have different tea and coffee options for post meal and I opted for their cappuccino. The flavor was just right and it came with a side of white and brown sugar cubes. 

I had a great time here. Will definitely be back for their dining room in the near future.

P.S.: their menus are seasonal.

Booked on Wednesday evening for Friday evening dinner. Surprised I could book so last minute, so we went with 5:45pm. 

Table for four to celebrate two birthdays at once. We got the five course tasting menu which required $50 deposit pp beforehand. 

Our servers were mainly Doug and Scott but by the end, everyone stopped by for something before. Service is excellent. Their recommendations for drinks were very spot on. They explain all the dishes upon arrival and coordinate with each other to drop off and pickup plates in unison. The timing between dishes was perfect. Nothing felt rushed nor did we have to wait long in between items. They noticed really quickly when my mom didn't like one of the dishes, so they arranged a replacement for her (which we all loved). They took care of food scraps and spillages seamlessly, but the only complaint was that there were two instances where it took more than one course's worth of time to acknowledge it. 

Interior. 
I love the simple, clean, bright design. I personally really like bench seating too. The spacing between tables was sufficient, you might hear other ppl's conversations but more as white noise. Overall volume of the restaurant was comfortable, not loud at all, can comfortably chat with your party. Depending on which direction you sit in, you can see the kitchen working. I wish I had that view. It seems quite massive and neat inside, but it'll probably distract me from my conversations. 
I like their table cloth and utensils. 
Another complaint would be the toilet. The floor was a bit wet. I also saw multiple people have issues with the lock. Even though it was locked from the inside, people can open it from the outside...? I also noticed they provide Byredo Vetyver hand wash. Smelled nice. 

Exterior
It's located on the ground floor of Park Avenue Tower. It's entrance is set back on the street with POPS seating outside which makes this location so welcoming.

-

Lastly the food. They change the menu regularly, so not much use to reference what I ate. I'm not familiar with Scandinavian food, so I can't necessarily comment on how right things are. Each dish was complex enough that I focused on enjoying it rather than dissecting its elements. 

Welcome drink, berry and apple tea. I wonder why they call it a tea rather than juice, but it was definitely refreshing and palette opening. 

Amuse bouche was a shrimp potato tart. Although small, the shrimp were so fresh. I was afraid the tart part will be stiff or boring like tortilla but it was quite flavorful. 

Fluke and cucumber
It was sashimi but it didn't bother me at all. It was refreshing and not oily at all. 

Scallop and leek 
They sliced thin pieces of scallop and radish (?) and layered them together. Upon arrival, soup like sauce was spooned into the bowl. I forgot what it was made out of but it tasted like mushrooms. There's horseradish so it gives you a healthy kick but nothing to the point where you need to drink water to take a break. 

We received bread after this. It was dense with a lot of grains, slightly a bit too salty but ok. The butter was super soft and creamy, which is surprisingly hard to come by

Halibut and trout roe. An onion puree/soup/sauce was scooped upon arrival. We actually asked for another spoonful around the table. That was a good decision because I was able to use up all that sauce. The halibut itself was tender and tasted clean. 

Beef and black garlic. 
Tbh the least favorite dish of the night. This was the one my mom frowned upon. The three pieces of beef are prepared differently. I think the middle one was stewed. It was the most tender and had some asian jerky flavor. The top and bottom ones had a strong smokey flavor. I wasn't a fan of it either but was quite intrigued by it. The potatoes had a slight sweetness. The dollop of cream on the side was too weak to balance out flavors of the beef, but it added some smoothness.

Duck. This was the replacement dish for my mom when she didn't like the beef. It might've been the best dish of the night. I think this is from the other prix fixe menu. The duck was so tender and flavorful despite tasting simple. The sauce was some plum sauce with corresponding plum. There was a log that seemed like a pumpkin mash fry. It was yummy too. 

Dark chocolate and currant dessert 
Peanut butter and jelly was the perfect description for this. My favorite part is the leaf. We all thought it was chocolate, but it was a cookie! 

Princess cake 
This was the complimentary birthday cake. I think is the least sweet and least heavy marzipan I've ever had - good thing. It wasn't exciting but just a cute touch.

Cookies 
There's a shortbread cookies and a chocolate one with coconut.

Complimentary smoked sea salt. At the end of the meal everyone got a small container of smoked sea salt that they use in the kitchen too.

Overall I truly enjoyed this experience even though it wasn't perfect. The whole package was worth the price.

Simply spectacular meal here. All the dishes had a very distinct taste and mostly seafood and and a couple of land dishes I believe. The presentation of the dishes was top notch.  I got the white truffle supplement which they shave  generously on top of the land dish. And the arctic bird nest desert - well, I've never seen anything like it. The desert is an actual birds nest. Very enjoyable meal. 

Service was excellent- all up to scooping up the crumbs and folding you napkin while you are away from tour chair.  Oh and the have a good selection of aquavits- little Scandinavian alcoholic drinks. My wife enjoyed those also.

Come here before they get their 3rd star (and the price will go up)! An amazing experience, guaranteed to leave you satisfied. 

We opted for the full tasting menu ($275 pp, before tax & tip), and got:

Tea to start.
Mini "tacos" with chanterelle, roe, and foam. Can't say what magic was in them, but they were absolutely delicious.
Shrimp tarts - which again, packed a lot of flavor into just a few bites.

We're off to a very good start!

Fluke & Cucumber Tartare - this light dish had signified the flavors of cucumber in many different ways, including the broth & pickles. I was pleasantly surprised by the portion. Refreshing.

Caviar & Langoustine - The star of the evening! Langoustine & apple tartare, with a layer of caviar on top, and a psycadelic creamy sauce poured on top. WOW.

King Crab & Cream, next to a crab dip - The softest crab I've had, with a rich cream sauce. Next to it is another plate with herbs, vegetables and the crab dip.  Served with a whole grain bread and butter (that kept on coming through the meal)

Sweetbreads & Plum - A contender to the langoustine: Smoky sweetbreads, crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, with layers of plum, and plum sauce. I already miss it.

Halibut & Trout Roe - Tender, perfectly cooked, and with strong flavors of dill.

Duck & Honeynut Squash - A modern take on duck & apple sauce, but with apple infused squash. I tried to eat it slowly so it would never end. Alas, it did.

Desserts:
Palette cleanser

Arctic Bird's Nest - an intricate dessert, filled with many flavors, each bite is different. Not too sweet. A feast of its own.

As we were celebrating a birthday, we also got a small Princess Cake.

I can't wait to come back here.

Perfection!!! The cleanest, lightest but most filling meal I have had in ages. Welcome to midtown and the sleek on point experience of aquavit! Staff is on point. From the moment you enter. Ushered to table in the updated dinning room, with a view of the kitchen and chef hard at work. This dinner is an event. This is Scandinavian so the meal is seafood focused. The only land meat was a venison carpaccio and a duck dish. Both were knock outs. Listen I could go through the menu...but why? These are chefs you can trust! Just go! And a two star Michelin restaurant at the price point is with it. Just go!

1. Staff and service: Seamless is the way I would describe the service here. The staff accommodate to your needs effortlessly. I would argue when it comes to fine dining, staff and service is more important than the taste of the food. What I enjoyed the most is how each dish was described to you either at the time of ordering or when the dish was served. No one seemed arrogant or haughty which was appreciated. I understand where the 2 Michelin stars come from.

2. Food taste/ quality: Scandinavian food is something that I rarely come across and I can say I was very happy to have experienced it here. I started off with an apple cocktail, which was one of the best cocktails I have ever had. Then warm bread starter is unlimited so ask to try both for sure, or for more if you're hungry but I would refrain as the meal is well portioned. Then an amuse-bouche broth with foie gras, which was tasty and interesting. For first I started off with a roe dish that had a creamy base that you eat with warm buttery flatbread, it was a bit strong as I don't eat much roe but I wanted to step out of my comfort zone but it was still delicious. Second I had the duck which was unique in flavor with a lingonberry reduction and roasted radicchio. It was fantastic but I loved the scallop dish more that my friend was having. Then ended with the signature birds nest dessert, which was worth the up-charge, as well as complimentary small sweets. When we  left, they also gave us smoked sea salt which was a thoughtful gesture. Cost was around $200 a person.

3. Ambiance: The ambiance here are foodies, and people who came for the experience. Not many business people or old couples. Most people were here to celebrate an occasion or for the food and it was honestly really nice that it wasn't pretentious.

4. Wait time / Reservation: Ofc no issues getting seated. We also had a member who was running a bit late, but seated us as we arrived and waited on us with drinks till we were ready. Really an exceptional experience.

Got the tasting menu with wine pairing for a 4 hour dinner birthday celebration. Some nice dishes as expected but the wine pairing was superb. It is on the expensive side but we were there for a long time and service is consistently good. Overall, definitely worth a try for the class of restaurant.

Aquavit was in my bucket list for a really long time. I finally make reservation couple weeks ahead for Saturday dinner after thanksgiving. We choose chef's tasting menu ($275 per head ). My partner said there's no other way to enjoy aquavit if it's not chefs tasting menu

When we arrived they asked if we want to add white truffle ( extra cost $230 for the 2 of us) on our duck menu. We said yes LOL 

The service is superb. The food are excellent. The sommelier helped us pick the last bottle of 2013 Valentini trebbiani d'Abruzzo ($375) its so superior 

Aquavit portion is so massive and huge I even have to ask couple of times are we don't yet ? 

Got nice smoked sea salt as parting gift 

Does it worth almost $1300 before tip for the 2 of us? YES !

We had drinks and foods to share at the bar area last week and it was so nice! The herring was perfect and delicious, amazing. We loved the meatballs too and their bread is superb! It was enjoyable evening

Promised my friend to blow up my pay check (aka going to a fancy Michelin star restaurant) with her and fulfilled my promise lol. It was in September so I don't have clear memory of the food but I do remember that I was pleasantly surprised by every single dish, even wowed by a few of them, and would definitely go back to try their new menu next time I'm in NY. The plating was also very aesthetic. I and my friends both liked their choices of plates, which enhanced the visual experience of the meal.

Three of us had dinner there last night. The food and service were excellent and, in particular, the sommelier was very knowledgeable and helpful as was the waiter. The experience, however, was ruined by the $345 upcharge for white truffles - the waiter had merely asked if we enjoyed white truffles without mentioning the $115 per person incremental charge. When we objected to this, the manager came and insisted that it was unnecessary  to mention the incremental charge and, further,  that "across the board" this had never been an issue. After a protracted and unpleasant exchange, the charge was removed. Had it not been for this incident with the manager we would have considered it a repeat event. But there are too many outstanding restaurants in this town to bother returning.

Intimate dining room, interesting dishes, and friendly staff without the stuffy-look-my-Michelin-stars atmosphere.

There are a good number of respectable restaurants (Daniel Boulud, Eleven Madison, Gabriel Kreuther, etc) in the city and so how does one go about picking a place if you want to splurge? For me, I wanted to try Nordic / Scandinavian cuisine, especially led by a female chef, Emma Bengtsson. 

Aquavit served an outstanding Nordic tea that I was really fond of, which is called honey berry tea. I could drink the whole carafe if I had the opportunity to. Shout out to the staff who actually served us the second carafe.

Back in 2014, wet-eared and wide-eyed, I added Aquavit to my giant list of NYC restaurants to try purely for the Arctic Bird's Nest dessert. Life happened, and I kept putting off coming here. Then I started traveling to Scandinavia and dining at actual award-winning New Nordic restaurants in the region, and Aquavit just seemed....superfluous.....to visit.

A friend recently reminded me of its existence, and I thought, why not? Scandinavian travel is an impossible dream right now, and what better way to make winter more bearable? 

We got the five-course tasting menu with extras and freebies:

- Flight of 3 aquavits to start (toasted rye, horseradish, lingonberry): The rye was the liquid form of their housemade rye and literally like drinking bread (in a way that beer isn't). The horseradish had us giggling like crazy because it was such a zany liquid flavor. And the lingonberry reminded me so much of Stockholm and Copenhagen, sigh.

Course #1 - Fluke and Fennel with Asian Pear: Refreshing and well-plated, but too salty. I would scale waaay back on the seasoning.

Course #2 - Scallop and Leek: A bit too pungent for my liking, but the scallop had the right texture and the vichyssoise was perfect.

Course #3 - Halibut and Trout Roe: Just pure seafood brine delectableness. My favorite course. So delicious, I forgot to take a photo of it! 

Course #4 - Wagyu Beef and Black Truffle: Our server was insistent that this was "real" wagyu beef, but I'm not quite sure that's possible in the USA. The beef was fine, as were the accompaniments, but I wasn't blown away. Know what would've been much more interesting? Venison.

Course #5 - Lemon and Tea (dessert): Scrumptious lemon tart/cake with oolong tea sorbet that was so creamy, I wasn't entirely convinced it was sorbet.

Of course, we couldn't come here without actually trying the legendary Arctic Bird's Nest Dessert, so we tacked that on for an extra $25. It was the best part of our meal, in my opinion--and so worth the hype.

If you've read my past Michelin reviews, you know I'm over that world and rarely frequent these types of restaurants anymore. One gets a bit jaded with the same molecular gastronomy / artful presentation / "Japanese influences" / French techniques, yadda yadda--and I've Michelined on all the inhabited continents. With that in mind, I absolutely think Aquavit deserves its two Michelin stars. While I wasn't blown away by every course, the phenomenal service, elegant decor, and abundance of complimentary food/drinks they surprised us with made the entire experience two-star-worthy.

Congrats, Aquavit. You made this surly curmudgeon smile.

You're never quite sure if a restaurant will live up to the hype, especially when its a place that's been on the foodie radar for many years.  

We had a surprisingly easy time getting reservations, but that may be down to lots of cancellations during NYCs recent COVID surge.  

We were fortunate then to experience this place on our first night in town.  The service was pitch perfect from start to finish.  The food as well exceeded my (high) expectations.  Lots of seasonable dishes, and a focus on "good" rather than "flashy" ingredients.  There were no courses that didn't work for me at some level.  The drink pairings were non-conventional and thoughtful (ie: I couldn't have done better myself off the wine list).  

All in all, a great experience and a great way to kick off a week-long NYC trip.

What can I say, two star Michelin rating kind of says it all. We had the tasting menu with wine paring. Mostly seafood preparations and it was a 3 hour feast!  Incredible and unique dishes of scallops, crab, fish and an amazing duck prior to an array of tasty desserts.  The wines selected were discussed and their history was elaborated upon - all were perfect matches for the dish offered. An experience in dining for sure.

Delicious Scandinavian food and a stellar wine pairing! This was my first 2 michelin star restaurant and it was definitely a great first experience. The star of the show was the Arctic birds nest for sure.

I have been here for dining and once for the outdoor cocktail experience they set up during COVID in 2020. The dinner was genuinely one of the best I've had in my life. The cocktail experience was similarly fantastic and at a very reasonable price point. I don't think I've had a single dish or amuse-bouche that was anything less than fantastic in the times I've eaten here. 

In my opinion the best restaurant in NYC. My only disappointment is that the signature arctic bird's nest dessert is no longer available a la carte!

An incredible restaurant! We came here for our anniversary and were treated to the best dinner and wine pairing ever! 

The staff was very polite and helpful from the beginning till the end of the experience. The food served was incredibly well cooked and the menu was diverse and interesting! As a note, the tasing menu changes periodically so make sure to check it online / call them before going in. 

In my opinion, the best part was the wine pairing. The options were extraordinary with a wonderful selection of rare wines from all around the world. We tasted wines we had never tasted before. 

It is a pricey restaurant, but it deserves all its Michelin stars and high price, as the service and quality are unparalleled!

Chef's Tasting Menu ($275): best *fine dining meal I've had in NYC!

Cuisine: 5/5 best food! 

Service: 5/5 everyone was very friendly though a bit slow so expect to be there for a while - we arrived at 7:15PM and left at 10:30PM

I'm still in awe of my meal from last night.  I tried two other 2 Michelin star restaurants in NYC recently, one which was good and the other which was disappointing (see my review of Daniel), and I think Aquavit has come out on top.  I'm surprised it was so easy to get a reservation. 

My favorite dishes - scallop, langoustine tartar, crab (some might call it "Soho, Tribeca, a delicious TRIFECTA"). These three dishes come out consecutively in that order and leave your tastebuds frazzled and dazzled. Also I typically do not love crab nor langoustine but wow, it's just done so well here!

I wasn't sure between the Chef's Tasting Menu and the 5 course menu, but the reviews that were raving about Aquavit tended to be the Chef's Tasting, while most reviewers who were disappointed did the 5 course. It seems the Chef's Tasting is the way to go!

Me and my boyfriend booked for valentines dinner long time ago. They called us 2 hours prior to the dinner time saying that our reservation is oversold and that we can either reschedule or change to their caviar bar for the same price( half a bottle champagne+a dozen oyster+caviar) . We were expecting a dinner for our special day and  this is what they did to us. This is definitely not a restaurant that would take its customers serious enough and plenty of other restaurants in NYC would at least be able to achieve that. I'm very disappointed at this restaurant and would not recommend it to my friends.

Had the chef's tasting menu. Would say it was one of the most memorable experience in nyc with my friends. I don't normally have Scandinavian food, but this is worth a try. Felt like the best dish was the dessert. Definitely recommend!

We visited Aquavit's bar room for dinner and it did not disappoint!  We were seated immediately upon arriving, and our servers were friendly and offered great recs.

The food was stellar all around.  We tried a few of the appetizers.  The standout was the shrimp skagen toast--the topping is light and citrusy, which is a perfect contrast to the very buttery brioche underneath.  It's almost like a lobster roll.  The gravlax is solid.  It's fresh and topped with a nice mustard sauce, but not quite as flavorful as the toast.  The only dish that let us down was the hamachi crudo.  The fish was a bit fishy, and the sauce didn't really shine.  We tried two mains.  The Arctic char was perfectly cooked and the sauce is so rich it's almost like eating movie theatre butter.  And the Swedish meatballs were similarly well cooked and came with the traditional accoutrements.  We then ended with their signature Bird's Nest dessert which is so beautiful to look at and just as fun to eat.  It's not on the bar menu but they do serve it there!

The drinks were equally impressive.  The high seas is like a cold version of glögg, with a side of sweet ice to give you some control over how sweet the drink is and how cold you want it.  The gillis grafstrom is definitely spirit-forward with a hint of dill.  However, we really enjoyed the aquavit tasting trio--each of the unique macerations really came through (especially the horseradish), and they even gave us a bonus aquavit to try.

The last item to mention is the seating area.  There are a number of two-tops by the bar (which also has some seating), and the area is dimly lit and minimalist in decor.  It's perfect for a date night.  Definitely worth a visit!
I haven't try something this amazing for a very long time, almost every dish have a great balance and an iconic palate of taste that is hard to forget.

So so disappointed. Not a 2 star, not a 1 star, barely average among New York restaurants. We sat  in the bar and ordered the abbreviated menu (like we have done at 11 Madison Park, Le Bernardin, Per Se, etc) We entered to an odd trio of staffers  loitering around the hostess station who failed to properly greet us . Next up was an uninformed and unhelpful "server" who we initially believed to be the busboy bc he barely said a word to us, after bringing the bread basket and herring trio, he didn't check on us for 30 min. We finally had to flag him down to bring the next course. It was now 10pm and not at all busy. Herring trio meh, served with cubes of a decent cheese and unseasoned boiled small potatoes. Nothing elevated or special about this dish. Swedish meatballs surprisingly flavorless gravy, the char cooked correctly but drowned in  a watery horseradish sauce. Just not even in the same universe of service, attention to detail or cooking we had enjoyed even at the superb 1 star Tempura Matsui earlier that day. It's an insult to the countless other restaurants in NY with better food and to the outstanding waitstaff they employ that this place has been given the  2 star distinction.

Absolutely phenomenal execution.

Started with shrimp skagen toast and hamachi crudo. Both fairly simple dishes but just so on point. The flavors and textures were just right. The flavor in the shrimp skagen toast honestly surprised me with richness and depth. The hamachi crudo was clean but not particularly noteworthy. Cod for the main was good, but left room for the masterpiece. The Arctic Birds Nest. Truly worth the hype. The combinations of flavors, textures, colors, temperatures. It's masterful and I'd come back just for that if it were an option.

Before anything gets thrown at me for docking a star, just want to say that the place / service / FOOD were definitely 5 stars and an amazing experience. I am grateful, if you decide upon this you really won't find anything like this anywhere.

The presentation and pairing of the food was impeccable. Really beautiful plating that my friend and I did not hesitate to take as many pictures as possible. There is also a bone broth not pictured that was really out of this world and flavorful. I especially loved the truffles with beef and one dessert with a peach sorbet and candies. The salmon too was also cooked just right.

My reasons for docking a star:

1. Price. I understand that the main courses include those pricier ingredients (uni, truffles); but we were charged $25 for a glass of wine that I later found in a grocery store for $12 and that last picture of the little cookies/chocolate cost us an additional $40? It felt very scammy.

2. I love, love uni. I have tried many uni around New York, but safe to say this uni was just okay? Really good uni has depth and tastes like the best parts of the ocean - I didn't get that vibe from this one. 

Despite this, I recommend trying If you have the time, money, and occasion (hahaha). The staff were the nicest and I felt like a princess here (HAHAHA)

Not worth it. The service was excellent from our servers, but the manager stopped by every table but ours. The main chef awkwardly avoided our table after talking to others but may have done this purposefully to target those doing the full tasting. We elected to do the 5-course and a few of the dishes fell flat and some too rich and not well balanced. The tasting of the root vegetable broth was amazing. The gravlox was meh. The sea bass dish broth was good but the bass itself was just not something I wanted to eat more of. The uni with duck egg was great but too rich overall. The cod was meh. The duck was meh like it had been sitting out for awhile and also not properly seasoned (duck I've made with just salt tastes much better). dessert was good. Ordered the bird's nest which was visually stunning. I came here on the advice of a friend who dined here twice in one week because it was so good. She's obviously not from New York, so not sure why I listened to her. I won't return unless it's for the bar menu since it's inexpensive. The white wine choices were all terrible. I tasted several of them. The servers, again, were all great and knowledgeable. It wasn't a bad experience. The ambiance is nice but I will not return to the dining room. Food just didn't taste good. The one dish that was good was the initial snack size serving of their root vegetable broth. The uni dish was next but the whole dish was overall too rich.

They have also raised prices recently. The tasting was $175 pp by itself when I thought it was $135 or $155. The addition of drinks (terrible wine selection) added up the bill. Bird's nest also increased from $20 to $25 but that was actually worth it in terms of presentation. Overall, the reason I wouldn't come back to the dining room because the food just didn't taste great. Presentation was all good, and it's clear there's innovation they change the food frequently. The story behind the chef is impressive, but it's not enough for me to fork over $700+ dollars again.

An unbelievable dining experience top to bottom. I did the 8 course chefs tasting menu with wine pairings, and every dish was stellar. Most of the time, even with Michelin restaurants, there's a clunker here and there, but not at Aquavit. I loved how seafood forward the menu was, and I loved each of the hot and cold presentations. Standouts were the king crab, the langoustine, the Arctic char, and anything where they used caviar. The arctic birds nest is the most beautiful dessert I've eaten. Food wise this is easily a three star experience, but the lack of over the top pageantry and choreography is probably what keeps Aquavit at 2 star status. I do think dish for dish my meal here was better than the standard 8 course menu at per se, so take that for whatever that's worth. 

Service was outstanding, and I only had two hours, but they were able to get through the entire 8 course (which is realistically 11-12 courses) in that amount of time. I'd probably skip the wine pairing next time, but for my first time there it was a really fun addition to the experience. If you're in NYC and enjoy seafood/fine dining, I cannot recommend Aquavit highly enough!

Go for the Chef tasting menu. I was debating between the 2 menu and was glad I went with it. 

The first impression was so so mainly because we went to Le Bernardin 2 days before. The dinning room and the setting wasn't impressive but I didn't expect it to be on par since Aquavit doesn't have the same Michelin star. 

However the food blew me away and I would recommend to anyone. The taste on it's own of the overall courses are better than all the 3 star Michelin restaurants. However if I were to go for the overall experience including the service, I would still go for the 3 star ones. 

Here is what I think of each dish

3/5 - amuse-bouche which is smoked salmon on a thin flat bread. It was ok but didn't wow me. At that time I was getting worried if this place is as good as I have heard 

5/5 bass and strawberry - I felt better and wow by this dish. Very light and refreshing with a little hint of spice. Love the crunchiness and the texture. Remind me of the fish salad in Thailand but more complex

6/5 scallop and carrot - this is our favorite. Fresh and melt in my mouth

5/5 Caviar and langoustine- another dish with texture and depth. 

5/5 crab - 2 ways of crab dishes. The first one is warm in the brown. It's lightly cook and melt in my mouth. The other bite is on the crab shell. It's lighter than the warm one. 

4/5 Black cod - first savory dish - it is very good. I just had other back code dish that is better

4.5/5 lamb - it's also berry good but nothing authentic that would stand out from the other high end restaurants 

5/5 Rhubarb cleansing plate - I'm back to wow again. By that time I was getting full and had some saltiness in my mouth from the butter in the cod and salts from the lamb. This mini dish was refreshing and i was ready for the star of the course which is the next course 

6/5 the bird nest- the chef should have got an award from coming up with this. It should be in the food museum. Every thing on the dish was no short cut and very creative. The white chocolate was smooth and not too sweet. The sorbet complimented the overall dish as well

Tea service was ok. Could have been better if served in a high end cup and setting. 

Overall Aquavit is the best value of all the Michelin star restaurants in NYC

I love this place! I've been here before and have had wonderful service and delicious meals every time. The food truly embodies the Norwegian heritage it strives to showcase. Today (4/18/22) is the first day they reopened for lunch. Lunch dining is open 12-2pm and offers a 2 or 3 course menu.

Aquavit has been a beacon of creative Nordic cuisine for decades, to the point that many New Yorkers might take the restaurant for granted.  But rather than coast on its longstanding reputation, chef Emma Bengtsson -- one of the most lauded chefs in the country -- and her exceptional team continues to push for new heights in terms of food, service and experience.  

The space is clean and modern, and the staff is exceptional -- everyone working on the night we were there, from the bussers to the soms -- seemed genuinely happy to be working at Aquavit.  The enthusiasm runs from top to bottom, making for that rare combination of elevated and fun.

We went for the chef's tasting menu, and the sommelier recommended an $80 (!) riesling that was insanely delicious.  He also poured two tastes of Rhones for us to choose from for our meat course.  All in all, exceptional wine service, and again delivered by a guy who clearly loves his job and sharing stories and leaving you educated about the wines you're drinking.  No pretense, just joy.

The food is a progression of clean and beautiful and completely realized courses.  Not a dud in the bunch.  Highlights include bass with green strawberry, sevruga caviar with langoustine, crab and sunchoke, and the epic "Arctic Bird's Nest" dessert.  A visit from Chef Emma was so special -- warm and welcoming and, I have to suspect, proud.  The meal leaves you awash in tastes and happiness and -- rare for a big-time tasting menu -- not feeling bloated or too full.  It's perfect.

Bottom line, if you are looking for a two-star Michelin experience that is not about affectation but is absolutely about great food, equally excellent service and a really fun night out, here's your place.

Perhaps the best fine dining restaurant I've been to in New York (yes, better than EMP, Bernardin, and Per Se). Had the Chef's Tasting menu (the pricier  one).

Absolutely stunning. Nearly every course was creative and delicious. Very focused on seafood, with some fun things with vegetables happening too. The caviar and langoustine combination was confidently luxurious. Don't get me started on the Arctic Bird's Nest, a dessert plate of so many things that I don't exactly remember. If you're vegetarian I'm sure they'll deliver a great meal, but I can't see it being on par with the pescatarian experience.

The only dish that I found underwhelming was a seemingly perfunctory "lamb and lettuce" - deboned rack of lamb served with cabbage-wrapped steak and charred lettuce head (the latter element was the best one on that plate). I dare say you should just tell the restaurant that you are pescatarian, if only so you can stick to what Aquavit does best. Everything was so good that this one course can't knock a star off for me.

There are two tasting menus offered: one for $225 after tip/tax, and another for $354 after tip/tax. Comparing the two, you are seriously doing yourself a disservice if you don't get the pricier one, as the most memorable dishes I had were exclusive to that "chef's tasting." If you can afford to spend $200+ on dinner, an extra $100 shouldn't break it for you.

Had some of the cocktails as well, which are similarly expensive but damn good.

I was looking for a Michellin Star restaurant in NY and this 2 star place was recommended to me. It costs $25/person to reserve a seat at the bar, but the restaurant was not packed when we went on a Saturday night, so they were able to seat us at a regular table, and the reservation money covers the cost of the meal. 
The interior design of the restaurant was very nice, with high ceilings and good lighting that gives it a romantic vibe. The service was great as well, checking in frequently for water refills and very respectful. They have three individual bathrooms which is nice, but surprisingly weren't the cleanest with quite a bit of trash and liquid on the bathroom floor. 

We started with the Nordic bread, which was average. The crust is crispy and the inside was soft, and comes with a warmed salted butter. I'm not sure if I could fully distinguish this from Cheesecake Factory bread without the butter. Unfortunately, Cheesecake Factory bread is complimentary and the  bread herewas about $10. 

Next was the herring trio. It was cut in pieces and served in 3 different spices/sauces. This was very delicious, with the right amount of saltiness, and  tasted great by itself or in any combo with the potatoes, cubed cheese, and crackers it came with. (~$25)

As someone who prefers vodka over whiskey or rum, I had to try the infused Aquavit. There's a variety of flavors and you can order a flight of 3 different flavors. It pairs well with most of the dishes, and goes down very smoothly and warms the back of your throat without feeling too much "burn". 

For the main course, I had the arctic Char, which was very savory and had a buttery sauce and dill that went very well with the fish, which had a crispy skin without being dry. (~$40)

Unfortunately we also had the Australian Wagyu ($58) and the Swedish Meatballs ($35). If you were expecting the Wagyu to melt in your mouth you will be disappointed. The umami sauce was solid but the meat was a bit chewy and overcooked and didn't completely absorb and/or go together well with the sauce. The Swedish meatballs don't look too different from Ikea meatballs. 

Lastly, for dessert I had the Arctic Bird's Nest. This dish to me was the star of the show mostly for the presentation. So much detail go into making it into a work of art, and it's hard to believe that every piece is edible, goes together well and is not too sweet. The egg is made of a frozen yogurt, sprinkled with some powdered sugar, and the nest is made of white chocolate, surrounded by edible flower petals. 
We also had a chocolate coffee mousse, which had a natural and strong coffee flavor, but was a bit too sweet and pales in comparison to the bird's nest. 

Overall, some dishes  (Arctic Bird's Nest, Arctic Char, Aquavit) were truly amazing and some of the best I've seen and tasted. The rest was lackluster and not entirely deserving of the high price they charge in my opinion.

I assume Michelin Stars were awarded to this restaurant for ambience and service.  Both are great. Food was meh. Maybe Nordic cousin is just not for me. I am not a fan of bland food. 
My husband and I went there for lunch. I started with HERRING SAMPLER. For some reason I expected delicate, fatty, melt in your mouth Herring Ivasy. It was not that. It was "fat free" kind that you can buy at any grocery store. It was in three different sauces. And I liked the orange one. I went well with the side potato. But neither sauce changed the taste or texture of the actual herring. Sauces and the herring were separate from each other even though they were mixed together. I was so disappointed that I had to insist on going for dinner to the Samovar restaurant near by where I could finally get great herring that I was dreaming about. 
My husband had GRAVLAX as his first course. I tasted it and did not feel any horseradish as it was stated in the menu. It was a mix of tiny shrimps with mayonnaise on brioche. Neither tiny shrimps no mayonnaise are particularly flavor reach. Mixing them together did not change that. I would recommend the chef to be more courageous with horseradish. 
Then I had ARCTIC CHAR. Again, salmon in creamy sauce, and tastes just like salmon in heavy cream would, basically - meh. Same with ICELANDIC COD ordered by my husband. But, to be fair, cod in itself has no taste. It takes on flavors of what it is prepared in. And, if it is mostly cream, there is not much flavor to absorb. 
For desert my husband had CARROT CAKE. He said that it was good. Carrot cake is not my thing and I did not taste it. I had PRINCESS CAKE. Took just one bite. Sponge cake part of it was bone dry. Jam and mascarpone cream layered between did not soak through and the cake just did not come together. So, for someone like me, a person seriously afflicted with a sweet tooth, to push a cake away, it has to really be not worthy of calories. Cocktails were good. I asked for Negroni and Side Car - no complains. My husband had infused vodka. He said that it was not typical 40%, maybe 35%, but he liked it anyway. Tea was also good. To bad I did not have a cake to go with my tea.
Overall, this restaurant did not have much Michelin about its food - no "molecular" methods of food preparation, no inventive combinations of ingredients, etc. But, it works for a filling meal in a nice environment with good service. Just don't order a Princess Cake and go to the Samovar if you want some good herring.

We sat at the bar and had one of the best meals ever. I can't praise Aquavit enough. We started with "Through the Woods" cocktails. Then we had the chilled pea soup, cod, spetzle, and then for dessert chocolate tart and marzipan cake. We finished the meal with two individual Pear/Vanilla infused Aquavits. Everything was top notch, with the cod being my favorite. The restaurant itself is beautiful, Scandinavian modern. Highly recommended.

A thoroughly amazing experience. Came here for a meal to celebrate, and the service, food, ambience and overall meal was fantastic.

The amuse bouche with the pine nuts and trout roe was the perfect teaser. The next couple of seaweed courses, including the caviar (paired so well with the gratin) were amazing. Finally, the signature dessert was delightful to eat. The meal finished with some chocolate truffles, caramels, and a souvenir of some smoked sea salt.

We also had some wine, and the sommelier was extremely knowledgeable (if a bit exuberant). When we were unsure of what dessert wines to pair, he proposed a flight which was the perfect choice (also pretty affordable, relatively speaking.)

Volume was great as well, without needing to raise your voice to converse, but also not too quiet as to make things awkward.

Overall, highly recommend!
So tasteful and well composed with wine! It was a fantastic experience, both food and drinks.
The chef tasting menu is simply amazing. Also try some of the homemade aquavit. And take your time you'll be there for 2 1/2 hours it's wonderful.

Food quality, ambiance, service, creativity and quantity was plentiful for the prix fixe meal. The only thing I wish they didn't have to do was use Tock reservations and charge an upfront cost of 100, which I believe was not used against the bill. They gave us the smoked salt, which is phenomenal

Really great dining experience for my boyfriends birthday. The service was flawless and of course food was all delicious. Heavy on seafood so be prepared for that but some of the freshest and best I've ever had. And of course the artic birds nest lives up to the hype!
Best experience ever.  I think the pictures speak for themselves.  The food was delicious, they were nice and kind, and it smoothed over a pretty rough day for the both of us.

Amazing amazing! Took the fiance here for a birthday lunch experience and was really happy we made it. Everything we ordered was a hit and delicious, from the herring sampler to the toast skagen (added the caviar); the cod and arctic char were absolutely amazing and the desserts were light, fruity and unique (princess cake and rhubarb profiterole)

The service was incredible and overall experience was a delight. Thank you Aquavit for having us!

I had the chief's tasting menu pair with wines. The foods were delicious and well prepared! The service was outstanding . At the end on my request they sent me a shot of aquavit . This was the worst drink I had for that night ! But even this was a very pleasant experience !

4.5. Very pleasant lunch at Aquavit. After being underwhelmed by a number of Michelin starred places (Le Bernardin and EMP) and beginning to feel jaded by NY food scene Aquavit delivered today. The atmosphere was very chill and relaxed. The room is not huge and about half the tables were empty on a Wednesday. The servers were attentive, refilling water, getting us what we need and offering excellent suggestions, especially the house made Aquavits which I had never had before. High Seas cocktail was great, I'd actually recommend stopping in to the bar here for cocktails and just trying some dishes if the course price is out of range for you.

The services is excellent and the gift of roast salt is a nice touch to end the meal. Everything was presented nicely and if you like Nordic cuisine the Food experience may be very enjoyable as well. I'm not used to this types of cuisine thus I find many of the dishes such as the cold fish difficult to eat. The preserve vegetables are too sour and the bread was not tasty. The desserts were great!

Tried the Chef's Tasting Menu ($275/pp, gratuity not included) on 7/23/22.

Got in at 5:30pm when service started, paid our bill at 8:15pm - 2 hr 45 min for the entire experience, but we took it really slow and had multiple discussions with the sommelier (A++ use of my time, more on him later). I think 2:15-2:45 would be a reasonable time estimate.

The menu does change frequently (as of writing on 7/27, the lamb has already been switched to wagyu beef), but tonight was 2 amuse-bouche, 5 seafood-forward courses, 1 lamb course, 1 palate cleanser, the signature, inimitable Arctic Bird's Nest dessert, and various bonbons. I intentionally didn't do any research on the individual courses themselves and I'm glad I didn't so that I could see each one and make my own opinions, so I won't provide too much of a breakdown, and I'm only attaching a picture of the Arctic Bird's Nest since everyone has already seen that one :)

The food is great, but everyone knows that. Where Aquavit exceeded for me was the service, specifically the details. Chairs are pulled out and pushed in for you by the hostesses, complimentary champagne is poured when you are first seated, dishes are served and taken away by multiple wait staff members who work seamlessly as a team, napkins are replaced/folded if you get up to use the restrooms, and probably even more little things that I didn't even consciously consider, but the professionals know add up to enhance the entire experience.

There are two service members in particular who absolutely made our night. Unfortunately, I don't have names, but I'm confident they do their jobs so well that anyone could pick them out. The first was our first server of the night, who took the time to have a real conversation with us (contents redacted, but it was awesome to feel like we had an instant friend on staff), checked in with us multiple times throughout the night to see if we needed anything. Absolutely zero sense that he wanted to do anything else with his night except be of service to us as much as we wanted. The second was the night's sommelier, whose passion for his craft was evident from the first time  he stopped at our table. He had an immediate recommendation for my partner that ended up being a huge hit (a really uniquely served cocktail), and turned my very nebulous request for wine into a glass of white that I enjoyed immensely. He stopped by a few more times throughout to see if we needed more drinks (especially notable before the lamb course in case I wanted a red) - neither of us did, but I hinted that I'm a big fan of dessert wine - like clockwork, he was back before the palate cleanser, bringing out 3 dessert wines and effusively describing all of them. When I chose one, he poured a sip for my partner as well - perfect touch. My only disappointment of the night was that I couldn't try a sip of all 3!

A small smoked sea salt container is given to you with the check, which I'll be using when cooking fish to give myself a taste of Aquavit again at home. Chef Bengtsson has the food figured out at Aquavit and her team has the service nailed as well, I'd recommend Aquavit to anyone in NYC looking for a night where everything will be just perfect!

It's been a while that we went fine dining due to covid concerns. 
It was an 8 course chefs tasting and everything on the menu was spectacular. The mock drink options were great too. We were educated on the supply. Gap time between dishes were a wait but I can see why based on presentation. We weren't full but definitely content.

2.5 Stars (more could be better than OK) - Rating it against what the price they charge should provide.  

In summary, a lack of attention to detail and mistakes drive this rating.

Not rating this on food because taste is rather subjective and all the dishes were just fine.  None of them terribly remarkable one way or the other, except for the Bird's Nest dessert.  

That dessert is in a league of its own, from complication, to artistry, taste, uniqueness, etc.  It really is special.

Now to the rating/experience, i.e. why not 5 stars

The dining room/location - Ground floor of a rather ho-hum office building providing a rather nondescript space to dine

Upon entering we were greeted by a gross dark grey commercial rug runner (with ~1" plastic border) covering the steps/wood floor.  It's not even fitted to the stairs or customized in any way.  More akin to something you'd pick up from a Grainger or Tractor Supply store.  It wasn't raining out either.

While being escorted to our table by a very pleasant host, someone in the kitchen dropped a bunch of plastic containers, well dropped some and caught some before they hit the floor but the commotion disturbed an otherwise quiet setting.

Bathroom to wash hands.  Tissue box empty (which a guest also mentioned after we left) and noticed screw cap covering the bolt holding toilet to floor was missing, leaving a rather unsightly/gross bolt contrasted against the white porcelain exposed.

Table ordered drinks, one was a can of beer.  Upon opening, server somehow actually got some on the couch, floor, and table.  He did not seem to know how to actually pour a beer into a glass (Shockingly amateurish)...weird.

With each new serving came an opportunity to (re) set the table and each time neither the knife or fork placed in front of me were straight or square to table edge.  They were placed down with care and attempt made to align nicely but each time they were off.  OCD'ish I know.

I finished my first drink and it was removed from the table without being asked if I'd like another or something else.  Maybe this is proper (I don't know) but seemed wrong having me to trouble a server to ask for another drink.

One of the dishes was a perfectly round stack of some good fish (Cod, if memory serves) that was topped with many dime sized round green slices.  You can tell each was placed with care around the edge in an attempt to show uniformity around the top but that went awry part way through where can tell a couple weren't placed evenly like all the others.

One server brings food wearing a mask but it's pulled down exposing his nose, yet covering mouth.  The unshaven face with a mask pulled down below nose create a relatively slovenly look for him.

Same server explained what the dish was, unintelligible.  We thanked him and when he left I asked if anyone knew what the dish was and no one did.

Kitchen is an open style with windows allowing you to look at the action.  This is nice but when you look over to see gloveless chefs (which I am OK with) scratching the back of their neck or just under their beard, it's not so nice.

Throughout the experience a tiny fly or two would show up occasionally causing my guests to waive their hand over the table in an attempt to get the flies enhance someone else's dining experience.

Not a place to avoid by any means but if you're particular and have higher expectations, given the cost and rating, lower them.

When I booked the only time available was 8:30 at a seat by the bar.  That seat was around the corner of the bar facing a wall, and to the right was around the corner of the bar with only a view of the ugly end of the bar and a wall. I didn't complain but since there was many tables open in the beautiful dining room I assumed this was a "special place" for late diners. I also guess they don't offer the tasting menu to late diners. 
Anyway my server for the first course was informative and charming. I loved the first course! Trio of herrings. My second course was cod with capers and beans. While the cod was nice the tiny cut of the almost raw beans made them impossible to fork elegantly, particularly considering the whole thing was floating in oil. 
At this point my server had disappeared and after a 15 minute wait a different server took my dessert order. Which was a delicious princess cake. 
My wrap on this is don't go late, don't be sat in the bar area and don't order the cod floating in oil, beans and capers. 
I will go back if I can book early seating in the dining room and am sure it will be superb and get the 5 stars I wish I could have given it.

My wife and I have been going here for years, we first stumbled onto it during a restaurant week and since then we have dined there several times at different levels and had food catered for special events as a service they have provided for holidays like Thanksgiving. The food is always great, the drinks are great, the service is great. I can honestly say that they have never disappointed me.

Gotta admit I knew nothing about Scandinavian cuisine before eating here and tend to prefer BIG flavors like Thai and Indian. But I try not to miss an opportunity to sample a Michelin started restaurant and this did NOT disappoint. We had the Chefs Tasting Menu. Every single dish was absolutely consistently delicious. Service excellent. Atmosphere modern and elegant. I look forward to our return.

Took one of my favorite people here for a very belated birthday dinner. We were both early, and had a cocktail at the bar - no one grabbed us to tell us that our table was ready - because Aquavit doesn't rush the clientele, they let us leisurely enjoy our drink (princess peach is a nice fruity starter rum cocktail), and when we realized we were a few minutes over our reservation time, we went to the hostess podium, and they immediately directed us to our very comfortable half-circle booth table, without having to deal with a separate check. The bartender just asked if we would like to add the drinks to our dinner bill, I agreed, and it was that simple.

We had the Chef's tasting, with the non alcoholic pairing, and truffle supplement, and while it didn't seem like a lot of courses, we were both completely stuffed after we finished dinner.

High Seas Cocktail: gin, wolfamer, citrus granita - a tiny dish of granita is meant to be tasted between sips of the beverage, and then poured in when melted - fun, and delicious!

Amuse Bouche(s): cucumber and smoked roe tart & cucumber water with chamomile oil - this heralded the start of a brilliant dinner, smoky yet fresh, the tart was a mouthful of happiness, and the cucumber "water" was anything but watery, it was a little spicy, rich, and almost meaty.

pre-dinner starter: I can't remember the details, but it was sliced radishes, and a creamy smoky fish on a chewy arepa sized flatbread, lovely, but completely overshadowed by the tart that preceded it.

Fluke and Elderflower: delicate and refreshing, a beautiful way to start the actual courses

Char and Pluot - loved the contrast of the tart plums with the smoky flaky fish - I might need to start adding plum slices to my bagels and lox

Caviar and Langoustine - everyone goes for the bird nest dessert, but this was the highlight of dinner for us, absolute perfection, the charred corn brought out the sweetness of the langoustines, and the caviar teased out briny flavors. Will be dreaming about this. Our server Sean was right, this was definitely a treat.

King Crab and Chanterelles: sea buckthorn hollandaise, puffed rice - the crispy rice was a great contrast to the creaminess of the hollandaise and the rich tender king crab

Cod and Summer Squash: butter poached cod, marinated zucchini, pickled squash, squash puree, citrus beurre blanc - we found this dish a tad too salty for our personal palates alone, but it paired very well with the Bax Botanics, sea buckthorn, lemon and thyme mocktail - and the mini sliced loaf of nutty rye and cultured butter. I don't even like rye, and I had a second slice.

Wagyu and Rosehip: gem lettuce, chanterelles, potato, cabbage terrine, with rosehip and onion purees - topped with truffle supplement - beautiful dish, but I have to admit, I was too full to truly appreciate this. The chanterelles and cabbage terrine were exquisite. I didn't love the beet beverage pairing when I tasted it beforehand, so Catherine kindly brought out another drink that she thought I might prefer despite my protestations that it was unnecessary. The cherry drink she brought was wonderful, but I have to admit that when I tried the beet drink after a bite of the wagyu - it brought out so much sweetness that I understood why it had been paired with the wagyu to begin with.

Pre-Dessert krumcake cone filled with creme fraiche sorbet and peach compote - I don't know why, but I adore bite sized cones, and the peach compote just made this the perfect summer pre-dessert
