Arctic Bird's Nest: goat cheese parfait eggs, sea buckthorn curd, blueberry sorbet, yogurt "snow", chocolate branches, honey tuile, halwa, edible flowers and berries - this dessert lives up to the hype. Complex, rich, sweet, but not saccharine - with pops of tartness, I felt like a wood nymph enjoying the joys of nature (says girl who abhors bugs and camping). This was served with a wonderful soba tea from Kettl in our own individual pots - which had a deep grain flavor that was almost savory and paired wonderfully with the dessert.

As if two desserts were not enough, a little box of tiny bites are also brought out, we had mustard caramels (I put this in my friend's bag for later and forgot it!!!!) bon bons, pate de fruit, and pepper short bread.

Truly exemplary service, beautiful and delicious dishes, definitely one of my top 10 meals of all time. So many little touches like the complementary finishing salt gift, a copy of the printed menu, the surprise princess cake for my friend's birthday, even the bathroom soap being Byredo made this meal an experience and not just a dinner. Every step of the meal was beautifully orchestrated, and the service was an absolute joy. They change the menu regularly, so I'm definitely going to go broke bringing other loved ones here. Not sure how I'll top this for the friend I already brought though!

Gone downhill. Aquavit used to be world class but has now lost its spark. 
I will caveat that we dined in the bar area having eaten in the main dining room many times but prior to 2019.

To start with, our waiter lacked any enthusiasm and insight. Did not provide any opinion or views of the menu (despite asking) and just overall made this dinner a dull experience.

Aquavit does not compare at all to other two Michelin star restaurants such as Jungsik, Daniel or Jean Georges.

The food looks aesthetically pleasing but lacks depth and is mostly bland. 

The cod schnitzel was so bland and dull it was basically inedible. The wagyu strip tasted as if it was boiled and lacked any sear. It definitely was not seasoned.
In addition, the Bordeaux came ice cold. 

None of the desserts looked appealing. Such a shame because our experience from years gone by was so positive.

Will not be coming back.
Had a fantastic cocktail tasting experience led by Liza at the bar. They realized I was celebrating my birthday and made it extra special. Would recommend to anyone!
We had a good experience at Aquavit. We enjoyed the Scandinavian twist of the menu. Food was tasty, but salty for our standards. reasonable wine list.

Such an unforgettable meal, 5/5. Experiences like these remind me why I love trying out different Michelins around the city - it shows you how beautiful cooking is. It's truly an art. 

First off, the reservation policy is super forgiving. I made a reservation months ago and couldn't make it due to an emergency that popped up and called about 10 min before our reservation to let them know. I expected to just eat the $50pp deposit, but the hostess told me I could apply the deposit towards a future reservation. Thus, I ended up making a new reservation for my boyfriend's birthday and couldn't be happier that I did. 

We did the 5-course tasting menu and I thought the entire meal was incredibly well-balanced in flavor. Aquavit celebrates all the ingredients used, balancing the sweet, savory, and citrusy flavors. The fluke and elderflower was definitely my favorite; as a tomato enthusiast, I thought the tomatoes paired beautifully with the tender fish. I was caught off guard by the char and pluot dish because I didn't expect to find all the yummy, smoky fish under the tarte plums. The duck was the perfect end to the savory courses, and I loved the plum in the dessert course. Aquavit even brought out a mini birthday cake for my boyfriend - such a thoughtful touch! 

This place is so well-deserving of its 2 Michelin stars.  I appreciated the thoughtfulness and creativity behind each dish, contrary to just throwing a bunch of caviar or foie gras on the plate and calling it a day. Service was top-notch and I loved how brightly-lit the interior was. I would love to come back to try the winter / fall menus.

One of my favorite restaurants! Not only was the service impeccable they tell you the story behind each course if you decide on the tasting menu. The food was delicious and fulfilling. The bar area was also nice! I will be back again

When I visit NYC and want to pamper myself, I go to Aquavit. Done it for at least 20 years. This week was no different. They offer a set meal at lunch although you can order à la Carte. As their name implies Aquavit is front and center. I chose the 3 flight. Two savory. Anise and caraway and wasabi. I had the sweet lingonberry for the third one

The starter was a king crab salad with fennel root and sliced kohlrabi with a meyer lemon sauce. The main was Arctic Char with pickled pear and cauliflower and ikura (salmon eggs). The third course was a selection of cheeses with Nordic crackers. 

As usual the flavors were very Nordic and clean and the overall meal was incredibly satisfying. I had a business appointment 4 blocks away and it truly set me up for that task. 

An always excellent experience.

Nice meal and space, service is not super personal or warm but not bad by any means. Dishes had great presentations, not all were hits but all were tasty. Not a super long tasting menu but filling. The birds nest dessert is a highlight. Definitely worth a stop to try some great Nordic food
Amazing experience. Attention to detail, taste, presentation. Loved every dish and will be back next time we're in NYC. SO good!

The place is beautiful. The plating is beautiful. The service is phenomenal. Tried the 8 course menu and felt overall it lacked something. There were interesting dishes and a few I could do without. The flavors were there and some even unexpected. In the end I wish there was another dish or two to somehow tie in the entire menu more and give my palate the wow factor I was craving.

Had a delicious lunch at Aquavit yesterday that left me yearning to come back for the dinner tasting menu.  Top notch service.  Delicious food, with each dish having an interesting twist from what I'm used to.  Started with the butternut squash soup - disliked the soup at first, but really enjoyed it after mixing the broth with the goat cheese and butternut squash pieces at the bottom of the bowl.  Loved the arctic char which came in a delicious, creamy sauce.  Enjoyed the cheese plate for dessert, but also tasted my husband's princess cake and thought it was delicious.  I will definitely return!

My husband joked that if you can't afford to go here, you should go take out a loan and come anyway . Not only was the food immaculate, but the service was absolutely outstanding. The staff was informative, friendly, and professional, helping in all ways possible. I was surprised to see that the crowd dressed more on the casual side - but perhaps that's the NY way!
Food was mediocre. Service was great. Honestly the most disappointed tasting I've had with aquavit so far. The duck was bland, best part of the whole meal was probably the beets on the duck dish.
The best fine dining in NYC to me. We loved the serve and the wine pairing very much. Highly recommend to have the desert...so good!

Very well deserving of its Michelin 2 stars.

The atmosphere speaks to its low key but classy vibe. The staff are very pleasant And accommodating, it was a lovely experience overall. 

The food was a combination of innovative and traditional - each bite had a mountain of flavors combined and I loved each dish I got. I was in love with most of their dishes. The foie gras was creatively frozen and spread over a Granny Smith apple salad. I won't go into each dish because they were all fantastic. The lamb was ok - I think every other dish hit so strongly that even though it was done finely (medium rare), it just did not have as strong of an impact as the other dishes. All in all, I would come back for another seating with friends/family!

This review is based on sitting in the bar area. I would overall give it a 3.5. 
Ambiance: 5
Food & Drinks taste & presentation: 3.5-4
Selection: 3.5
Service: 3.5
Value: 3

I must say I was somewhat disappointed. I haven't been in in a few years, and as the first time back since the pandemic I was very much looking forward to coming in and introducing a friend to the restaurant and enjoying a really special michelin meal. 

Our experience was a mixed bag. Here is a bit of what we tried. 

The not so great items..
The beet cocktail was beautiful, but much too savory for a cocktail. I don't prefer sweet cocktails, but this wasn't balanced and did need a little sweetness to balance it. It was missing a bit of something. 
The Swedish meatballs sadly were the worst item we tried, surprisingly. They had zero flavor, as did the mashed potatoes served with them. 

The star dishes..
Shrimp Toast - by far the highlight of the evening! Although, the $25 for the caviar on top was not necessary.  
The gravlax was good, but not as good as it used to be with mustard seeds previously served with it. 
The short rib was also fantastic with the truffle and foie gras. 

I was also surprised with the lack luster and uninspiring plating of the dishes. I recall the desserts being presented very modern and creative, so I was surprised by the main dishes being presented more like you are eating at someone's house. 

The desserts are amazing here, but sadly we weren't able to have time to stay for dessert, as we had a show to make and service slowed down significantly as we got our entrees and the restaurant got busy. Our waitress then became obsolete.

This is where I was somewhat unimpressed. For having 2 Michelin stars you would expect top notch service! No one wiped our table down in between courses, even as we pointed out the mess. The server just pointed out that the "table gets to eat too". Not impressed to have my new clean fork sat atop the food spillage from the previous course. We also asked for a sommelier. When the som came over he didn't really introduce himself or ask our wine preferences. He simply poured a wine without giving us a menu or other options. The wine he selected, while was good, turned out to be $35 a glass. These type of details were disappointing. When you spend hundreds of dollars you do expect more. 
I don't know if this is the typical service in the bar area, but it certainly doesn't entice me to pay double in the dining room in the future. 

One final note would be the bar food menu selection. You would think although the bar is A La Carte that you would still be able to select any of the items from the tasting menu, but a la carte, but you cannot. It is a completely different menu, unfortunately. 

I'd likely return for Aquavit and dessert at the bar, but I likely wouldn't sit at a table in the bar again, because of the service. I hope this place will return to the greatness it once was!

Been back again for their lunch service. 
Finally had the chance to order their princess cake. 
Heavenly slice of deliciousness; highly recommend folks grab a slice when visiting! Cream is refreshing and not overly sweet. The fondant is super soft and playdough like (without the play dough taste).

I wanted to like it: really badly, as I think Scandinavian social democracy is the right blueprint for the United States. But it's really a mixed bag. Some of what should be mindblowing, like the caviar, gets overpowered by fish flavor, rather than counterbalanced by something complementary, like egg. Other stuff, like the "would you like truffles with that ca-ching ca-ching" (yes, we said) and lambchops just don't mix well together. (When did this trend of putting truffles on absolutely everything start?) 

I will say the famous bird's nest desert is phenomenal, and I might return just to try that again in a year or two. It looks like an actual birds nest and a bunch of wood -- the last thing you'd want to eat -- but then you take a bite and it's chocolate ecstasy. 

But it's not enough to salvage the overall meal, which also takes three hours because of flawed execution and huge delays in between dishes. When you've been to places like Atera and Jean-Georges that bring them out with militantly timed precision, sitting around idling is just not fun.

I had a great memory of spending the Xmas eve afternoon at aquavit and the smorgasbord was fantastic .....This was years ago. 
This year it was a huge disappointment. My family and I were seated in the back room which was bare with just a minimum center piece 
It felt like sitting in a hospital 
When we told the waiter the room was very cold He explained that the heat in the building had been turned down for the weekend and suggested we should get our coats! 
In a Michelin rated restaurant?!!!!
The food was nowhere near as good as I remember It didn't have any special flavor and touch. The ham was served in rolled up slices with som graded cheese on top The herring was ok, nothing special The steamed salmon was tasteless and sad locking decorated with soggy slices of cucumber. 
The food doesn't live up to its former reputation at all 
I'm sure the restaurant could try harder to find someone that could cook Scandinavian all though no one near Marcus Samuelson 
My son had to prepay the $225:- per person and it felt like a waste of a lot of money.
We had a reunion and decided to enjoy our time at the restaurant as much as we could BUT we will not come back

More than worthy of its Michelin and a personal preference above several other NY two stars.

At the end of the day the food has a particular POV (thankfully not generic) and if you like flavors such as cured fish and capers and butter and horseradish and pumpernickel and licorice (prepared in a very refined manner) ... you may love this. If not, then you should probably try something more anodyne.

Staff was excellent and the space is just right.

FWIW, the dining room and bar shouldn't be compared, totally different experiences.

If you are looking for a dining experience, this restaurant will not disappoint. It's in the heart of Manhattan next to Park avenue, which sets the right tone beautifully decorated establishment. Greeted by a polite hostess we immediately noticed the Scandinavian influences wrapped around a modern motif. The servers were very helpful and described the dishes In a perfectly enticing way, leaving us salivating for them to step aside for us to dig in.

Dig in we did. The preparation was unique, the flavors were amazing. The textures and taste of each serving, and there were about nine, were an unexpected surprise each time. If you like fish, you will not be disappointed. If meat is your palate, you'll find yourself asking why they'd put it on the menu. It was hard, cold and lacked flavor.

However, the desert was spectacular. Probably one of the best I have ever tried. That alone deserves a Michelin star, and they have two.

I attended Aquavit for a wine dinner in the group dining room.  The food was stellar, particularly the fluke crudo (which was swimming in a deliciously bright citrus sauce), Amish chicken, and the most deliciously crispy duck breast I can remember eating.  Everything was packed with flavor, but nothing was heavy.  One of the elite spots in the city right now.

Absolutely stunning. Aquavit located in midtown has a subtle elegance that can't be ignored with its classy vibes. We came to celebrate a birthday. We made reservations and was seated immediately. The hustle and bustle of the open kitchen was great to watch but you can barely hear it through the glass windows and doors. There was more servers than guest and you felt very well taken care of. Every dish was provided with much thought and flavors were brought in together harmoniously. The menu was mostly seafood with the exception of the lamb. Every seafood piece was fresh and the lamb was not game-y at all. One of us opted for no lamb and got the duck instead. The biggest surprise was our dessert! The artic bird's nest was a dream, balancing the perfect textures and tasted to create an exquisite illusion with an indescribable tasting profile. 10/10!

Really solid food that served as an elegant demonstration of how the skillful use of acidic ingredients can elevate a dish. The caviar and potato course is a strong contender for the best thing I've ever eaten. Wasn't a fan (despite the hype) of the bird's nest dessert; felt like it was too busy. Nevertheless, it didn't detract much from an otherwise outstanding experience.
Everything about our dining experience was perfect. I would award the coveted third Michelin star if I could.

Came in December 2022. My boyfriend and I started with the Aurora melonalis and Beet me up Scotty! cocktails, which were good if not amazing, and did the chef's tasting menu. I would say the three highlights were:

+ Potato chip caviar potato course
+ King crab from Norway - this ruined me for all other crab
+ THE BIRDS NEST DESSERT - insane

Salt as a take-home gift was also perfect. Execution was fantastic overall.

The server was very attentive and conscientious of my nut allergy. Restaurant had a really nice ambiance. 

The bread basket we ordered was hands down one of the best things I have ever tasted in my life. I have only been to NYC twice, but this place will be on my list when I return simply because of the bread.

Having said that, I was unimpressed with the other food. I got the Swedish meatballs and my potatoes were cold. I don't like my food to be really hot, but even this was too cold for me. 

Also, I learned that I don't like Aquavit (the drink)!
Eveything was so spectacular the plating of each dish was so beautiful. Can't wait to come back!

Food: 3
Decor: 4
Service: 5

Came here for a work dinner with a party of 5. They have 2 Michelin stars and serve Nordic food, which was definitely unique.

175 pp

Hors d'oeuvre
Great. Really liked the chip with yellowtail and radish, as well as the red dish afterwards.

Fluke and Melon
Okay. The combination of fluke and melon was unique, but overall thought it fell a bit short. Also wished there was a bit more uni.

Foie gras and grannysmith
Good. Foie gras was tasty, and the julienned grannysmith apple provided some nice acid to balance.

Cod and endive
Good. Cod was cooked well as was the endive, and the foam added some nice flavor.

Duck and beets
Good. Duck was cooked perfectly and wasn't too gamey or hard to chew. Beets provided some nice acidic balance.

Meatballs
Okay. We added this to our dinner, and they were pretty good.

Honeycrisp and fennel
Okay. Interesting combination and pretty plating, but wasn't blown away by it.

Petit fours
Good. Truffle, gelee, and caramel.

Service was excellent. Overall, glad I was able to visit and check this place out, but was hoping I would enjoy it more than I did given the two stars.

Came here for dinner; some solid eats and they have a reasonably priced menu, as far as 2 Michelin star places go.

We started with the herring sampler, which was definitely my favorite of the night. The herring itself was tangy and sweet, and I enjoyed getting to try the 3 different flavors. They all complimented the herring quite well, and honestly I have a hard time picking a favorite!

We ordered 3 entrees to share--the short rib, Swedish meatballs, and arctic char. Honestly, I think we expected the entrees to be smaller since it's a Michelin star spot, but it actually ended up being plenty of food! My favorite was probably the arctic char, which was cooked perfectly and had great texture. I also liked the radish that paired with the char. The short rib was soft and tender, and the meatball was juicy and I enjoyed having the tartness of the berry to contrast. I did feel that some of the dishes were a tad too salty for my taste, however.

One of my least favorite Michelin rated restaurants visited so far. I expected a lot for two stars and it certainly was no Jean George or Gabriel Kreuther. The attention to detail and service just wasn't there for me. My fiancé who isn't as much of a foodie as me even mentioned that it just felt like a "regular" restaurant. Not the Michelin quality we so highly anticipated. No black gloves, greetings from the manager, in depth knowledge of menu, bread or dessert carts. Maybe the French have just spoiled me? 

Simply put, the menu and experience was boring. I was in and out in an hr tops. You spends upwards of $1000 at Michelin restaurants to experience new foods and combinations that make your eyes light up. The food is basically art but this was just food cooked well... The most exciting dish I had was the bird's nest dessert. Flawlessly executed dish but even that was just okay because the concept is popular in NYC restaurants at the moment. I've had versions of it at least three times already elsewhere. This one being the best though, I must say. 
My favorite bite? the bread. Now that was like no bread I've ever tasted before. It was excellent from taste to texture. 

Don't get me wrong, the staff was very pleasant and the food was enjoyable. However, if it weren't for the caviar tasting add on, I would've left very disappointed. The whole ordeal was just rushed and lack luster.

So delicious. At $85 for a full course TWO michelin star lunch, Aquavit punches far above its weight. They present scandinavian food in a very comforting light, reminiscent of homey New England dishes with sour/earthy twists. Every dish piqued my interest, the service was kind and warm, and I left with the same satisfaction and fullness that I would have from a burger and fries. Amazing lunch.

This was it. This was absolutely hands down the BEST meal I've had in my life. Will forever be looking for any meal that gives me the experience I had at this one. Every single bite and flavor profile was so intentionally crafted, our servers were amazing and hilarious, and the salt they gave us as a gift at the end was an incredible touch to the whole meal. 

I will definitely be returning to try the tasting menu!
Lovely lovely food and experience, but not an accessibly priced menu. Makes sense why such an older crowd.

I had Easter Lunch here. It was beautiful. Great presentations and wonderful seafood. Specially loved Swedish bouillabaisse. Carrot cake was good surprise . And birds nest was perfectly cute for Easter.
The food was incredible. The service perfect. I learned a lot about the wines and had pleasant (but appropriately brief) conversations with the sommelier.

Taking a trip down memory lane and recalling when I booked two dinners at Aquavit within three months in 2022 because I loved it so much. 

Aquavit is fantastic if you've never had Scandinavian food before. Their food is truly so spectacular, with light airy courses that highlight their fresh ingredients, and their PLATING - absolutely gorgeous, and explains their two Michelin stars. 

Since it was over a year ago, I can't remember the exact dishes but some remain the same throughout their tasting menu iterations: the Arctic bird nest dessert (AMAZING), and the caviar and potatoes starter for example. I tried both the regular tasting menu and the more extensive Chef's menu, and I have to say that if you've got a medium sized appetite like me, the regular tasting menu works just fine. If you really want to indulge, then you have to go with the Chef's menu but just be prepared to have the staff roll you out of the restaurant. 

Also their cocktails are just lovely - must add on to the start of your meal for a really special night.

Great service and beautifully presented plates. I want to rate 3.5 but the app won't let me. The flavors were a bit too timid for me overall and a bit light on the seasoning across the board, otherwise I would have rated higher. One dish had a nice umami broth but I needed more umami! The bread is to die for. The crab was so delicate (a highlight). I get it - I think there are folks who appreciate subtle and delicate flavors - but for me, I like bolder flavors (e.g. Aska).
Fun, innovative meal.  My husband brought me here for my birthday and I loved it.  A little different from the more typical French options available for prix fixe fine dining.
Beautiful restaurant with wonderful and attentive staff. However, I think I learned maybe this type of food is not for me. Light, pickled flavors, everything was very delicate and thoughtful.

Read about the Annual Herring Festival on Aquavit's IG  page so we made a reservation. 
Apparantly to experience the 'festival' you had to sit in the lounge. Not the dining room where only the tasting menu is offered. 
The festival is not really a festival at all. I've had their herring (3 kinds) in the dining room at a previous lunch. 
This time we were offered a choice of 3 or 5 types of herring. We ordered all 5,  that were served with crackers, potatoes and bites of cheese). 
All the dishes were very good. 
We also ordered cold tomato soup and an entree of salmon. 
The food, as always, is delicious. 
The lounge was quiet with only 3 tables taken. 
I would have preferred to sit in the dining room and wish I completely understood what was being offered. 
The server was friendly and masked.
Great presentation. It was good food but it was my first experience with Scandinavian so perhaps I'm just not a huge fan of scandi food

Went for a special occasion. This place is one of the best places in the city and isn't even priced that high tbh OG I think the food they serve. Brilliant experience and I will totally go back again :) 

Service was excellent. For two stars, this place is very cool and definitely not uptight. The decor adds to the charm and to the laid back vibe 

They started us off with the chilled Vegetable broth with a chamomile oil emulsion - so much flavor in that tiny thing 

Sommelier did not push us at all for wine - love that! 

Ordered some cocktails - horses and carriage is one of those elegantly made cocktails. It's art in a glass - the after taste stays like a warm hug 

I ordered a Negroni off menu and was very pleased 

Another complimentary dish was the Shrimp canapé. Little tart was delicious and went with the super fresh dill forward shrimp Topping. Just when I was beginning to think of this was predictable they gave us a cod skin that crisped up by baking and had a cucumber gel and something else I can't for life of me remember. Omg! That was so umami and craftily done :) 

I think this was precisely the moment they got my heart :) 

Yellow tail crudo came with a beautiful cilantro oil and fermented tomato water. Burst of subtle flavors with the yellowtail shining like the bright star that it was. Lovely, great dish

Ok confession - I am not a fish person and was most concerned with the trout.  It when they brought out the blackened trout with that smoked yogurt and the beet and horseradish sorbet on top sitting pretty on a blackened seaweed tuille, I became a convert. The green strawberries were just the burst of freshness I wanted in that dish. 

Ofc by this time I'm head over heels in awe with the chef's talent and they could have stopped trying. But their Cod with the smoked dill sauce and asparagus turnip somehow managed to elevate the experience even further. 

The rye bread with cultured butter is a nice little palette changing course in between though 

Finally, they got out the duck breast that was skin crisped and served with the Cherry compote thing - heaven! Such an elegant dish and bold flavors although not showing off! You know what I mean?

Alright, ending the night with the oat and elderflower dessert - it was great but since the bar was like up there in the sky beyond stratosphere this course was possibly my least loved.

We ordered the arctic nest for the table as well - and so glad we did. The white chocolate eggs with that honey tuille and the yogurt snow - there was drama with the snow thing there was finesse and ofc there was taste. 

Plug in for the server who recommended their lavender martini - I will go back again and again till my bank requests me not to to have those martinis and the rye bread 

Alright I'm done with my PDA.

Disclaimer: this was my first Michelin-starred restaurant experience. As someone who enjoys eating out frequently with a diverse palate, this was by far the highest quality meal I have ever had. We decided to do the 3 course lunch menu.

Every dish was perfectly crafted. The ingredients were very fresh & crisp. Presentation was neat & clean. The menu was simple, yet elegant. Each bite was a unique & perfectly crafted work of art. You could tell that there was great attention to detail in the various elements that comprised each dish. Flavors were very well balanced.

Wait service was fantastic. Attentive, personable, friendly, yet not over-intrusive.

I could write a short story on each of these dishes but my absolute favorites were the scallop crudo, arctic char, & the arctic bird's nest!

I'm convinced that the negative reviews on this restaurant are people who have an unrefined palate or those who consider chains like Olive Garden as "good" food. 

Great experience overall! Highly recommend for a nice meal out!

Follow me on IG for more food pics/videos @jason.chews

o m g

best and craziest meal of my life. i don't think i need to describe the food, just look at the pictures. everything was so thoughtful, down to the service. i really, really appreciated the server at the end who came over to our table and asked if we had any questions about the restaurant, and then proceeded to point out different things in the kitchen. worth the chunk that was taken out of my bank account
Went back for a walk-in lunch.  Had the tasting menu and was delicious once again.  One of the best seafood focused restaurants I go to.

I came here for lunch the last time that I was in NYC so I just had to come back and try out their full chef's tasting menu for dinner this time! I'm so glad that I did. 
This was one of the best meals that I've ever had in NYC and in general. I can not get over how delicious, balanced, and satisfying that each dish was. You can tell so much time and effort went into plating and creating these dishes, they are all so beautiful yet restrained. 
This menu was actual perfection, the sauces in each dish were very satisfying and tied everything together so well. 
I will never forget how the white asparagus and langoustine course tasted, that was one of my favorite dishes ever. 
The lamb was cooked to perfection and came with insanely delicious creamed morels and a potato terrine, I loved this course so much. 
Dessert started with a "Rhubarb and Blossoms" course that was so unique and yummy, I also loved that it came with a drink. 
I've always wanted to try their iconic Arctic Bird's Nest dessert since I saw it on instagram last year and it did not disappoint, it was so intricate and the flavors were wonderful, the "eggs" are so cute and cool. 
As you can tell I loved everything but my absolute favorites were the Langoustine & White Asparagus, Trout & English Peas, and the Caviar & Potato. 

I will definitely be back some day, this was such a fantastic meal and I cannot recommend Aquavit enough!

This was my first time trying a Scandanavian fine-dining experience, and I was not disappointed! I had a lovely experience and would definitely highly recommend a visit to anyone that is thinking about trying it out. The food is exquisite, and beyond that the service and ambience remarkably refined.

The tasting menu was 7 courses with some amuse bouches to start and some sweets at the end. Everything was beautifully crafted, and the pacing was great. There was never any moment that felt too long of a wait or too rushed.

My favorite standout dish was definitely the Arctic Bird's Nest, which is the signature dessert! I saw some behind the scenes in a short documentary on how they put it together, but it was so much more majestic in-person. I'm obsessed with the snowy garnish on top to simulate real snow, and biting into the egg to reveal a sweet yolk was absolutely delightful. The rest of the presentation pulls its weight too texture and flavor. Overall a superb dish to finish the night with!

This is more of a 3.5. The service was phenomenal, and everything felt very upscale. The chef's kitchen looked very well run. The food was yummy, but I just can't justify the price for dishes they serve. Nordic cuisine is very fishy, so keep that in mind when you're deciding! The flavors were elevated, but not very fun/experimental, if that makes sense. Nothing stood out very much. This would be best suited for a nice business lunch or dinner.

Aquavit offers exquisite seasonal Nordic cuisine from the talented Chef Emma Bengtsson, who is only the second female chef in the United States to win 2 Michelin stars.

Located around the corner from the Dining Room (which only serves the tasting menu), the Bar Room at Aquavit offers more approachable a la carte options from the same Michelin star menu at surprisingly reasonable prices!
We have dined here a few times  and they have always delivered great service and food.

Very memorable experience at Aquavit. The tasting menu was well curated and every plate was beautiful presented. My favorite had to be the cod/tomato and the duck. Both were very well paired and the flavor profiles popped. The cod was super flaky and the acid from the tomato made it melt in my mouth. The duck was beautifully seared and had a perfect crunch.

The service was (of course) impeccable and the ambiance was elegant. Very seafood forward but I recommend!

What a great meal to end 2023. We opted for the lunch chef's tasting menu that consisted of 3 savory courses and 2 desserts--highlighting the famous Arctic's Bird's Nest, a true iconic and signature dish for divine reasons. Each course was plated with utmost detail and care which equaled its flavors. Lots of points for the great pace between dishes and explanations as well. 

The dining room is intimate and provides the perfect ambiance looking out 5th Ave during this time of year with all the Christmas lights. Honored to say the seafood/fish element will definitely be bringing me back. Fantastic service as well all throughout, bravo!

My husband and I came here for his birthday and had a lovely time.  We had the Chef's Tasting Menu and had our minds blown at first bite!  The restaurant is beautiful and serene.  Service was near perfect.  The only issue we had was  trying to get someone to give us our check so we could pay.  Other than that, staff was attentive, friendly without being nosy, kind, and knowledgeable.  I had such a lovely time I'm considering trying to get a reservation for my birthday!

Had the lunch menu. 

The shrimp toast dish was perfect - the crunchiness and butteriness of the brioche toast combined with the refreshing shrimp taste in a creamy mayonnaise, with dill and lemon to provide a fresh and tangy element and balance the richness. 

The wagyu was not good especially with the supplement prices. I felt the wagyu could have been more tender and buttery, as it lacked the melt-in-your-mouth feeling. There were a couple nice and surprising flavours on the plate. However, the jus was a bit bitter and failed to enrich the beef flavours. The crispy potato and cabbage felt like uninspired pairings with little synergy.

The Arctic Bird's Nest was a work of art, truly beautifully and masterfully constructed. There is a very delicious blend of goat cheese and yogurt flavours along with a fruit jam for sweetness and tanginess, dark chocolate to offset the sweetness, and tulle for a crunch. Despite the dessert being a visual masterpiece, it was not out of this world flavor-wise.

That brings me to my biggest critique. For the calibre of dining, the flavours were nothing truly special. Delicious, but not exceptional.

This was likely our 3rd or possibly our 4th time to Aquavit during the last 20 years. First time at their original location and then all the rest here.

Atmosphere is inviting and helps increase the anticipation of what's to come.

The diversity of the menu and the preparations are still excellent. However, we were disappointed that the level of service, from reception, and throughout the meal, was not up to prior visits and expectations. Though we arrived at 6:15, before most other diners, service for wine and amuse bouche was exceedingly slow for the first 30 minutes. Service especially from the sommelier who exhibited an attitude, was not appropriate.

This is a costly dining experience, and for $1000 per couple, everyone should be on their top game.

Aquavit offers a Scandinavian fare, and they offer a lunch, tasting, and a chef's tasting menu, as well as takeout options.

We came here with a group of friends while we were in town, and we all opted for the chef's tasting menu.

We had:
+Yellowtail and Pear
+Scallop and Chestnut
+Caviar and Potato - this was a favorite within our group
+Lobster and Sunchoke
+Black Bass and Cauliflower
+Duck and Broccoli Rabe
+Apple and Long Pepper
+Arctic Bird's Nest - a fun and tasty dessert that we enjoyed

Everything was well-presented and aesthetically pleasing.

Service was friendly, and the ambiance was sophisticated and relaxing.

+chef's tasting menu 
+takeout available

Deeply enjoyable Michelin 2 Star restaurant at an accessible price point. The 5 course tasting did not cost much more than a meal at a steakhouse featuring a decent bottle of wine. 

Aquavit is a beautiful restaurant and all of the preparations, in a seafood-forward format, were memorable. The corner table for 6 here was really neat. I'd just note that the pomp and drama you'd find a more traditional French Michelin experience were largely (but not entirely) absent. This is more like Elske in Chicago than Le Louis XV in Monaco. And, considering the culture reflected, I'd think rightfully so.

We had lunch here and it was delightful. They have a price point that seem more accessible for a 2 michelin star restaurant. They offer a three course lunch here for eighty-five (two course for seventy five). It's a nice place to go for a more casual Michelin level dining experience.

Aquavit is the place where dill and pickled vegetables run the show. As a Scandinavian restaurant, I understand the somewhat heavy usage of dill. Nonetheless, the small dining room smelled amazing with views of the kitchen. The tasting menu was not too quick and not too long as it was about 2 hours for 8 courses. The main winners of the night were the scallop foam dish that tasted spectacular as it hit almost all of the flavor profiles. The star of the day was the bird's nest and it was crazy. A fun presentation with delicious flavors and the egg almost tasted like ice cream. The duck was good as it has a nice char. I wasn't a fan of the sun choke with the lobster but it did not ruin my experience. The black bass was delicious too. The yellowtail and pear were refreshing as well. All in all, Aquavit offered a fantastic tasting menu that wasn't too heavy as I left content but not overly full. Also, Aquavit makes in house aquavit but just watch out because it is strong. A memorable experience that matched expectations for a 2 star.

Aquavit is exceptional in every way. My husband and I went for their lunch for our wedding anniversary and it blew us away. The lunch included yellowtail & pear, cod & cauliflower, beef & black trumpet, and arctic bird's nest for dessert. We added the cheese board for an extra price. Every bite was outstanding - so fresh, creative, and flavorful. We really were exported to Scandinavia during our meal. 

My husband got a cocktail and I got a mocktail. Both delicious. 

Their decor is minimalist, sharp, understated, and neutral, and I enjoyed it. 

Service was on top of everything. I loved the open kitchen concept. 

They gave us a goody bag with smoked sea salt to use for cooking. 

Deserving of all of the awards and accolades. Such a standout in the expensive restaurants category!

Food, service, ambience...all were exceptional and far above most previous dining experiences. We had the chef's tasting menu along with the wine pairing and thoroughly enjoyed the almost three hour experience.

A bit more old school Michelin restaurant in decor and service but that's not a complaint.  The food was EXCELLENT the staff was perfection, I liked the classic modernist Scandinavian decor.  Personally I think this is underrated and often forgotten when people are thinking of the best restaurants in the city.  Check it out for some amazing seafood and you won't be disappointed.

We came here for lunch tasting menu. The service was top notch, we received lots of snacks and gifts. All the courses were well-paced and delicious. The seafood dishes were fresh. You need to get the artic bird nest, it was a masterpiece and all the flavors went so well with each other. I would definitely recommend?

The dining room is stunning, and I love that you can see into the kitchen as they are preparing and plating everything. It was very cool to see Chef Emma Bengtsson at work. The dishes were bright and delicious, and a little surprising (in the best way possible). Service was friendly and personable.

I would have given Aquavit five stars, but I must restrict it to four solely due to the level of service we encountered. Candidly, I could consider lowering it by another half-star, but that wouldn't be fair since the food was truly exceptional. In the politest way possible, the service for a two-star Michelin restaurant felt amateurish.

Food: We selected the Chef's Tasting Menu because, let's be honest, we wanted the "Arctic Bird's Nest" dessert, which was one of the most beautiful and delicious desserts I have ever eaten. We were also celebrating a birthday, and the accompanying celebratory cake was equally delectable. Setting aside the exceptional desserts, the Chefs Tasting Menu at Aquavit was a triumph, showcasing a breadth of flavors and culinary craftsmanship that stood impressively on its own.

Every dish we enjoyed at Aquavit was a refined expression of Nordic cuisine, elevated by inventive and tasteful additions that took the flavors to new heights. For instance, the Langoustine with Meyer lemon featured a delicate shrimp "cracker" on top that was unlike anything I've ever tasted. The caviar and potato dish and the red snapper with apple both showcased culinary elegance, using the freshest ingredients to highlight their natural flavors. Each dish and its elements were thoughtfully paired with sauces and garnishes that subtly enhanced the natural flavors without overpowering them. And the BREAD! I find myself wishing for a small bakery attached to the restaurant so that I can indulge in their exquisite bread daily.

Chef Emma Bengtsson has established herself as an exceptional culinary talent, which is evident in Aquaivits' culinary offerings. As the first Swedish female chef to earn two Michelin stars and only the second in the U.S. to do so, Chef Bengtsson masterfully combines traditional techniques with bold, contemporary flavors. Her approach creates a Nordic dining experience deeply rooted in tradition yet strikingly modern.

We didn't explore the full range of their cocktail offerings, opting instead for classic martinis, which were excellent. We also enjoyed a few rounds of Aquavit, "water of life," which I highly recommend trying.

Service: As I mentioned, the service did not meet the expectations for a restaurant with two Michelin stars. This was not just a one-off instance. Everyone lacked polish, from the check-in staff to the bartenders (we had a few drinks before dinner in the bar room) and the wait staff in the main dining room. Specifically, the front-of-house staff was not responsive to some requests and was slightly awkward. The bartenders were not the friendliest group. In the main dining room, it felt like every waiter was on their first day.

Despite the shortcomings in service, the remarkable quality of the dishes at Aquavit ensures that I would not hesitate to return or recommend this restaurant to others. The need for service improvement is mentioned not as a deterrent but as a constructive suggestion to align the entire experience with the high standards set by their culinary offerings.
One of the finest restaurants I've ever been! It was truly a privilege and honor to taste their food and wine. Impeccable service and romantic ambiance.

A most excellent experience. Great food well served. A restaurant which richly deserves its reputation. 

Andrew Goldman

I was not sure about this place. I honestly had a doubt, and I was not enthusiastic to go to Aquavit. 

I was w r o n g ! It was a fantastic experience!

You should try and do the pairing with some very unique wine selection!

Went to Aquavit as part of a recent trip to NYC. Was curious having Scandinavian ancestors, but I can pretty much guarantee they did not have a menu quite like Aquavit. The food was exceptional and our service from Virginia and wait staff was perfect. Topping it off, Patrick gave a very nice tour of the Kitchen after our late lunch reservation, making it a great meal and experience. The Birds Nest dessert blew me away for both presentation and deliciousness. Honestly, one of the best dining experiences, and I must thank my wife for picking this restaurant, she had carte Blanche, and will be a cherished memory.

Aquavit was my first michelin star restaurant experience in my 20's and so the nostalgia alone had me hooked but really the food was exceptional! I went back 2 more times within the last 20 years and the last time I went I did feel a little underwhelmed. The service was not what it used to be...not horrible but just not as attentive. However, if you're a seafood lover, you really should not miss out on dining here.

I came here a couple of days ago for an anniversary dinner and the experience was amazing! We opted for the tasting menu paired with the wine and the servers were very knowledgeable on the dishes and wines! The food itself was delicious and so fresh and flavorful! The service was also amazing as the servers were always checking in with us. The ambiance was stellar as well! Perfect spot for a romantic dinner - would definitely recommend

Had birthday celebration dinner here.
Service was amazing! Everyone was nice and patient enough to explain everything to us.

We all had 5 courses meal set. 
Taste was pretty random between dishes, feel like they pull each dish from somewhere else as a course menu. Food presentation was pretty as a Michelin starred  place should be. 
Overall everything still tasted good, but not as 2 stars michelin level. 

Drinks were not Francy but classic! Yummy but not Amazing.
 
Classic decor, not really giving romantic vibe, more like modern design. You will see open kitchen while dinning.

I would say, if you have not tried, give it a try! It was a different vibe and experience than a lot of classic Michelin 2 -3 stars in the city

Service could definitely improve. The irony is, this is a 2 Michelin star but the service and lack of attentiveness felt like I was dining in a casual fast food place. 
(Was promoted by Yelp to update the review)

Overall, my experience at Aquavit was excellent. The food was above average, especially the seafood, and the service was generally okay, despite a small accident when we were served the first small bite.
When we arrived, we were greeted warmly and professionally. The refreshment drink, made of cucumber, lime, and oil, was refreshing and excellent - a great start to the meal. After the refreshment drink, we were served a small bite, but unfortunately, the whole dish slipped from the waiter's hand. It wasn't the waiter's fault; the design of the dish was not user-friendly and difficult to handle with one hand. The food ended up on my pants and the floor, but thankfully, I had a napkin covering my lap.
I wasn't upset, as accidents happen. I went to the bathroom to clean myself and sat on the other side of the table while they cleaned the mess. They asked if I wanted to sit on the other side of the table or remain seated in the same place. I chose to remain seated. While I was waiting, one of the waitresses in a gray suit (an Asian lady) informed me that I couldn't sit on that side because people would walk by. I believe they should have communicated internally before addressing the guest. A more professional approach would have been to say, "Sorry for the mess. We will have someone clean it for you, and you can remain seated in the same place. I apologize, but we can't let you sit on this side because people would walk by."
Once the dinner resumed, we started to enjoy our meal again. All the seafood tasted excellent. I loved the king crab leg, scallop (so fresh and perfectly cooked), caviar, spot prawn, and red snapper. The chef is truly skilled at making sauces. Additionally, the restaurant made it up to us by adding caviar to our scallop, which was a delightful gesture.

Went for the three-course lunch menu and found a hair in the cod dish. A two Michelin star restaurant can definitely do better. 
staff were nice and gave a complimentary princess cake, but the cake also tasted pretty average. very disappointed, to be honest .

Celebrated my birthday here for lunch! I enjoyed the three course meal with the herring sampler to start. It was nice to try and it came prepared in three ways. Next, i had the classic Swedish meatballs which tasted authentic with lingonberries and light mashed potatoes. Finally, i enjoyed the princess cake for dessert, which was delicious. I also tried the fluke crudo which had a strawberry sauce and the pappardelle which had complex flavors and included well prepared vegetables like chanterelle mushrooms. The service was great and they gave me a birthday ice cream and cookies and thanked me for celebrating there.

Aquavit is well deserving of the 2 Michelin stars. Every dish we tried was amazing and creative, the service was attentive and professional, just an overall enjoyable experience. We went late on a Friday night and were one of the last people to leave, and did not feel rushed at any point of the night. 

My only con was the drink prices. I know, fine dining, Michelin stars, but not being able to get a single glass of wine for less than $40? Seems kind of insane, even in NYC.

Absolutely stunning. This sums up everything about Aquavit. The dining room is understated chic. The service was perfect. The food, "sigh", was divine. We had the Chef's Tasting Menu and it met all expectations and more. Each dish just kept getting better. The bread course might be the best I've ever had. The famous Arctic Bird's Nest dessert was as perfect as a plated dessert can get. Their two Michelin Stars are certainly well deserved. Thank you, Aquavit for a truly memorable dining experience.

A friend and I stopped by without reservations on a Wednesday afternoon. Promptly seated, we were offered 2 or 3 course menu for 65/75 if you wanted dessert.  We got the 2 course which was plenty of food. I had the herring to start with a shot of horseradish aquavit. Followed by Swedish meatballs with lingonberries and mashed potatoes. Everything was delicious and they even brought out some rye bread when I inquired if they had some.

Went there for a dinner with a group.  Not the first time.  Food and service are always exceptional. 

Started with cold fish starter.  Super well prepared with some vegetables and other accompaniments 

Smoked samlmkn of course was next.  A little salty for me but the usual trimmings.  Amazing 

Cod is one of my favourite fish. That was a perfect way to end.  Delicious as always, well prepared in a nice broth.  

Great meal.  I recommend this place.

We had a lovely dinner in a private room.  The service was fantastic and the atmosphere was welcoming.

We had options of salmon or chicken, I picked the chicken and it was delish!  The scallop was very tasty and the chocolate tart was a perfect finisher!

So glad I had the opportunity to have dinner here!

Had dinner here as part of a large group in the private room in the back. Knowing this is a 2 star Michelin restaurant I was wondering what might set it apart. A few things...the rolls as stupid as this might sound were perfect. As if they were just baked. The salad was dressed perfectly and the candied pecans that accompanied it were great. Main of steak was very tasty. Dessert was a delicious chocolate tart. I would go back on my own for sure! P.S. The small passed appetizers were over the top!!

It's not often that you find yourself experiencing exquisite Swedish fine dining. Being Swedish, this was an absolute treat. Cocktail wise, please delight in the Depeche Mode. It's a bourbon based cocktail with a sweet counterpart of pineapple. We enjoyed the chefs tasting menu- starting off with the most interesting melange of elk tartar and a pumpkin spiced gummy. Probably the best pop of flavor I've had in awhile. 
Patrick and River were great to us, it helped elevate the experience.

Having been to multiple Scandinavian countries, I definitely wanted to try this 2 Michelin starred Scandinavian restaurant! We stopped by for lunch on my birthday during our trip to NY. Service was phenomenal and the food was incredible.

For the lunch menu you can order a 2 course, 3 course, or full tasting menu. What we didn't know is that if you order the 2 course, you can order mix-match your two courses (i.e. 2 desserts OR 1 appetizer and 1 dessert OR 1 entrée and 1 dessert, etc.). We got appetizers and entrees for our two course which fluke crudo & shrimp toast skagen and both got the cod entrée. We also ordered lattes and I got a lingonberry aquavit. For my birthday they were gracious enough to provide a complimentary princess cake which was delectable. Not to mention lunch is at a great and approachable price point.

Thanks for a memorable birthday lunch!

I've been eating at Aquavit since it first opened. While the early days were exciting, after a while it meandered as Marcus took on other projects. Now it seems that Aquavit has had a bit of a resurgence. Not as innovative as it was in the early days, but truly good food.

Good but just not two star Michelin in my opinion. Yes we ate in the Bar rooms and would have at least expected a representation of the main dining room menu. The service was good but not two star Michelin. The food was good. Has the salmon which was lovely and nicely presented. My wife had the Swedish meatballs which were nothing so outstanding although recommended by our waiter.
A spectacular experience on all levels.  Service staff was very knowledgeable and  courteous. Food was unique,delicious and well balanced.

First time visiting a Michelin star Scandinavian restaurant. Located in midtown, this place gives a very chill, relaxing vibe. It was slow given we visited on a Tuesday night. Entire staff was very attentive and they were so sweet to give us complimentary cakes even though we hadn't shared we were celebrating our birthdays (they just overheard us). It was definitely unexpected but definitely appreciated. Food was good as we had the Chef's tasting menu. Chef was able to accommodate my no meat preference. However I must say the price wasn't worth us paying approximately $340 each but I am glad to give this place a try.

I was lucky enough to squeeze in three courses at their bar seating before my broadway show and I'm so glad I did. Some of the best food of my life and a beautiful restaurant. The ceiling in the bar area was so unique and elegant with the wood slats in soft waves above you. The lighting could not have been better, enough to see clearly but so soft and inviting. The staff worked together as a team and you could tell they wanted everyone there to have the best experience possible. 
They were very cognizant of timing for me as I had to be at a show at 7. They coursed everything perfectly and I even had time for an espresso with dessert.
They took my entire order at the start to better course everything for me and were very helpful when I asked about portions at the beginning as I was eating alone. It is fine dining so your plate will not be loaded. I got an appetizer, entree and dessert and was able to eat all but a couple bites of each comfortably along with a cocktail, the High Coast. The cocktail was simple with an anise aquavit base with lingonberry and soda. It was light, refreshing but flavorful and unique. 
I got the crab Sagan to start. I could have left happy after this. It was stunning. Piled with crab. The dressing was delightful. Somehow rich and light at the same time. The perfect flavor compliments to the generous crab. The "toast" base was like an uncrustable in the best way. The perfect piece of bread. My mom used to make a crab salad on toast dish growing up and it made smile to think about it here. This delight was followed by the salmon entree. Best cooked salmon of my life. The creamy cucumber dill sauce was reminiscent of my favorite childhood salad that my grandma used to make. I finished the meal with the princess cake. Oh my. No words. Perfectly sweet, spongy but not soggy all the right textures and gorgeous. 
The meal brought me on a journey from euphoric to tears of nostalgia to transcendent. A month later I'm still talking about it so often my husband is sick of hearing about it. He's just jealous he didn't get to experience it with me.

Leif Ericsson walked so aquavit could run 

Very solid Nordic cuisine, i wish it were more authentic tho like being in an igloo or something

Never had fancy Scandinavian food! Haven't really had that much exposure to Scandinavian food at all! Besides ikea, and whatever they served on Icelandic air. 

I was quite pleasantly surprised by aquavit! The interior feels modern, upscale, and very calm. I like the open kitchen where you can see the chefs hard at work. I was thoroughly impressed by how smooth their operations were, both in the kitchen, and on the floor. 

My friends and I got the 5 course tasting menu, which I felt like was a sufficient amount of food. The price point was also fair. 

Standout dishes were that tartar tart that was served as an amuse bouche. It was a burst of flavors and textures that were soo delightful. The Chilean sea bass was also really well done. The tomato and other fermented vegetables as well as the broth were perfect accompaniments to the delicate fish. The iberico pork was also soo good. The meat was so tender, and perfectly cooked. 

I was disappointed by the scallop and cauliflower dish. Overall, it was good, but the cauliflower foam it came with, as well as the other fermented vegetables overpowered the scallop :c it kinda felt like the scallops were just added as an afterthought for a different texture. 

Service was immaculate, which was to be expected. Everything was so smooth, and we felt very well taken care of throughout the whole meal. Or "show" as the host said lol

Overall, I'd recommend this place! Try some reimagined Scandinavian food. I'd like to come back and try their larger tasting menu one day. Gotta have that birds nest you know

Service was fantastic. Staff was very attentive and always came to check on us. They were very particular to detail both in service and with their food.

The place was very clean and there's a large glass to watch the chefs cook. I do wish the dividers were a little lower to have more viewing of the chefs since I always enjoy watching them prepare. 

Scallops - godly - good portion must try
Shrimp toast - awesome as well, buttered toast
Meatballs - good, the mash potato has a unique taste
Wagyu - little tough, could have been better 
Arctic birds nest - very unique presentation item, one of their signatures, pricey but enjoyable 

Overall little pricey but very enjoyable. 

Service: 5/5
Food: 4.5/5
Ambiance: 4.5/5

Came to celebrate my husband's birthday and it didn't disappoint. Loved the minimalistic vibes and how you can see the chefs through the glass partition. 

Their Christmas lunch was the perfect holiday treat - we started with a buffet style assortment of small bites. Really fun, something that I've never seen at a Michelin star restaurant, and you got to try a bit of everything. 

Entrees were the stars for me - every item was cooked perfectly, great flavors. Ended with their gingerbread cake rolled into a Yule log - so cute! 

Lastly, the service was top notch - really attentive and my husband had never felt more like a princess than when they gave him a princess cake for his birthday!
Chef Emma and all of the teams are amazing. The food and cocktails are so beautiful. Enjoy!

Probably the classiest Scandinavian restaurant outside Scandinavia itself.  It's premium priced but worth it for the great food and service.

5 star food: this ain't ya IKEA Swedish meatballs for $7 papi!  The sauces and flavor combinations are unbelievably good and mostly healthy.  Try anything with salmon and you almost can't go wrong.

5 star service:  there was a cool Nordic flair to everything.  Service was sort of super efficient but friendly

5 star ambience:  the interior and vibe of the place can best be described as slick IKEA ad, but NOT on a budget and nothing to put together yourself.
Great food. Great service. Wish I had a loaf of bread for myself. The dessert for chef tasting was exquisite.

The menu was very enjoyable and interesting. Service was excellent and on par with other 2+ Michelin-starred restaurants. 

As of Feb 2025, they offer 2 tasting menus and we opted for the Chef's Tasting Menu as it includes their famous "Arctic Bird's Nest" (but costs $100 more than the normal Tasting menu).
Michelin 2 stars Aquavit is one of my favorite restaurants. The cuisine is ALWAYS delicious! Service is ALWAYS friendly and attentive. The restaurant is beautiful. I love the Chef's Tasting Menu.

Wonderful dinner and evening. Cool to be able to see the kitchen working. We went with the 7 course, which was really too much food for the both of us. We tried the non alcoholic pairing which in hind-site I would skip next time. The food was detailed and creative. It's a fantastic experience, and I would recommend.
Fantastic birthday lunch with my husband - highly recommend! Especially loved the Arctic Bird's Nest!

Great service. We love visiting Michelin restaurants and this one caught our eye while in NYC. Simplistic yet vibrant ambiance that makes you feel welcomed immediately. The food was fantastic, probably one of the best wine pairings we've ever had. Every flavor and element of the food and wine together hit every check mark. Would def visit again.

Love the bar menu at Aquavit! There's a handful of tables that can be booked in advance. Same great service, beautiful space, and many of the same wonderful flavors at a more reasonable price. The istebrand sausage and the sea bass burger were true standouts. They also have a full menu of imported aquavit and unique cocktails.

I absolutely loved our experience at Aquavit. When we first arrived to our reservation, they let us know we'd be able to sit at the bar or, the front, dining area. We were really looking forward to sitting in the main dining room, so we waited a bit and they had it taken care of! It was well worth the short wait, as we got to talking and enjoyed some wine prior to dinner. 

The dining room is spacious and when seated, you can peer into the kitchen which is well lit and bright, located directly behind the diners. It's quite the experience and an enjoyable one at that :)

The dinner here is phenomenal. 10/10 recommend! I'll let the photos speak for themselves. Just know both dinner and dessert did not disappoint!!! We left so happy and delighted we experienced a beautiful dining experience at Aquavit.
